facts.claim: The Alaska Division of Motor Vehicles' Request for Crash Report Form (Form 440) can be used to request Crash Report Form 12-200, which is completed by law enforcement.
facts.quote: Crash Report Form 12-200 completed by law enforcement

facts.claim: Form 440 can also be used to request Crash Report Form 12-209, which the requester completed themselves.
facts.quote: Crash Report Form 12-209 completed by myself

facts.claim: An investigating law enforcement officer must forward an electronic report of the accident to the Department of Administration within 24 hours after completing the investigation, though an officer may submit a written report in some cases.
facts.quote: shall, within 24 hours after completing the investigation, forward an electronic report of the accident to the Department of Administration. However, the law enforcement officer may submit a written report

facts.claim: This reporting duty in AS 28.35.080(e) applies to every law enforcement officer who investigates a motor vehicle accident for which a report must be made in the regular course of duty.
facts.quote: Every law enforcement officer who, in the regular course of duty, investigates a motor vehicle accident for which a report must be made

facts.claim: The Alaska Department of Administration provides vehicle registration and driver licensing through the Division of Motor Vehicles.
facts.quote: The Department of Administration also provides indigent defense and children’s advocacy through the Public Defender Agency and the Office of Public Advocacy, and vehicle registration and driver licensing through the Division of Motor Vehicles

facts.claim: Alaska Department of Public Safety (DPS) public records can include State Trooper Collision Reports.
facts.quote: DPS public records could include Alaska State Trooper Incident Reports, Body-Worn Camera Footage, State Trooper Collision Reports, etc.

facts.claim: DPS does not hold the records of local police departments or federal law enforcement agencies.
facts.quote: DPS does not possess the records of local police departments or federal law enforcement agencies.

facts.claim: DPS records requests are started online through the DPS public records portal at dpsalaska.justfoia.com.
facts.quote: You will be redirected to the DPS public records portal: https://dpsalaska.justfoia.com/publicportal/home/newrequest

facts.claim: After completing the DPS request form, the requester clicks Submit to file the request electronically.
facts.quote: After completing the form, click on “Submit” to electronically submit your request.

facts.claim: Form 440 can be mailed to the Division of Motor Vehicles, Attn: Driver Services, 4001 Ingra Street, Ste 101, Anchorage, AK 99503, or emailed to doa.dmv.ads@alaska.gov.
facts.quote: You can mail this form to: Division of Motor Vehicles; Attn: Driver Services; 4001 Ingra Street, Ste 101; Anchorage, AK 99503 or email to doa.dmv.ads@alaska.gov.

facts.claim: The signed Form 440 can be submitted by email to doa.dmv.ads@alaska.gov, or the printed paper original can be mailed.
facts.quote: Submit your signed form 440 by e-mail at doa.dmv.ads@alaska.gov OR mail your printed paper original to:

facts.claim: Requests for copies of previously submitted self-reports must be made in writing to DMV Driver Services using DMV form 440.
facts.quote: Requests for copies of previously submitted reports for your records must be made in writing to the Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV) Drivers Services using DMV form 440.

facts.claim: Form 440 gives 907-269-5551 as the DMV phone number for questions.
facts.quote: For any questions you may contact the DMV at 907-269-5551.

facts.claim: Form 440 requires the date of the incident or crash.
facts.quote: Date of Incident/Crash (required)

facts.claim: Form 440 requires the name of the driver.
facts.quote: Name of Driver (required)

facts.claim: Form 440 asks for the crash report or incident number if available.
facts.quote: Crash Report/Incident # (if available)

facts.claim: Form 440 asks, optionally, for the region or city where the crash occurred.
facts.quote: Region or City the Crash Occurred (optional)

facts.claim: Form 440 has a field for the requester's Alaska driver's license number.
facts.quote: Alaska Driver's License Number

facts.claim: Form 440 is signed by the requester, who acknowledges that improper release of information and false representations to gain DMV record information are prohibited acts.
facts.quote: My signature on this document acknowledges that I understand that improper release of information and/or false representations to gain information from DMV record are prohibited acts.

facts.claim: A DPS records request should include enough detail for the assigned employee to locate the specific records.
facts.quote: include enough detail to allow the assigned employee to locate the specific records being requested.

facts.claim: The DMV charges a $10 fee per crash report requested, payable by check or money order to the State of Alaska, or by VISA, MasterCard or American Express if the requester provides an email address.
facts.quote: There is a $10 fee per crash report requested. Payment can be made by check or money order payable to the State of Alaska. Payment via VISA, MasterCard, or American Express is acceptable by providing your email address.

facts.claim: For card payment, the DMV emails an invoice and mails the crash report once payment has been made.
facts.quote: An invoice will be emailed and once payment has been made, we will mail your crash report to you.

facts.claim: DPS says most requests for police reports have no cost, that most video, photo or audio requests cost $36.49 per request, and that requesters are contacted before processing if a charge applies.
facts.quote: Should your public information request incur a charge; you will be contacted prior to the request being processed. Most requests for police reports have no cost and most video, photo, or audio requests are charged $36.49 per request.

facts.claim: Under Alaska's public records regulations, a public agency must respond to a compliant public records request as soon as practicable, but not later than the 10th working day after receiving it.
facts.quote: as soon as practicable, but not later than the 10th working day after the date the agency receives a request for public records that complies with this chapter, the public agency shall

facts.claim: A public agency may extend that 10-working-day period by up to 10 more working days if it notifies the requester within the original period.
facts.quote: A public agency may extend the basic 10-working-day period established under (a) of this section for a period not to exceed 10 additional working days by providing notice to the requester within the basic 10-working-day period.

facts.claim: Form 440 states that all motor vehicle records are subject to the federal Driver Privacy Protection law and are confidential under Alaska law (AS 28.10.505).
facts.quote: *All motor vehicle records are subject to the Federal Driver Privacy Protection (Chapter 123, Section 2721) and considered confidential under Alaska law (AS 28.10.505).

facts.claim: Personal information from these records may be released only to individuals or organizations that qualify under one of the exceptions listed on the back of Form 440.
facts.quote: Personal information from these records may only be released to individuals or organizations that qualify under one of the exceptions listed on the back of this form.

facts.claim: A requester can qualify by obtaining the information as part of their own personal record.
facts.quote: I qualify to obtain this information as part of my own personal record

facts.claim: One listed exception is written consent from the person who is the subject of the information.
facts.quote: By written consent of person who is the subject of the information.

facts.claim: Another listed exception is use by an insurer, insurance support organization or self-insured entity for claims investigation, anti-fraud activities, rating or underwriting.
facts.quote: For use by an insurer or insurance support organization, or by a self-insured entity, or an agent, employee, or contractor of an insurer, in connection with claims investigation activities, anti-fraud activities, rating, or underwriting;

facts.claim: Another listed exception is use in connection with a civil, criminal, administrative or arbitration proceeding in a court or government agency.
facts.quote: For use in connection with a civil, criminal, administrative, or arbitration proceeding in a court or government agency

facts.claim: As quoted on Form 440, AS 28.10.505 defines personal information as information that identifies a person, such as name, address, telephone number and medical or disability information, but not information on vehicular accidents.
facts.quote: Personal information means information that identifies a person, including a name, address, telephone number, and medical or disability information, but does not include information on vehicular accidents

facts.claim: DPS says public information requests are subject to certain exceptions and reasonable fees.
facts.quote: public information requests are subject to certain exceptions and reasonable fees.

facts.claim: A driver in an accident causing bodily injury, death, or total property damage to an apparent extent of $2,000 or more must file a report within 10 days after the accident.
facts.quote: The driver of a vehicle involved in an accident resulting in bodily injury to or death of a person or total property damage to an apparent extent of $2,000 or more shall, within 10 days after the accident

facts.claim: The driver's written or electronic report goes to the Department of Administration and, if the accident occurs within a municipality, to the local police department.
facts.quote: forward a written or electronic report of the accident to the Department of Administration and to the local police department if the accident occurs within a municipality.

facts.claim: The driver's report is not required if a peace officer investigated the accident.
facts.quote: A report is not required under this subsection if the accident is investigated by a peace officer.

facts.claim: For such an accident, the driver must also immediately notify the local police department if it occurs within a municipality, or otherwise the Department of Public Safety.
facts.quote: shall immediately by the quickest means of communication give notice of the accident to the local police department if the accident occurs within a municipality, otherwise to the Department of Public Safety.

facts.claim: The accident report form can be obtained from the department's website, any local police department, or the Department of Public Safety.
facts.quote: The form of accident report required under (b) of this section can be obtained from the department's Internet website, any local police department, or the Department of Public Safety.

facts.claim: The driver report, Form 12-209, lets a driver self-report a crash and provide documentation to their insurance company.
facts.quote: the driver report (Form 12-209) to provide the user a way to self-report a crash and provide documentation to his or her insurance company.

facts.claim: The self-report form is for crashes where law enforcement did not respond to the scene, or where a responding officer told the driver to self-report.
facts.quote: Use this form if law enforcement did not respond to the scene of the crash, OR you were instructed by a responding officer to self-report the crash.

facts.claim: Crash forms are due within 10 days of the crash date, and the Certificate of Insurance within 15 days.
facts.quote: Crash forms are required within 10 days and Certificate of Insurance within 15 days of the crash date.

facts.claim: AS 28.22.021 requires proof of motor vehicle liability insurance after an accident that causes bodily injury or death, or property damage to a person exceeding $501.
facts.quote: requires the owner or operator of a motor vehicle to provide proof of motor vehicle liability insurance when that person is involved in an accident that results in bodily injury to or death of a person, or damage to the property of a person exceeding $501.

facts.claim: DMV Form 466 (Certificate of Insurance) is for drivers whom an officer told, after an investigation, to provide proof of insurance and who were given a case number.
facts.quote: Use this form if a law enforcement officer instructed you to provide proof of insurance at the scene of the crash after conducting an investigation and you were provided with a case number.

facts.claim: Alaska's DMV regulation requires a driver in a crash with bodily injury, death, or property damage over $2,000 to submit a written crash report within 10 days, unless a peace officer investigated.
facts.quote: A driver who is involved in a motor vehicle crash that results in bodily injury or death or property damage to a person in excess of $2,000 shall submit a written crash report to the department within 10 days from the date of the crash, unless the crash was investigated by a peace officer.

facts.claim: The department must suspend the driving license, permit and nonresident operating privileges of a person who fails to report an accident under AS 28.35.080 until the report is filed.
facts.quote: The department shall suspend the license or permit to drive and the nonresident operating privileges of a person failing to report an accident as provided in AS 28.35.080 until the report is filed.

facts.claim: A report made under this chapter may not be used as evidence in a criminal or civil action arising out of the accident it covers.
facts.quote: A report made in accordance with this chapter may not be used in evidence in a criminal or civil action arising out of the accident that is the subject of the report.

facts.claim: DMV's printable Certificate of Insurance (Form 466) can be filed on paper: it must be completed in full and mailed or faxed to the Division of Motor Vehicles within 15 days from the date of the crash.
facts.quote: THIS FORM MUST BE COMPLETED IN FULL AND MAILED OR FAXED TO THE DIVISION OF MOTOR VEHICLES WITHIN 15 DAYS FROM THE DATE OF THE CRASH.

facts.claim: Questions about DPS public records requests can be emailed to dps.publicinforequest@alaska.gov.
facts.quote: For questions please e-mail dps.publicinforequest@alaska.gov.

facts.claim: A records request must go to the agency that holds the records: Alaska agencies can respond only about records in their own possession or control and are not required to retrieve records from, or refer requests to, other agencies.
facts.quote: Contacting the correct public agency is important: agencies can only respond as to the records in their own possession or control. Agencies are not required to retrieve records from or refer requests to other agencies.

facts.claim: Alaska's Public Records Act applies to all state and local government agencies in Alaska; the federal Freedom of Information Act does not apply.
facts.quote: The APRA applies to all state and local government agencies in the State of Alaska. The federal Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) does not apply.

facts.claim: Written public records requests can be submitted on paper or electronically; the Department of Law cites DPS as an agency whose electronic request forms improve tracking and can help it respond more quickly.
facts.quote: Written requests can be submitted in hard copy or electronically. Some agencies—for example, the Department of Public Safety—have electronic forms that improve tracking and that can help the agency respond more quickly.

facts.claim: The Department of Law says the state executive branch, except the Alaska Railroad Corporation, is subject to the Department of Administration's public records regulations at 2 AAC 96.100–96.470.
facts.quote: The executive branch, except for the Alaska Railroad Corporation, is subject to regulations implemented by the Department of Administration at 2 AAC 96.100 – 2 AAC 96.470.

facts.claim: An agency may take the 10-working-day extension only when one or more circumstances listed in the regulation exist, and only for the specific documents those circumstances affect.
facts.quote: The basic 10-day period may be extended only when one or more of the following circumstances exist, and then only as to those specific documents within the request as to which the circumstances apply:

facts.claim: The time between an agency's notice that a request will generate chargeable fees and the requester's arrangement to pay them is excluded from the 10-working-day response period.
facts.quote: Any time that elapses between the time a requester is sent notice that processing the request will generate chargeable fees and the time the requester makes suitable arrangement for payment of those fees under 2 AAC 96.355 and 2 AAC 96.360 is excluded from the 10-working-day period

facts.claim: An agency must give a written response granting or denying a written public records request within the time limit; if no response arrives by then, the requester may consider the request denied.
facts.quote: A public agency shall give a written response granting or denying a written request for public records within the prescribed time limit. If a response is not received by a requester by the expiration of the time limit, the requester may consider the request denied.

facts.claim: A requester can administratively appeal a public records denial to the agency head within 60 working days from the date the denial was issued.
facts.quote: If you want to administratively appeal a denial, you have 60 working days from the date the denial was issued to submit your appeal to the agency head.

facts.claim: Department of Law guidance says that if searching for and copying records will exceed five person-hours in a calendar month, state agencies charge the hourly rate of the most cost-effective employee who can do the work.
facts.quote: If searching for and copying records under AS 40.25.110 will exceed five person-hours in a calendar month, agencies charge the hourly rate (based on the salary and benefit costs) of the most cost-effective individual who can do the work.

facts.claim: Another Form 440 exception covers use by a government agency, including a court or law enforcement agency, in carrying out its functions, or by a private person or entity acting on a government agency's behalf.
facts.quote: For use by a government agency, including a court or law enforcement agency, in carrying out its functions or by a private person or entity acting on the behalf of a government agency in carrying out its functions.

facts.claim: Under DMV regulations, a driver in a crash causing bodily injury, death, or property damage to a person over $501 must submit a completed certificate of insurance report to the department within 15 days from the date of the crash.
facts.quote: A driver who is involved in a motor vehicle crash that results in bodily injury or death or property damage to a person in excess of $501 shall submit the completed certificate of insurance report required by AS 28.22.021 and 2 AAC 90.510 to the department within 15 days from the date of the crash.

facts.claim: Under DMV regulations, a required crash report must be submitted directly to the division's main office by the person who prepared it, and a mailed report must be postmarked within 10 days from the date of the crash.
facts.quote: a crash report required under AS 28.35.080 must be submitted directly to the division's main office by the person who prepared the report. If mailed, the mailing of the crash report must be postmarked within 10 days from the date of the crash.

facts.claim: DMV's Form 466 states that the mandatory insurance laws require filing proof of insurance with the State of Alaska, and that failing to do so will result in suspension of the driver's license.
facts.quote: The mandatory insurance laws require you to file proof of insurance with the State of Alaska. Failure to do so will result in the suspension of your driver’s license.

facts.claim: For a crash with no personal injury, or with property damage between $501 and $2,000, completing the 12-209 self-report still meets the DMV's proof-of-liability-insurance requirement.
facts.quote: When a motor vehicle crash results in no personal injury or results in property damage between $501 and $2,000, completing the 12-209 provides valuable crash and location information that helps DOT and still meets the requirement for proof of liability insurance to DMV shown above.

facts.claim: Failing to make an accident report required by AS 28.35.080 is a misdemeanor punishable on conviction by a fine of up to $200, up to 90 days in jail, or both.
facts.quote: A person failing to make a report as required in AS 28.35.080 is guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction is punishable by a fine of not more than $200, or by imprisonment for not more than 90 days, or by both.

facts.claim: If the driver is physically incapable of making the required written accident report and is not the vehicle's owner, the owner must make the report within five days after learning of the accident.
facts.quote: Whenever the driver is physically incapable of making a written report of an accident as required in AS 28.35.080 and the driver is not the owner of the vehicle, then the owner of the vehicle involved in the accident shall within five days after learning of the accident make the report

facts.claim: Giving information in a required accident report while knowing or having reason to believe it is false is punishable by a fine of up to $1,000, up to one year in jail, or both.
facts.quote: A person who gives information in reports as required in AS 28.35.080 knowing or having reason to believe that the information is false is punishable by a fine of not more than $1,000, or by imprisonment for not more than one year, or by both.

gaps.reason: No official source I read says Form 440 or a DPS records request can be delivered in person. The DMV form and the DOT&PF page give only mail and email for Form 440, and DPS gives only its online portal.

No official source says how soon a crash report is available for copying after a crash, or how long the DMV takes to fulfil a Form 440 request. The only time frames found are the officer's 24-hour filing duty (AS 28.35.080(e)) and the general 10-working-day response rule for public records requests (2 AAC 96.325), which is not crash-report specific.

The $10 DMV fee comes from Form 440 itself. I did not find a statute or regulation that sets it, and the form mentions no separate card or convenience fee. DPS says only that 'most' police report requests have no cost, with no specific fee for a State Trooper Collision Report.

State sources confirm only that DPS does not hold local police records and that every investigating law enforcement officer must forward a report to the Department of Administration. No state page explicitly says whether a Form 440 request to the DMV will return a report written by a city police department, or how to request one directly from a city police department. City pages such as anchoragepolice.com are municipal, not state, sources, and I did not use them as sources.

No official page explains whether a member of the public should request a trooper-written crash report from DPS (through its records portal) or from the DMV (Form 440), or whether both routes return the same document.

The DPS JustFOIA portal (dpsalaska.justfoia.com) returned 403 Access Restricted, so I could not verify its form fields or any crash-report-specific options. No official online portal for buying or downloading DMV crash reports was found. Form 440 goes by mail or email.
DPS says its requests are 'subject to certain exceptions', but no official page I read lists specific restrictions on who may get a State Trooper Collision Report.

facts.claim: The Alabama Law Enforcement Agency (ALEA) sells copies of crash reports online or in person at any ALEA Driver License Office.
facts.quote: Crash Reports may be purchased online HERE or in person at any ALEA Driver License Office.

facts.claim: Under Ala. Code § 32-10-7(a), the completed written report of an investigated motor vehicle accident must be forwarded to the director within 24 hours after the investigation is completed, on the uniform accident report form the director supplies.
facts.quote: shall, within 24 hours after completing such investigation, forward the necessary completed written report or copy thereof of such accident to the director on the uniform accident report form supplied by the director.

facts.claim: Ala. Code § 32-10-7(a) allows local police departments and their contracted agents to keep copies of the written accident reports.
facts.quote: Local police departments, and their contracted agents, may retain copies of the written reports.

facts.claim: ALEA's online Purchase Crash Report service lets you request a copy of a crash report that you can then view and download.
facts.quote: Request a copy of a crash report which will be available to view and download.

facts.claim: Reports bought through ALEA's online service can be viewed and downloaded for up to 5 days after the request is submitted.
facts.quote: Crash reports will be available to view and download for up to 5 days after your submission.

facts.claim: To buy a copy of the Alabama Uniform Traffic Crash Report by mail, you fill in ALEA's crash report request letter and send it with $15.00 by cashier's check, certified check or money order payable to the Alabama Law Enforcement Agency.
facts.quote: In order to purchase a copy of the Alabama Uniform Traffic Crash Report please complete the section below and return this letter with $15.00 in the form of a cashier's check, certified check, or money order made payable to the Alabama Law Enforcement Agency.

facts.claim: The mail-in request form is returned to Alabama Law Enforcement Agency, Crash Reports, P.O. Box 1471, Montgomery, AL 36102-1472.
facts.quote: Print and Return Completed Form To: Alabama Law Enforcement Agency Crash Reports P.O. Box 1471 Montgomery, AL 36102-1472

facts.claim: The mail-in form says personal checks and cash are not accepted and the request must include a self-addressed, stamped envelope.
facts.quote: NO PERSONAL CHECKS WILL BE ACCEPTED. DO NOT SEND CASH. Return request with self-addressed, stamped envelope.

facts.claim: Crash reports can be bought in person at any ALEA Driver License Office.
facts.quote: Crash Reports may be purchased online HERE or in person at any ALEA Driver License Office.

facts.claim: The mail-in request form asks for the requester's name and address, each driver's full name, date of birth and driver license number, the county and date of the accident, the street or highway number, and the names of any fatalities.
facts.quote: Print your name and address below: ... Driver's Full Name Date of Birth Driver License Number County of Accident: Date of Accident: Street or Highway #: Name of Fatalities (if any occurred):

facts.claim: To use ALEA's online service you need a personal email address, a valid credit card and information about the crash.
facts.quote: You will need to provide Personal email address Valid credit card for payment Crash information

facts.claim: ALEA lists the fee for a copy of a crash report as $15.
facts.quote: Copy of Crash Report - $15

facts.claim: On ALEA's fees page, personal checks are not accepted; money orders, cashier's checks, cash and credit cards are accepted.
facts.quote: NOTE: NO PERSONAL CHECKS ARE ACCEPTED. Money order, cashier’s check, cash, or credit card are accepted.

facts.claim: Ala. Code § 32-2-8 caps the fee the Director of Public Safety charges for a copy of a record or report at $15 per record or report, unless another law sets a different fee.
facts.quote: the director shall set and collect a fee not to exceed the sum of fifteen dollars ($15) for each record or report, unless a different fee is otherwise prescribed by law.

facts.claim: ALEA says it can take up to 15 business days from the date of a crash for the report to be available online.
facts.quote: It can take up to 15 business days from the date of a crash for the crash report to be available online.

facts.claim: Crash reports for crashes that occurred 10 or more years ago cannot be bought through ALEA's online service.
facts.quote: Crashes that occurred 10 or more years ago are not available for purchase.

facts.claim: ALEA says Alabama Code 32-10-7 governs who is eligible to buy crash reports.
facts.quote: Alabama Code 32-10-7 governs who is eligible to purchase crash reports.

facts.claim: A person involved in the accident, including drivers, passengers and pedestrians, may get the accident report.
facts.quote: a. A person involved in the accident made the basis of the accident report, including, but not limited to, drivers of and passengers in the automobiles and pedestrians involved in the accident that is the subject of the report.

facts.claim: A parent or guardian of a minor involved in the accident may get the report.
facts.quote: b. A parent or guardian of a minor who is a person involved in the accident made the basis of the accident report.

facts.claim: A personal representative, executor or other legal representative of the estate of a deceased person involved in the accident may get the report.
facts.quote: c. A personal representative, executor, or other legal representative of the estate of a deceased person who was involved in the accident made the basis of the accident report.

facts.claim: If no personal representative has been appointed by a probate court, any heir of the deceased person may get the report.
facts.quote: Where no personal representative has been appointed by a probate court of competent jurisdiction regarding the probate or administration of the estate of a decedent, any heir of the decedent shall be authorized to receive an accident report.

facts.claim: An insurer of a person involved in the accident, or its written designee, may get the report for insurance business purposes.
facts.quote: d. An insurer or its written designee of a person involved in the accident made the basis of the accident report, if the purpose of the request is for insurance business purposes.

facts.claim: An attorney of a person involved in the accident, or the attorney's employee, may get the report but must provide written signed consent from the represented person.
facts.quote: e. An attorney of a person involved in the accident made the basis of the accident report, or an employee of the attorney. The attorney or employee of the attorney shall provide written signed consent by the represented person to request the report.

facts.claim: An owner or lienholder of a vehicle in the accident may get the report.
facts.quote: g. An owner or lienholder of an automobile in the accident that is the subject of the report.

facts.claim: A governmental entity responsible for the road or bridge where the accident happened, or for law enforcement investigations, may get the report.
facts.quote: f. A governmental entity responsible for either maintenance, repair, and oversight of the public road or bridge on which the accident occurred or for law enforcement investigations.

facts.claim: Accident reports must also be disclosed when a properly executed subpoena or court order directs it.
facts.quote: (2) When disclosure is directed by a properly executed subpoena or court order.

facts.claim: Accident reports are also made available to news-gathering organizations, solely for publishing or broadcasting the news.
facts.quote: Accident reports prepared pursuant to this section shall be made available pursuant to Section 32-2-8, to a news-gathering organization solely for the purpose of publishing or broadcasting the news.

facts.claim: For reports released to news-gathering organizations under this subsection, ALEA limits personal identifying information to the name and age of the person involved for 30 days after the accident.
facts.quote: For 30 days following the accident, the Alabama State Law Enforcement Agency shall limit any personal identifying information contained in any accident report released pursuant to this subsection to the name and age of the person involved.

facts.claim: Ala. Code § 32-10-7(c) allows the department to contract with a third party to give eligible persons and entities electronic access to reports.

gaps.reason: I could not confirm the total online price or any card or processing fee from an official page. The ALEA portal page I could read showed only a $0.00 placeholder before the captcha. An Alabama Interactive help page (alabamainteractive.atlassian.net) says $17.00, which is $15.00 plus a $2.00 processing fee, but no official government page I read links to or names it, so it is not a source.

Ala. Code § 32-10-7 requires investigated accident reports to be forwarded to the director and lets local police keep copies. No official page I read says whether ALEA's online portal or mail service returns reports written by city police or county sheriffs, or tells requesters to go to the local agency. Local procedures (for example LexisNexis or city records offices) vary, and I did not verify them from official pages.
ALEA says reports can be bought at any ALEA Driver License Office, but no official page I read lists the ID or information needed in person, or whether the copy is given out the same day.

The only official timing is the portal's "up to 15 business days" for online availability. No official source gives a processing time for mail requests. The vendor help page's other figures (10 years of online reports, reports from January 1, 2006 onward) are not from an official page.

Official sources conflict. Ala. Code § 32-7-5 requires a written report to the director within 30 days for any death, injury or property damage over $250, on a form the director prescribes. ALEA's current manual and SR-31 form describe a $500 threshold and require filing only when the at-fault party was uninsured. No alea.gov page I found names a current general driver report form; the older SR-13 appears only on non-state sites. Also, the manual says "$500 or more" while the SR-31 form says "in excess of $500".

I did not read the definitions section, so I have not confirmed that "director" in § 32-10-7(a) means the Director of Public Safety within ALEA. Section 32-10-7(b) does name the Alabama State Law Enforcement Agency as the agency releasing reports.

The mail-in crash report form gives the ZIP as 36102-1472, while ALEA's SR-31 materials use P.O. Box 1471, Montgomery, AL 36102-1471. I could not confirm which ZIP+4 is correct for crash report requests. The form is also undated, and the forms page I read does not list it, so it may be out of date.
I found no official page confirming that reports can be ordered by phone or email. A third-party summary mentioned an older ALEA news release about this, but I did not find or read it.

The online purchase system (crashreports.ark.org) lists a flat $25.00 per report, while the DPS page and Act 672 set $10 for people involved in the crash. No official page says whether involved parties can get the $10 rate online or must use the mail-in form.

The DPS page says reports are typically available at troop headquarters, but no official page read gives walk-in counter hours, in-person payment methods or an in-person procedure at Little Rock headquarters or troop offices.

No official source was read that gives fees or procedures for requesting a report directly from a city police department or county sheriff. Act 672 amended only subsection (b) of § 27-53-210, and the official current text of the local-agency subsection was not read.

Beyond the juvenile-occupant rule and the ID requirement for involved parties, no official source read describes other restrictions or a confidentiality period. The official current text of Ark. Code § 27-53-305 (reports as public records) was not read.
No official page read confirms submitting the SR-1 by email or in person, or names the Ragland Building street address. Only the P.O. Box address on the form was confirmed.

facts.claim: Requests for reports from county or local agencies must go to the agency that investigated the crash in that jurisdiction.
facts.quote: Requests for these records need to be directed to the investigative agency in that jurisdiction.

facts.claim: To request a DPS report online, create an account on the DPS Public Services Portal and select "Request a Report or Records."

facts.claim: DPS sends people who want a copy of a previously completed police report to its Public Services Portal at https://psp.azdps.gov/.

facts.claim: In-person requests go to the Arizona DPS Public Services Center at 2222 W. Encanto Blvd, Phoenix, AZ 85009.

gaps.reason: No official source found that says how many days after a crash a report becomes available. DPS gives only processing information: requests are handled in the order received, and its automated process usually fills eligible unredacted-report requests within 48 hours after portal submission. A.R.S. 28-667 sets a 24-hour completion deadline for the officer's report, not a release date. The figure of about 14 days found in search results came only from law-firm and other non-official sites.

The DPS page lists no convenience or card-processing fee for portal or card payments, and the portal (psp.azdps.gov) returned a 403/maintenance page, so any checkout fee could not be confirmed. No statute or rule was found that sets the $9.00 report fee; it comes from the DPS fee schedule. Fees charged by city and county agencies were not researched and vary by agency.
psp.azdps.gov could not be loaded (HTTP 403 / maintenance page), so the portal's request fields and steps could not be read directly.
No specific DPS form name or number for mailed collision-report requests was found. The DPS page only says to submit 'In Writing' to the Public Records mailing address.

For requests outside the automated process (mail, in person, or online requests not eligible for automation), DPS does not list required details such as date, location, names or ID. Only the automated-process rules are stated: an incident number of 'I' plus 8 digits with no hyphens, and the requester must meet the statutory eligibility categories.

A.R.S. 28-667(C)(5) requires agencies to forward a copy of every report to ADOT, but no official ADOT page was found that offers copies of crash reports to the public. ADOT's crash-report pages cover forms and officer training only. There appears to be no single statewide public request system for reports by all agencies.

No official state page names a vendor portal (such as BuyCrash) for Arizona crash reports. City police and county sheriff reports must be requested from each investigating agency, whose methods, fees and timelines were not researched one by one.

No official source was found that requires drivers to file their own written crash report with ADOT/MVD or any other state agency, or that sets a form, deadline or damage threshold for one. Official sources show only the duty under A.R.S. 28-666 to give immediate notice to police for injury or death crashes, and the optional DPS Citizen's Report of a Collision tool for minor State Highway crashes. A non-official site's claim that an 'SR-1' must be filed with MVD could not be confirmed.

facts.quote: Your personal check or money order must be sent with your request and made out to the California Highway Patrol.

facts.claim: The CHP does not accept cash for mailed requests and says it does not accept credit or debit cards at this time.
facts.quote: NO CASH PLEASE if you are requesting the report by mail. We do not accept Credit or Debit cards at this time.

facts.claim: The CHP FAQ says the collision report fee is paid by cash or check and tells you to contact your local Area office about it.
facts.quote: There is a fee for the collision report (cash or check); contact your local area office.

facts.claim: The CHP says it charges a nominal fee to cover reproduction costs and tells you to contact the CHP office where the report was filed to find the cost of your report.
facts.quote: The CHP charges only a nominal fee to cover reproduction costs (To determine the cost of your report, please contact the CHP office where the report was filed).

facts.claim: The CHP tells CHP 190 filers to contact the Area office they are submitting the form to for the exact fee.
facts.quote: Submit applicable fees (contact the Area office you will be submitting the form to for the exact amount).

facts.claim: CHP General Order 110.2 (revised December 2014) sets a charge of $10.00 per 25 pages for report copies in any format.
facts.quote: Report copies provided in any format, require a charge of $10.00 per 25 pages.

facts.claim: CHP General Order 110.2 says a person with proper interest may review a report in its entirety without charge.
facts.quote: A person who has proper interest may review a report in its entirety without charge.

facts.claim: Under Vehicle Code 20012, a request for a copy of an accident report must be accompanied by a fee that may not exceed the actual cost of providing the copy.
facts.quote: A request for a copy of an accident report shall be accompanied by payment of a fee, provided such fee shall not exceed the actual cost of providing the copy.

facts.claim: The CHP advises calling the CHP office handling the incident ahead of time to see whether your report is available for pick up.
facts.quote: Call the CHP office overseeing the incident ahead of time to see if your traffic collision report is available for pick up.

facts.claim: The CHP lists proper Parties of Interest as drivers, bicyclists, pedestrians, passengers, parents of minors, legal guardians, vehicle or property owners, legal representatives, manufacturer representatives, and insurance companies with a valid claim or policy number.
facts.quote: A proper Party of Interest (i.e., Drivers, Bicyclists, Pedestrians, Passengers, Parents of Minors, Legal Guardians, Vehicle or Property Owners, Legal representatives, Manufacturer Representatives, or Insurance Companies with a valid claim or policy number)

facts.claim: The CHP says any involved or interested party can get a copy of a collision report.
facts.quote: Any involved or interested party can get a copy of a collision report.

facts.claim: The CHP FAQ says that to receive a copy you must be an involved party, passenger, property owner, or licensed insurance agent with a signed release from an involved party.
facts.quote: To receive a copy of a report you must be an involved party, passenger, property owner, or licensed insurance agent (with a signed release from your insured, an involved party).

facts.claim: If you are not sure you are entitled to a copy, the CHP asks you to contact any CHP Area office to verify whether you are a proper Party of Interest.
facts.quote: If you are not sure you are entitled to a copy of the report/investigation, please contact any CHP Area office to verify whether you are a proper Party of Interest.

facts.claim: Under Vehicle Code 20012, reports are disclosed to any person with a proper interest, including the drivers involved, their guardians or conservators, the parent of a minor driver, a driver's authorized representative, and any named injured person.
facts.quote: to any person who may have a proper interest therein, including, but not limited to, the driver or drivers involved, or the guardian or conservator thereof, the parent of a minor driver, the authorized representative of a driver, or to any named person injured therein

facts.claim: Vehicle Code 20012 also covers owners of damaged vehicles or property, persons who may incur civil liability, and attorneys who declare under penalty of perjury that they represent any of those persons.
facts.quote: the owners of vehicles or property damaged thereby, persons who may incur civil liability, including liability based upon a breach of warranty arising out of the accident, and any attorney who declares under penalty of perjury that he or she represents any of the above persons

facts.claim: Under CHP General Order 110.2, parents of adult children are not persons of proper interest unless they have a signed authorization from the involved adult child.
facts.quote: Parents of adult children are not considered a person of proper interest, unless they have a signed authorization from the involved adult child.

facts.claim: For fatal collisions, CHP General Order 110.2 places proper interest with the surviving spouse, minor children through their guardians, or a court-appointed family member under Probate Code 6401.
facts.quote: In cases involving fatal collisions; proper interest lies with the surviving spouse, minor children when released through their guardians, or court appointed family member per California Probate Code 6401.

facts.claim: CHP General Order 110.2 authorizes insurance company representatives who supply the policy or claim number in effect at the time of the collision and hold the name of the insured.
facts.quote: Representatives of insurance companies that supply the policy or claim number that was in effect at the time of the collision and hold the name of the insured.

facts.claim: Under CHP General Order 110.2, a declaration under penalty of perjury that someone represents a person with proper interest permits release of the report to the attorney or their identified agent.
facts.quote: Such declarations permit release of the report to the attorney or their identified agent.

facts.claim: Vehicle or component manufacturer representatives must present a letter from the manufacturer, dated within the last 12 months, certifying their authority.
facts.quote: Such representatives must present a letter from the manufacturer, dated within the last 12 months, certifying their authority.

facts.claim: Under CHP General Order 110.2, until a collision report is complete the CHP can give the public only the time, date and location of the collision, the make of the vehicles, and occupant names (except in fatal collisions).
facts.quote: Until a collision report is complete, the following information can be provided to the public: (1) Time of collision. (2) Date of collision. (3) Location of collision. (4) Make of vehicle(s) involved. (5) Names of vehicle occupants (other than fatal collisions).

facts.claim: If you do not know which police department investigated the collision, the CHP says to contact your local police department or a CHP office for help identifying the right law enforcement agency.
facts.quote: If you do not know the police department who investigated the collision, you can either contact your local police department or CHP Office to assist you in identifying the proper law enforcement agency.

facts.claim: Vehicle Code 20012 makes the law enforcement agency to which an accident was reported, as well as the CHP, responsible for disclosing the entire contents of its accident reports.
facts.quote: the Department of the California Highway Patrol or the law enforcement agency to whom the accident was reported shall disclose the entire contents of the reports

facts.claim: The CHP's Crash Investigation Manual says allied agencies should establish crash report retention schedules suited to their needs.
facts.quote: Allied agencies should establish a retention schedule suited to their needs.

facts.claim: You or your insurance agent, broker or legal representative must send an SR-1 report to the DMV within 10 days if anyone is injured (however minor) or killed, or property damage is over $1000.
facts.quote: You or your insurance agent, broker, or legal representative must complete an SR-1 report and send it to DMV within 10 days if someone is injured (no matter how minor the injury) or killed, or property damage is over $1000.

facts.claim: The DMV says an SR-1 is required in addition to any report made to the police, the CHP or your insurance company.
facts.quote: An SR-1 report is required in addition to any other report made to the police, CHP, or your insurance company.

facts.claim: The DMV says paper SR-1 submissions are likely to take longer to process.
facts.quote: Please note that paper submissions are likely to take longer to process.

facts.claim: Vehicle Code 16000 requires an accident that caused more than $1,000 in damage to any one person's property, or bodily injury, or death, to be reported within 10 days after the accident.
facts.quote: that has resulted in damage to the property of any one person in excess of one thousand dollars ($1,000), or in bodily injury, or in the death of any person shall report the accident, within 10 days after the accident

facts.claim: Under Vehicle Code 16000, no SR-1 report is required if the vehicle was owned or leased by, or under the direction of, the United States, California, another state, or a local agency.
facts.quote: A report is not required under subdivision (a) if the motor vehicle involved in the accident was owned or leased by, or under the direction of, the United States, this state, another state, or a local agency.

facts.claim: The SR-1 form (Rev. 6/2025) says California law requires accidents on a California street/highway or private property to be reported to the DMV within 10 days if there was an injury, death or property damage over $1,000.
facts.quote: California law requires traffic accidents on a California street/highway or private property to be reported to the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) within 10 days if there was an injury, death or property damage in excess of $1,000.

facts.claim: The SR-1 form says the driver must file it with the DMV regardless of fault.
facts.quote: The law requires the driver to file this SR 1 form with DMV regardless of fault.

facts.claim: The SR-1 form says reports filed with a law enforcement agency, insurance company or the CHP do not satisfy the SR-1 filing requirement.
facts.quote: This report must be made in addition to any other report filed with a law enforcement agency, insurance company, or the California Highway Patrol (CHP) as their reports do not satisfy the filing requirement.

facts.claim: The SR-1 form warns that late reporting could lead the DMV to suspend a driver license.
facts.quote: Untimely reporting could result in DMV suspending a driver license.

facts.claim: An insurance agent, attorney or other designated representative may file the SR-1 for the driver.
facts.quote: An insurance agent, attorney, or other designated representative may file the report for the driver.

facts.claim: A paper SR-1 is mailed to the DMV Insurance Unit, Mail Station J237, P.O. Box 942884, Sacramento, CA 94284-0884.
facts.quote: Department of Motor Vehicles Insurance Unit Mail Station J237 P.O. Box 942884 Sacramento, CA 94284-0884

facts.claim: Under Vehicle Code 20008, if the accident occurred within a city, that written report may go to either the CHP or the city's police department.
facts.quote: if the accident occurred within a city, to either the Department of the California Highway Patrol or the police department of the city in which the accident occurred

facts.claim: The CHP says it cannot accept traffic collision reports online at this time.
facts.quote: At this time, we are unable to accept reports online.

facts.claim: You can file a traffic collision report at any CHP office in California, wherever the collision occurred.
facts.quote: You may visit any CHP office anywhere in California to file a traffic collision report, regardless of where the collision occurred.

facts.claim: CHP General Order 110.2 says the authority for releasing collision reports is California Vehicle Code Section 20012.
facts.quote: The authority for release of collision reports is contained in California Vehicle Code (VC) Section 20012.

facts.claim: CHP officers normally give parties of interest at a crash scene a CHP 418, Crash Report Information, form that tells them the Traffic Crash Report will be available.
facts.quote: The CHP 418 shall normally be used by the CHP to notify parties of interest at a crash scene of the availability of the Traffic Crash Report.

facts.claim: The CHP's Crash Investigation Manual says all crash reports shall be retained for a minimum of four years from the date of the crash.
facts.quote: All crash reports shall be retained for a minimum of four years from the date of the crash.

facts.claim: The California Crash Reporting System (CCRS) dataset on data.ca.gov is described as statistic crash records within the State of California.
facts.quote: Statistic crash records within State of California

facts.claim: For a mailed request, the CHP FAQ says to include a copy of your CHP 418 (Crash Report Information) card and a copy of your valid driver license.
facts.quote: Remember to include a copy of your CHP 418 (Crash Report Information) card and a copy of your valid driver license.

facts.claim: The CHP says the CHP 190 form is available in both English and Spanish.
facts.quote: The form contains areas to fill out information and is available in both English and Spanish.

facts.claim: To request by mail, mail the CHP 190 and a photocopy of your driver license to the CHP office (jurisdiction) that filed the report.
facts.quote: If you prefer to handle this through the mail, you can complete the form CHP 190 (Application for Release of Information), which can be downloaded from this website. Mail the form and a photocopy of your driver license to the CHP jurisdiction that filed the report

facts.claim: People who live outside California can get a CHP collision report by mail.
facts.quote: How can I get a copy of a CHP collision report if I live out-of-state? You can obtain a copy of a collision report by mail.

facts.claim: The statewide CHP FAQ also points people to the CHP Crash Report Search website to get their crash report.
facts.quote: You can also visit the following website to obtain your crash report: CHP | Crash Report Search

facts.claim: Under CHP General Order 110.2, a CHP Area can fax a copy of the report to another CHP Area or to any other location the person with proper interest asks for.
facts.quote: Sending a fax copy of the report from one CHP Area to another CHP Area, or any other location requested by person who has proper interest.

facts.claim: The CHP lists insurance companies, attorneys, the coroner, Caltrans and parents of minors as examples of interested parties who can get a collision report.
facts.quote: Interested parties include but are not limited to: Insurance companies Attorneys Coroner Caltrans Parents of minors

facts.claim: Under CHP General Order 110.2, when one collision is a primary or associated cause of later collisions, all drivers and passengers in all of those reports have proper interest.
facts.quote: When a collision is either a primary or associated collision factor of a subsequent collision or collisions, all drivers and passengers in all reports are considered to be persons who have proper interest.

facts.claim: CHP General Order 110.2 also authorizes any person, company or corporation named in a legal action, or who may incur civil liability from a collision, to buy a copy of the report.
facts.quote: Any person, company, or corporation named in a legal action or who may incur civil liability resulting from a collision.

facts.claim: Under CHP General Order 110.2, a written statement saying you represent a person with proper interest counts as a declaration under penalty of perjury.
facts.quote: A written statement from an individual stating they represent a person who has proper interest is deemed to be a declaration under penalty of perjury.

facts.claim: A person requesting a report as someone's representative must complete a CHP 190 before buying the report.
facts.quote: The individual shall complete a CHP 190, Application for Release of Information, (Annex A) prior to purchasing the report.

facts.claim: Manufacturer representatives are parties of interest only for collisions involving the manufacturer's make of vehicle, or vehicles with its component installed.
facts.quote: Such representatives are parties of interest for only those collisions which involved the manufacturer's make of vehicle or vehicle(s) in which a component has been installed.

facts.claim: On request, the CHP Area commander schedules a discussion of the collision investigation between a person with proper interest (or their agent) and the officer who wrote the report.
facts.quote: Upon request, the CHP Area commander shall schedule discussions of collision investigations between a person who has proper interest, or agents thereof, and officer who wrote the report.

facts.claim: A person with proper interest may not record a case discussion with the CHP officer.
facts.quote: A person who has proper interest shall not be allowed to record these discussions.

facts.claim: An involved party who disagrees with part of a CHP collision report can write a supplemental statement that includes the report number, their name and the items they dispute.
facts.quote: If you are the involved party in a traffic collision, and disagree with any portion of the report, you may write a "supplemental" statement. In your written statement, please include: The report number Your name The specific item or items with which you disagree

facts.claim: The supplemental statement can be taken to any CHP office or sent by US Mail, and the CHP replies by US Mail.
facts.quote: You may bring this statement into any CHP office, or send it via US Mail. You will receive a response by US Mail.

facts.claim: Caltrans keeps copies of all state highway-related crash reports for ten years from the month of the crash, and requests go to the Caltrans Legal Division (for duplicates missing from local files or purged).
facts.quote: The California Department of Transportation retains copies of all state highway-related reports for ten years from the month of the crash. Requests should be directed to the Caltrans Legal Division.

facts.claim: CHP Headquarters keeps copies of fatal crash reports for the current year plus three.
facts.quote: California Highway Patrol Headquarters retains copies of fatal crashes for the current year plus three.

facts.claim: The CHP keeps reports of crashes involving felony charges for serious bodily injury or death for seven years from the crash date.
facts.quote: Reports for crashes involving felony charges for serious bodily injury or death shall be retained for seven years from the date of the crash.

facts.claim: The CHP keeps unsolved fatal hit-and-run crash investigations indefinitely.
facts.quote: All unsolved fatal hit-and-run crash investigations shall be retained indefinitely.

facts.claim: Under Vehicle Code 20008, if the agency that receives a driver's injury or fatal accident report is not responsible for investigating it, that agency must immediately forward the report to the responsible law enforcement agency.
facts.quote: If the agency which receives the report is not responsible for investigating the accident, it shall immediately forward the report to the law enforcement agency which is responsible for investigating the accident.

facts.claim: Under Vehicle Code 20008(b), the owner or driver of a common carrier vehicle in an injury or fatal accident reports to the CHP by the 10th day of the month after the accident.
facts.quote: The owner or driver of a common carrier vehicle involved in any such accident shall make a like report to the Department of California Highway Patrol on or before the 10th day of the month following the accident.

facts.claim: The DMV does not accept an SR-1, or act against non-reporting or uninsured motorists, unless someone involved (or their designee) sends the SR-1 and the DMV receives it within one calendar year of the accident.
facts.quote: DMV does not accept reports or take actions against non-reporting or uninsured motorists unless this SR 1 form is sent to DMV by someone involved in the accident or their designee and the report is received by DMV within one calendar year of the accident date.

facts.claim: The SR-1 form says accidents on a military base, or on the driver's own property involving only the driver's personal property with no injury or death, are not reportable.
facts.quote: occurring on a military base or occurring on the driver's own property involving only the personal property of the driver and there was no injury or death are not reportable.

facts.claim: The DMV lets drivers file an SR-1 online with its 'Start an SR-1' button.
facts.quote: Report a traffic accident by filing an SR-1. Start an SR-1

facts.claim: Before filing an SR-1, the DMV says to gather your DL/ID card, your license plate number or VIN, your insurance information, and the other party's vehicle and insurance information if applicable.
facts.quote: Your driver’s license or identification (DL/ID) card Your vehicle’s license plate number or vehicle identification number (VIN) Your vehicle’s insurance information Other party’s vehicle and insurance information, if applicable

facts.claim: The DMV offers a Spanish version of the SR-1 form as a PDF.
facts.quote: A printable copy of the form (PDF) is available if needed. Please note that paper submissions are likely to take longer to process. Spanish version (PDF).

gaps.reason: I could not confirm the CHP Crash Portal's price or any card or convenience fee. crashes.chp.ca.gov refused connections from both WebFetch and the fallback fetcher, and no chp.ca.gov page I read gives a portal fee. Non-official sources disagree: some say $22 and some say free. Neither figure should be published until someone confirms it on the portal.

The CHP's FAQ pages post a page-based fee schedule ($10.00 per 01-25 pages and so on). But the Request a Crash Report page and the CHP 190 page both tell requesters to contact the Area office for the exact amount. The guide should present the schedule as CHP's posted rates and advise confirming with the office. For in-person payment, the only stated methods are 'cash or check' (FAQ). For mail, cards are explicitly not accepted.

No official page I could open says how soon after a crash a CHP report is usually available. A search-engine snippet credited to the Crash Portal's registration page says reports are 'typically available within eight (8) business days', and news articles repeat this. I could not open the portal to confirm it. The CHP FAQ only says to call the office ahead of time.

I could not confirm what the Crash Portal requires because the portal would not load. Unconfirmed points include account registration, crash card or QR code details, accepted payment methods and whether downloads are immediate. Official CHP pages only link to its login page.
No official CHP page I read names a third-party vendor portal, such as LexisNexis BuyCrash or CARFAX Crashdocs, for CHP reports.

I did not research how individual city police departments and county sheriffs handle requests, what they charge, or which vendor portals they use. I found no statewide official directory of them. Only the general Vehicle Code 20012 rules apply statewide: disclosure to people with a proper interest, and a fee no higher than the actual cost.

The CHP's SWITRS page returned HTTP 403, so I could not read how the statewide crash database (SWITRS/CCRS) relates to copies of individual reports. The data.ca.gov CCRS page only describes 'statistic crash records'.
No official source I read sets a time-based confidentiality or waiting period before release. Access is limited by the proper-interest rule in Vehicle Code 20012 and by CHP General Order 110.2.

The 'CHP 190' link in the body of the Request a Crash Report page (https://www.chp.ca.gov/EnforcementAndPlanningDivisionSite/Documents/CHP190.pdf) returned HTTP 403. The working form link is https://www.chp.ca.gov/siteassets/files/chp190.pdf, labeled 'CHP 190 - Crash Request Form (PDF)' on the same page.

I did not open the online SR-1 form itself (https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/dmv-virtual-office/accident-reporting/accident-reporting-form/), only the DMV page that links to it. Its exact steps are unverified.
