facts.claim: The Colorado State Patrol Central Records Unit keeps Colorado State Patrol criminal justice records and releases information to the public, other law enforcement agencies and insurance companies.
facts.quote: The Colorado State Patrol Central Records Unit (CRU) is responsible for the retention of Colorado State Patrol (CSP) Criminal Justice Records, as well as the release of information to the public, other law enforcement agencies, and insurance companies.

facts.claim: A basic crash report from the Colorado State Patrol can be requested through its Central Records Unit.
facts.quote: A basic crash report can be requested through our Central Records Unit with the Colorado State Patrol.

facts.claim: Crash reports that drivers file online go directly to the Department of Revenue, and the Colorado State Patrol cannot get copies of them; the State Patrol directs people to the Department of Revenue at 303-205-5600.
facts.quote: The reports submitted online are filed directly with the Department of Revenue. The Colorado State Patrol does not have access to obtain copies, please contact the Department of Revenue at 303-205-5600.

facts.claim: The Colorado Division of Motor Vehicles (Department of Revenue) receives crash reports from law enforcement agencies and enters the data into the driver license system.
facts.quote: Please allow 90 days for receipt of the crash report by the law enforcement agency and for data to be entered into the driver license system.

facts.claim: The Colorado Department of Revenue's Division of Motor Vehicles keeps crash information for seven years.
facts.quote: The department maintains crash information for seven years.

facts.claim: Colorado law, as amended by HB26-1127, requires law enforcement officers who are notified of or investigate traffic crashes in their jurisdictions to send reports of those crashes to the department within five days after receiving the information or completing the investigation.
facts.quote: to submit reports of all such accidents CRASHES to the department on the form provided, including insurance information received from any driver, within five days of AFTER the time they receive such THE information or complete their investigation

facts.claim: The Division of Motor Vehicles crash report request form (DR 2489) asks for the police department report number or case number, and the driver's information section must be completed.
facts.quote: Crash Information (Driver’s information section must be completed) Police Department Report Number or Case Number

facts.claim: All records requests to the Colorado State Patrol must be submitted on its Records Request Portal.
facts.quote: All requests for records must be submitted on the appropriate Colorado State Patrol Records Request Portal.

facts.claim: Records requested through the Colorado State Patrol portal are delivered to the requester's portal account, and the requester is notified by email.
facts.quote: The agency's criminal justice records, if available, will be delivered to your portal account, and you will be notified via email.

facts.claim: The Colorado State Patrol Central Records Unit accepts records requests only in writing or electronically through the electronic request system, email or fax.
facts.quote: The Colorado State Patrol, Central Records Unit will only accept records requests made in writing or electronically via the electronic request system, e-mail, or fax.

facts.claim: The Colorado State Patrol Central Records Unit lists phone 303-239-4180, fax (303) 239-4347 and email cdps_csprecords@state.co.us.
facts.quote: 303-239-4180 (303) 239-4347 (Fax) cdps_csprecords@state.co.us

facts.claim: The Colorado State Patrol Central Records Unit is at 700 Kipling Street, Lakewood, Colorado 80215.
facts.quote: Central Records Unit 700 Kipling Street Lakewood, Colorado 80215

facts.claim: The Colorado State Patrol mails the requester's copy of the report after the request and payment are received, and asks that only one request form be submitted to avoid duplicate charges.
facts.quote: Your copy of the report will be mailed to you as soon as possible after your request and payment has been received. To avoid duplicate charges please submit only ONE (1) request form.

facts.claim: A request for a crash report from the Division of Motor Vehicles can be mailed to the Colorado Department of Revenue, Division of Motor Vehicles, P.O. Box 173350, Denver, CO 80217-3350.
facts.quote: of the completed form to the Colorado Department of Revenue, Division of Motor Vehicles, P.O. Box 173350 Denver, CO 80217-3350.

facts.claim: In-person crash record requests to the Division of Motor Vehicles are made by appointment at the Westgate Office.
facts.quote: at the Westgate Office, 3265 S. Wadsworth Blvd. #3A, Lakewood, CO 80027.

facts.claim: To get a copy of a Colorado State Patrol crash report, you need the driver's name, the crash date, the case report number and the crash location.
facts.quote: If you would like to obtain a copy of your crash report, the following information is needed: Name of the Driver Date of the Crash Case Report Number Location of the Accident

facts.claim: The Colorado State Patrol Incident Report form shows the case report number in its upper right-hand corner.
facts.quote: This form will also contain the case report number in the upper right-hand corner.

facts.claim: To get a copy of your own crash report from the Division of Motor Vehicles, you complete form DR 2559, Permission to Release Driver Records to Self or Another Person.
facts.quote: To obtain a copy of your own crash report, you will need to: Complete and submit form DR 2559 Permission to Release Driver Records to Self or Another Person

facts.claim: Requesting someone else's crash report from the Division of Motor Vehicles with their permission requires form DR 2559 signed by that person.
facts.quote: Requires the signature of the person in interest authorizing you to inspect the record.

facts.claim: The other route to someone else's crash report from the Division of Motor Vehicles is form DR2489, Requestor Release and Affidavit of Intended Use.
facts.quote: Complete and submit form DR2489 Requestor Release and Affidavit of Intended Use

facts.claim: Form DR 2489 also asks for the crash city or county.
facts.quote: Crash Location City/County

facts.claim: Every field in the requester information section of form DR 2489 must be filled in for the request to be completed.
facts.quote: In order for this request to be completed, all fields in this section must be filled out.

facts.claim: To request a confidential crash (counter) report, form DR 2559 asks for the confirmation number and the crash date.
facts.quote: If you are requesting a copy of a confidential crash (counter) report (Pursuant to § 42-4-1610, C.R.S.), fill out the following. Confirmation Number Date of Crash (MM/DD/YY)

facts.claim: Form DR 2489 lists a Division of Motor Vehicles non-certified search fee of $9.25.
facts.quote: Non-Certified Search Fee - $9.25

facts.claim: Form DR 2489 lists a Division of Motor Vehicles certified search fee of $10.25.
facts.quote: Certified Search Fee - $10.25

facts.claim: Form DR 2559 lists the same fees: a $9.25 non-certified search fee and a $10.25 certified search fee.
facts.quote: Non-Certified Search Fee - $9.25 DMV.Colorado.gov Certified Search Fee - $10.25

facts.claim: The Colorado State Patrol crash page does not state a fee; it tells requesters to contact the Central Records Unit for costs, and to pay by check or money order payable to the Colorado State Patrol or by credit card.
facts.quote: Contact the Colorado State Patrol Central Records Unit for associated costs. Payment may be made by check or money order made payable to the Colorado State Patrol or via credit card.

facts.claim: The Colorado State Patrol treats every records request as a request for criminal justice records under the Colorado Criminal Justice Records Act (CCJRA).
facts.quote: All records requests submitted to the Colorado State Patrol will be considered requests for agency criminal justice records under the CCJRA.

facts.claim: The Colorado State Patrol fee schedule charges $5.00 for an initial criminal justice record of up to 10 pages; it does not name crash reports.
facts.quote: Initial Criminal Justice Record to include up to 10 pages……………………………… ............................... $ 5.00

facts.claim: The Colorado State Patrol fee schedule charges $30.00 an hour for staff time spent locating and producing records.
facts.quote: The CSP shall charge $30.00 an hour for all staff time associated with locating and producing records

facts.claim: Credit card payments to the Colorado State Patrol go through the Colorado Statewide Internet Portal Authority and are subject to e-commerce portal pricing; the page does not give the amount.
facts.quote: Credit Card services are made possible under the authority of Colorado Statewide Internet Portal Authority as designated in statute CRS 24.37.7-101, and are subject to an e-commerce portal pricing.

facts.claim: Colorado State Patrol crash reports are not available immediately after a crash, and processing may take up to 10 working days.
facts.quote: Please note that reports are not available immediately following a crash; processing times vary and may take up to 10 working days.

facts.claim: For criminal justice records requests, the Colorado State Patrol says it will try to respond typically within three working days after receiving the request.
facts.quote: the agency will make every effort to respond within a timely manner typically three working days after receipt of the request.

facts.claim: The Division of Motor Vehicles asks requesters to allow 90 days for it to receive the crash report from the law enforcement agency and enter the data.
facts.quote: Please allow 90 days for receipt of the crash report by the law enforcement agency and for data to be entered into the driver license system.

facts.claim: Mailed Division of Motor Vehicles record requests take 7-10 working days to process after the Department receives them.
facts.quote: (For mailed requests, please allow 7-10 working days to process after received by Department)

facts.claim: The Colorado State Patrol will not release records unless the requester signs a statement that the records will not be used for direct solicitation of business for pecuniary gain.
facts.quote: The Department will not release records under the CCJRA unless the requester signs a statement affirming that the records will not be used for the direct solicitation of business for pecuniary gain.

facts.claim: Apart from records of official actions, release of Colorado State Patrol criminal justice records is at the official custodian's discretion.
facts.quote: Except for records of official actions, which must be available for inspection, all other criminal justice records may be open for inspection, subject to the discretion of the official custodian.

facts.claim: Division of Motor Vehicles crash report requests are subject to the federal Driver's Privacy Protection Act.
facts.quote: Your request is subject to the Driver's Privacy Protection Act (DPPA), a federal law that restricts public access to personal information held in motor vehicle records

facts.claim: The Division of Motor Vehicles denies driver record inspection to anyone other than the person in interest or a government agency carrying out official functions unless they sign and return the Affidavit of Intended Use.
facts.quote: The Department or the Department’s authorized agent shall deny inspection of any driver record to any person, other than a person in interest, or a federal, state, or local government agency carrying out its official functions, who has not signed and returned the Affidavit of Intended Use.

facts.claim: A driver-filed online report is called a counter report and is released only with the written consent of the driver who filed it, using form DR 2559.
facts.quote: A counter report can only be requested through written consent of the driver submitting the counter report using form DR 2559

facts.claim: If a police officer was not called to the crash scene, the Division of Motor Vehicles says you may file a crash report online.
facts.quote: If a police officer was not called to the scene of the crash you may file a crash report online.

facts.claim: Online crash reports filed by individuals are not investigated by a law enforcement agency and are called counter reports.
facts.quote: If a crash report is filed online by an individual, the report does not get investigated by a law enforcement agency and is referred to as a "counter report."

facts.claim: If a police officer came to the scene and collected the needed information, you do not need to file any forms unless the Department of Revenue sends you a letter.
facts.quote: If you were involved in a crash and a police officer was called to the scene to obtain all the needed information, you do not need to provide any forms unless you receive a letter from the Department of Revenue

facts.claim: The Colorado State Patrol says crashes must by law be reported immediately to the agency with jurisdiction, citing CRS 42-4-1601.
facts.quote: Crashes are required by law, under CRS 42-4-1601 to be reported to the agency having jurisdiction immediately.

facts.claim: When a crash does not qualify for a police response during an accident alert, the Colorado State Patrol tells drivers to file their accident report online as soon as possible.
facts.quote: File your accident report online as soon as possible.

facts.claim: The Colorado State Patrol says a report can be filed online or at a troop office where the accident occurred.
facts.quote: A report can be filed either on-line or at a troop office where the accident occurred.

facts.claim: If you did not give the trooper proof of current insurance, you must fill out a financial responsibility form within ten days of the accident.
facts.quote: If you did not supply the Trooper with current insurance, you will need to fill out a financial responsibility form within ten (10) days of the accident.

facts.claim: The Colorado State Patrol basic crash report is a synopsis and does not include witness statements, digital media or other parts of the investigation.
facts.quote: This report contains information that represents a synopsis of the crash and does not include any witness statements, digital media or any other aspect of the crash investigation.

facts.claim: Under the DPPA, you cannot access someone else's personal information from their driving record unless you have their written consent or your request falls under one of the law's specific permissible uses.
facts.quote: This law means you cannot access someone else's personal information from their driving record unless you have their written consent or your request falls under one of the specific "permissible uses" defined by the law.

facts.claim: The DMV's online counter report service only accepts crashes that happened less than 60 days ago and were not investigated by law enforcement.
facts.quote: This service allows you to report accidents that occurred less than 60 days ago which was not investigated by law enforcement.

facts.claim: Online counter reports are not investigated by law enforcement and are kept for record purposes only.
facts.quote: If a crash report is filed online by an individual, the report does not get investigated by a law enforcement agency. The reports are kept for record purposes only.

facts.claim: Form DR 2559 gives a different DMV mailing address for record requests, PO Box 173345, Denver CO 80217, from the P.O. Box 173350 on the crash records web page.
facts.quote: or by mail at Colorado Department of Revenue, Division of Motor Vehicles, PO Box 173345 Denver CO 80217

facts.quote: Category - Select - Crash Information Crash Records Death Certificates and Notifications Other Please describe your request in detail.

facts.claim: Form DR 2489 also requires the DR 2478 Driver Record Statement of Fact, unless the chosen permissible use says it is not needed.
facts.quote: Note - the DR 2478 is required unless where indicated.

facts.claim: DR 2489 requires requesters to say whether the request is for federal immigration enforcement. If it is, they must submit a copy of the warrant, court order or subpoena.
facts.quote: Required: Per §24-74-105 C.R.S., Is this request being completed for the purpose of investigating for, participating in, cooperating with, or assisting in Federal Immigration Enforcement? Yes, please submit a copy of the warrant, court order or subpoena.

facts.claim: DR 2489 lists insurers and insurance support agencies as a permissible use when the request is for claims, investigations, anti-fraud activities, rating or underwriting.
facts.quote: By an insurer or insurance support agency in connection with claims, investigations, anti-fraud activities, rating or underwriting.

facts.claim: DR 2489 also lists use in a civil, criminal, administrative or arbitral proceeding, or under a court order, as a permissible use.
facts.quote: In connection with a civil, criminal, administrative or arbitral proceeding in any court or before a self-regulatory body, including service of process, investigation, execution or enforcement of judgment, or pursuant to a court order.

facts.claim: Unlike the basic crash report, the Colorado State Patrol's Complete Case File covers the entire investigation report, including witness statements and other written reports if obtained.
facts.quote: Complete Case File This encompasses the entire investigation report and does include if obtained; witness statements and other written reports.

facts.claim: For dash camera or body-worn camera video, the Colorado State Patrol must confirm availability and payment before it processes the request.
facts.quote: Availability and payment must be obtained for Dash Camera or Body-worn camera prior to processing a request.

facts.claim: The Colorado State Patrol may require a $50.00 deposit when research time will run past one hour.
facts.quote: If the Record Custodian determines that the research time will extend beyond one hour, a A $50.00 deposit may be required.

facts.claim: The Colorado State Patrol fee schedule lists $.25 for each one-sided photocopied page, $5.00 for a CD, DVD or USB drive, and $5.00 for postage.

facts.claim: The Colorado State Patrol processes records requests in the order received, and requesters can track status by logging into their portal account.
facts.quote: Requests are processed in the order they are received. You can track the status of your request by logging into your account.

facts.claim: The Colorado State Patrol Central Records Unit is open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday, and is closed on weekends and holidays.
facts.quote: 8 a.m. - 5 p.m. Monday – Friday Closed Saturdays, Sundays and Holidays

facts.claim: Under HB26-1127 (effective August 12, 2026), if someone involved in a crash dies of crash injuries within 30 days, the officer who was notified of or investigated the crash must send the department an amended report within five days of learning of the death.
facts.quote: IF A PARTICIPANT IN A CRASH DIES WITHIN THIRTY DAYS AFTER THE CRASH AS A RESULT OF AN INJURY SUSTAINED IN THE CRASH, THE LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER WHO WAS NOTIFIED OF OR INVESTIGATED THE CRASH SHALL SUBMIT AN AMENDED REPORT TO THE DEPARTMENT WITHIN FIVE DAYS AFTER RECEIVING NOTIFICATION OF THE DEATH.

gaps.reason: The CSP Central Records Unit page says credit card payments are 'subject to an e-commerce portal pricing', but no official page I read gives the amount of that card or convenience fee.

The CSP crash page sends requesters to the Central Records Unit for costs. The CSP fee schedule (CSP 402A, 1/13/2023) lists $5.00 for an 'Initial Criminal Justice Record to include up to 10 pages' but never names crash reports, so the exact price of a crash report is unconfirmed. The DMV page's 'required fee' link redirects to an unrelated vehicle taxes page; the $9.25/$10.25 search fees come from forms DR 2559 and DR 2489.

The CSP Records Request Portal (coloradostatepatrol.govqa.us) returned HTTP 403 to every fetch, so I could not confirm its request categories, required fields or on-screen fees. The current DMV crash records page offers no online request for crash report copies, only mail and in-person appointments.

The DMV crash records page gives P.O. Box 173350, Denver, CO 80217-3350 for mailed requests, but the current DR 2559 and DR 2489 forms print PO Box 173345, Denver CO 80217-3345. Which box applies to crash report requests is unconfirmed. The CSP page says reports are mailed to requesters but does not give a postal address for sending requests. The CRU address is 700 Kipling Street, Lakewood.

No state page I read tells the public how to request a report directly from a city police department or county sheriff, or what those agencies charge. State law requires all law enforcement officers to send crash reports to 'the department', and the DMV says it receives reports from law enforcement agencies. Whether a DMV copy is the full officer-written report or only the data entered into the driver license system is not stated. Local police and sheriff procedures appear only on city and county sites, which fall outside the state-source rule.

I could not open the official text of C.R.S. 42-4-1606 or 42-4-1610: the leg.colorado.gov Title 42 PDF returned 403. No official source I read gives a filing deadline or damage or injury threshold for the online counter report. The DMV says drivers 'may' file online when no officer came. Deadlines of 30 or 60 days appear only on city or county and law-firm pages, which disagree and are not state sources. The CSP page cites 'CRS 42-4-1601' for the duty to report immediately to the agency having jurisdiction.

No official page I read confirms whether CSP crash reports are restricted to involved parties or whether juveniles' identities are withheld. That claim appears only on law-firm sites. The CSP page describes release of non-official-action records as at the custodian's discretion, plus a signed no-solicitation statement.

correction unverifiable: The quote does appear on the locations page: 'Westgate 3265 S. Wadsworth Blvd., #3A, Lakewood, CO 80227 Hours: 8 a.m. - 5 p.m., Mon. - Fri.' But it supports only the address. facts.claim: The DESPP Reports and Records page is for Connecticut State Police incident reports.
facts.quote: Please note: This page is intended to provide access to Connecticut State Police Incident Reports.

facts.claim: Under state law, the Commissioner of Transportation prescribes one uniform accident report form for the State Police and for every police department.
facts.quote: The Commissioner of Transportation shall prescribe for the Division of State Police within the Department of Emergency Services and Public Protection and for each police department and officer and other suitable agencies or individuals a uniform investigation of accident report

facts.claim: The law covers crashes where someone is killed or injured, or where any one person has more than $1,000 in property damage.
facts.quote: In each motor vehicle accident in which any person is killed or injured or in which damage to the property of any one individual, including the operator, in excess of one thousand dollars is sustained

facts.claim: For those crashes, the investigating officer or agency must send one copy of the report to the Commissioner of Transportation within five days after finishing the investigation.
facts.quote: shall, not later than five days after completing such investigation, complete and forward one copy of such report to the Commissioner of Transportation.

facts.claim: Many simple State Police crash reports may be online at BuyCrash within thirty business days of the crash, where they can be bought and downloaded at once.
facts.quote: Many simple motor vehicle accidents may be available online at http://www.BuyCrash.com * within thirty business days following the date of the accident. Available accidents through this site may be purchased and downloaded at the time of purchase.

facts.claim: Crashes not online within 30 days, serious-injury and fatal crashes, and other investigative reports may be requested from the Reports and Records Unit through the GovQA online portal.
facts.quote: All other accidents which are not available online within 30 days from the date of the accident, serious injury, fatalities, and other investigative reports may be requested directly from the Reports and Records Unit via the online customer portal, at GovQA.

facts.claim: After a GovQA request is submitted, the invoice appears in the customer account and can be paid online by debit or credit card.
facts.quote: After your request is submitted, your invoice will be available in your customer account and may be paid directly online via debit or credit card.

facts.claim: A free Accident Information Summary is available at accidents.despp.ct.gov.
facts.quote: For a free copy of an Accident Information Summary, please click this link: https://accidents.despp.ct.gov

facts.claim: The Accident Information Summary is for information only and is not the official accident report.
facts.quote: The summary is for informational purposes only and is not the official accident report. Most Accident Information Summaries are available to the parties involved in an accident on the DESPP Internet website.

facts.claim: The DPS-96-C form says many crash reports can also be obtained online at buycrash.lexisnexisrisk.com.
facts.quote: Many crash reports may also be obtained online at buycrash.lexisnexisrisk.com

facts.claim: A copy of an accident report can also be requested by mailing Form DPS-96-C, "Request for Copy of Report."
facts.quote: You may also obtain a copy of an accident or incident report by mailing a completed request form, DPS-96-C “Request for Copy of Report.”

facts.claim: Form DPS-96-C and the check or money order go to the DESPP Reports & Records Unit at 1111 Country Club Road, Middletown, CT 06457-2389.
facts.quote: Mail the check or money order in the amount required and this request to: DESPP-Reports & Records Unit, 1111 Country Club Road, Middletown, CT 06457-2389

facts.claim: The DESPP FAQ says not to email or fax the mail-in request; send it by U.S. mail only.

facts.quote: Enclose search fees (C.G.S. § 29-10b non-refundable search fee regardless if a report is produced or not) by check or money order payable to "Treasurer - State of CT" in the proper amount:

facts.claim: If information in the online summary is restricted, you may get a copy of the Accident Information Summary at the State Police Troop for the area where the crash happened.
facts.quote: Connecticut General Statutes may restrict what information is provided in the summary. In cases where information is restricted, you may visit the State Police Troop in the area in which your accident occurred to obtain a copy of the Accident Information Summary.

facts.claim: Questions about State Police reports can be directed to (860) 685-8250.

The DESPP page says it covers only Connecticut State Police incident reports. §14-108a has every police department send reportable crash reports to the Commissioner of Transportation, but no official source found says CTDOT gives copies to the public. Two CTDOT pages tried (Crash-Data-Collection-Initiatives-and-Programs and PP_SysInfo/Accident-Records) returned 404, and the CTDOT accident-records pamphlet PDF did not load. Municipal police sites were not used because they are not state sources.

The price BuyCrash charges for a Connecticut report could not be confirmed. BuyCrash returned 403 (Cloudflare), and no state page states the amount. DESPP says only that vendor convenience fees may apply. Fees charged by local police departments were not researched from official state sources.

For full reports, the only official timing found is BuyCrash availability 'within thirty business days' and the §29-10c 30-day access rule for involved parties. No official processing time was found for GovQA or mailed requests. DESPP says only that requests are processed in the order received. The DESPP FAQ still says reports are 'normally available within ten business days' on Docview.us.com, which conflicts with the current Reports and Records page, so it was not used for timing.

The DESPP FAQ page that describes mail requests also names Docview.us.com as the online source, and that conflicts with the current Reports and Records page (BuyCrash and GovQA). The FAQ may be partly out of date. The DPS-96-C form (Rev. 9/27/23) is the more current mail source. The FAQ's form link (ct.gov/dps/lib/dps/reports_and_records/dps-0096-c.pdf) is broken; use the portal.ct.gov PDF instead.

No official source says a full State Police crash report can be requested in person. The only in-person option found is getting a restricted Accident Information Summary at the local State Police Troop.
The GovQA portal returned 403 to automated fetches, so its request form fields, account requirements and any portal-specific fees could not be read.

No current official source found that requires Connecticut drivers to file their own crash report with a state agency, and none that says they do not. The only finding is that §14-108 ('Report of accidents') is repealed. The statute text read does not state what the repealed section required. The CT DMV forms results surfaced in search showed no driver accident report form, but the DMV page itself was not opened and read.
§29-10c covers records of the Division of State Police only. No official source was read on who may get crash reports held by municipal police departments.

gaps.reason: No official online portal for first-party PD-10 requests was found. MPD's page lists only email, mail and in-person (by appointment). No DC government page found names or links a vendor crash-report portal such as BuyCrash or Crashdocs. The only online portal found is the DC FOIA public access website, which is the third-party (FOIA) route.

The PD-10 email address on the MPD page is hidden by Cloudflare email protection in the page source, so text fetchers see '[email protected]'. I decoded it from the page's data-cfemail attribute as mpd.public-docs@dc.gov, which is what a browser shows. The quote for that fact is the browser-rendered sentence. Check it in a browser before publishing.

No official source says how soon after a crash a PD-10 becomes available to request. The only time frames found are the six-week mail-in processing time and the DC FOIA response deadlines. MPD training material says officers must submit and approve reports by the end of their tour, but that is not a statement about public availability.

MPD's page gives the $3 insurer fee but not the payment method, payee or any card or convenience fee. The page also says PD-10 requests are first-party only while describing insurer copies, and it doesn't explain how insurers request them. MPD's FOIA page says FOIA processing fees may be charged but gives no amounts.

The header of PD Form 10B still shows an older address (MPD Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Office, 300 Indiana Avenue, NW, Room 4153), and its footer is dated January 14, 2015 (GO-SPT-401.03 Attachment B). The current request page says to mail requests to the Public Documents Section at 441 4th Street, NW, Room 550 South. The guide should use the page's address, not the form header.

DC has no separate county or city crash-report system beyond MPD, and no DC government page was found that says what to do when another police agency operating in DC handled the crash (for example U.S. Park Police, U.S. Capitol Police or Metro Transit Police), or whether MPD holds those reports. MPD's page covers only reports written by MPD officers. Lead only, not recorded as a fact: the U.S. Park Police's own federal pages say crash reports for its Washington, D.C.-area incidents are requested from USPP Records (https://www.nps.gov/aboutus/foia/how-to-request-an-accident-report.htm, and https://www.nps.gov/subjects/uspp/foia-requests.htm, which gives USPP_Records@nps.gov). These are federal nps.gov pages, outside this task's state/DC source definition.

No official source says outright whether MPD's Public Documents Section holds crash reports from every law-enforcement agency in DC or only its own. Its page describes only MPD officers' PD-10 and PD-251 reports. D.C. Code § 50–1731.07(b) says MPD gives DDOT a copy of each accident report, but no official page says DDOT gives individual reports to the public.

It is unclear whether DC drivers must currently file the Motor Vehicle Crash Report for PROPERTY DAMAGE ONLY form. The form PDF (created 2011) and MPD training material (approved 4/26/2023) describe it. But MPD's web page for the form now permanently redirects to DDOT's 'What To Do After A Non-Injury Crash?' page, which doesn't mention filing any form. DDOT's current checklist is marked for informational purposes only, DC DMV says not to report any crash to DMV, and the D.C. Code accident-report subchapter (§ 50–1301.10 et seq.) is repealed. The only submission details found are on a 2011 DDOT envelope PDF (DDOT - Safety Division Crash Records Box, PO Box 20164, Washington, DC 20077-7822; fax (703) 858-1358; www.ddot-hso.com/CrashForm), which I could not confirm as current. No official source gives a current legal deadline or dollar threshold for drivers to self-report.
No confidentiality waiting period was found. MPD sends third parties to FOIA, but no official source says what a non-involved third party receives (for example a full or a redacted PD-10).

gaps.reason: No official Delaware State Police or State of Delaware page names an online portal or a vendor (BuyCrash, CARFAX Crashdocs, PoliceReports.US) for crash reports. The DSP page says requests must be made by mail. None of the local agency pages reviewed (Wilmington, Newark, New Castle County, Middletown, Cheswold) names a vendor portal.

No official Delaware source gives a typical number of days or weeks before a crash report is available. The DSP page is silent on timing, and Cheswold only says to call and confirm the report is ready.

The DSP page lists only check or money order, so no card or convenience fee applies to DSP requests. No official source gives a separate DSP fee schedule or rule beyond the page and 21 Del. C. §313(c)(2), which leaves the fee to each investigating agency.

No official page says whether the Delaware State Police can supply reports written by other agencies. DSHS is the official custodian, but the state's crash data description directs authorized parties to the reporting police agency, and the DSP page does not say it handles other agencies' reports.

The DSP page asks only for a copy of the collision information exchange form and payment. It does not separately list a report number, names or ID, though 21 Del. C. §313(c)(2) requires proof of identity for any requester.
The DSP page does not state its own eligibility rules. Eligibility here comes from 21 Del. C. §313(c) and local agency pages.

No official source names a driver-filed state crash report form or deadline. Under 21 Del. C. §4203 the driver reports to the police agency with jurisdiction, and DSHS may require supplemental reports on its own forms only when it considers the original report insufficient.

Not every Delaware municipal police department or Kent and Sussex County agency was reviewed. The Dover Police Department's crash report page is on doverpolice.org, not a .gov domain, so it was not used as a source.

facts.claim: The Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles (FLHSMV) is Florida's official repository for crash records.
facts.quote: FLHSMV is the state’s official repository for crash records.

facts.claim: FLHSMV says it is responsible for the collection and dissemination of crash reports.
facts.quote: the FLHSMV is responsible for the collection and dissemination of crash reports.

facts.claim: Florida law requires long-form and short-form crash reports prepared by law enforcement to be submitted to the department (FLHSMV), and the officer's own agency may also keep them.
facts.quote: Long-form and short-form crash reports prepared by law enforcement must be submitted to the department and may be maintained by the law enforcement officer’s agency.

facts.claim: The Florida Crash Portal is FLHSMV's portal for obtaining official Florida law enforcement agency crash reports.
facts.quote: Welcome to the Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles’ portal for obtaining official Florida law enforcement agency crash reports.

facts.claim: FLHSMV says the Florida Traffic Crash Report is used by law enforcement officers in Florida to report traffic crashes to FLHSMV.
facts.quote: is used by law enforcement officers in Florida to report traffic crashes to the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles (FLHSMV).

facts.claim: Traffic crash reports can be bought online through the FLHSMV Crash Portal.
facts.quote: Traffic crash reports can be purchased through the FLHSMV Crash Portal.

facts.claim: Reports bought online are available immediately, must be downloaded within 48 hours, and a download link is emailed to the address given with the request.
facts.quote: reports become available online immediately and must be downloaded within 48 hours of the request. A download link will be emailed to the email address provided at the time of the request.

facts.claim: Reports from the portal come as a Zip file containing PDF files.
facts.quote: Crash reports are provided as a Zip file containing PDF files.

facts.claim: Requests for 10 or fewer crash records may be filled at the FHP Troop Station nearest to where the crash occurred.
facts.quote: Requests for 10 or fewer crash records may be fulfilled at the FHP Troop Station nearest to where the crash occurred.

facts.claim: Requests for more than 10 records must be mailed with a request letter describing the reports, a signed statement for each report, and payment.
facts.quote: Requests for more than 10 records must include a request letter detailing the crash report you are requesting, a signed statement, for each crash report requested, payment must be mailed to:

facts.claim: The mailing address is Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles, Crash Records, 2900 Apalachee Parkway, MS 28, Tallahassee, FL 32399.
facts.quote: Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles Crash Records 2900 Apalachee Parkway, MS 28 Tallahassee, FL 32399

facts.claim: Payment must be included with a mailed request, by check or money order made out to FLHSMV.
facts.quote: Payment must be included with the request. Check or money order should be made out to “FLHSMV.”

facts.claim: To get a crash report by mail or in person, you must complete a signed statement.
facts.quote: Customers requesting a crash record must complete a signed statement to receive a crash report mail or in person.

facts.claim: HSMV Form 94010 asks for the date of crash, the crash report number and law enforcement agency case number if known, the location and county of the crash, and the parties involved.
facts.quote: Date of Crash Crash Report # (if known) Law Enforcement Agency Case # (FHP or other, if known) Location of Crash County (where crash occurred) Parties Involved

facts.claim: Section One of HSMV Form 94010 is a sworn statement for obtaining a crash report within 60 days of filing.
facts.quote: SECTION ONE: Sworn Statement for Obtaining Crash Report within 60 Days of Filing

facts.claim: HSMV Form 94010 includes a notary section.
facts.quote: (Print, Type or Stamp Commissioned Name of Notary Public)

facts.quote: The fee for crash reports is $10.00 per report, per section 321.23, Florida Statutes. Customers are limited to a maximum of 10 reports per transaction.

facts.claim: The self-report form number is HSMV 90011S.

facts.quote: Once completed, a copy of the “Driver Self Report of Traffic Crash” can be emailed to SelfReportCrashes@flhsmv.gov.

facts.claim: A self-report can also be mailed to Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles, Crash Records, 2900 Apalachee Parkway, MS 28, Tallahassee, FL 32399.
facts.quote: Once complete, mail a copy of the report to:Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles Crash Records 2900 Apalachee Parkway, MS 28 Tallahassee, FL 32399

facts.claim: The driver must complete all applicable areas of the self-report form and sign it.
facts.quote: Please complete all applicable areas within the form. Customers must sign the report.

facts.claim: FLHSMV advises keeping a copy of the submitted self-report for your records and insurance purposes.
facts.quote: Please keep a copy of the submitted report for your records and insurance purposes.

facts.claim: A driver who fails to file the required written report commits a noncriminal traffic infraction, punishable as a nonmoving violation.
facts.quote: Any driver failing to file the written report required under subsection (1) commits a noncriminal traffic infraction, punishable as a nonmoving violation as provided in chapter 318.

facts.claim: During the 60-day confidential period, the portal sells crash reports only to people who meet a statutory exception. The buyer must disclose the exemption, give a driver license number and perform an attestation.
facts.quote: Crash reports sold prior to or during this timeframe can only be sold to those individuals who meet one of the exceptions required by statute. A purchaser must disclose the exemption on the webpage and provide their driver license number. Additionally, requestors must perform an attestation

facts.claim: Sixty days after a crash report is filed, FLHSMV's crash portal says it may be made available to any person or entity eligible under s. 316.066(2)(b), Fla. Stat., or in accordance with a permissible use listed in the federal Driver's Privacy Protection Act, 18 U.S.C. s. 2721(b).
facts.quote: After 60 days the crash report is filed, the crash report may be made available to any person or entity eligible to access crash reports under 316.066(2)(b), Fla. Stat., or in accordance with any of the permissible uses listed in the Driver Privacy Protection Act (DPPA), 18 U.S.C. s. 2721(b)

facts.claim: HSMV Form 94010 has a Section Two, a DPPA certification, for requests made 60 days or later after a report is filed. At that point reports may be released to any person or entity in accordance with a DPPA (federal Driver's Privacy Protection Act) permissible use.
facts.quote: SECTION TWO: DPPA Certification for Obtaining Crash Report 60 Days or Later After Filing Pursuant to § 316.066(2)(f), Fla. Stat., crash reports may be made available 60 days after filing to any person or entity in accordance with any of the permissible uses

facts.claim: On Form 94010 the requester swears, under penalty of perjury, that the answers are true and complete and that the report will not be used for commercial solicitation of crash victims or knowingly disclosed to a third party for that purpose.
facts.quote: Under penalty of perjury, I swear (or affirm) that the foregoing answers are true and complete and that the requested report will not be used for commercial solicitation of crash victims or knowingly disclosed to any third party for purposes of such solicitation.

facts.claim: Form 94010's notary block allows the statement to be sworn before a notary either in person or by online notarization.
facts.quote: Sworn to (or affirmed) and subscribed before me by means of ❑ physical presence or ❑ online notarization

facts.claim: Form 94010 asks for the requester's name, date of request, reference number, street address, telephone and fax numbers, city, state, ZIP and email address.
facts.quote: Name of Requester Date of Request Reference # (Case/File Name) Street Address Telephone Number Fax Number City State Zip Email Address

facts.claim: Florida law lets a third party acting on behalf of an authorized person or entity obtain a crash report, but the third party may disclose it only to the authorized person or entity.
facts.quote: A crash report may also be made available to any third party acting on behalf of a person or entity authorized under this section to access the crash report, except that the third party may disclose the crash report only to the person or entity authorized

facts.claim: FLHSMV's FAQ says a crash report that has been submitted to FLHSMV can be provided to a requester who meets an exemption in s. 316.066, even if the investigation is not complete.
facts.quote: If a crash report has been submitted to FLHSMV, regardless if the investigation is complete or not, it can be provided as a public record request, if the party meets an exemption outlined in section 316.066, Florida Statutes.

facts.claim: When a long-form report is not required for a crash on a public road, the officer must complete a short-form crash report or provide a driver exchange-of-information form.
facts.quote: In any crash for which a Florida Traffic Crash Report, Long Form is not required by this section and which occurs on the public roadways of this state, the law enforcement officer shall complete a short-form crash report or provide a driver exchange-of-information form

facts.claim: The confidentiality and access rules in s. 316.066(2) are subject to the Open Government Sunset Review Act and stand repealed on October 2, 2027 unless the Legislature reenacts them.
facts.quote: This subsection is subject to the Open Government Sunset Review Act in accordance with s. 119.15 and shall stand repealed on October 2, 2027, unless reviewed and saved from repeal through reenactment by the Legislature.

facts.claim: FLHSMV says public records requests for additional crash data should be sent to CrashRecords@flhsmv.gov.
facts.quote: Public records requests for additional data should be submitted to CrashRecords@flhsmv.gov.

facts.claim: The HSMV 90011S form's own instructions say to email it to SelfReportCrashes@flhsmv.gov or mail it to Florida Highway Safety & Motor Vehicles, Self Report Crash Team, 2900 Apalachee Pkwy, MS 28, Tallahassee, Florida 32399.
facts.quote: Submit this via email to SelfReportCrashes@flhsmv.gov, OR; Mail this report to: Florida Highway Safety & Motor Vehicles Self Report Crash Team 2900 Apalachee Pkwy, MS 28 Tallahassee, Florida 32399

facts.claim: For a self-report sent by email, FLHSMV says to complete all applicable fields, including signature and date, and that instructions are on page 2 of the form.
facts.quote: Please complete all applicable fields within the linked form, including signature and date. Instructions can be found on page 2 of the form.

gaps.reason: From this environment, the live official sites (flhsmv.gov, services.flhsmv.gov and fdot.gov) returned HTTP 403 'Access Denied', and leg.state.fl.us and flsenate.gov refused connections. WebFetch, the hound fetcher, curl and a browser were all tried. Every fact was therefore read from an Internet Archive Wayback Machine capture of the official page, and the original official URL is embedded in each sourceUrl. Capture dates run from 2025-09-12 to 2026-10-08. The statute captures show the 2025 Florida Statutes, so any 2026 amendments to s. 316.066 or s. 321.23 are unconfirmed. Re-check against the live pages from a US connection before publishing.

The captured portal page only shows the notice that comes before the search step. The fields the portal needs to find a report (for example report number, driver name, date or VIN) were not visible, and I did not click through. The only confirmed online requirements are stating the exemption, giving a driver license number and making the attestation.

No official state page I read explains how to get a copy directly from a city police department or county sheriff's office, or what those agencies charge. State sources confirm only that law enforcement reports must be submitted to FLHSMV and 'may be maintained by the law enforcement officer’s agency', and that the sworn statement is filed with the 'state or local agency in possession of the information'. Local procedures and fees were not researched from state sources.

The FLHSMV page does not say whether the $2.00 convenience fee or any other charge applies to mail or in-person requests, or which payment methods FHP Troop Stations accept. For mail it says only check or money order made out to 'FLHSMV'. Notary costs for Form 94010 are not stated.

The FLHSMV page says a 'signed statement' is needed for mail and in-person requests, and the statute calls it a 'written sworn statement'. Form 94010 has a notary section, but no official page I read says in plain words that the form must be notarized. The FLHSMV page also does not list which ID to bring to an FHP Troop Station, although s. 316.066(2)(d) requires a valid driver license or other photo ID.
FHP Troop Station addresses and hours were not confirmed. The FHP troop boundaries page was not read because the live flhsmv.gov site was blocked.
No official source states how long an in-person request at an FHP Troop Station takes. The 4-6 weeks figure applies to mailed requests.

The sources differ on access after 60 days. The FLHSMV FAQ says 'After sixty-days, all crash reports are public record and can be released', but s. 316.066(2)(f) and the crash portal say that after 60 days reports go to people eligible under paragraph (b) or for a permissible use under 18 U.S.C. s. 2721(b) (DPPA). The guide should not say 'anyone' after 60 days without that qualifier.

The $500.00 'apparent damage' threshold for notifying law enforcement comes only from the FLHSMV page, which cites s. 316.065, Florida Statutes. I did not read s. 316.065 itself. The FLHSMV page also says drivers 'are eligible to self-report', while s. 316.066(1)(e) says the driver 'shall' submit a written report within 10 days, so the guide should state the statutory requirement.

facts.claim: The Georgia Department of Transportation (GDOT) is the designated state agency for managing and storing the state's crash reports.
facts.quote: Georgia DOT is the designated state agency for managing and storing the states crash reports.

facts.claim: GDOT keeps the reports it receives in an electronic database it calls the Georgia Electronic Crash Accident System (GEARS), and a user ID and password are needed to access submitted reports in that database.
facts.quote: All reports received by Georgia DOT are maintained via an electronic database called Georgia Electronic Crash Accident System (GEARS). A unique User ID and Password are required to access submitted crash reports.

facts.claim: Under O.C.G.A. § 40-9-31, as quoted by GDOT, every state and local law-enforcement agency must send GDOT the original of any accident report it prepares.
facts.quote: Each state and local law enforcement agency shall submit to the Department of Transportation the original document of any accident report prepared by such law enforcement agency

facts.claim: For a crash investigated by the Georgia State Patrol, the Department of Public Safety (DPS) says you may contact a local State Patrol Post or the DPS Open Records Unit.
facts.quote: If the crash was investigated by the Georgia State Patrol, you may contact a local State Patrol Post or the Open Records Unit.

facts.claim: DPS directs requesters for all crash reports not investigated by the Georgia State Patrol to GDOT's Crash Reporting Unit.
facts.quote: For all other crash reports, please contact the Crash Reporting Unit for the Georgia Department of Transportation.

facts.claim: The DPS fee page sends requesters to the EPORTS portal to get copies of crash reports electronically.
facts.quote: Please visit the EPORTS portal,which allows requestors to seek and receive copies of citations, incident reports, and crash reports by electronic means.

facts.claim: An EPORTS request must include the incident date range and the request type, and should include other details such as the report number or the people involved.
facts.quote: You must provide the correct timeframe for the “Incident Date” and indicate the “Request Type” (i.e. citation, crash, or incident report).  Both are indicated by an asterisk (*).  You should provide other criteria (e.g. report number, involved parties)

facts.claim: Through EPORTS, an uncertified electronic copy of a single crash report costs $5.00.
facts.quote: The cost for an uncertified electronic copy of a single crash report is $5.00.

facts.claim: DPS also accepts requests by mail or email using its request form, but these take longer to process than EPORTS.
facts.quote: Yes, but a request made by mail or email requires DPS to take additional steps, which therefore requires additional processing time. If EPORTS is unavailable for your use, please download and complete the DPS request form (click here) and return it to the address shown on the form.

facts.claim: DPS says its Open Records Request Form helps it find a crash report, but using the form is not required.
facts.quote: This form serves to assist the Georgia Department of Public Safety (“DPS”) in efficiently locating and providing responsive documentation for a DPS incident report, citation, or crash report. DPS does not require its use.

facts.claim: Georgia law requires anyone getting a crash report to give a sufficient statement of need, which in EPORTS means stating your lawful connection to the crash or the people in it.
facts.quote: Georgia law requires a sufficient statement of need for anyone to acquire a crash report. See O.C.G.A. § 50-18-72(a)(5).  By utilizing EPORTS, you must simply identify your lawfully recognized connection to the crash event or parties.

facts.claim: DPS crash reports are generally ready within three to five business days of the crash, but multi-vehicle crashes and those with serious injury or death often take longer.
facts.quote: Crash reports and incident reports are generally prepared and available within three to five business days of the occurrence, although multi-vehicle crashes and those resulting in serious injury or death often require additional completion time.

facts.claim: Once submitted, EPORTS requests for available reports are generally processed within three business days.
facts.quote: Available reports will be processed generally within three business days after submission.

facts.claim: DPS keeps crash reports for three years plus the current year, and older reports are no longer available.
facts.quote: The state retention schedule for crash reports, incident reports, and citation is three (3) years plus current year. Documents outside this retention schedule are no longer available.

facts.claim: The Columbus (Georgia) Police Department says its accident reports can be viewed, downloaded and printed at www.buycrash.com for a nominal fee.
facts.quote: Simply go to www.buycrash.com and you will be able to view, download and print your accident report for a nominal fee.

facts.claim: Columbus Police also let you pick up a copy of a Motor Vehicle Accident Report in person at Desk Services in the lobby of the Public Safety Building.
facts.quote: You may personally pick up a copy of a Motor Vehicle Accident Report from Desk Services, located in the lobby of the Public Safety Building.

facts.claim: The Gwinnett County Police Department says people involved in a Gwinnett County collision, or their authorized legal or insurance representative, can get their reports online at www.buycrash.com for a charge.
facts.quote: anyone involved in a collision in Gwinnett County or his or her authorized legal/insurance representative can obtain their accident reports online on www.buycrash.com. Please be advised there is a charge for this service.

facts.claim: Georgia's Drivers' Manual tells drivers to notify the nearest law-enforcement agency immediately if anyone is injured or killed, or if property damage exceeds $500.00.
facts.quote: Notify the nearest law enforcement agency immediately if anyone is injured or killed, or if property damage exceeds $500.00;

facts.claim: O.C.G.A. § 40-6-273, as quoted by GDOT, requires the driver in a crash causing injury, death, or apparent property damage of $500.00 or more to notify the local police department immediately by the quickest means.
facts.quote: The driver of a vehicle involved in an accident resulting in injury to or death of any person or property damage to an apparent extent of $500.00 or more shall immediately, by the quickest means of communication, give notice of such accident to the local police department

facts.claim: EPORTS, the DPS online system, lets people request and receive copies of DPS-prepared reports, including motor vehicle crash reports, and also lets them pay for copies of records requested from and received from DPS.
facts.quote: secure online system designed for individuals to request and receive copies of DPS-prepared reports - traffic citations, motor vehicle crash reports, incident reports, and arrest reports. EPORTS also allows you to pay for copies of any records requested of and received from DPS.

facts.claim: EPORTS provides copies of available citations, incident reports and crash reports prepared by DPS law enforcement; similar reports prepared by municipal and county police departments, sheriffs' offices or other state agencies are not available through EPORTS.
facts.quote: EPORTS provides copies of available citations, incident, and crash reports prepared by DPS law enforcement. Similar reports prepared by municipal and county police departments, sheriffs’ offices or other state agencies are not available through EPORTS.

facts.claim: When an EPORTS request is complete you receive an email; you then click 'Search by Request #', enter the Request # from the email, and click 'Review and Pay' to pay for and download the report.
facts.quote: You will receive an email notifying you when your request is “Complete.” Click the blue “Search by Request #” button and enter the Request # from the email. Step 3 (Pay) – After you enter the Request #, click the “Review and Pay” button to pay and download your report.

facts.claim: EPORTS purchases must be made with a credit or debit card; accepted cards include VISA and MasterCard, and EPORTS cannot accept electronic checks or Discover cards.
facts.quote: Purchases must be made using a credit or debit card. Accepted cards include VISA and MasterCard. EPORTS cannot accept electronic checks or Discovery cards.

facts.claim: DPS prefers online payment when available; otherwise a check or money order must be sent to the Georgia Department of Public Safety, Attention: Open Records Unit, referencing the ORU number, at 959 United Avenue SE, Atlanta, Georgia 30316.
facts.quote: The preferred method of payment is online payment when available. Otherwise, a check or money order must be sent to: The Georgia Department of Public Safety Attention: Open Records Unit REFERENCE ORU# ________________ 959 United Avenue SE Atlanta, Georgia 30316

facts.claim: The DPS Open Records Request Form lists the Georgia Department of Public Safety at 959 United Avenue SE, Atlanta, Georgia 30316, with the email openrecords@gsp.net and phone (404) 624-7591.
facts.quote: GEORGIA DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY 959 UNITED AVENUE SE ATLANTA, GEORGIA 30316 openrecords@gsp.net (404) 624-7591

facts.claim: The DPS request form asks for the report number, the date, the full names of the subjects or victims involved, and the city and county where the crash occurred.
facts.quote: 3. What is the Report Number of the Incident/Citation/Crash? 4. What is the Date of the Incident/Citation/Crash? 5. What is the Full Name of the SUBJECT(S) or VICTIM(S) involved? 6. What is the CITY and COUNTY where the Incident/Citation/Crash occurred?

facts.claim: The DPS form's checklist for crash-report requesters includes: my property was damaged in the crash, I was in the crash, my minor child was injured in the crash, I was injured in the crash, I am an attorney for one of the parties, I witnessed the crash, and I am an insurance representative.
facts.quote: My property was damaged in the crash ___ I was in the crash ___ My minor child was injured in the crash ___ I was injured in the crash ___ I am an attorney for one of the parties involved in the crash ___ I witnessed the crash ___ I am an insurance representative

facts.claim: DPS says redaction means all lawfully protected personal and confidential information, including phone numbers, day and month of birth, and medical information, is redacted or hidden from view; Georgia law does not require redaction of dashcam video.
facts.quote: Redaction means that all lawfully protected personal and confidential information, including phone numbers, day and month of birth, and medical information, will be redacted or hidden from view. Georgia law does not require redaction of dashcam video.

facts.claim: Gwinnett County Police hard-copy accident reports are typically available for pickup four business days after the report was taken.
facts.quote: Reports are typically available for pickup four business days after the report was taken.

facts.claim: DPS says EPORTS is for documents prepared by the Georgia State Patrol, the Motor Carrier Compliance Division and the Capitol Police.
facts.quote: DPS offers EPORTS as an online platform for efficiently seeking and obtaining available and responsive documents prepared by the Georgia State Patrol, Motor Carrier Compliance Division and Capitol Police.

facts.claim: Only crash reports, incident reports and citations/warnings can be requested through EPORTS; for other records, DPS says to email openrecords@gsp.net.
facts.quote: Only crash reports, incident reports and citations/warnings can be requested via EPORTS. For additional records please email openrecords@gsp.net.

facts.claim: DPS's official Charging Chart lists a crash report at $5.00 each.
facts.quote: Crash Report $5.00 each

facts.claim: DPS charges $5.00 per set of photos for download, including any review and redaction.
facts.quote: Photos $5.00 per set for download, including any review and redaction

facts.claim: DPS charges $10.00 to download video and dashcam recordings.
facts.quote: Video and Dashcam (e.g., Witness Statements) $10.00 for download

facts.claim: DPS asks requesters not to send the same request in more than one format (for example by both mail and email), because each one gets its own response and its own charge.
facts.quote: Please do not submit the same request through multiple formats (e.g., both by US Mail and email), as this will result in your receiving multiple responses and being charged for each request you make.

facts.claim: DPS says a request is complete and payment is due once the record is made available, whether or not the requester inspects or accepts it.
facts.quote: Pursuant to the Open Records Act, a request is deemed complete, and the payment is due, when the record is made available, whether it was inspected or accepted by the requester or not.

facts.claim: DPS retrieves, reviews, redacts and produces EPORTS reports only during office hours (Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.), so a request submitted on a Saturday should not be expected before the following Tuesday.
facts.quote: Responsive, available reports are retrieved, reviewed, and redacted by us, as well as produced to you during office hours, M-F, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. For example, if you submit an EPORTS request on a Saturday, you should not expect document production until at least the following Tuesday

facts.claim: EPORTS accepts requests for citations, crash reports and incident reports 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, except during periodic routine maintenance.
facts.quote: Yes, EPORTS is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, and 365 days a year for requesting citations, crash, and incident reports, excluding the limited downtown for periodic, routine maintenance.

facts.claim: If an EPORTS search for a recent DPS crash report returns no results, the report is likely not ready yet, and you should search again later.
facts.quote: If you are attempting to search for a recent crash or incident report prepared by DPS law enforcement, and you receive no results, it is likely such report is not ready; you should try your search again later.

facts.claim: An EPORTS guest gets back to a request by entering its reference ID number under 'Search by Request Number', and the record stays available for three years.
facts.quote: If you are a Guest, you must input the reference ID number corresponding to your request under “Search by Request Number,” and the responsive record will remain available for three (3) years.

facts.claim: The EPORTS FAQ offers a downloadable Georgia Motor Vehicle Crash Report Overlay for reading the codes on a crash report.
facts.quote: The Georgia Motor Vehicle Crash Report Overlay is available for download here . Use the Overlay to interpret codes provided on the crash report.

facts.claim: For EPORTS questions, DPS says to email eportshelp@gsp.net during business hours, Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, excluding holidays.
facts.quote: please submit an email to eportshelp@gsp.net during regular business hours, Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM - 4:30 PM, excluding holidays.

facts.claim: DPS's open-records notice (effective July 24, 2020) says that if you are only requesting a crash report, you may submit the request, preferably in writing, directly to the Georgia State Patrol post that serves the county where the crash occurred.
facts.quote: If you are ONLY requesting a crash report, incident report, or citation, you may submit your request, preferably in writing, directly to the Georgia State Patrol (GSP) Post that serves the county where the incident occurred.

facts.claim: DPS gives 404-624-7591 as the phone number of its Open Records Unit.
facts.quote: If you have questions, contact the DPS Open Records Unit at 404-624-7591.

facts.claim: For photographs or other DPS records related to a crash, DPS says to send an Open Records Act request to its Open Records Unit.
facts.quote: How do I obtain photographs or other records related to my crash or incident? To obtain records from the Georgia Department of Public Safety, please direct your Open Records Act requests (under O.C.G.A. 50-18-70) to DPS Open Records Unit.

facts.claim: When requesting DPS records, DPS asks for the names of the subjects or victims, the records being requested, the Georgia county or city, the date of the incident, and the crash or incident report number if known.
facts.quote: The names of the subjects or victims of the investigation or report The records being requested The Georgia county or city where the incident occurred The date of the investigation or incident associated with your request The crash report number or incident report number, if known

facts.claim: The DPS request form also asks which law enforcement agency responded to the crash and for the officer's name or badge number.
facts.quote: What Law Enforcement Agency made the arrest, wrote the citation, or responded to the crash? What is the Officer's Name or Badge Number?

facts.claim: The DPS form also lets crash-report requesters claim a personal, professional or business connection with a party to the crash, and asks them to explain it.
facts.quote: I have a personal, professional or business connection with a party to the crash (Explain)

facts.claim: Gwinnett County Police accident reports can be picked up at any of seven police locations, Monday through Friday (offices are closed on county holidays), and cost $5.
facts.quote: Incident and accident reports may be obtained at any of the 7 locations listed below. Reports are available Monday through Friday. Offices/Precincts are closed on county holidays. Please refer to the website calendar section for a complete list of holidays. Accident reports are $5

facts.claim: Gwinnett County Police say to call 770.513.5000 for the status of a police report.
facts.quote: To get the status of a police report, please call 770.513.5000.

facts.claim: GDOT accepts crash data requests by email at CrashInquiries@dot.ga.gov; requesters must give a full description of the data and the location or area, and these requests are normally processed within five business days.
facts.quote: Customers electing to request data can simply email their request to CrashInquiries at CrashInquiries@dot.ga.gov. Customers will need to provide a full description of the data and the location or area. These requests are normally processed within five (5) business days.

facts.claim: Georgia's Drivers' Manual says that if you damage an unattended vehicle, you must either find the owner or leave your name, your address and the name of the owner of the vehicle you were driving in a conspicuous place where the owner will find it.
facts.quote: If you damage an unattended vehicle, you must either locate the owner or leave your name, address, and the name of the owner of the vehicle you were driving, in a conspicuous place where the owner will find it.

links.label: GDOT Crash Data (Crash Reporting Unit email contact)
links.officialEvidence: Georgia DOT subdomain crashmanual.dot.ga.gov, live (HTTP 200). The page states 'Georgia DOT is the designated state agency for managing and storing the states crash reports.'

gaps.reason: I could not confirm from a live official state page that GDOT's statewide reports are sold through LexisNexis BuyCrash. Every dot.ga.gov URL (CrashReporting.aspx, request_form.pdf, HowToBuyCrashReports.pdf) returned a 'Request Rejected' firewall page to WebFetch, curl, hound (stealth mode) and a Playwright browser. An Internet Archive capture from 2026-10-07 (https://web.archive.org/web/20261007091510/https://www.dot.ga.gov/GDOT/pages/CrashReporting.aspx) reads: 'Police crash reports are available through Buycrash. Crash reports can be purchased directly via the BuyCrash website or by mailing a request to GDOT via the GDOT Request Form.' It links to https://buycrash.lexisnexisrisk.com/ui/home and gives BuyCrash support as 1-866-215-2771. The archive is not an official source, so check this on the live page before publishing. The Columbus and Gwinnett County police pages above do name www.buycrash.com for their own reports.

I could not read GDOT's mail-in 'Individual Accident Report Request' form on dot.ga.gov because the site blocked access. An Internet Archive copy captured 2026-09-19 (https://web.archive.org/web/20260919010711id_/https://www.dot.ga.gov/DriveSmart/Data/Documents/Crash%20Reports%20and%20Forms/request_form.pdf) shows these details. It goes by mail to Georgia Dept. of Transportation, 935 United Ave. SE, Bldg 24, Atlanta, GA 30316. It asks for the last name on the report, crash date, reporting agency or report number, requester contact details, a signed statement of need, and categories A, B, C, E, F, G and I under O.C.G.A. § 50-18-72(a)(5). Its note says 'IT WILL TAKE AT THE LEAST TWO WEEKS'. Verify all of this on the live form before publishing.

The GDOT mail-request fee and the BuyCrash online price are not confirmed from a live official page. The archived GDOT form (not an official source) says 'Reports Cost $5 each. Additional $2 charge for certified report, if requested. Please make payment by money order or cashier’s check (NO CASH OR PERSONAL CHECKS)'. No official page I could read states BuyCrash's current price or any convenience fee. Columbus PD says only 'a nominal fee' and Gwinnett says only 'there is a charge'. For DPS/EPORTS, no official page mentions a card or convenience fee on top of the $5.00.

For reports held by GDOT, or bought through BuyCrash for city and county crashes, I found no official live page that says how soon they become available. The 'normally processed within five (5) business days' on crashmanual.dot.ga.gov/data covers crash-data requests, not copies of individual reports, so I did not use it.

I could not open the official O.C.G.A. text of § 50-18-72(a)(5): the state code is hosted by LexisNexis behind a script-driven viewer. Who may get a report is therefore cited only from DPS's own summary and form. I found no official statement of a time-limited confidentiality period for crash reports.

No official source I read requires Georgia drivers to file their own written crash report with a state agency. The DDS manual and O.C.G.A. § 40-6-273, as quoted by GDOT, require only immediate notice to law enforcement. Law-firm sites mention an SR-13 or DDS-912 driver form, but I found no official page confirming any such form, deadline or filing agency.

Under § 40-9-31 local agencies must send their reports to GDOT, but no live official state page told me whether every city and county report can be bought through BuyCrash or the GDOT form. Practice varies by agency: for example, Columbus and Gwinnett offer both BuyCrash and in-person pickup. Readers should also be told to contact the investigating agency directly.
