gaps.reason: I found no official page describing a statewide crash-report request system, state police or highway patrol that issues copies of Hawaii crash reports. The official sources show that the four county police departments (Honolulu, Hawaiʻi County, Maui, Kauaʻi) write and keep the reports. HDOT's SHACA system receives their crash data, but I found no HDOT page offering copies of individual reports to the public. I also could not confirm what role, if any, the state Department of Law Enforcement plays in crash reports.

I could not read the full text of HRS §291C-20, so the exact statutory list of 'parties of interest' is unconfirmed. capitol.hawaii.gov and data.capitol.hawaii.gov returned Cloudflare 403 to WebFetch, curl, a stealth fetcher and a browser. The Hawaii County page cites the statute but does not list who qualifies.

Search snippets point to HRS §291C-16 (immediate notice to police) and HRS §287-4 (a written or in-person report to the chief of police within 24 hours when someone is injured or killed, or damage is apparently over $3,000). Both statute pages on capitol.hawaii.gov returned 403, so I could not confirm the text, deadline or threshold. I found no official source requiring drivers to file their own crash report with a state agency.
The Kauaʻi Police Department Records Section page gives no fee for copies of police or accident reports, and no other official Kauaʻi page with a fee came up.

No official Hawaii state or county page I read names a vendor crash-report portal such as LexisNexis BuyCrash, CARFAX Crashdocs or PoliceReports.US. The Hawaiʻi County page lists no online option. HPD accepts requests by email but has no online portal for report copies; its frontlinepss.com system is only for filing certain non-emergency reports, not collisions. The Maui GovQA portal returned 403, so its request steps are unverified.

HPD gives no standard turnaround for report copies, only that reports over 10 pages may not be available the same day and that reports are released once the case is closed. No official source gives a typical delay between a crash and the report becoming available in any county.

The Kauaʻi Records window hours on the official page are a temporary notice tied to a staffing shortage ('until further notice'), so current hours may differ. The Maui Records Section page says it is closed on Fridays 'until further notice'.

facts.claim: Iowa Code section 321.266(3) places a crash-reporting duty on every law enforcement officer who investigates a crash that must be reported under subsections 1 and 2.
facts.quote: Every law enforcement officer who, in the regular course of duty, investigates a motor vehicle accident of which report must be made as required in subsections 1 and 2

facts.claim: Under Iowa Code section 321.266(3), the investigating officer must forward a written report of the crash to the department within twenty-four hours after completing the investigation.
facts.quote: shall, within twenty-four hours after completing such investigation, forward a written report of such accident to the department.

facts.claim: Iowa Code section 321.271 makes all written crash reports filed by law enforcement officers under section 321.266 available to any party to the accident, the party's insurance company or its agent, the party's attorney, the federal motor carrier safety administration, or the attorney general.
facts.quote: All written reports filed by a law enforcement officer as required under section 321.266 shall be made available to any party to an accident, the party’s insurance company or its agent, the party’s attorney, the federal motor carrier safety administration, or the attorney general

facts.claim: Iowa Code section 321.271 sets the fee for a copy of an officer's crash report requested from the department at four dollars for each copy, on written request.
facts.quote: on written request to the department and the payment of a fee of four dollars for each copy

facts.claim: The attorney general and the federal motor carrier safety administration do not have to pay a fee for a copy of an officer's crash report.
facts.quote: However, the attorney general and the federal motor carrier safety administration shall not be required by the department or the law enforcement agency to pay a fee for a copy of a report filed by a law enforcement or investigating officer.

facts.claim: Under Iowa Code section 321.271, when the investigating officer's own law enforcement agency keeps a copy of a crash report filed with the department, a copy must be made available to any party to the accident.
facts.quote: If a copy of an investigating officer’s report of a motor vehicle accident filed with the department is retained by the law enforcement agency of the officer who filed the report, a copy shall be made available to any party to the accident

facts.claim: A copy kept by the investigating agency is provided on written request and payment of a fee, and other law enforcement agencies and the attorney general are among those who may request it.
facts.quote: other law enforcement agencies, or the attorney general, on written request and the payment of a fee.

facts.claim: A driver-filed crash report is for the department's confidential use, but on request of a person involved, that person's insurer or its agent, or that person's attorney, the department must disclose the identity and address of the other persons involved.
facts.quote: shall be for the confidential use of the department, except that upon the request of any person involved in the accident, the person’s insurance company or its agent, or the attorney for such person, the department shall disclose the identity and address of other persons involved in the accident

facts.claim: On written request, the department must give the person who filed a driver's crash report a copy of that person's own report.
facts.quote: The department, upon written request of the person making the report, shall provide the person with a copy of that person’s report.

facts.claim: The Iowa DOT charges $4 for a copy of an officer's crash report.
facts.quote: A copy of the officer's report of an accident costs $4.

facts.claim: The Iowa DOT says state law allows officer crash reports to be given only to persons involved in the accident, their attorney, insurance companies or insurance agents.
facts.quote: State law allows these reports to be given only to persons involved in the accident, their attorney, insurance companies or insurance agents.

facts.claim: To get an officer's crash report from the Iowa DOT, you complete the Request for Copy of Investigating Officer's Report of an Accident form, print and sign it, and mail it with $4 to the address shown on the DOT page.
facts.quote: Complete the Request for Copy of Investigating Officer’s Report of an Accident Form Print and sign the form. Mail the completed form and $4 to the address at the bottom of this page.

facts.claim: The address at the bottom of the Iowa DOT records page is Bureau of Enforcement, Audits, & Records, Iowa Department of Transportation, P.O. Box 9204, Des Moines, IA 50306-9204.
facts.quote: Bureau of Enforcement, Audits, & Records Iowa Department of Transportation P.O. Box 9204 Des Moines, IA 50306-9204

facts.claim: The Iowa DOT keeps the $4 processing fee even if no crash report exists for the information submitted.
facts.quote: The $4 processing fee will be retained even if no crash report exists for the information submitted.

facts.claim: The Iowa DOT charges $4 for a limited information accident report.
facts.quote: A $4 fee is required to obtain a limited information accident report.

facts.claim: For limited information about a crash, such as date, time, specific location and immediate facts and circumstances, the Iowa DOT says to contact the address on its page or e-mail Accident.Support@iowadot.us.
facts.quote: For limited information regarding an accident, such as date, time, specific location, and immediate facts and circumstances, contact the address at the bottom of this page, or e-mail: Accident.Support@iowadot.us

facts.claim: To get a copy of a driver's accident report you completed within the last 10 years, the Iowa DOT says to follow its instructions for ordering other documents related to a driver's license record or your accident report.
facts.quote: To obtain a copy of an accident report that you completed within the last 10 years, follow the instructions above for "Ordering other documents related to an Iowa driver's license record or your accident report."

facts.claim: To get your personal accident report from the Iowa DOT, you complete the Privacy Act Agreement For Request of Motor Vehicle Records form.
facts.quote: Get a copy of a traffic ticket(s), previously issued driver's license applications showing license history in Iowa, your personal accident report, or any other document related to your Iowa driver's license record. Complete the Privacy Act Agreement For Request of Motor Vehicle Records form

facts.claim: In its section for ordering other documents, including your own accident report, the Iowa DOT asks for a legible photocopy of your driver's license or non-driver ID card and charges 50 cents per document.
facts.quote: Make a legible photocopy of your driver's license or non-driver ID card. Payment must be included with the request. The cost is 50 cents per document.

facts.claim: In that section, the Iowa DOT says to pay by check made payable to "Treasurer, State of Iowa" mailed to the address on its page.
facts.quote: a check for the appropriate amount made payable to "Treasurer, State of Iowa" to the address at the bottom of this page.

facts.claim: The Iowa DOT says a driver in an Iowa crash causing death, personal injury, or total property damage of $1,500 or more should contact the nearest law enforcement agency to have it investigated.
facts.quote: The driver involved in an accident occurring anywhere within the State of Iowa causing death, personal injury, or total property damage of $1,500 or more should contact the nearest law enforcement agency to have the accident investigated.

facts.claim: If no law enforcement agency investigates, the crash must be reported on an Iowa Accident Report form, and failing to return it within 72 hours of the crash may result in suspension of driving privileges.
facts.quote: If a law enforcement agency does not investigate the accident, it must be reported on an Iowa Accident Report form. Failure to return an accident report form within 72 hours from the time of the accident may result in suspension of your driving privileges.

facts.claim: The Iowa DOT warns that failing to complete the insurance coverage information on the driver's report may result in suspension of driving and registration privileges.
facts.quote: Failure to complete insurance coverage information may result in the suspension of your driving and registration privileges.

facts.claim: The Iowa DOT page says to sign the driver's report and mail pages 3 and 4 to the address at the bottom of that page.
facts.quote: After signing the completed accident report form, mail pages 3 and 4 (you do not need to mail the instruction sheet nor accident code sheet) to the address at the bottom of this page.

facts.claim: Iowa Code section 321.266 requires the driver in a crash causing injury, death, or apparent total property damage of $1,500 or more to send a written report to the department within seventy-two hours.
facts.quote: The driver of a vehicle involved in an accident resulting in injury to or death of any person, or total property damage to an apparent extent of one thousand five hundred dollars or more shall, within seventy-two hours after the accident, forward a written report of the accident to the department.

facts.claim: The driver's report is not required when a law enforcement agency investigates the crash.
facts.quote: However, such report is not required when the accident is investigated by a law enforcement agency.

facts.claim: The driver's crash report form is Iowa DOT form 433002, Iowa Accident Report.
facts.quote: 433002. Iowa Accident Report

facts.claim: Form 433002 says Iowa crashes causing death, personal injury, or total property damage of $1,500.00 or more must be reported on it, and asks drivers to return it as soon as estimates can be obtained.
facts.quote: An accident occurring anywhere within the State of Iowa causing death, personal injury, or total property damage of $1,500.00 or more must be reported on this accident report form. Please return form to our office as soon as estimates can be obtained.

facts.claim: Form 433002 tells drivers to sign the report and return it to Iowa Department of Transportation, Driver & Identification Services, 6310 SE Convenience Boulevard, Ankeny, IA 50021.
facts.quote: Sign the accident report and tear at the perforated line and return accident report to: Iowa Department of Transportation Driver & Identification Services 6310 SE Convenience Boulevard Ankeny, IA 50021

facts.claim: The Iowa DOT form for requesting an officer's crash report is form 431007.
facts.quote: 431007. Request for Copy of Investigating Officers Report of an Accident

facts.claim: The header of Form 431007 lists PO Box 9278, Des Moines, IA 50306-9278, phone 515-244-1052 and e-mail privacy.agreements@iowadot.us.
facts.quote: PO Box 9278 | Des Moines, IA 50306-9278 PH: 515-244-1052 E-mail: privacy.agreements@iowadot.us

facts.claim: Form 431007 says it must be completed with all required attachments before the Iowa DOT will consider a request for crash reports.
facts.quote: This Agreement must be completed with all required attachments before the Iowa Department of will consider a request for crash reports.

facts.claim: A requestor using Form 431007 must attach a legible photocopy of a driver's license or non-driver identification card.
facts.quote: Requestor must attach a legible photocopy of his or her driver's license or non-driver identification card.

facts.claim: Form 431007 asks for payment of $4.00 for each crash report requested.
facts.quote: Submit payment of $4.00 for each crash report requested.

facts.claim: Part B of Form 431007 asks for a party's name, address and driver license or non-driver ID number, plus the date, approximate location and county of the crash.
facts.quote: PART B. INFORMATION REQUESTED Name of Party to the Accident (Last) (First) (Middle Initial) Address Driver License or Non-Driver ID Number City State Zip Code Date of Crash Approximate Location of Crash County of Crash

facts.claim: Form 431007 says only requestors who meet the criteria in its Part A can get the information from the Iowa DOT.
facts.quote: Only Requestors who meet the criteria outlined in Part A are eligible to obtain such information from the Iowa Department of Transportation.

facts.claim: On Form 431007 a party to the accident can be a driver, owner or lessee, a passenger or pedestrian, a parent or guardian who attaches custody, guardianship or power-of-attorney documents, or an owner of damaged property.
facts.quote: I am a party to the accident (If you check this box, please identify your status, below): Driver, Owner, or Lessee Passenger or Pedestrian Parent or Guardian (attach documents verifying custody, guardianship, or power of attorney) Owner of damaged property

facts.claim: Form 431007 requires an insurance company representative to attach proof of status with the insurer, and an attorney for a party to attach a copy of the judicial branch's website showing good standing.
facts.quote: I represent the insurance company whose insured was a party to the accident (attach proof of your status with the insurance company) I am an attorney for a party to this accident (attach a copy of the judicial branch’s website showing you to be in good standing)

facts.claim: Form 431007 also covers a law enforcement officer from an agency other than the investigating one, who includes the $4.00 fee and attaches law enforcement ID.
facts.quote: I am a law enforcement officer with an agency other than the one that investigated the accident, and I have included the $4.00 fee (attach your law enforcement ID)

facts.claim: On Form 431007 the requestor certifies, under penalty of perjury, that all information in Parts A, B, C and any attachments is true and correct.
facts.quote: I certify under penalty of perjury and pursuant to the laws of the State of Iowa that all information completed and contained in Parts A, B, C, and any attachments hereto, is true and correct.

facts.claim: The Iowa State Patrol page on the Department of Public Safety website offers access to accident information and reports produced by the Iowa State Patrol for the entire state.
facts.quote: Access accident related information and reports produced by the Iowa State Patrol for the entire state.

facts.claim: The Iowa State Patrol Crash Reports website gives the public access to crash reports produced by the Iowa State Patrol for the entire state.
facts.quote: This site is intended to give the public access to Crash reports that are produced by the Iowa State Patrol for the entire state.

facts.claim: Viewing a report posted on the Iowa State Patrol Crash Reports website is free.
facts.quote: There is no charge to view any report that is posted on this site.

facts.claim: Reports stay on the Iowa State Patrol Crash Reports website for only 15 days, after which they are available at the Iowa State Patrol District Office during normal business hours.
facts.quote: Currently, reports will only be available on this site for 15 days. Any reports older than 15 days will be available at the Iowa State Patrol District Office, during normal business hours, while the department researches an archive feature.

facts.claim: The Iowa State Patrol Crash Reports website can be searched by date, type, county or any combination.
facts.quote: Crash and incident reports may be searched by date, type, county or any combination.

facts.claim: If more information is needed, the online Iowa State Patrol reports say which State Patrol District Office to contact during normal business hours.
facts.quote: If further information is needed, the online reports will advise which Iowa State Patrol District Office to contact, during normal business hours.

facts.claim: Hard copies of the site's information can be inspected at each Iowa State Patrol district office, for that district only, during normal business hours.
facts.quote: Hard copies of this information will be available for inspection at each district office. Information will be relevant to that district only and can be viewed during normal business hours.

facts.claim: The Iowa State Patrol crash reports site does not provide information such as dates of birth, home phone numbers or social security numbers.
facts.quote: As such, information such as dates of birth, home phone numbers, social security numbers etc. will not be provided.

facts.claim: On the Iowa State Patrol site, the minimal report is called in by the trooper to the State Patrol Communications Center shortly after a major incident or crash.
facts.quote: The minimal report is called into the State Patrol Communications Center by the Trooper shortly after a major incident or Crash has occurred.

facts.claim: The Iowa State Patrol's full report has much more detail than the minimal report and can include a crash diagram.
facts.quote: The full report has much more detail and can include a diagram in the Crash report.

facts.claim: Under Iowa Code section 321.271(3), the date, time, specific location, and immediate facts and circumstances surrounding a crime or incident are not kept confidential under that section, except in unusual circumstances where disclosure would plainly and seriously jeopardize an investigation or pose a clear and present danger to an individual's safety.
facts.quote: shall not be kept confidential under this section, except in those unusual circumstances where disclosure would plainly and seriously jeopardize an investigation or pose a clear and present danger to the safety of an individual.

facts.claim: Under Iowa Code section 321.266(1), a driver in a crash causing injury or death must immediately notify the county sheriff, the nearest State Patrol office, or another peace officer, by the quickest means of communication.
facts.quote: involved in an accident resulting in injury to or death of any person shall immediately by the quickest means of communication give notice of such accident to the sheriff of the county in which said accident occurred, or the nearest office of the state patrol, or to any other peace officer

facts.claim: Under Iowa Code section 321.271(1), a driver's written crash report filed with the department cannot be admitted or used as evidence in any civil or criminal case arising out of the facts it is based on.
facts.quote: The written report filed with the department shall not be admissible in or used in evidence in any civil or criminal case arising out of the facts on which the report is based.

facts.claim: Under Iowa Code section 321.271(1), along with the other involved persons' identities and addresses, the department may disclose the names of their liability insurance companies.
facts.quote: the department shall disclose the identity and address of other persons involved in the accident and may disclose the name of the insurance companies with whom the other persons have liability insurance.

facts.claim: Form 431007 must be completed and approved before a requestor can get personal information from the Iowa DOT.
facts.quote: This Privacy Act Agreement for Request for Copy of Investigating Officer's Crash Report must be completed and approved before a Requestor can obtain personal information from the Iowa Department of Transportation.

facts.claim: Part C of Form 431007 must be completed. The requestor signs the agreement and initials each certification item.
facts.quote: PART C. CERTIFICATION (This Section Must Be Completed) By signing this Privacy Act Agreement Request for Motor Vehicle Records and initialing each item below, I, the Requestor, certify that:

facts.claim: Form 433002 says drivers should also report the crash directly to their insurance company, and that failing to do so may jeopardize their automobile liability insurance.
facts.quote: IMPORTANT: This accident should also be reported directly to your insurance company. Failure to report may jeopardize your automobile liability insurance.

facts.claim: Part A of Form 431069 (Privacy Act Agreement for Request of Motor Vehicle Records) has a checkbox for requesting a copy of your own record.
facts.quote: I am requesting a copy of my own record.

facts.claim: The Iowa State Patrol crash reports FAQ says Iowa Code chapter 22 requires law enforcement to provide the date, time, specific location, and immediate facts and circumstances surrounding a crime or incident.
facts.quote: Chapter 22 of the Iowa Code requires law enforcement to provide the date, time, specific location, and immediate facts and circumstances surrounding a crime or incident.

facts.claim: The Iowa State Patrol crash reports FAQ says no information will be disclosed that would plainly and seriously jeopardize an investigation or pose a clear and present danger to an individual's safety.
facts.quote: Additionally, no information will be disclosed that would plainly and seriously jeopardize an investigation or pose a clear and present danger to the safety of an individual.

gaps.reason: The live iowadot.gov pages, including the records and accident reports page and the PDF forms on iowadot.gov, returned Cloudflare HTTP 403 to every automated fetch, including a real browser. All Iowa DOT web-page facts come from the Internet Archive capture of the official page dated 2026-06-10, the newest capture listed. Check them against the live page before publishing.

The official sources give conflicting mailing addresses. The DOT web page says to mail officer-report requests and driver reports to Bureau of Enforcement, Audits, & Records, P.O. Box 9204, Des Moines, IA 50306-9204. The header of Form 431007 lists PO Box 9278, Des Moines, IA 50306-9278 and privacy.agreements@iowadot.us. Form 433002 (10-23) says to return driver reports to Driver & Identification Services, 6310 SE Convenience Boulevard, Ankeny, IA 50021. Because the live DOT page could not be read, I could not confirm which address is current.

No official source found says how soon after a crash a copy is usually available from the Iowa DOT or a local agency. The statute only requires the officer to send the report to the department within 24 hours after finishing the investigation. The State Patrol site says reports stay online for 15 days but not how soon they are posted.

No official online ordering or payment option for Iowa DOT copies of officer crash reports was found. The DOT page says to print, sign and mail the form. The GovOS page for Form 431007 offered only a print button, but that is my observation, not an official statement. Free online viewing exists only for State Patrol reports, on accidentreports.iowa.gov.

No card or convenience fee is stated anywhere, since no online payment was found. The DOT's officer-report instructions do not say how to pay the $4; only the separate 'other documents' section says to pay by check to 'Treasurer, State of Iowa'. Iowa Code 321.271 lets a local agency charge a fee for its retained copy but does not set the amount, so local fees vary (Davenport lists $15.00 online).

No official source found confirms that the Iowa DOT accepts walk-in requests for copies of officer crash reports. In-person access found only for State Patrol material: hard copies for inspection at district offices, and Patrol reports older than 15 days held there.

No official page says in one sentence that the DOT's records include reports written by city police and county sheriffs. That conclusion rests on Iowa Code 321.266(3), which requires every investigating law enforcement officer to send reports to the department, and 321.271(2), which makes all officer-filed reports available on written request to the department. The State Patrol website holds only reports produced by the State Patrol.

Only one local agency (Davenport Police) was checked, on the City of Davenport's own site, which is local government rather than state. The web-search budget for this run ran out, so the processes and fees of other city police departments and county sheriffs (for example Des Moines, Cedar Rapids, Polk County) and any Iowa Administrative Code rules were not checked.

None of the official sources read mention a crash report number. Form 431007 asks for party and crash details (name, address, license or ID number, crash date, approximate location, county) but has no report-number field. Whether a report number speeds up a request could not be confirmed.

The GovOS page for Form 433002 shows a 'Submit & Sign' button, but no official text says drivers may file the report online instead of mailing it. The DOT page says to mail pages 3 and 4. Online filing could not be confirmed.

facts.claim: The Idaho Office of Highway Safety (OHS), part of the Idaho Transportation Department, maintains the statewide collision database.
facts.quote: The Idaho Office of Highway Safety (OHS) maintains the statewide collision database, publishes crash statistics, and administers federal highway safety grant funds.

facts.claim: Police who respond to crashes on Idaho roads file the crash information with OHS.
facts.quote: Thousands of crashes happen each year on Idaho roads. Police responding to these crashes file the information with OHS for record keeping and statistical analysis.

facts.claim: Once a crash report is completed, the responding law enforcement agency sends it to OHS electronically, where a crash analyst reviews it.
facts.quote: Once a crash report is completed, the responding law enforcement agency transmits the information to OHS electronically where the report is reviewed by a crash analyst.

facts.claim: A Vehicle Crash Report (VCR) is completed for every motor-vehicle crash on public property that causes more than $1500 in property damage to any one person, or any injury or death.
facts.quote: A Vehicle Crash Report (VCR) is filled out for every crash that involves a motor vehicle, occurs on public property and results in more than $1500 property damage ($750 before January 1, 2006) for any one person involved in the crash or results in an injury or fatality to any person involved.

facts.claim: ITD takes crash report requests online through its Crash Reports portal, and the charge is $7.00 plus a transaction fee.
facts.quote: Submit a crash report request online. The charge is $7.00 plus transaction fee.

facts.claim: Through the ITD Crash Reports portal, a PDF of one report costs $7.00 plus transaction fees through Idaho.gov.
facts.quote: The price for a PDF of one report is $7.00 + transaction fees through Idaho.gov.

facts.claim: ITD says that under Idaho Code, OHS charges $7 for each copy of a crash report, if applicable.
facts.quote: In accordance with Idaho Code, the Office of Highway Safety (OHS) charges $7 for each copy of a crash report, if applicable.

facts.claim: The ITD portal cites Idaho Code 49-202 as the law that allows a charge for copies of collision records.
facts.quote: Collision records are considered public information. Idaho Code 49-202 allows for a charge for copies.

facts.claim: ITD says crash records are public information and are available to the general public.
facts.quote: Crash records are considered public information, and as such, are available to the general public.

facts.claim: ITD's Order a Crash Report page says crash reports are available to the general public for $7.00 plus a transaction fee.
facts.quote: Crash reports are available to the general public. The charge is $7.00 plus transaction fee.

facts.claim: The ITD portal searches for a report by first name, last name, city, county, the last 4 digits of a driver's license, case ID, and a date range.
facts.quote: First Name Last Name City County Driver's License (Last 4 digits) Case ID Date From Date To

facts.claim: If a report does not show up in the portal search, the portal lets you send a request to the ITD office instead.
facts.quote: Don't see your report? Send a request to our office.

facts.claim: ITD says a new report takes a few weeks to become available online and may take much longer depending on the law enforcement agency involved.
facts.quote: It will take a few weeks for a new report to become available online. It may take much longer depending on the law enforcement agency involved.

facts.claim: A report bought through the ITD portal can be downloaded for up to 7 days.
facts.quote: A purchased report may be downloaded for up to 7 days.

facts.claim: The ITD purchase covers the crash report only, because OHS does not have access to photos or other crash documents.
facts.quote: This purchase is for the crash report only. OHS does not have access to photos or additional crash documents.

facts.claim: For questions, the Office of Highway Safety lists email ohsweb@itd.idaho.gov, phone (208) 334-8000 and mailing address PO Box 7129, Boise, ID 83707.
facts.quote: Email: ohsweb@itd.idaho.gov Phone: (208) 334-8000 Address: PO Box 7129 Boise, ID 83707

facts.claim: The Idaho County Sheriff's Office no longer provides accident reports and sends requesters to the Idaho Transportation Department's crash report portal.
facts.quote: The Idaho County Sheriff’s Office will no longer be providing accident reports. Accident reports may now be obtained from the Idaho Transportation Department

facts.claim: The ITD Driver's Handbook says you must report to police any motor vehicle crash in which someone is injured or property damage is more than $1,500.
facts.quote: You must report to police any motor vehicle crash in which someone is injured or property damage is more than $1,500.

facts.claim: The handbook says that if you damage an unattended vehicle or other property, you must also notify police if the damage was more than $1,500 or someone was injured.
facts.quote: If the owner cannot be located, leave a note telling about the crash with your name and phone number. You must also notify police if the damage was more than $1,500 or someone was injured.

facts.claim: If a report doesn't show up in the search, the portal's 'Request Crash Report' form asks for the crash search details (name, city, county, last 4 digits of the driver's license, case ID and date range). It also asks for the requester's name, email and phone, with space for additional comments.
facts.quote: Request Crash Report Back to Crash Reports Search Information First Name Last Name City County Driver's License (Last 4 digits) Case ID Date From Date To Contact Information Name Email Phone Additional Comments Send Request

facts.claim: OHS can also provide statistical crash information that is not in the crash dashboard or the annual Idaho Traffic Crash reports. Other charges may apply.

gaps.reason: I could not confirm whether the Idaho State Police also releases crash reports directly, or what it charges. isp.idaho.gov, including the District pages and procedure EHP-02-06 on public records requests, refused connections from both WebFetch and the fallback fetcher, so no ISP page could be read.

The amount of the 'transaction fee' added to the $7.00 is not stated on any ITD page I read. The portal links to an Access Idaho pricing page (accessidaho.org/pricing.html), but that domain did not resolve.
The text of Idaho Code 49-202, which ITD cites as allowing the copy charge, could not be read because legislature.idaho.gov refused connections. The $7 figure comes only from ITD pages.

Idaho Code 74-124, which reportedly gives people involved in a collision, their legal representative and their insurer a right to an unaltered copy, could not be opened (legislature.idaho.gov was unreachable), so it is not used. ITD pages say crash records are available to the general public. No ITD page I read states a confidentiality period.

I found no official mail-in request form or form number for crash reports. ITD lists a PO Box (PO Box 7129, Boise, ID 83707) only as Office of Highway Safety contact information, not as a way to request reports by mail.
I found no official source that describes an in-person way to request a crash report from ITD/OHS.

The ITD pages do not say whether ID or a signed form is required. The portal's search fields (name, city, county, last 4 digits of a driver's license, case ID, date range) are the only stated inputs. The 'Send a request to our office' form also asks for the requester's name, email and phone, but I read it only through a rendered view of the app and did not cite it.

ITD says the police who respond to crashes file reports with OHS, but no official page I read says that every city police or county sheriff report can be bought in the ITD portal, or how city departments such as Boise, Meridian or Nampa release their own crash reports. Their official pages were either not crash-specific or did not load. The only local example I confirmed is the Idaho County Sheriff, which refers requesters to ITD.

No official source I read requires drivers to file their own crash report with a state agency. The ITD Driver's Handbook only requires reporting to police. Idaho Code 49-1305, the notice-of-accident statute, could not be opened because legislature.idaho.gov was unreachable.
The only official timing statement is 'a few weeks', possibly much longer depending on the agency. I found no specific number of days.

gaps.reason: None of the ISP or IDOT pages I read offers a way to request a copy of a crash report in person. Only online (E-Pay) and mail requests are described.

The fee statute (625 ILCS 5/11-416) is on ilga.gov, which refused connections from every fetch tool I tried, so I could not read its text. The $5.00, $20.00 and E-Pay service fees above come only from ISP pages.

No official source says how soon after a crash a report becomes available. ISP only says an E-Pay request may take 10 or more business days to process, and IDOT gives the 10-day deadline for agencies to submit reports to IDOT.

IDOT receives and analyses crash reports statewide, but no official page I could read says whether IDOT gives copies of individual crash reports to the public. The confidentiality provisions (625 ILCS 5/11-408 and 5/11-412) are on ilga.gov, which I could not reach.

No official page I read limits copies to involved parties. ISP says requests fall under FOIA and are released redacted, with an unredacted copy needing a subpoena or a judge's order. The statutory confidentiality text on ilga.gov could not be read.

State sources say only to contact the investigating agency. No state page describes how city police departments or county sheriffs handle requests, what they charge or how long they take. City and county websites are not state sources under these rules, so I did not use them.

No official Illinois page names a public vendor portal such as LexisNexis BuyCrash for requesting reports. IDOT lists BuyCrash only as an electronic reporting option for law enforcement agencies submitting reports to IDOT, so it is not listed as a request portal.
I could not read the driver reporting statutes (625 ILCS 5/11-401, 11-406, 11-407) on ilga.gov. The thresholds and the 10-day deadline above come from the ISP Crash Reports page.

gaps.reason: The ISP Crash Reports page gives no amount. It only says 'a nominal fee'. BuyCrash.com returned 403 and could not be read, so the current price and any convenience or card fee are unconfirmed. The governing statute (IC 9-26-9-3, formerly IC 9-29-11-1) could not be read because iga.in.gov is script-only and blocked the fetch. The $12 figure comes only from a 2014 Public Access Counselor opinion and from city police pages (Fort Wayne, West Lafayette, Shelbyville), not from a current ISP fee schedule.

No state-level official source gives how soon a report is on BuyCrash after a crash. Only local pages address timing: Fort Wayne says two to three days, and Shelbyville says officers have three working days to complete reports. These describe those agencies only.
The ISP page does not list the search details BuyCrash needs, and BuyCrash.com could not be read. The required details listed come only from city pages (Fort Wayne, Stilesville, West Lafayette).

No current official page states any restriction to involved parties or any confidentiality period. The only official statement found is a 2014 Public Access Counselor opinion saying accident reports are public records. The current statute could not be read on iga.in.gov to confirm this still applies.

No official ISP mail-in form or mailing address for members of the public requesting a crash report was found. The ISP page names only BuyCrash for the public and the APRA portal for government agencies. Mail requests were confirmed only for the West Lafayette Police Department.
No in-person option at the Indiana State Police for members of the public was found on an official page. In-person pickup was confirmed only for some city agencies (West Lafayette, Shelbyville).

No current official source names a crash report form that drivers must file themselves with a state agency, or gives a filing deadline or damage threshold for one. The BMV page describes only the insurer-filed Certificate of Compliance after the BMV receives an accident report. An older BMV operator report form (SR21, 2006) turned up only as a copy on nhtsa.gov and could not be confirmed as current.

The ISP page says its repository holds 'all crash reports for the State of Indiana', but no official page confirms that every city and county agency's reports are on BuyCrash. Fort Wayne's page notes some of its reports may be unavailable there. The officer-investigation damage threshold could not be verified: the Indiana Criminal Justice Institute page says $1,000, a non-official copy of the code suggests $2,500 after a 2024 amendment, and iga.in.gov could not be read to settle it.

gaps.reason: KDOT's own crash-records and open records pages (ksdot.gov/about/contact/open-records, ksdot.gov/bureaus/offchiefcoun/openrecords.asp, ksdot.gov/bureaus/burTrafficSaf/citizenservices.asp) returned HTTP 403 to every fetch tool. I could not confirm whether KDOT releases copies of individual crash reports to the public, or its process or fee. KDOT is confirmed only as the statewide repository of crash data.

The KHP GovQA Records Portal returned HTTP 403, so its form fields, fees and any card or convenience fee could not be read. The KHP Records page (updated January 2026) links GovQA as 'Order an Official Report', while the KHP contact page and the kansas.gov crash log pages still link https://www.kansas.gov/accident-reports/. Both were live when checked, and no official page says which one KHP prefers.

The kansas.gov online system says the total reflects Kansas.gov electronic payment processor pricing and includes portal funding, but it does not state the online amount or a separate convenience fee. Only the base $5.00 report and $2.00 witness statement fees are confirmed. No statute or rule setting the $5 fee was found.

No official source gives a typical number of days before a KHP crash report is available; KHP says only that there is a delay. K.S.A. 8-1611 sets a 10-day deadline for officers to forward reports to KDOT, which is not the same as when the public can get a copy.

The mailing address conflicts between official pages. The kansas.gov crash log, FAQ and accident report contact pages list KHP Records at 708 SW Jackson, Topeka, KS 66603. The current kansashighwaypatrol.gov pages and the July 2025 open records brochure list General Headquarters at 122 SW 7th Street, Topeka, KS 66603. Confirm by phone at (785) 296-6800 before mailing. No official named mail-in request form was found.

No official statewide page says outright that crashes handled by a city police department or county sheriff must be requested from that agency. The KHP system covers reports by KHP personnel, and Wichita PD is one official local example of an agency giving out its own reports. Local fees and processes vary and were not researched agency by agency. The Wichita 'How To Obtain Copy Of Certain Reports' PDF could not be parsed.

No current requirement was found for drivers to file their own written crash report with a state agency. K.S.A. 8-1606 is shown as repealed in 2011, and K.S.A. 8-1607 lets the Division of Vehicles require a written report only when it deems one necessary. No current driver report form name or deadline was found on an official site.

The official pages disagree on Kansas Turnpike crashes in the preliminary crash log. The kansas.gov crash log FAQ says Turnpike crashes are not included, while the KHP Records page says they appear under 'Kansas Turnpike Authority' in the county dropdown. No Kansas Turnpike Authority crash report request page was found.

facts.quote: You may also send a written request to the Official Custodian of Records at KSP for a copy of the report via U.S. mail, e-mail, facsimile, or hand-delivery, as explained above.

facts.claim: KSP gives the mailing address for its Records Custodian as the Public Records Branch, 1266 Louisville Road, Frankfort, KY 40601, phone 502-782-1873.
facts.quote: Kentucky State Police Public Records Branch Attn: Records Custodian 1266 Louisville Road Frankfort, KY 40601 502-782-1873

facts.claim: KSP's fax number for open records requests is 855-592-7656, sent to the attention of the Official Custodian of Records.
facts.quote: The fax number is 855-592-7656. Send to the attention of Official Custodian of Records.

facts.claim: KSP's open records page links to an online submission portal for open records requests and says to use it for an immediate response.
facts.quote: For an immediate response to your open records request please use the above hyperlink.

facts.claim: A KSP request must be written and signed, include your printed name, and describe the record specifically, for example by name, date and location.
facts.quote: To make an Open Records Request to the Kentucky State Police, you must submit a written request to the Official Custodian of Records. Sign the request, print your name, and describe the records (be specific, i.e., name, date, location) you wish to inspect or obtain copies of.

facts.claim: KSP asks requesters to include their address and phone number.
facts.quote: Please include your address and phone number. Mail, email, fax, or hand deliver your request to the Kentucky State Police Official Custodian of Records at the following address:

facts.claim: On its general open records page, KSP says it charges 10 cents per released page; the page does not give a separate accident-report fee.
facts.quote: The Kentucky State Police charges 10 cents per released page.

facts.claim: KSP's official custodian sends a letter saying how much the requester owes for records.
facts.quote: The official custodian sends a letter stating how much requesters owe for records.

facts.claim: KSP says accident reports are made available to the parties to the accident, parents or guardians of a minor party, and insurers or their written designee for insurance business purposes.
facts.quote: Accident reports shall be made available to: The parties to the accident; The parents or guardians of a minor who is party to the accident; Insurers or their written designee for insurance business purposes of any party who is the subject of the report;

facts.claim: Accident reports are also available to the parties' attorneys, and to a party to litigation who files a request with a copy of the first page of a District or Circuit Court clerk-stamped complaint naming all parties.
facts.quote: The attorneys of the parties to the accident; Any party to litigation who files with the department a request for the report and includes a copy of the first page of a District or Circuit Court clerk-stamped complaint naming all parties;

facts.claim: The KSP list also includes the Department of Workplace Standards for occupational safety and health investigations, and law enforcement agencies, within the statute's limits.
facts.quote: The Department of Workplace Standards in the Labor Cabinet if the accident report is pertinent to an occupational safety and health investigation; and A law enforcement agency, subject to the limitations in subsections (4)(b) and (7) of this section.

facts.claim: A news-gathering organization must complete a KSP-29 form confirming its status.

facts.claim: KSP says to allow 10 days for an officer to complete a crash report and for it to become available in KSP's system.
facts.quote: Please allow 10 days for the report to be completed by the officer and made available in our system.

facts.claim: The civilian report is only needed when no law enforcement officer investigated the crash.

facts.claim: If you did not save your civilian collision report, you can get a copy through an Open Records Request to the KSP Custodian of Records.

facts.claim: KSP's Civilian Collision Records Section can be reached by email at kspciviliancollision@ky.gov.
facts.quote: How do I contact the Kentucky State Police Civilian Collision Records Section? E-mail: kspciviliancollision@ky.gov

facts.quote: For questions about obtaining a collision report, call Central Records at (859) 258-3568 during regular business hours.

facts.quote: If you do not know your incident report number, you can email LMPDAccidentReport@louisvilleky.gov or call 502-574-6857 (Monday through Friday between 8 am to 4 pm).

gaps.reason: I could not confirm KSP's fee for a copy of a crash report. The fee is reportedly set by 502 KAR 15:010, and search snippets suggest separate paper and website prices, but the Kentucky Legislature site (apps.legislature.ky.gov) would not connect from any fetch tool, so I could not read the official text. The KSP Open Records page lists only a general 10-cents-per-page charge. BuyCrash's price and any convenience fee could not be checked because the site blocked access (Cloudflare 403).
I could not open BuyCrash, so I could not confirm what search details it asks for (for example report number, date, last name, badge or licence number) for Kentucky reports.

The only official statement of the self-report threshold and deadline (over $500 property damage, within 10 days) is KSP's October 2019 news release. I could not read the current text of KRS 189.635 because the Legislature site was unreachable, and search snippets indicate it was amended and renumbered in 2024 (SB 162). The current threshold and deadline need checking against the statute. I also could not open the online portal to read its current instructions.

Official sources conflict on whether local-agency reports must be requested from KSP or from the local agency. Campbell County says all requests now go directly to KSP, but Louisville Metro Police still sells its own reports. I could not read 502 KAR 15:010, which reportedly makes the originating agency responsible for providing copies, or the Attorney General guidance Campbell County cites, so there is no confirmed statewide rule. KSP data includes reports from state and local officers, but no official page I read confirms that the KSP custodian or BuyCrash will supply reports from every local agency.

I could not read the current KRS 189.635 directly (Legislature site unreachable). The duty for every agency to file reports with KSP comes from KSP's Traffic Collision Facts quoting the statute, which uses older wording ('forms supplied by the bureau').

The only official timing found is KSP's note to allow 10 days for an officer's report to appear in its system, plus the 5-business-day decision period for records requests. No official source gave times for fatal or complex crashes or for BuyCrash availability.
Campbell County's page also lists owners of damaged property as eligible requesters, but KSP's list does not include them and I could not check the statute, so I left this out.

facts.claim: The Louisiana State Police Traffic Records Unit is the central processing location for all crashes handled by the Louisiana Department of Public Safety and State Police.
facts.quote: The Traffic Records Unit is the central processing location for all accidents handled by Louisiana Department of Public Safety and State Police.

facts.claim: The Traffic Records Unit receives requests for copies of reports from the public, insurance companies and attorneys, and copies are available online and at each Troop.
facts.quote: Requests are received from the public, insurance companies, and attorneys for copies of the reports. These copies are available online at the Louisiana State Police Website and at each Troop.

facts.claim: The State Police online crash report site does not have crashes worked by city police or a local sheriff's office; only crashes worked by Louisiana State Police are found there.
facts.quote: If my crash was worked by city police or my local sheriff's office, can I find that crash here on this website? No. Only crashes worked by Louisiana State Police will be found here.

facts.claim: Under Louisiana law, the state police, any local police department and any sheriff's office must each provide copies of crash reports.
facts.quote: The state police, any local police department, or any sheriff's office shall provide copies of crash reports

facts.claim: Louisiana law says crash reports are owned by the law enforcement agency that created them, while collective data is owned by the state.
facts.quote: All data and reports shall be owned by the law enforcement agency who created the report, and all collective data shall be owned by the state of Louisiana.

facts.claim: State police or the sheriff's office investigate reportable crashes outside the corporate limits of a city or town.
facts.quote: It shall be the duty of the state police or the sheriff's office to investigate all crashes required to be reported by this Section when the crash occurs outside the corporate limits of a city or town

facts.claim: The police department of each city or town investigates reportable crashes inside its corporate limits.
facts.quote: it shall be the duty of the police department of each city or town to investigate all crashes required to be reported by this Section when the crashes occur within the corporate limits of the city or town.

facts.claim: When a crash occurs inside a city or town, the investigating agency must forward a copy of the crash report to that city or town's police department.
facts.quote: if the crash occurred within the corporate limits of a city or town, the investigating law enforcement agency shall forward a copy of the crash report to the police department of the city or town

facts.claim: Within 48 hours after completing an investigation, the investigating agency must forward a copy of the crash report or its data to the Department of Transportation and Development.
facts.quote: Within forty-eight hours after completing the investigation, the investigating law enforcement agency shall forward a copy of the crash report or data contained in the report to the Department of Transportation and Development.

facts.claim: Louisiana law allows third-party vendors under contract with a state or local agency to sell individual crash reports on the agency's behalf.
facts.quote: Third-party vendors under contract with a state or local agency shall not be prohibited from selling individual crash reports on behalf of the agency.

facts.claim: After online checkout, customers can print a PDF copy of the report they bought.
facts.quote: Once checkout is complete, customers will be able to print a PDF copy of the requested report(s).

facts.claim: The State Police request form says reports are bought online through the "LSP STATEWIDE CRASH REPORTS & PHOTOS" link on the LSP home page.
facts.quote: Purchase online crash reports by clicking on the “LSP STATEWIDE CRASH REPORTS & PHOTOS” link on the LSP home page.

facts.claim: The online portal says buyers receive an email with instructions for downloading the report.
facts.quote: You will receive an email with instructions for how to download the report.

facts.claim: The portal's FAQ says reports and photos cannot be bought on a cell phone and a desktop or laptop must be used.
facts.quote: Can I purchase a crash report using my cell phone? No, a desktop or laptop must be used to purchase any reports or photographs.

facts.claim: The online portal states that only report number requests for accidents on non-toll roads on or after August 31st 2018 can be ordered through it.
facts.quote: Only Report Number Request for accidents that occurred on non-toll roads on or after August 31st 2018 can be ordered using this service.

facts.claim: Under the State Police retention schedule, reports and photos for crashes worked by State Police are kept on the website for up to five years.
facts.quote: Per the Louisiana State Police record retention schedule, official reports and photos pertaining to crashes worked by Louisiana State Police are stored on the website as far back as five (5) years from the current date.

facts.claim: Crash reports can also be bought in person at any local State Police Troop office, and fatal crash reports can only be bought in person at a Troop office.
facts.quote: Crash reports may also be purchased in person at each local Troop Office. Fatal crashes can ONLY be purchased in person at each local Troop Office.

facts.claim: Fatal crash reports are not available through the online portal.
facts.quote: Fatal crash reports are not available online.

facts.claim: Buying a report at a Troop requires submitting the Crash Request Form.
facts.quote: You will be required to submit a Crash Request Form available on the link below when purchasing report(s) at a Troop.

facts.claim: The State Police crash request form is numbered DPSSP 3125 (01/23).
Section I of the request form asks for the date of crash, location or highway number, parish, Troop, driver's name and crash report number.
facts.quote: Date of Crash Location of Crash/Highway No. Parish Troop Name of Driver Crash Report Number

facts.claim: The vehicle and insurance details in Section II of the form are not required to get a copy of a crash report.
facts.quote: This information may be required by your insurance agent to complete your claim. It is not required to obtain a copy of a crash report.

facts.claim: To search online, you need either the crash report number or the driver's first and last name, the parish where the crash happened and the crash date.
facts.quote: You must have either the crash report number (8 or 11 digit number), OR the name of the driver involved in the crash (first and last name spelled correctly), the parish that the crash occurred in, and the crash date.

facts.claim: The portal says it can search by case number, driver license number, license plate number or involved party last name.
facts.quote: This service can now be used to perform a real time search using either a case number, driver license number, license plate number, or involved party last name.

facts.claim: A crash report bought online from State Police costs $11.50 plus $2.50 + 2.5%, payable only by Visa, MasterCard, American Express or Discover.
facts.quote: Each crash report purchased online will cost $11.50 plus $2.50 + 2.5% and can only be purchased with the following credit cards: Visa, MasterCard, American Express and Discover.

facts.claim: The online portal lists each report at $11.50, payable by Visa, MasterCard or American Express credit or debit card.
facts.quote: Each report costs $11.50, payable by Visa, MasterCard, or American Express credit or debit card.

facts.claim: The portal's FAQ says a report costs $11.50 plus a small convenience fee.
facts.quote: It costs $11.50 per report plus a small convenience fee.

facts.claim: At a State Police Troop, a report costs $16.50 by certified check, company check or money order, or $16.50 plus $2.50 + 2.5% by credit card.
facts.quote: If purchasing a crash report at a Louisiana State Police Troop, a certified check, company check, or money order of $16.50 or a credit card payment ($16.50 plus $2.50 + 2.5%) must accompany the request for all crashes.

facts.claim: Personal checks and cash are not accepted at Troop locations.
facts.quote: Personal checks and cash will not be accepted at Troop locations.

facts.claim: Crash photos bought online cost $10.00 each plus a small convenience fee.
facts.quote: It costs $10.00 per photo plus a small convenience fee.

facts.claim: State law caps the crash report fee at five dollars for a report of two pages or less and twenty dollars, including all service fees and other charges, for a longer report.
facts.quote: may charge a fee, not to exceed the sum of five dollars per report that does not exceed two pages, and not to exceed twenty dollars, inclusive of all service fees and other charges, per report that exceeds two pages.

facts.claim: If State Police set a lower charge for electronic copies, local police departments and sheriff's offices must charge that same amount for electronic copies.
facts.quote: If the state police establishes a lesser charge for electronic copies of crash reports, then a local police department or sheriff's office shall charge the amount established by state police for any electronic copies of crash reports provided pursuant to this Subsection.

facts.claim: The portal's FAQ says certified copies of a crash report can only be bought by mail.
facts.quote: Certified copies of the crash report can only be purchased by mail.

facts.claim: Crash photos can be downloaded when buying a report online, or requested from the State Police Traffic Records-Photo Lab.
facts.quote: Crash photos can now be downloaded online when purchasing a crash report online or by submitting a request to the Louisiana State Police Traffic Records-Photo Lab.

facts.claim: To get photos from the Photo Lab, complete Sections I and III of the Crash Report Request Form and send it by mail, fax or email.
facts.quote: If you wish to obtain photos from the Photo Lab, please fully complete Sections I and III of the Crash Report Request Form and submit it by mail, fax or email to the contact information listed below.

facts.claim: The Photo Lab's mailing address is Louisiana State Police, Traffic Records-Photo Lab, P.O. Box 66614 (Box A-27), Baton Rouge, LA 70896.
facts.quote: Louisiana State Police, Traffic Records-Photo Lab, P.O. Box 66614 (Box A-27), Baton Rouge, LA 70896

facts.claim: State Police ask requesters to wait fifteen (15) working days after the crash before requesting reports or photographs.
facts.quote: Please allow fifteen (15) working days after the crash before submitting a request for reports or photographs.

facts.claim: For fatal crashes, photo requests can be submitted only after a sixty (60) day wait.
facts.quote: Fatality crashes require a sixty (60) day wait period before photo requests can be submitted.

facts.claim: The request form asks requesters to allow approximately 10-15 business days after the crash before requesting a copy.
facts.quote: Please allow approximately 10-15 business days after the crash before requesting a copy of the report.

facts.claim: The online portal says reports are available 10-15 business days after the accident or once they are approved.
facts.quote: Reports will be available 10-15 business days after the accident, or once they are approved.

facts.claim: The portal says to allow approximately 15 or more business days after the crash for the report and photos to be ready.
facts.quote: Please allow approximately 15 or more business days after the crash occurs for State Police to have the crash report and photos ready.

facts.claim: State law says that, on request, crash reports must be made available to eligible persons within seven working days after the crash investigation is completed.
facts.quote: Upon request, crash reports shall be made available to the above-enumerated persons within seven working days following the completion of the crash investigation.

facts.claim: Crash reports are confidential, exempt from the public records law, and available only to the parties to the crash, parents or guardians of a minor party, and certain other listed requesters.
facts.quote: The reports required by this Section, and the information contained in the reports, shall be confidential, shall be exempt from the provisions of R.S. 44:1 et seq., and shall be made available only to the parties to the crash, parents or guardians of a minor who is a party to the crash

facts.claim: Insurers, and insurance support organizations under contract to provide claims and underwriting, of a party who is the subject of the report may also get it.
facts.quote: and insurers, or an insurance support organization under contract to provide claims and underwriting, of any party which is the subject of the report

facts.claim: A healthcare provider, or its agent, that treated a party who is the subject of the report may also get it.
facts.quote: to any healthcare provider, or their agent, that rendered healthcare services to any party which is the subject of the report

facts.claim: Succession representatives of the parties, attorneys for the parties or succession representatives, and news-gathering organizations asking about a specific crash may also get the report.
facts.quote: to the succession representatives of those parties or the attorneys of the parties or succession representatives; or to a news-gathering organization that requests documents related to a specific crash.

facts.claim: Louisiana's crash reporting duties apply to a driver in a crash that causes injury, death, or property damage over five hundred dollars.
facts.quote: The driver of a vehicle involved in a crash resulting in injury to or death of any person or property damage in excess of five hundred dollars shall:

facts.claim: Such a driver must immediately notify the local police department if the crash is inside an incorporated city or town, or the nearest sheriff's office or state police station if it is outside one.
facts.quote: Immediately give notice of the crash to the local police department if the crash occurs within an incorporated city or town or, if the crash occurs outside of an incorporated city or town, to the nearest sheriff's office or state police station.

facts.claim: In an area under an evacuation order or a declared state of emergency, the driver has seventy-two hours after the crash to give the required notice and information.
facts.quote: If the crash occurs in a geographical area under order of evacuation by a competent authority or is under a declared state of emergency, the driver shall comply with the provisions of Paragraphs (1) and (2) of this Subsection within seventy-two hours after the occurrence of the crash.

gaps.reason: Three sources could not be read live. legis.la.gov refused or timed out every connection, and crashreports.dps.la.gov returned a Cloudflare 403. Statute and portal facts therefore come from Internet Archive captures of those official pages: R.S. 32:398 (16 Jul 2026), R.S. 32:871 (17 Jan 2026), portal home (5 Oct 2026) and portal FAQ (24 Feb 2025). Check them against the live pages before publishing.

Official sources disagree on the online fee and accepted cards. The LSP Traffic Records page and form say $11.50 plus $2.50 + 2.5%, with Visa, MasterCard, American Express and Discover. The portal home page says $11.50 payable by Visa, MasterCard or American Express. The portal FAQ says $11.50 plus a small convenience fee. The exact amount charged at checkout could not be confirmed.

Official sources give different waiting times: 15 working days (LSP page), about 10-15 business days (form and portal), about 15 or more business days (portal FAQ), and the statute's seven working days after the investigation is completed. No single official figure could be confirmed.

The portal FAQ says certified copies can only be bought by mail, but no official page found gives the mailing address, fee or form for a certified-copy request by mail. Only the Photo Lab's mail address, used for photo requests, was confirmed.

No official source found requires a driver to file a written crash report with a state agency. R.S. 32:398(A) requires only immediate notice to the local police, sheriff or state police. R.S. 32:871 makes a written claim report to the commissioner optional ('may report'). The OMV claim form name and deadline appeared only on non-government or unverified pages, so they are not included.

Request methods, fees and portals for individual city police departments and parish sheriff's offices were not researched. State sources confirm only that those agencies provide copies of their own reports, within the statutory fee caps.

The portal limits online orders to crashes on non-toll roads on or after August 31st 2018, but no official source found explains how to get reports for toll-road crashes or for State Police crashes before that date or older than the five-year online retention period.
R.S. 32:398(I) limits access to listed requesters, but no State Police page found explains how eligibility is checked for online or Troop purchases.

facts.claim: The Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) provides copies of police crash reports filed by state or local Massachusetts police agencies and processed by the RMV.
facts.quote: A standard or certified copy of a motor vehicle police crash report filed by a state or local Massachusetts Police Agency and processed by the Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV)

facts.quote: A standard or certified copy of a motor vehicle police crash report filed by a state or local Massachusetts Police Agency and processed by the Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV)

facts.quote: can be requested by an individual involved in the crash, a Massachusetts business whose vehicle was involved in the crash, an Authorized Recipient, or a Permitted User under the Federal Driver Privacy Protection Act (DPPA).

facts.quote: Operator of vehicle Vehicle owner Occupant in vehicle Vulnerable User involved crash (formerly non-motorist) Witness to the crash Property Owner (if there was property damage due to the crash)

facts.claim: The RMV's request form describes crash report information as otherwise protected under Chapter 64 of the Acts of 2016, and a person can authorize its release to an authorized recipient.

facts.quote: To start your online request, you will need to select “Request Crash Report” in the Reports Section of the myRMV Online Service Center.

facts.claim: Mail requests are accepted only from requesters without a Massachusetts-issued credential, Authorized Recipients, or DPPA permitted users without access to the Crash Program.
facts.quote: Requests for copies of Police Crash Reports by mail will only be accepted for requestors who do not have a Massachusetts issued credential, Authorized Recipients, or DPPA permitted users without access to the Crash Program.

facts.claim: By mail, send the completed form, a copy of identification, and a money order or check payable to MassDOT to the Registry of Motor Vehicles, Crash Records, P.O. Box 55889, Boston, MA.
facts.quote: Send completed form, copy of identification, and payment (money order or check made payable to MassDOT) to: Registry of Motor Vehicles Crash Records P.O. Box 55889 Boston, MA 02205

facts.claim: The mail form is titled "Request for Copy of Police Crash Report" and is used to request either a standard or a certified copy.
facts.quote: For customers who do not have a Massachusetts issued credential, Authorized Recipients, or DPPA Permitted Users without access to the CRASH Program, complete this form to request either a standard or a certified copy of a police crash report.

facts.claim: A certified copy carries the official stamp of the Registrar of Motor Vehicles, while a standard copy does not.
facts.quote: The standard police crash report does not contain the official stamp of the Registrar of Motor Vehicles. • The certified copy of the police crash report will contain the official stamp of the Registrar of Motor Vehicles.

facts.claim: An individual requesting online must provide a driver's license or learner's permit number, first and last name, date of birth, the driver's Social Security Number, an email address, and the applicable fee.

facts.quote: Massachusetts registered Business Entities must have a Federal Identification Number (FID), last 4 digits of the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN), plate type, and registration number.

facts.claim: Mail requests must include the completed form, the fee, and a photocopy of the requester's license or state ID, and are not processed without the ID copy.

facts.quote: Date of Crash MM/DD/YYYY City/Town Where Crash Occurred Was there property damage? Yes No Person First and Last Name License # and State Plate # and State

facts.quote: Authorized recipient requests must submit a photocopy of both the person authorizing the release of the crash report’s license/state issued ID card and the authorized recipient’s license/state issued ID card.

gaps.reason: The RMV's request page lists only online and mail routes. I found no official page offering in-person crash report requests at an RMV service center.
No official page says whether myRMV adds a card or convenience fee to the $20 search fee.

No state page says whether people can also get a copy straight from the city or town police department that wrote the report, or what that costs. Some municipal police sites, such as Lowell, describe their own processes, including BuyCrash. They are not state sources, and no mass.gov page names a vendor portal, so none of this is included.

The Massachusetts State Police public records page (https://www.mass.gov/how-to/submit-a-public-records-request-to-the-massachusetts-state-police) describes general public records requests, with the first four hours free and up to $25 per hour after that. It does not mention crash reports, so it is not listed as a crash report route.

I couldn't read the statute requiring police to send crash reports to the RMV (M.G.L. c. 90 §29) or the text of c. 90 §26, because malegislature.gov refused the connection. The §26 thresholds come from the RMV's own pages and form, which cite that section.
No official source gives a typical number of days before a report appears in the RMV system. The RMV says only to wait at least 4 weeks before requesting and to allow 4 weeks for processing.

facts.claim: The Maryland Department of State Police (MDSP) provides motor vehicle crash reports kept in the State's central repository to legally entitled parties.

facts.quote: Copies of State Police investigated accident reports may be obtained either through the Central Records Division or reviewed at the installation in the area of the occurrence.

facts.claim: For an email request, MDSP says to email the completed request form and then mail a $4 check or money order to complete the submission.

facts.claim: The online form's contact text gives msp.crd@maryland.gov as the Central Records Division's email address. On the MDSP page itself the address is obfuscated.
facts.quote: Email: msp.crd@maryland.gov

facts.claim: The MSP Central Records Division's listed address is 1711 Belmont Avenue, Baltimore, MD 21244.
facts.quote: 1711 Belmont Avenue Baltimore, MD 21244
