gaps.reason: On 2026-10-09 every request to dps.mn.gov returned HTTP 404, including the homepage, and assets.dps.mn.gov returned 403. This happened with WebFetch, smart_fetch (HTTP and stealth) and curl. The DPS crash report page and the PS2503 form were therefore read from Internet Archive snapshots dated 2026-09-04 and 2026-08-30, not from the live site. Check the live page and form before publishing. The web search budget also ran out partway through, so no further official pages could be found, for example a State Patrol records page.

None of the official pages I read offered an online request portal for state crash reports. The DPS page lists only in-person, deputy registrar and mail requests. No official Minnesota page I read names a vendor portal such as BuyCrash. Some local agencies take requests online; Minneapolis is one example.

The $5 fee is confirmed by DPS, the PS2503 form and statute. No official source I read mentions a card, convenience or extra deputy-registrar fee. Accepted payment methods for in-person requests were not stated; the form mentions only checks and money orders payable to DVS.

No official state page says outright that DVS can supply reports written by city police and county sheriffs. The statute requires any investigating peace officer to report to the commissioner of public safety, and the PS2503 form asks for a 'Law enforcement case #', which suggests DVS has all agencies' reports, but this was not stated. Local fees and processes vary. Only Minneapolis was checked, and it does not charge for individual accident reports.

I could not check whether the Minnesota State Patrol releases copies of its own crash reports or sends requesters to DVS. The search budget ran out, and the State Patrol pages on dps.mn.gov were unreachable.

DPS says drivers no longer submit crash reports to DVS because section 169.09, subdivision 7 was repealed effective July 1, 2021. However, subdivisions 9, 14a and 17 of the current statute still mention reports by individuals or drivers. No official source I read explains this, so the guide should rely on the DPS statement and the repeal.
DPS says only that reports are available three weeks after the incident. No official source I read gives a processing or mailing time after the request is submitted.
The DPS page gave no office hours or phone number for the Records Unit or the Downtown Saint Paul Exam Station.

facts.claim: The Missouri State Highway Patrol's Patrol Records Division is the data repository for statewide motor vehicle crash reports.
facts.quote: The Patrol Records Division serves as a data repository of statewide motor vehicle crash reports

facts.claim: The Patrol Records Division gets crash information from law enforcement agencies across Missouri that are authorized to investigate traffic crashes, and those agencies submit it on the Missouri Uniform Accident Report.
facts.quote: Motor vehicle traffic crash information is obtained from law enforcement agencies across the state that are authorized to investigate traffic crashes and that submit crash information via the Missouri Uniform Accident Report.

facts.claim: The Patrol's Missouri Uniform Crash Report Preparation Manual says the Missouri State Highway Patrol was selected as the statewide repository for motor vehicle crash data and reports.
facts.quote: The Missouri State Highway Patrol was selected as the statewide repository for motor vehicle crash data/reports and was given the responsibility of training law enforcement officers throughout the State on completing the MOCARS crash report form.

facts.claim: The manual quotes section 43.250 RSMo, titled 'Law enforcement officers to file accident reports with patrol, when', which covers every law enforcement officer who investigates a vehicle accident resulting in injury or death, or apparent property damage of five hundred dollars or more to one person.
facts.quote: 43.250. Law enforcement officers to file accident reports with patrol, when - Every law enforcement officer who investigates a vehicle accident resulting in injury to or death of a person, or total property damage to an apparent extent of five hundred dollars or more to one person

facts.claim: Under section 43.250 RSMo as quoted in the manual, the investigating officer must forward the accident report to the superintendent of the Missouri State Highway Patrol within ten days after the investigation.
facts.quote: shall forward a report of such accident to the superintendent of the Missouri state highway patrol within ten days after his or her investigation of the accident

facts.claim: All motor vehicle crash reports the Patrol Records Division receives are archived for permanent preservation and computerized.
facts.quote: All motor vehicle crash reports received by the Patrol Records Division are archived for permanent preservation and computerized.

facts.claim: After review, data from crash reports that meet specific criteria are entered into the MoCARS database.
facts.quote: Once the crash reports are reviewed, data from reports meeting specific criteria are encoded into MoCARS.

facts.claim: Since August 1, 2024, the Missouri State Highway Patrol has handled requests for a Missouri Uniform Crash Report electronically.
facts.quote: Since August 1, 2024, requests for a Missouri Uniform Crash Report or Marine Accident Investigation Report are handled electronically.

facts.claim: You can request, receive and pay for a crash report online by credit or debit card, and checks and money orders are still accepted with a copy of the invoice.
facts.quote: You can request, receive, and pay for these documents online by credit or debit card; checks and money orders are still accepted with a copy of the invoice.

facts.claim: To request a traffic crash report, use the Patrol's Public Records Center and choose Traffic Crash Report Request; reconstruction reports, photographs and videos go through the same process.
facts.quote: Reconstruction reports, photographs and videos are covered by the same process. Use the Public Records Center and choose either Traffic Crash Report Request or Boating Crash Report Request.

facts.claim: The Patrol Records Division page says traffic crash reports, reconstruction reports and report photographs are requested through the MSHP public records portal.
facts.quote: Request traffic crash, boating crash, and reconstruction reports and report photographs through the MSHP public records portal.

facts.claim: The Patrol still accepts faxed requests, but they take longer to process.
facts.quote: Faxed requests are still received but take longer to process.

facts.claim: The Patrol's older Request a Traffic Crash Report page says copies of reports of crashes from 1997 or later can be sent to the headquarters of the troop where the crash occurred or requested from the nearest Highway Patrol headquarters.
facts.quote: Requests for report copies of crash reports, including certified copies, that occurred in 1997 or later can either be forwarded to the Highway Patrol headquarters of the troop where the motor vehicle crash occurred, or requested from the Highway Patrol headquarters nearest you.

facts.claim: The same page says requests for crashes from 1996 or earlier, certified crash reports, crash report photographs and reconstruction reports must go to the Patrol Records Division.
facts.quote: However, requests for report copies of crashes that occurred in 1996 or earlier, certified crash reports, crash report photographs or crash reconstruction reports must be forwarded to the Patrol Records Division.

facts.claim: The older Request a Traffic Crash Report page says requests to the Patrol Records Division may be mailed to Missouri State Highway Patrol, Patrol Records Division, P.O. Box 568, Jefferson City, Missouri 65102, Attention: Traffic Crash Reports.
facts.quote: Requests submitted to the Patrol Records Division may be mailed to Missouri State Highway Patrol, Patrol Records Division, P.O. Box 568, Jefferson City, Missouri 65102, Attention: Traffic Crash Reports.

facts.claim: To help locate a report, you may need to give the date of the crash, the location and the names of the people involved.
facts.quote: Crash reports can be requested from the Patrol Records Division. You may need to provide the date of the crash, the location, and the names of involved parties to help locate the report.

facts.claim: Crash report requests require identifying information such as the date, location and parties involved in the crash.
facts.quote: Requests require identifying information such as the date, location, and parties involved in the crash.

facts.claim: The Missouri State Highway Patrol charges a $6.00 fee for each basic motor vehicle crash report.
facts.quote: Currently, the Missouri State Highway Patrol charges a $6.00 fee for each basic motor vehicle crash report.

facts.claim: A copy of a Patrol-investigated traffic crash report costs $6.00.
facts.quote: Yes. The cost for a copy of a Patrol investigated traffic crash or boating crash report is $6.00.

facts.claim: Additional fees apply for reconstruction reports, photographs, certified copies, crash data retrieval information, CD copies and electronic mapping data.
facts.quote: Additional fees apply for copies of reports of reconstructed crashes, photographs, certified copies of reports, photographs, crash data retrieval (CRD) electronic information, computer disk (CD) copies and electronic mapping data.

facts.claim: Electronic requests can be paid by check, money order, or debit or credit card, and a check or money order must come with the invoice and be payable to DPS - Missouri State Highway Patrol.
facts.quote: When using the electronic request process mentioned in FAQ#1, requests may be paid either by check/money order or debit/credit card. If paying for request by check or money order, please provide invoice with payment and make payable to: DPS - Missouri State Highway Patrol

facts.claim: The Patrol accepts payment by personal check, money order, cashier's check, business check or credit card.
facts.quote: Payment is accepted by personal check, money order, cashier's check, business check, or credit card.

facts.claim: The Patrol does not accept cash payments for crash reports and returns them.
facts.quote: Cash payments are not accepted and will be returned.

facts.claim: The Patrol Records Division says fees depend on the nature of the request, including copies and reconstruction reports.
facts.quote: Fees will be determined based upon the nature of your request, including copies and reconstruction reports.

facts.claim: For a crash the Highway Patrol investigated, the Patrol says to wait 10 days from the date of the crash investigation before requesting a copy of the basic crash report.
facts.quote: To obtain a copy of a basic motor vehicle crash report, including certified copies, investigated by the Highway Patrol, wait 10 days from the date of the crash investigation then follow the link below to complete the records request form.

facts.claim: The Patrol reports a backlog of crash reports and says that even if you request after 10 days, you may not receive the report for an extended period.
facts.quote: NOTE: The Patrol is currently experiencing a backlog of crash reports. Please submit your request after 10 days; however, you may not receive your report for an extended period of time.

facts.claim: The Patrol's standard processing time for records requests is 20 to 30 business days, and archived reports and complex cases may take longer.
facts.quote: Standard processing time is 20 to 30 business days. Archived reports and complex cases may require extended processing.

facts.claim: Processing times vary with the complexity of the crash and the current workload, and a report must be reviewed and entered into MoCARS before copies can be provided.
facts.quote: Processing times vary depending on the complexity of the crash and current workload. Reports must first be reviewed and entered into MoCARS before copies can be provided.

facts.claim: Copies of crash reports are available only after the finalized Missouri Uniform Accident Report reaches the Patrol Records Division and is entered into MoCARS.
facts.quote: The availability of statistical information about motor vehicle crashes, details of a specific crash, and copies of crash reports is contingent upon the finalized Missouri Uniform Accident Report reaching the Patrol Records Division and being entered into MoCARS.

facts.claim: Highway Patrol reconstruction reports are generally available within 45 to 60 working days from the date of the crash.
facts.quote: Highway Patrol reconstruction reports are generally available within 45 to 60 working days from the date of the crash.

facts.claim: The Missouri Attorney General's Sunshine Law guide says a person involved in an incident, or whose property is involved, is generally entitled to records that might otherwise be closed, including an accident report, for purposes of investigating a civil claim or defense.
facts.quote: Generally, a person who was “involved in any incident or whose property is involved in an incident” is entitled to records that might otherwise be closed, including an accident report, “for purposes of investigation of any civil claim or defense.”

facts.claim: The guide says this also covers the person's lawyer, insurance company or close family member, citing Section 610.100.4.
facts.quote: This includes the individual’s lawyer, insurance company, or close family member. Section 610.100.4.

facts.claim: The Patrol Records Division says records requests should be submitted in writing in accordance with the Missouri Sunshine Law (Chapter 610, Missouri Revised Statutes).
facts.quote: Records requests should be submitted in writing to the Patrol Records Division in accordance with the Missouri Sunshine Law (Chapter 610, Missouri Revised Statutes).

facts.claim: The Patrol's online crash reports search shows preliminary information only on injury and fatal crashes investigated by the Missouri State Highway Patrol, and crashes investigated by other agencies are not included.
facts.quote: Information on this site is preliminary information relating to motor vehicle injury and fatal crashes investigated by the Missouri State Highway Patrol. (Crashes investigated by agencies outside the Missouri State Highway Patrol are not included.)

facts.claim: The Highway Patrol does not keep reconstruction reports prepared by local law enforcement agencies, and those must be requested from the investigating agency.
facts.quote: Local law enforcement agencies' reconstruction traffic crash reports are not maintained by the Highway Patrol and must be requested from the investigating agency.

facts.claim: The Missouri Attorney General's office notes that some towns do not have their own police departments and may be patrolled by county sheriffs, neighboring police departments or the highway patrol.
facts.quote: Some towns do not have their own police departments. They may be patrolled by county sheriffs, neighboring police departments or the highway patrol.

facts.claim: The Missouri Attorney General's website lets you look up contact information for local police and county sheriffs by city or county name.
facts.quote: To view contact information for your local police or county sheriff, enter the name of your city or county in the corresponding field below.

facts.claim: Entries in the Patrol's online crash reports search are posted automatically, stay online for 1 year and are unofficial.
facts.quote: They are posted here automatically and remain online for 1 year. This site is hosted and maintained by the Missouri State Highway Patrol and the reports are unofficial.

facts.claim: If a crash is not shown in the online search, the Patrol says to contact the local Highway Patrol troop headquarters or the Patrol Records Division at General Headquarters.
facts.quote: If you do not see the crash report you are looking for, please contact the local Highway Patrol troop headquarters (see map above) or the Patrol Records Division at General Headquarters.

facts.claim: For questions about Highway Patrol-investigated traffic crash reports, you can call the appropriate troop headquarters or the Patrol Records Division at (573) 526-6113, ext. 1702.
facts.quote: If you have questions regarding requests for Highway Patrol investigated traffic crash reports, you may telephone the appropriate troop headquarters or the Patrol Records Division at (573) 526-6113, ext. 1702.

facts.claim: The Patrol Records Division, not the Custodian of Records, handles requests for accident reports, reconstructions and accident-related photographs.
facts.quote: The Custodian of Records handles requests for departmental records apart from accident reports, reconstructions and accident-related photographs, which are handled by the Patrol Records Division.

facts.claim: For crashes investigated by local police agencies, the Highway Patrol refers requests for report copies to that local agency.
facts.quote: Requests for report copies relating to crashes investigated by local police agencies are referred to the local agency.

facts.claim: In most cases the Highway Patrol does not work crashes inside city limits unless the local police department asks it to.
facts.quote: In most cases, the Patrol does not work traffic crashes that occur within the city limits unless asked to do so by the local police department.

facts.claim: Crashes investigated by city or county officers are still filed with the Highway Patrol but do not appear in the Patrol's online crash search.
facts.quote: Crashes investigated and reported by city or county law enforcement officers are still filed with the Patrol but do not appear on this site.

facts.claim: The Patrol investigates thousands of non-injury crashes each year, but those crashes do not appear in its online crash search.
facts.quote: The Missouri State Highway Patrol investigates thousands of non-injury motor vehicle crashes each year. However, radio crash reports on these types of crashes are not made because of the strain they would cause on various computer systems. Consequently, they do not appear on this site.

facts.claim: Anyone involved in a Highway Patrol-investigated crash, or their attorney, can contact the investigating officer's troop headquarters to question any part of the report.
facts.quote: Any party involved in the crash, or their attorney, can contact the Highway Patrol troop headquarters of the officer investigating the crash to question any part of the report.

facts.claim: The online crash entries come from the trooper's preliminary radio report, and the information may change once the official report is completed.
facts.quote: After the accident investigation and the official report have been completed, information obtained may require the "unofficial" report to be changed (as reported in the radio report).

facts.claim: Under Section 610.100.4 RSMo, as reprinted in the Attorney General's Sunshine Law booklet, a person involved in an incident (or whose property was involved), or their attorney or insurer, can get a complete, unaltered and unedited incident report by written request.
facts.quote: his or her attorney or insurer, involved in an incident or whose property is involved in an incident, upon written request, may obtain a complete unaltered and unedited incident report concerning the incident

facts.claim: The statute's family route is narrower than 'close family member': a parent or legal guardian can request for a minor, and a family member within the first degree of consanguinity can request only if the involved person is deceased or incompetent.
facts.quote: Any individual, legal guardian or parent of such person if he or she is a minor, his or her family member within the first degree of consanguinity if such individual is deceased or incompetent

facts.claim: After such a written request under Section 610.100.4, the agency must provide the material within thirty days or file a motion asking the circuit court to keep it closed.
facts.quote: Within thirty days of such request, the agency shall provide the requested material or file a motion pursuant to this subsection with the circuit court having jurisdiction over the law enforcement agency

facts.claim: Under Section 610.100.2 RSMo, as reprinted in the AG booklet, every state, county and municipal law enforcement agency must keep records of incidents reported to it, and all incident reports and arrest reports are open records.
facts.quote: Each law enforcement agency of this state, of any county, and of any municipality shall maintain records of all incidents reported to the agency, investigations and arrests made by such law enforcement agency. All incident reports and arrest reports shall be open records.

facts.claim: Missouri's Sunshine Law requires a custodian of records to respond to a records request no later than three business days after receiving it. The response can be the records, or a detailed explanation of the delay and the earliest date the record will be available.
facts.quote: The Sunshine Law requires a custodian of records to respond to a records request as soon as possible but no later than three business days after receipt of the request, with the records or a detailed explanation of the cause for further delay

links.label: MSHP Contact Us (all nine troop headquarters)
links.officialEvidence: Page on the official Missouri State Highway Patrol site (statepatrol.dps.mo.gov, 'A Division of the Missouri Department of Public Safety'). The MSHP FAQ answers 'Where is my nearest troop headquarters?' with a link to this page: 'See the Contact Us page for all nine troop headquarters'. Fetched with HTTP 200, and Troops A through I are listed.

gaps.reason: Not confirmed. The Missouri Department of Revenue site (dor.mo.gov, including its forms and Driver Guide) and the Revisor of Statutes site (revisor.mo.gov) returned HTTP 403 or refused connections from this environment, and no MSHP or Attorney General page I read covers a driver's own crash report. Whether drivers must file a report with a state agency (form, deadline, thresholds) still needs checking on those official sites.

No official page I could read gives a card or convenience fee for online payment, the dollar amounts of the additional fees (certified copies, photographs, reconstruction reports, crash data retrieval, CDs, mapping data), or the statute or rule that sets the $6.00 fee. The Public Records Center (mshp.govqa.us) returned HTTP 403, so its payment screens could not be checked.

Not confirmed whether the Patrol redacts personal information for requesters who were not involved in the crash (for example under the federal Driver's Privacy Protection Act) or otherwise limits who can get a copy. The Public Records Center returned HTTP 403, and the older SHP-842 request form at machs.mo.gov now returns HTTP 404, so neither could be read.

No official page I could read says whether the Patrol Records Division provides copies of basic crash reports written by city police departments or county sheriffs, or that such reports must be requested from the local agency. The MSHP request and fee pages refer to Patrol-investigated reports, and only local agencies' reconstruction reports are explicitly directed to the investigating agency. The statewide repository does receive reports from all investigating agencies.

No current official page I could read describes an in-person or walk-in procedure for crash reports. The older MSHP page mentions requesting from Highway Patrol (troop) headquarters, but the newer FAQ says requests have been handled electronically since August 1, 2024.

Official pages conflict. The older MSHP page says to mail a completed form with a check or money order to P.O. Box 568, Jefferson City, Missouri 65102. The newer FAQ says requests have been handled electronically since August 1, 2024, with checks and money orders accepted alongside a copy of the invoice. The paper form (SHP-842) is no longer posted (HTTP 404), and no current mail-in form name or number was found.
The fax number for faxed requests was not found on any official page I could read.

The Public Records Center itself (https://mshp.govqa.us/WEBAPP/_rs/) could not be opened (HTTP 403 from this environment), so its form fields, account requirements and on-screen fees were not checked.

Some MSHP pages were read on the www.machs.mo.gov host because www.mshp.dps.missouri.gov, apps.mshp.dps.mo.gov and mshp.dps.mo.gov refused connections from this environment. machs.mo.gov is a State of Missouri domain serving the same MSHP pages. The shared WebSearch budget ran out early in this task, so later pages were found by following links from official pages instead of new searches.

facts.claim: The Driver Service Bureau of the Mississippi Department of Public Safety says crash reports completed by the Mississippi Highway Patrol (MHP) can be obtained in person at each district Highway Patrol station for $15.00 or online for $20.00.
facts.quote: A crash (accident) report completed by the Mississippi Highway Patrol (MHP) is available at each district Highway Patrol station in person ($15.00) or online ($20.00).

facts.claim: Mississippi Code Section 63-3-411, as reproduced in 2026 House Bill 354 on the Legislature's site, requires an officer who investigates a crash outside city limits to forward a written report to the department within six days after completing the investigation.
facts.quote: shall forward within six (6) days after completing the investigation a written report of the accident to the department if the accident occurred outside the corporate limits of a municipality

facts.claim: The same section requires city police departments to forward crash reports to the department within six days of the date of the crash.
facts.quote: Police departments shall forward such reports to the department within six (6) days of the date of the accident.

facts.claim: Under Section 63-3-411, the highway patrol or the sheriff's office must investigate reportable crashes that happen outside city limits.
facts.quote: It shall be the duty of the highway patrol or the sheriff's office to investigate all accidents required to be reported by this section when the accident occurs outside the corporate limits of a municipality

facts.claim: Under the same section, each city's police department must investigate reportable crashes that happen within its city limits.
facts.quote: it shall be the duty of the police department of each municipality to investigate all accidents required to be reported by this section when the accidents occur within the corporate limits of the municipality

facts.claim: For crash reports not written by MHP, the Driver Service Bureau tells people to contact the appropriate local law enforcement agency or obtain the report online for $20.00.
facts.quote: For all other accident reports on state highways, county roads, and city streets, please contact the appropriate local law enforcement agency or obtain a crash report online ($20.00).

facts.claim: ReportBeam's Mississippi agency list includes the Mississippi Highway Patrol alongside city police departments and county sheriff's offices, such as the Meridian Police Department and the Monroe County Sheriff's Office.
facts.quote: Meridian Police Department Mississippi Select Mississippi Highway Patrol Mississippi Select Monroe County Sheriff's Office Mississippi

facts.claim: ReportBeam's public-access state list shows 68 Mississippi agencies whose reports can be bought there.
facts.quote: Mississippi 68

facts.claim: The Department of Public Safety's Accident Investigation page says eligible people can buy a crash report online at www.reportbeam.com by choosing "Purchase a Report" under the "Public Access" tab.
facts.quote: Anyone elgible to purchase a crash report online can do so by visiting www.reportbeam.com and select “Purchase a Report” under the “Public Access” tab.

facts.claim: The state's ms.gov crash report portal warns that, once a purchased report has been emailed, it stays available for only 24 hours, so buyers should save a copy when they download it.
facts.quote: ATTENTION: Once a crash report has been purchased and emailed to the purchaser, the crash report will only be available for 24 hours. Be sure to save a copy when downloading the crash report.

facts.claim: ReportBeam emails purchased reports to the address the buyer provides.
facts.quote: Requested reports are emailed to the address provided.

facts.claim: MHP crash reports can be picked up in person at any district Highway Patrol station for $15.00.
facts.quote: A crash (accident) report completed by the Mississippi Highway Patrol (MHP) is available at each district Highway Patrol station in person ($15.00) or online ($20.00).

facts.claim: The Driver Service Bureau's fee table for MHP crash reports lists a mail-in or walk-in price of $15.00 and an online price of $20.00.
facts.quote: Crash Reports (MHP only) Mail-in or Walk-in $15.00 Online Purchase $20.00

facts.claim: Below that fee table, the page gives a regular-mail address labelled Driver Record's Division/Reinstatement, P.O. Box 1459, Canton, MS 39046.
facts.quote: Regular Mail: Driver Record's Division/Reinstatement P.O. Box 1459 Canton, MS 39046

facts.claim: ReportBeam says people without a credit card can buy the report directly from the agency.
facts.quote: You can still purchase the report by contacting the agency directly and purchasing the report directly through them.

facts.claim: If a report cannot be found on ReportBeam, it tells requesters to contact the agency that issued the report, or the reporting officer.
facts.quote: If you are still unable to find a report, contact the agency who issued the report (and/or the reporting officer) to find out what is missing.

facts.claim: The DPS Accident Investigation page says the Commissioner raised the fee for a copy of a Mississippi Uniform Crash Report from $10 to $15 per copy.
facts.quote: Effective immediately, Commissioner Santa Cruz has approved the increase in the fee for the purchase of a copy of a Mississippi Uniform Crash Report from $10 per copy to $15 per copy.

facts.claim: The same page puts the fee for buying a report online through ReportBeam at $20.00.
facts.quote: The online fee is $20.00.

facts.claim: The Driver Service Bureau's crash report page states that a $5.00 handling fee is charged.
facts.quote: A $5.00 handling fee is charged.

facts.claim: To find an MHP report on ReportBeam, a requester can enter the report number the officer provided.
facts.quote: You can quickly find a report by typing in the Report Number provided by the officer and clicking on the 'Show Search Results' button.

facts.claim: Without the report number, ReportBeam's advanced search for MHP reports needs the incident date and an involved party's name.
facts.quote: Alternatively, you can use the advanced search to find the report by entering the incident date and an involved party's name.

facts.claim: Once the report is found, ReportBeam requires a credit card or an account to buy it.
facts.quote: Once you have found the report, you will need a credit card or account to purchase the report.

facts.claim: The ms.gov crash report portal asks the requester to check a box agreeing to its eligibility disclaimer.
facts.quote: By checking, I agree with the disclaimer above.

facts.claim: On the ms.gov portal, a requester must declare that they are an involved party, a representative of an involved party's estate, an involved party's next of kin, an involved party's legal representative, or an involved party's insurer or insurer's representative.
facts.quote: I am declaring that I am one of the following: 1) A party involved in the crash; 2) A representative of an involved party’s estate; 3) An involved party’s next of kin; 4) Legal representative of an involved party; or 5) Insurer or representative of insurer of an involved party.

facts.claim: The portal states that Mississippi Code Section 63-3-417 bars anyone else from acquiring a Mississippi Uniform Crash Report.
facts.quote: Mississippi Code Ann. § 63-3-417 prohibits any other person or entity from acquiring a Mississippi Uniform Crash Report.

facts.claim: Section 63-3-417, as posted by DPS, lets the department release report information on written request from a person involved in the crash, that person's spouse or next of kin, a person against whom a claim is made because of the crash, or the representative of their estate.
facts.quote: the department may, upon written request of any person involved in an accident, the spouse or next of kin of any such person, or any person against whom a claim is made as a result of the accident or upon written request of the representative of his estate

facts.claim: Under the same section, the department may give the requester, their lawyer or their insurer's representative any information in the report except the parties' own version of the crash as set out in a written report the parties filed.
facts.quote: disclose to such requester or his legal counsel or a representative of his insurer any information contained in such report except the parties' version of the accident as set out in the written report filed by such parties

facts.claim: Fraudulently obtaining a crash report without authorization is a misdemeanor, punishable by a fine of up to $2,500.00, up to six months in county jail, or both.
facts.quote: shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and such person, upon conviction, shall be punished by a fine of not more than Two Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($2,500.00), or imprisonment in the county jail for a term of not more than six (6) months, or by both such fine and imprisonment.

facts.claim: Under Section 63-3-411(1), as reproduced in 2026 House Bill 354, the driver in a crash that causes injury, death or apparent total property damage of $500.00 or more must immediately give notice of the collision by the quickest means of communication.
facts.quote: The driver of a vehicle involved in an accident resulting in injury to or death of any person or total property damage to an apparent extent of Five Hundred Dollars ($500.00) or more shall immediately, by the quickest means of communication, give notice of the collision

facts.claim: That notice goes to the local police department if the crash is inside a city or town, and otherwise to the nearest sheriff's office or highway patrol station.
facts.quote: give notice of the collision to the local police department if the collision occurs within an incorporated municipality, or if the collision occurs outside of an incorporated municipality to the nearest sheriff

facts.claim: The department may require a driver involved in a reportable crash to file supplemental reports if it finds the original report insufficient.
facts.quote: The department may require any driver of a vehicle involved in an accident, of which report must be made as provided in this section, to file supplemental reports whenever the original report is insufficient in the opinion of the department.

facts.claim: If a vehicle owner had insurance at the time of the crash but could not show proof, they must send proof to the Driver Service Bureau Record's Division within 60 days to avoid a driver's license suspension.
facts.quote: If the owner of the vehicle had vehicle insurance at the time of the accident but was unable to show proof due to unknown circumstances, the owner must send proof to the Driver Service Bureau Record's Division within 60 days to avoid having their driver's license suspended.

facts.claim: House Bill 354 (2026 Regular Session), whose text is quoted above for Section 63-3-411, died in committee on February 3, 2026.
facts.quote: 02/03 (H) Died In Committee

facts.claim: Under Section 63-3-411(3), as reproduced in 2026 House Bill 354, an officer who investigates a crash inside city limits forwards the written report to that city's police department within six days after completing the investigation. Reports on crashes outside city limits go to the department.
facts.quote: within six (6) days after completing the investigation a written report of the accident to the department if the accident occurred outside the corporate limits of a municipality, or to the police department of the municipality if the accident occurred within the corporate limits

facts.claim: Section 63-3-415(2), brought forward unchanged in 2025 House Bill 153, requires every crash report required by Section 63-3-411 to be made on the department's statewide uniform traffic accident report form. HB 153 died, and no 2026 bill touched 63-3-415.
facts.quote: Every accident report required by Section 63-3-411 from a law enforcement officer or individual shall be made on the "statewide uniform traffic accident report" form provided by the department.

facts.claim: Section 63-3-417, as posted by DPS, makes required crash reports and supplemental reports confidential to the department, except as the section otherwise provides.
facts.quote: All required accident reports and supplemental reports shall be without prejudice to the individual so reporting and, except as otherwise provided in this section, shall be for the confidential use of the department

facts.claim: Section 63-3-417(3) lets the crash report be used to prove that a vehicle's owner and operator were uninsured in an action on an uninsured motorist claim, but only as provided in Section 13-1-124.
facts.quote: The report required by Section 63-3-411 may be used in proving uninsured status of the owner and operator of a vehicle in any action to enforce a claim under the uninsured motorist provisions of an automobile liability policy, but only as provided in Section 13-1-124.

facts.claim: Section 63-3-417(2) separately allows the department to supply vehicle-specific crash data in bulk electronic form to any person or entity for compiling vehicle history reports.
facts.quote: the department may supply vehicle-specific accident data to any person or entity, in bulk electronic form, for the purpose of compiling vehicle history reports for use by law enforcement, consumers and businesses.

facts.claim: ReportBeam delivers a purchased report as an Adobe Acrobat PDF file.
facts.quote: The report will be made available as an Adobe Acrobat PDF file.

facts.claim: If a ReportBeam report does not arrive or will not open, ReportBeam tells buyers to email support@aps.us.
facts.quote: If you did not receive the report, or have problems opening the report, please email support@aps.us for additional help.

facts.claim: ReportBeam's general FAQ suggests giving only the date and a partial address in an advanced search, and checking that a report number is correct and includes any dashes or other characters.
facts.quote: Provide the date and a partial address only. If you are having trouble locating a report by the crash report number, make sure you have received the proper number and used any dashes or other characters needed.

facts.claim: The Driver Service Bureau's crash report page gives 601-487-7028 for further information. The office is open 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, and closed on state holidays.
facts.quote: For further information, contact us at: 601-487-7028. We are open from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday. (Closed on state holidays.)

facts.claim: The Driver Service Bureau page says that, under Section 63-15-4(4), a driver's license may be suspended if no vehicle insurance is listed on the accident report.
facts.quote: According to MS state statute 63-15-4 (4), a driver's license privileges may be suspended if they do not have vehicle insurance listed on the accident report

facts.claim: An owner who obtained insurance only after the crash must also provide proof of insurance within 60 days of the crash to avoid suspension.
facts.quote: To avoid suspension, if the owner obtained insurance after the accident, they must also provide proof of insurance within 60 days of the accident.

facts.claim: An owner cited for failing to provide proof of insurance after a crash must do two things: resolve the citation with the appropriate court and give proof of insurance to the Driver Service Bureau. Otherwise the license will be suspended.
facts.quote: (1) It is the owner's responsibility to ensure that the citation is handled properly with the appropriate court. (2) The owner provides proof of insurance to the Driver Service Bureau. The driver's license will be suspended if both of these requirements are not met.

facts.claim: The Driver Service Bureau's fee table lists an Accident Suspension Reinstatement fee of $100.00.
facts.quote: Accident Suspension Reinstatement $100.00

gaps.reason: No official source says how soon a report is usually available after a crash. Section 63-3-411 only sets six-day deadlines for officers and city police to forward reports to the department, and the ms.gov 24-hour window covers downloading after purchase, not availability.

Two official DPS pages point to different online routes, and neither is dated. The Accident Investigation page sends buyers to reportbeam.com, while the Highway Patrol menu and the Driver Service Bureau link to ms.gov/dps/crash_reports. The ms.gov portal's search fields, checkout fees and list of covered agencies sit behind its disclaimer form, which I did not submit, so I could not confirm them.

The Driver Service Bureau page says "A $5.00 handling fee is charged" but not which purchases it applies to, or whether it is on top of the $20.00 online price. No card or convenience fee is stated anywhere. The DPS fee notice is undated (it names Commissioner Santa Cruz). I found no statute or rule that sets the fee.

No official mail-in request form, list of what to include, or accepted payment method was found. The Driver Service Bureau lists a $15.00 mail-in price and a P.O. box labelled "Driver Record's Division/Reinstatement", but it does not say outright that crash report requests should be mailed there.

No official statewide source gives local police or sheriff fees or request procedures. The Driver Service Bureau says to contact the local agency or buy online. ReportBeam lists 68 Mississippi agencies, so a local report may not be online if that agency is not one of them.

I quoted Section 63-3-411 from the text of 2026 House Bill 354 on the Legislature's site, which reprinted the existing section. That bill died in committee and did not change the quoted subsections, but I did not read the official codified Mississippi Code (published through LexisNexis). I also could not confirm from code text that "the department" in Chapter 3 means the Department of Public Safety, though DPS posts Section 63-3-417 as its own eligibility rule.

I found no official source requiring drivers to file their own written crash report with a state agency. Section 63-3-411 requires immediate notice to the police, sheriff or highway patrol, plus supplemental reports if the department asks. I did not check the Motor Vehicle Safety-Responsibility Law (Title 63, Chapter 15) against an official text because the session's web search budget ran out during this research.

facts.claim: In Montana's motor vehicle code (Title 61), "department" means the Montana Department of Justice, acting directly or through its authorized officers or agents.
facts.quote: "Department" means the department of justice acting directly or through its duly authorized officers or agents.

facts.claim: The Montana Highway Patrol is under the control and supervision of the Montana Department of Justice.
facts.quote: There is hereby created a "Montana highway patrol" under the control and supervision of the department of justice.

facts.claim: Under MCA 61-7-109(3), a written report of an investigated crash must be forwarded to the department within 10 days after the investigation is completed.
facts.quote: after the accident by interviewing participants or witnesses, shall within 10 days after completing the investigation forward a written report of the accident to the department.

facts.claim: MCA 61-7-109(3) applies to any law enforcement officer who, in the regular course of duty, investigates a motor vehicle crash in which a person is killed or injured or property damage exceeds $1,000.
facts.quote: A law enforcement officer who in the regular course of duty investigates a motor vehicle accident in which a person is killed or injured or in which damage to the property of a person exceeds $1,000

facts.claim: The department must tabulate all accident reports and publish statistics on the number and circumstances of traffic crashes at least annually.
facts.quote: The department shall tabulate and may analyze all accident reports and shall publish annually or at more frequent intervals statistical information based thereon as to the number and circumstances of traffic accidents.

facts.claim: Montana crash reports and supplemental information filed under the accident-reporting law are confidential and not open to general public inspection, except as the law provides.
facts.quote: Except as provided in this section, all accident reports and supplemental information filed as required by this part are confidential and not open to general public inspection.

facts.claim: Montana law lets certain people examine and copy a crash report filed by law enforcement, including witness statements, without a court order.
facts.quote: The report and supplemental information, including witness statements, filed by law enforcement personnel, as required by this part, may be examined and copied, without obtaining a court order, by:

facts.claim: A person named in the report or involved in the crash may examine and copy the law enforcement crash report.
facts.quote: (a) a person named in the report or involved in the accident;

facts.claim: That person's representative designated in writing, or that person's insurance carrier, may also examine and copy the report.
facts.quote: (b) the representative of the person referred to in subsection (2)(a), designated in writing, or the insurance carrier of that person;

facts.claim: A party to a civil action arising from the crash may examine and copy the report.
facts.quote: (c) a party to a civil action arising from the accident;

facts.claim: If the person is deceased, the executor, the administrator, or the attorney representing the executor or administrator may examine and copy the report.
facts.quote: (d) the executor, the administrator, or the attorney representing the executor or administrator if the person is deceased; or

facts.claim: The general public, including commercial entities, may examine and copy reports for research into the history of vehicles, but the department may not disclose the name, address, telephone number or other identifying information of any reporting person or accident victim.
facts.quote: (e) the general public, including commercial entities, for purposes of research into the history of vehicles, but the department may not disclose the name, address, or telephone number of, or other information allowing the identification of, any reporting person, accident victim

facts.claim: The Helena Police Department files crash reports for vehicle crashes within the City of Helena.
facts.quote: Crash reports are filed by the Helena Police Department for vehicle crashes within the City of Helena.

facts.claim: The Helena Police Department tells people to contact the Montana Highway Patrol at (406) 444-3278 for crashes outside Helena city limits or investigated by another agency.
facts.quote: For crashes occurring outside the city limits, or investigated by another agency, contact the Montana Highway Patrol at (406) 444-3278.

facts.claim: The Helena Police Department releases its crash reports only to people listed on the report, such as property owners, insurance companies, vehicle drivers and vehicle owners.
facts.quote: Crash reports may only be disseminated to the person(s) listed on the report written by the assigned police officer, including property owners, insurance companies, vehicle drivers, vehicle owners, etc.

facts.claim: Helena Police Department crash reports can be picked up in person at the Law Enforcement Center or requested by mail.
facts.quote: Reports can be picked up in person at the Law Enforcement Center, or by mail.

facts.claim: The Helena Police Department lists items that must be included with a mailed crash report request.
facts.quote: If requested through the mail, the following must be included in the request:

facts.claim: A mailed crash report request to the Helena Police Department must include a copy of the requester's driver's license.
facts.quote: a copy of their driver’s license

facts.claim: A mailed crash report request to the Helena Police Department must include a self-addressed, stamped envelope.
facts.quote: a self-addressed, stamped envelope

facts.claim: A mailed crash report request to the Helena Police Department must include a check made out to the Helena Police Department for $15.00.
facts.quote: a check made out to the Helena Police department for $15.00

facts.claim: The Helena Police Department's fee list shows $15.00 for an Accident/Crash Report.
facts.quote: Accident/Crash Report - $15.00

facts.claim: At the Helena Police Department, insurance agencies or attorneys not listed as involved parties must include an authorization to release form or assignment of rights signed by the involved party.
facts.quote: If insurance agencies or attorneys request crash reports and are not listed as an involved party on the report, requests must be accompanied by an authorization to release form or assignment of rights, signed by the party involved.

facts.claim: The Helena Police Department requires those insurer or attorney requests to be submitted on company letterhead.
facts.quote: Request must be submitted on company letterhead, to ensure identity.

facts.claim: The Helena Police Department says its crash reports can also be obtained through CrashDocs.org.
facts.quote: Crash reports can also be obtained through CrashDocs.org.

facts.claim: The Helena Police Department's Support Services Records Division will not fax crash reports.
facts.quote: The Support Services Records Division WILL NOT fax call for service or crash reports records

facts.claim: The Billings Police Department charges $30 for a crash report and accepts debit or credit cards.
facts.quote: Accident reports are also available. The fee is $30 and you can pay with a debit or credit card.

facts.claim: The Billings Police Department asks requesters to allow 10 business days after the crash for its crash report to be available.
facts.quote: Please allow 10 business days after the crash for the document to be available.

facts.claim: The Billings Police Department says citizens and their insurance companies may purchase crash reports through the service on its Order Police Reports page.
facts.quote: Citizens and their insurance companies may purchase crash reports through this service.

facts.claim: The Billings Police Department directs report questions to its Police Records Department at (406) 657-8460.
facts.quote: If you have any questions, please contact the Police Records Department at (406) 657-8460.

facts.claim: Montana cities and towns may by ordinance require a driver involved in a crash to also file a crash report, or a copy of the report filed with the Department of Justice, with a designated city department.
facts.quote: Any incorporated city, town, village, or other municipality may by ordinance require that the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident shall also file with a designated city department a report of such accident or a copy of any report herein required to be filed with the department of justice.

facts.claim: Montana's immediate-notice rule (MCA 61-7-108) covers a driver who knows or reasonably should have known of involvement in a crash causing injury or death, striking a deceased person's body, or apparent property damage of $1,000 or more.
facts.quote: The driver of a vehicle who knows or reasonably should have known that the driver has been involved in an accident resulting in injury to or death of any person, striking the body of a deceased person, or property damage to an apparent extent of $1,000 or more

facts.claim: That driver must immediately notify, by the quickest means, the local police department if the crash is within a municipality, or otherwise the county sheriff's office or the nearest highway patrol office.
facts.quote: shall immediately by the quickest means of communication give notice of the accident to the local police department if the accident occurs within a municipality, otherwise to the office of the county sheriff or the nearest office of the highway patrol.

facts.claim: The driver of a motor vehicle involved in a Montana crash in which a person is killed or injured or property damage over $1,000 is sustained must report it in writing within 10 days after the crash.
facts.quote: The operator of a motor vehicle that is in any manner involved in an accident within this state in which a person is killed or injured or in which damage to the property of a person in excess of $1,000 is sustained shall, within 10 days after the accident, report the matter in writing

facts.claim: The driver's written report goes to the department, but it is not required if the crash was investigated and reported by a law enforcement officer.
facts.quote: report the matter in writing to the department unless the accident was investigated and reported by a law enforcement officer as provided in subsection (3).

facts.claim: Every written crash report must be made on the form approved by the department.
facts.quote: Every accident report required to be made in writing shall be made on the appropriate form approved by the department and shall contain all of the information required therein unless not available.

facts.claim: The department may suspend the driving privilege of a person who fails to report a crash as required until the report is filed.
facts.quote: The department may suspend the license or permit to drive of any resident or the nonresident operating privilege of any person failing to report an accident as herein provided until such report has been filed.

facts.claim: The Montana Highway Patrol's form for a driver's own report is titled Montana Highway Patrol Vehicle Crash Report.
facts.quote: MONTANA HIGHWAY PATROL VEHICLE CRASH REPORT

facts.claim: The Montana Highway Patrol Vehicle Crash Report form is numbered HQ 1598.

Form HQ 1598 says that if no investigating officer or agency produces a written report and damage exceeds $1000.00, the driver must report the crash in writing within ten days to Montana Highway Patrol, PO Box 117, Boulder, MT 59632.
facts.quote: If the investigating officer or agency does not produce a written report and the damage is in excess of $1000.00 the operator of the vehicle must report such crash within ten days in writing to the department at this address: Montana Highway Patrol - PO Box 117 Boulder, MT 59632

facts.claim: The City of Billings says non-injury crashes that law enforcement did not investigate may be reported using a form linked on its Non-Investigated Crash Reporting page.
facts.quote: Non-injury accidents that are not investigated by law enforcement may be reported to the Montana using the following link:

facts.claim: The Helena Police Department's Records Division is the central repository for law enforcement reports and records generated by the Helena Police Department, the Lewis and Clark County Sheriff's Office and the East Helena Police Department, and treats them as confidential.
facts.quote: The Records Division is the central repository for all law enforcement reports and records generated by the Helena Police Department, the Lewis and Clark County Sheriff’s Office, and the East Helena Police Department. These records are considered to be confidential.

facts.claim: Mail for the Helena Police Department's Records Division goes to Helena Police Department, Attn: Records, 406 Fuller Ave, Helena, MT 59601.
facts.quote: All correspondence for the Records Division can be mailed to: Helena Police Department Attn: Records 406 Fuller Ave Helena, MT 59601

facts.claim: Helena Police Department Records Clerks are available Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., excluding City of Helena holidays, and can be reached at 406-447-8469.
facts.quote: Records Clerks are available to assist you Monday through Friday 8:00 a.m. - 4:30 p.m., excluding City of Helena holidays. To reach a Records Clerk please call 406-447-8469.

facts.claim: For vehicle incidents, the City of Great Falls releases police reports to parties named in or involved in the report (drivers, vehicle owners, passengers), insurance carriers, and the parties' legal representatives, who must include documentation with the request.
facts.quote: Parties named or involved in the report/incident (drivers, vehicle owners, passengers) Insurance carriers Legal representatives of parties (attorneys, Court-appointed guardians, parents of minors, etc. - documentation must be provided with request)

facts.claim: Great Falls requires a separate request form, with its own $15 fee, for each incident; a form listing several incidents is returned unprocessed.
facts.quote: Request form (below), completed for each separate incident request. The $15 admin fee is required for each individual request. Multiple incidents on one form will not be accepted and will be returned.

facts.claim: Great Falls charges a $15 non-refundable administrative search fee per police report request, paid by check or money order payable to the City of Great Falls.
facts.quote: A $15 check or money order payable to the City of Great Falls for non-refundable administrative charges for the search, for each request.

facts.claim: Great Falls keeps the $15 fee even when a report is denied, for example when the requester isn't legally authorized, the report can't be found or located, it involves a felony or fatality, or it is outside the city's jurisdiction.
facts.quote: Note that payment will be processed and NOT refunded even if the report is denied, including: if requestor not legally authorized to request, report not found, not enough information provided to locate, involves a felony or fatality, or report not within jurisdiction.

facts.claim: A Great Falls police report request needs the requester's notarized signature stating they are a named party or are legally authorized to request the report; without notarization, the request is returned and payment isn't processed.
facts.quote: A notarized signature from the requestor stating the requestor is a named party in the report or is legally authorized to request it; If not notarized, payment will not be processed and request will be returned.

facts.claim: The City of Great Falls says to expect 2 to 4 weeks for a police report request to be completed.
facts.quote: The report will be pulled and processed, please expect 2 to 4 weeks for completion (or until prosecution is complete for non-vehicle incidents).

facts.claim: In Great Falls, reports under 5 pages are mailed automatically, or securely emailed at no further cost if the requester gives an email address on the form.
facts.quote: If under 5 pages, the report will be automatically mailed to you, OR if you provided your email address on the form the report will be securely emailed at no further cost.

facts.claim: The City of Great Falls typically does not process report requests involving felonies or fatalities and refers those requesters to the Cascade County Attorney's Office at 406-454-6915.
facts.quote: Document Requests typically NOT processed by the City of Great Falls when involving: Felonies - contact Cascade County Attorney's Office at 406-454-6915. Fatalities - contact Cascade County Attorney's Office at 406-454-6915.

facts.claim: For reports from outside Great Falls city limits or created by a different agency, the City of Great Falls refers requesters to the Cascade County Attorney's Office (for Sheriff reports) or the Montana Highway Patrol.
facts.quote: Outside of City limits or created by a different agency - contact Cascade County Attorney's Office (for Sheriff), Montana Highway Patrol, etc.

facts.claim: Great Falls calls the officer's crash report the State Accident Form and says law enforcement creates it when a vehicle accident causes $1,000 in damage.
facts.quote: The State Accident Form is created by law enforcement personnel when a vehicle accident occurs and $1,000 in damage is sustained.

facts.claim: If the driver is physically incapable of making the written crash report and is not the vehicle's owner, the owner must make the report within 10 days after learning of the crash (MCA 61-7-110(3)).
facts.quote: physically incapable of making a written report of an accident as required in 61-7-109, and such driver is not the owner of the vehicle, then the owner of the vehicle involved in such accident shall within 10 days after learning of such accident, make such report not made by the driver.

facts.claim: A driver's required written crash report, or a supplemental report the department requires, may not be used as evidence in any civil or criminal trial arising from the crash (MCA 61-7-109(5)).
facts.quote: A report required by subsection (1) or (2) may not be used as evidence in any trial, civil or criminal, arising out of an accident.

facts.claim: Violating Montana's crash-reporting duties, including the immediate-notice and written-report rules in MCA 61-7-108 and 61-7-109, is a misdemeanor; a first conviction carries a fine of $200 to $300 or up to 20 days in jail (MCA 61-7-118(1)).
facts.quote: a person violating any provision of 61-7-103, 61-7-105 through 61-7-110, or 61-7-112 through 61-7-114 is guilty of a misdemeanor. Upon a first conviction, the offender shall be punished by a fine of not less than $200 or more than $300 or by imprisonment for not more than 20 days.

facts.claim: Crash reports that a city requires drivers to file under a local ordinance are for that city department's confidential use and are subject to the confidentiality rules in MCA 61-7-114.
facts.quote: All such reports shall be for the confidential use of the city department and subject to the provisions of 61-7-114.

facts.claim: The Montana Department of Justice may disclose the identity of a person involved in a crash when that identity is not otherwise known or when the person denies being present at the crash (MCA 61-7-114(1)).
facts.quote: The department may disclose the identity of a person involved in an accident when the identity is not otherwise known or when the person denies being present at the accident.

facts.claim: The Billings Police Department is at 316 N. 26th St., 4th Floor, Billings, MT 59101, with mailing address PO Box 1554, Billings, MT 59103, and is open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
facts.quote: Location Billings Police Department 316 N. 26th St., 4th Floor Billings, MT 59101 Mailing Address Billings Police Department PO Box 1554 Billings, MT 59103 Hours Monday-Friday, 8 a.m.- 5 p.m.

gaps.reason: Could not read the Montana Highway Patrol's crash-records request instructions. Search results pointed to https://www.dojmt.gov/montana-highway-patrol/crash-records/ (titled 'Crash Records') and a 'Crash Release Form' PDF at https://dojmt.gov/wp-content/uploads/Crash-Release-Form-Fillable.pdf. Every dojmt.gov URL, including robots.txt, returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare block) to WebFetch, hound smart_fetch (HTTP and stealth browser), curl and a Playwright browser. The web search budget then ran out, so no other official copy could be located. The request form, its mailing address, and any email, fax or in-person options for MHP records are unconfirmed.

The MHP crash report fee could not be confirmed from an official page. Unverified search-result snippets attributed a '$2.00 non-refundable search fee' (and $10.00 for photos) to the blocked DOJ crash-records page. Do not publish those amounts until the page itself is read. No statute or administrative rule setting the fee was found.

No readable official source states how soon MHP crash reports become available. The only official timing found: MCA 61-7-109(3) gives the officer 10 days after completing the investigation to forward the report, and Billings PD says to allow 10 business days for its own reports.
MHP's requester requirements (crash ID or report number, date, county, driver names, ID, signed release form) are unconfirmed because the DOJ form and page could not be opened.
MHP's own release policy could not be read, including whether agents such as attorneys and insurers need written permission. Only the statute (MCA 61-7-114) was confirmed.

No official source confirmed an online portal for MHP crash reports. CrashDocs.org and BuyCrash were found only on city police pages (Helena and Billings), and only for those departments' own reports.

Not confirmed whether MHP releases copies of crash reports written by city police or county sheriffs. MCA 61-7-109(3) requires every investigating officer to forward reports to the Department of Justice, and Helena PD sends people to MHP for crashes 'investigated by another agency', but MHP's own page could not be read.

Only the Helena and Billings police department pages were read. No county sheriff page was read, and fees, methods and timing vary by agency, so the Helena ($15.00) and Billings ($30) figures cannot be generalized.

The HQ 1598 copy read is hosted by the City of Billings (PDF metadata dated 2022-09-26), so it could not be confirmed as the current version on dojmt.gov. Its printed immediate-notice threshold ($500.00 in property damage) conflicts with the $1,000 threshold in current MCA 61-7-108 (2025). Use the statute for thresholds.
MHP records contact details (email, phone, fax) were not confirmed from a state page. The only MHP phone number found, (406) 444-3278, comes from the City of Helena police records page.

facts.claim: The North Carolina Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV) keeps crash reports in a database of records that contain confidential personal information and are not available to the public.
facts.quote: The North Carolina Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV) maintains records containing confidential personal information in its database that are not available to the public. Such records include Crash Reports.

facts.claim: Crash reports investigated by all North Carolina law enforcement agencies are forwarded to the North Carolina Division of Motor Vehicles.
facts.quote: Crash reports investigated by all of North Carolina's law enforcement agencies are forwarded to the North Carolina Division of Motor Vehicles.

facts.claim: All law enforcement officers in North Carolina are to use the DMV Crash Report Form, on paper or electronically, to report motor vehicle crashes.
facts.quote: The DMV Crash Report Form (paper or electronic) is to be used by all law enforcement officers to report motor vehicle crashes in North Carolina.

facts.claim: The law enforcement agency must submit a crash report to the DMV within 10 days after receiving it.
facts.quote: The law enforcement agency must submit the report to the Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV) within 10 days after receiving it.

facts.claim: The DMV's crash report manual says G.S. 20-166.1 requires the investigating officer to make a written crash report within 24 hours after the investigation is completed.
facts.quote: After the investigation of a crash is completed, North Carolina General Statute 20-166.1 requires that the investigating officer make a written report of the crash within 24 hours.

facts.claim: Unredacted crash report copies require a permissible use under the federal Drivers Privacy Protection Act (DPPA), 18 USC 2721-2725.
facts.quote: Crash reports are highly regulated and require a Federal Drivers Privacy Protection Act (or DPPA), 18 USC 2721-2725 Permissible Use for unredacted copies, as they can contain personal information about more than one person.

facts.claim: A person who was involved in a crash can order a redacted copy of the crash report in person or by mail.
facts.quote: If you were personally involved in a crash, you can order a redacted copy of the crash report in person or by mail.

facts.claim: Individuals cannot order a crash report online from NCDMV.
facts.quote: Individuals cannot order a crash report online.

facts.claim: Individuals receive only a redacted report, with some personal details such as names or addresses hidden.
facts.quote: You will only receive a redacted report, which means some personal details (like names or addresses) will be hidden.

facts.claim: A business or organization based in or licensed to operate in North Carolina, such as an insurer, attorney's office or private investigator, can request an unredacted crash report by mail, in person or online.
facts.quote: If you are business or organization, like an insurance company, attorney's office, or private investigator, that is based in or licensed to operate in North Carolina, you can request an unredacted crash report that includes full details either by mail, in person, or online.

facts.claim: Out-of-state businesses and organizations must submit their requests by mail.
facts.quote: If you are an out-of-state business or organization, requests will need to be submitted by mail.

facts.claim: Businesses and organizations must confirm a federal permissible use and submit identification that verifies their profession or agency status.
facts.quote: You will need to confirm that your request meets one of the permissible uses allowed under federal privacy law. You will also be required to submit identification that verifies your profession or agency status.

facts.claim: Requests that do not meet a permissible use receive only the redacted version.
facts.quote: Requests that do not meet a permissible use will only receive the redacted version.

facts.claim: To order by mail, print and fill out the Crash Report Request (TR-67A) form and mail it with payment to the address on the form.
facts.quote: To order a crash report by mail, fill out the Crash Report Request (TR-67A) form (forms are not fillable so they must be printed) and mail it along with payment (see fee below) to the address listed on the form.

facts.claim: Mailed requests go to Traffic Records Branch, Crash Reports Unit, 3106 Mail Service Center, Raleigh, NC 27697-3106, with checks payable to NCDMV, and cash is not accepted for mailed requests.
facts.quote: Cash not accepted for mailed requests. Make checks payable to NCDMV and mail requests to: Traffic Records Branch, Crash Reports Unit, 3106 Mail Service Center, Raleigh, NC 27697-3106

facts.claim: NCDMV asks requesters to allow 10 business days from receipt for a mailed request to be processed.
facts.quote: Please allow 10 business days from the time of receipt for the request to be processed.

facts.claim: A check or money order must be made payable to NCDMV and signed, and forms must be completely and correctly filled out to avoid delay or return of the request.
facts.quote: To avoid delay or return of your request, ensure that forms are completely and correctly filled out and that your check or money order, made payable to NCDMV is signed.

facts.claim: In-person requests require a printed Crash Report Request (TR-67A) form and payment.
facts.quote: To request a crash report in person, submit the Crash Report Request (TR-67A) form (forms are not fillable so they must be printed) and payment to:

facts.quote: Raleigh Central Services/License Plate Agency (Go to the door that reads Vehicle Registration, NOT Driver License) 4121 New Bern Ave. Raleigh, NC 27616
