facts.quote: Huntersville License Plate Agency 12101 Mt. Holly-Huntersville Road Huntersville, NC 28078

facts.claim: In-person requests for five records or fewer can be received immediately, and larger requests must be submitted by mail.
facts.quote: Customers or businesses requesting five records or less in person can receive them immediately, but larger requests will need to be submitted by mail.

facts.claim: Businesses and organizations based in or licensed to operate in North Carolina can order a crash report online.
facts.quote: If you are business or organization, like an insurance company, attorney's office, or private investigator, that is based in or licensed to operate in North Carolina, you can order a crash report online.

facts.claim: Online orders require the requester's North Carolina driver license or ID card number, the requester's Social Security, ITIN or U.S. Visa number, the involved driver's license number, and the date of the crash.
facts.quote: The following information is required: The North Carolina driver license or ID card number of the requestor Social Security number, Individual Taxpayer Identification number, or U.S. Visa number of the requestor Driver license number of driver involved in the crash Date of the crash

facts.claim: The fee table on the NCDMV Crash Reports page lists $6.50 for a certified copy.
facts.quote: Certified Copy $6.50

facts.claim: Form TR-67A says the cost of a crash report is currently $6.50.
facts.quote: Web Site: https://www.ncdot.gov/dmv/offices-services/records-reports/Pages/crash-reports.aspx for cost of a Crash Report, currently $6.50.

facts.claim: Since Jan 1, 2013, the DMV has provided only certified crash reports, citing NCGS § 20-42(b) and § 20-4.02.
facts.quote: As of Jan 1, 2013, only certified Crash Reports are available from the Division. NCGS § 20-42(b) and § 20-4.02.

facts.claim: Form TR-67A asks for the driver's name, the driver license number, the date of the crash and the county of the crash.
facts.quote: I hereby request a copy of a certified Crash Report for: Name of Driver DL# Date of Crash County of Crash

facts.claim: Form TR-67A asks for the requester's ID type, ID number and state of issuance, for example a driver's license or state ID number for individuals involved.
facts.quote: Please include ID Type, ID number, and State of Issuance (e.g. Driver’s License/State ID # for individuals involved, Bar/License # for attorneys or private investigators, Tax ID # for businesses, etc.)

facts.claim: The requester signs form TR-67A, acknowledging that information about individuals in the crash report is privileged, confidential and not to be made public.
facts.quote: My signature on this document acknowledges that I understand that: The information about individuals obtained in the Crash Report is privileged, confidential, and not to be made public.

facts.claim: DMV denies the request if the form is not completed or the explanation is not sufficient.
facts.quote: Failure to complete this form or to provide sufficient explanation will result in DMV denying your request.

facts.claim: DMV discloses crash reports under the federal Driver's Privacy Protection Act of 1994 (18 U.S.C. § 2721 et seq.) and North Carolina General Statute § 20-43.1.
facts.quote: DMV discloses these records in accordance with the Federal Driver’s Privacy Protection Act (DPPA) of 1994, 18 U.S.C. § 2721 et seq. and North Carolina General Statute § 20-43.1.

facts.claim: Form TR-67A lets a party involved in the crash who has no DPPA permissible use request a redacted copy.
facts.quote: I am a party involved in the crash without a DPPA Permissible Use and I am requesting a redacted copy.

facts.claim: Form TR-67A also has an option for a requester who does not qualify under a DPPA permissible use to request a redacted copy.
facts.quote: I do not qualify under a DPPA Permissible Use and I am requesting a redacted copy.

facts.claim: For crash reports, DPPA permissible uses 3, 5, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 do not apply.
facts.quote: Permissible Uses 3, 5, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 are not applicable.

facts.claim: Permissible use (6) on form TR-67A covers insurers, insurance support organizations and self-insured entities in connection with claims investigation, antifraud activities, rating or underwriting.
facts.quote: (6) For use by any insurer or insurance support organization, or by a self-insured entity, or its agents, employees, or contractors, in connection with claims investigation activities, antifraud activities, rating or underwriting.

facts.claim: Permissible use (4) on form TR-67A covers use in connection with civil, criminal, administrative or arbitral proceedings in a federal, state or local court or agency.
facts.quote: (4) For use in connection with any civil, criminal, administrative, or arbitral proceeding in any Federal, State, or local court or agency or before any self-regulatory body

facts.claim: The DMV Crash Reports Unit can be reached at 919-861-3068.
facts.quote: For additional information, contact the Crash Reports Unit at 919-861-3068.

facts.claim: The State Highway Patrol's online Collision Reports system has crashes investigated by the North Carolina State Highway Patrol since May 16, 2013.
facts.quote: Crashes investigated by the North Carolina State Highway Patrol since May 16, 2013, are available in this system.

facts.claim: Highway Patrol crash reports are normally entered into its Collision Reports system within 5 to 7 business days.
facts.quote: Reports will normally be entered into the system within 5 to 7 business days.

facts.claim: A report from the Highway Patrol's Collision Reports system is not a certified crash report.
facts.quote: This report is NOT a certified crash report.

facts.claim: The Highway Patrol's Collision Reports page says a certified crash report may be requested from the NC DMV.
facts.quote: You may request a certified crash report from the NC DMV.

facts.claim: The Highway Patrol's Collision Reports system can be searched by report number, name, driver's license number or vehicle plate number.
facts.quote: Search by Report Number Name Driver's License Number Vehicle Plate Number DMV-349 Terms of Use

facts.claim: Searching the Highway Patrol's Collision Reports system requires reading and accepting the Terms of Use for form DMV-349.
facts.quote: You must click here to read and accept the Terms of Use for form DMV-349

facts.claim: Drivers must immediately report to the nearest law enforcement officer or agency any crash in which someone is killed or injured or the total damage to vehicles and other property appears to be $1,000 or more.
facts.quote: You are required by law to make an immediate report to the nearest law enforcement officer or agency of any crash when any person is killed or injured or the total damage to vehicles and other property appears to amount to $1,000 or more.

facts.claim: Failing to make that report may lead to prosecution and suspension of the driver license.
facts.quote: Failure to make the report may result in prosecution, and your driver license could be suspended.

facts.claim: In certain cases, the driver of a vehicle in a reportable crash must provide proof of financial responsibility (liability insurance) on DMV-provided forms that are filed with DMV.
facts.quote: In certain cases, North Carolina law also requires the driver of a vehicle involved in a reportable crash to provide proof of financial responsibility (liability insurance) on forms provided by the Division of Motor Vehicles. These forms must be completed and filed with DMV.

facts.claim: The DMV-349 Terms of Use on the Highway Patrol's crash report search ask the user to certify, under 18 U.S.C. § 2721 and N.C.G.S. § 20-43.1, that they are qualified to obtain the information for their own personal record or that they qualify under one of the listed exceptions.
facts.quote: Pursuant to 18 U.S.C. § 2721 and N.C.G.S § 20-43.1, I certify that I am qualified to obtain this information for my own personal record or I qualify under one of the exceptions listed below:

facts.claim: The State Highway Patrol says certified crash reports must be obtained from NCDMV, citing G.S. 20-42.
facts.quote: Certified crash reports must be obtained from NCDMV pursuant to § 20-42.

facts.claim: The Highway Patrol's search by report number asks for the report number, the driver's last name (left blank if there was no driver), the accident date and the county, and the DMV-349 terms must be accepted.
facts.quote: Report number Lastname (If no driver, leave blank) Accident date County

facts.claim: For crash reports, the permissible uses printed on page 2 of TR-67A, numbers (1), (2), (4), (6), (7) and (8), are the only exceptions that allow an unredacted copy.
facts.quote: *For the purposes of Crash Reports, the Permissible Uses listed below are the only exceptions that are allowable to obtain an unredacted crash report.

facts.claim: Permissible use (1), for government agencies and those acting on their behalf, is accepted for in-person or mailed transactions only. Permissible use (2) carries the same restriction.
facts.quote: (1) For use by any government agency, including any court or law enforcement agency, in carrying out its functions, or any private person or entity acting on behalf of a Federal, State, or local agency in carrying out its functions. (For in person or mailed transactions only.)

facts.claim: Licensed private investigators and security services must select another permissible use together with permissible use (8).
facts.quote: (8) For use by any licensed private investigative agency or licensed security service for any purpose permitted above. (Must select another Permissible Use in combination with this Permissible Use.)

facts.claim: Permissible use (7) on TR-67A covers notifying the owners of previously towed or impounded vehicles.
facts.quote: (7) For use in providing notice to the owners of previously towed or impounded vehicles.

facts.claim: Form TR-67A warns that knowingly making a false statement on the form, or misrepresenting your identity or how you qualify under the DPPA, carries state and federal criminal and civil penalties.
facts.quote: There are state and federal criminal and civil penalties for any of the following: (a) knowingly making a false statement or representation on this Form, or (b) misrepresenting my identity, or how I qualify under the DPPA

facts.claim: NCDMV's permissible-use terms say a request for 'the applicant's own personal record' does not apply to crash reports unless there is a DPPA permissible use.
facts.quote: For the applicant's own personal record (Not applicable to Crash Reports without a DPPA Permissible Use)

facts.claim: NCDMV's permissible-use terms say the motor-vehicle-related permissible use cannot be used for online crash report orders.
facts.quote: Motor Vehicle Related (not applicable to online Crash Reports)

facts.claim: Viewing a downloaded crash report needs a PDF viewer, and NCDMV recommends a laptop or desktop.
facts.quote: Please note: To download and view a crash report, a PDF viewer (e.g., Adobe Acrobat Reader) is needed. It's recommended to use a laptop or desktop to download and view crash reports properly.

facts.claim: A reportable crash in North Carolina must meet at least one criterion, including a fatality, a non-fatal personal injury, or total property damage of $1,000 or more.
facts.quote: a reportable motor vehicle traffic crash must meet at least one of the following criteria: • The crash resulted in a fatality, or • The crash resulted in a non-fatal personal injury, or • The crash resulted in total property damage amounting to $1,000.00 or more

facts.claim: If an injured person dies from the crash within 12 months and the death was not in the original report, the investigating officer must file a supplemental report that includes the death.
facts.quote: When a person injured in a reportable crash dies as a result of the crash within 12 months after the crash, and the death was not reported in the original report, the law enforcement officer investigating the crash must file a supplemental report that includes the death.

facts.claim: Drivers involved in a crash must give their name, address, driver license number, vehicle registration number and insurance company, and get the same information from the others involved.
facts.quote: Three things you must do if involved in a crash: • Provide your name, address, driver license number, vehicle registration number and the name of your vehicle insurance company; • Be sure to obtain the same information from others who were involved in the crash

gaps.reason: WebSearch was unavailable because this turn's shared search limit was used up. I found pages by fetching known official URLs (ncdot.gov, connect.ncdot.gov, ncshp.gov) and following their links, so a search might still turn up other official pages.

I could not confirm any convenience, card or processing fee for online orders. The online portal needs a PayIt sign-in, which I did not do, and no official page I read gives an online surcharge or the payment methods accepted in person.

I could not read the statute that sets the fee (G.S. 20-42(b), cited on form TR-67A). ncleg.gov returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch, curl and hound. The $6.50 figure comes only from the NCDMV page's fee table and the July 2024 TR-67A form.

Sources conflict. The NC State Highway Patrol FAQ (https://www.ncshp.gov/ncshp/frequently-asked-questions) still says 'The fee for a crash report is five dollars ($5.00).' It also gives older DMV addresses (1100 New Bern Ave.; 3105 Mail Service Center, Raleigh 27699-3105). The current NCDMV page and the July 2024 TR-67A both say $6.50, so the $5.00 figure looks out of date and should not be used.

State sources confirm only that reports from all NC law enforcement agencies, including city police and county sheriffs, go to NCDMV. I could not confirm from a state source whether local agencies also release copies themselves, or at what fee. The public-records provisions of G.S. 20-166.1 could not be read because ncleg.gov blocked access.

No official source gives a total time from crash to when a report can be ordered from NCDMV. The available figures are: the officer's report within 24 hours and the agency's submission to DMV within 10 days (both from the DMV-349 manual, not the statute itself), 10 business days to process a mailed request, same-day in-person service for five or fewer records, and 5 to 7 business days for Highway Patrol reports to appear in its own search system.

I found no state form for drivers to file their own crash report. The NCDMV Driver Handbook says to report to law enforcement instead. It says that in certain cases drivers must file financial-responsibility (liability insurance) forms with DMV, but it does not name the form or give a deadline.

I could not confirm what the Highway Patrol's Collision Reports search returns (for example a viewable or downloadable report) or whether it charges anything, because that would mean submitting a search. The page says only that the report is not certified.

I could not read G.S. 20-166.1 (reports of crashes) directly because ncleg.gov returned HTTP 403. The reporting duties and time limits come from NCDMV's DMV-349 Instructional Manual (revised February 2023), which cites that statute.

facts.claim: The North Dakota Highway Patrol says crash reports are available from the North Dakota Department of Transportation (NDDOT) and are requested through an online form at ndcrash.primepublicsafety.com.
facts.quote: Crash reports are available from the NDDOT, complete this form to request a crash report: https://ndcrash.primepublicsafety.com/ndcrash/ecommerce/ndcrash.jsp

facts.claim: State law requires law enforcement crash reports to be transmitted electronically to the Department of Transportation using software the director prescribes.
facts.quote: The report must contain all the information required therein unless the information is not available, and must be transmitted electronically to the department of transportation using the software prescribed by the director.

facts.claim: State law requires every law enforcement officer who investigates a crash that must be reported to forward a report of it to the department within ten days after the crash.
facts.quote: Every law enforcement officer who investigates a vehicle crash for which a report must be made as required in this chapter shall forward a report of such crash to the department within ten days after the crash.

facts.claim: NDDOT says North Dakota Century Code 39-08-09 defines a reportable crash as one that results in injury, a fatality, or at least $4,000 in total property damage.
facts.quote: North Dakota Century Code 39-08-09 defines a reportable crash as a motor vehicle traffic crash which results in injury, fatality, or at least $4,000 in total property damage.

facts.claim: NDDOT says crashes involving undomesticated animals with no injury or fatality are not reportable, regardless of the property damage amount.
facts.quote: Crashes involving undomesticated animals where there was no injury or fatality, regardless of the property damage amount, are not reportable.

facts.claim: NDDOT says reports for traffic crashes that are reportable to NDDOT are available for purchase online.
facts.quote: Reports for traffic crashes that are Reportable* to the North Dakota Department of Transportation are available for purchase online.

facts.claim: NDDOT asks people who have trouble purchasing a crash report to contact it through the contact link on its Purchase Crash Report page.
facts.quote: If you have trouble purchasing a crash report, please contact us.

facts.claim: NDDOT has an online contact form for questions about purchasing a crash report.
facts.quote: Questions about purchasing a crash report? Contact us below.

facts.claim: To get a copy of a North Dakota crash report from NDDOT, you must be able to provide at least two of these: the date of the crash, a last name, and the county of the crash.
facts.quote: To obtain a copy of the State of North Dakota crash report, a person must be able to provide at least two of the following: Date of Crash Last Name County of Crash

facts.claim: If you don't have those details, NDDOT says to contact the law enforcement agency that investigated the crash to get them.
facts.quote: If you don’t have this information, please contact the Law Enforcement Agency that investigated the crash to obtain these details.

facts.claim: State law says crash reports held by a public entity other than the department of transportation and a law enforcement agency that contracts with service providers are exempt records.
facts.quote: Crash reports held by a public entity other than the department of transportation and a law enforcement agency that contracts with service providers are exempt records.

facts.claim: NDDOT charges a $7 fee to locate and provide a crash report.
facts.quote: There is a $7 fee to locate and provide the crash report.

facts.claim: The North Dakota Highway Patrol says crash reports cost $7.
facts.quote: Crash reports cost $7.

facts.claim: NDDOT says buyers receive their report(s) immediately if the report is available for purchase.
facts.quote: Customers will receive their report(s) immediately if the report is available for purchase.

facts.claim: NDDOT says you may not be able to locate a crash report if it has been less than 10 days since the crash occurred.
facts.quote: You may not be able to locate a crash report if the following conditions apply: It has been less than 10 days since the crash occurred.

facts.claim: Except as the statute provides, crash reports that law enforcement officers must forward, and the information in them, are not privileged or confidential.
facts.quote: Except as provided in subsection 5, reports required to be forwarded by law enforcement officers and the information contained in the reports is not privileged or confidential.

facts.claim: State law makes certain information in a crash report an exempt record unless the requester is one of those the statute lists, including a party to the crash, a party's legal representative, the insurer of any party to the crash, and the agent of that insurer.
facts.quote: the following information contained in the report is an exempt record as defined in section 44-04-17.1 unless the requester is a party to the crash, a party's legal representative, the insurer of any party to the crash, the agent of that insurer

facts.claim: The exempt information is a party's driver identification number, telephone number, insurance company name and policy number, and day and month of birth.
facts.quote: a. Driver identification number of a party in the report; b. Telephone number of a party in the report; c. Insurance company name and policy number of a party in the report; and d. Day and month of birth of a party in the report.

facts.claim: A driver involved in a crash that causes injury or death, or apparent property damage of at least $4,000, must immediately give notice of the crash.
facts.quote: The driver of a vehicle involved in an accident resulting in injury to or death of any individual, or property damage to an apparent extent of at least four thousand dollars, shall immediately give notice of the accident

facts.claim: That notice goes to the local police department if the crash happened within a municipality, and otherwise to the county sheriff's office or the state highway patrol.
facts.quote: shall immediately give notice of the accident to the local police department if the accident occurs within a municipality, otherwise to the office of the county sheriff or the state highway patrol.

facts.claim: A driver who violates this notice requirement must be assessed a fifty-dollar fine.
facts.quote: A driver who violates this section must be assessed a fine of fifty dollars.

facts.claim: If a driver does not have the required insurance information to give the investigating officer, the driver must supply it to the driver's license division within five days of the crash, in the form the division requires.
facts.quote: If the driver does not have the required information concerning insurance to furnish to the investigating law enforcement officer, then within five days of the accident the driver shall supply that information to the driver's license division in the form the division requires.

facts.claim: A driver whose crash with an undomesticated animal damages only the driver's own vehicle is exempt from the notice requirement, regardless of the amount of damage.
facts.quote: The driver of a vehicle involved in an accident with an undomesticated animal resulting in property damage only to the driver's vehicle is exempt from the notice requirements of this section, regardless of the amount of damage to the driver's vehicle.

facts.claim: The North Dakota Highway Patrol says to contact the local police department if the crash happened in a municipality, and otherwise the county sheriff's office or the Highway Patrol.
facts.quote: If you are involved in a crash and it occurred in a municipality, contact the local police department. If outside a municipality, contact the sheriff's office of the county where it occurred or contact the NDHP.

facts.claim: State law lets any incorporated city or other municipality require, by ordinance, that a driver involved in a crash file a report of the crash with a designated city department.
facts.quote: Any incorporated city or other municipality may by ordinance require that the driver of a vehicle involved in a crash shall file with a designated city department a report of such crash or a copy of any report herein required to be filed with the director.

facts.claim: State law says copies of crash reports are not admissible as evidence in any action for damages or criminal proceedings arising out of a motor vehicle crash.
facts.quote: Copies of crash reports are not admissible as evidence in any action for damages or criminal proceedings arising out of a motor vehicle crash.

facts.claim: The director may send a copy of a crash report to the registered owner of each vehicle involved without a request.
facts.quote: The director, without a request under subsection 4, 5, or 6 may send a copy of a crash report to the registered owner of each vehicle involved as indicated by the report.

facts.claim: On request from a party to the crash, a party's legal representative, the insurer of any party to the crash, that insurer's agent, or the legal representative or insurer of someone defending or investigating a prior or subsequent claim or crash involving a party, and on payment of a fee of up to seven dollars, the director must release a completed copy of the crash report; the request must be made on the form the director prescribes.
facts.quote: Upon request from a party to the crash, a party's legal representative, the insurer of any party to the crash, the agent of the insurer, or the legal representative or insurer of an individual involved in defending or investigating a prior or subsequent claim or crash involving a party to the crash

facts.claim: Unless the requester is a party to the crash, a party's legal representative, the insurer of any party, that insurer's agent, or the legal representative or insurer of someone defending or investigating a prior or subsequent claim or crash involving a party, a minor party's name, driver identification number and uniquely owned telephone number in a crash report are exempt.
facts.quote: Unless the requester is a party to the accident, a party's legal representative, the insurer of any party to the accident, the agent of that insurer, or the legal representative or insurer of an individual involved in defending or investigating a prior or subsequent claim or accident

facts.claim: On request from any person and payment of a fee of up to seven dollars, the director may furnish a copy of an investigating officer's crash report that does not contain exempt information, if the report shows the crash is one for which a driver is required to file a report under section 39-08-09.
facts.quote: the director may furnish to a requester a copy of an investigating officer's crash report which does not contain any exempt information that may not be disclosed, if the report shows that the crash is one for which a driver is required to file a report under section 39-08-09.

facts.claim: The North Dakota Highway Patrol says crash reports are available instantly through an online request system that replaced the mail-in request form, which is no longer accepted, and that reports cost $7.
facts.quote: Instant access to crash reports is available through an online request at https://ndcrash.primepublicsafety.com/ndcrash/ecommerce/ndcrash.jsp This system replaces the mail-in request form, which is no longer accepted. Crash reports cost $7.

facts.claim: The Highway Patrol's Request a Crash Report page defines a state-reportable crash as one involving an injury, a fatality or at least $4,000 in total damage, and says reports are requested online through the NDDOT website for $7.00.
facts.quote: A state reportable crash is one that involves an injury, a fatality, or at least $4,000 in total damage. Access a crash report through an online request from the NDDOT website. A report costs $7.00.

facts.claim: NDDOT says you may not be able to locate a crash report if the crash did not result in injury, a fatality or at least $4,000 in property damage.
facts.quote: You may not be able to locate a crash report if the following conditions apply: It has been less than 10 days since the crash occurred. The crash did not result in injury, fatality, or at least $4,000 property damage.

facts.claim: The footer of NDDOT's Purchase Crash Report page gives the department's address as 608 East Boulevard Avenue, Bismarck, ND 58505-0700, and its phone number as 701-328-2500.
facts.quote: North Dakota Department of Transportation 608 East Boulevard Avenue | Bismarck, ND 58505-0700 | 701-328-2500

facts.claim: If the driver is physically unable to give notice of a crash and is not the vehicle's owner, the owner must give the notice and the insurance information the driver did not give within five days after learning of the crash.
facts.quote: Whenever the driver is physically incapable of giving notice of a crash and the driver is not the owner of the vehicle, then the owner of the vehicle involved shall within five days after learning of the crash give the notice and insurance information not given by the driver.

facts.claim: If the driver is physically unable to give immediate notice of a crash and another occupant of the vehicle could do so, that occupant must give the notice or have it given.
facts.quote: Whenever the driver of a vehicle is physically incapable of giving an immediate notice of a crash and there was another occupant in the vehicle at the time of the crash capable of doing so, the occupant shall make or cause to be given the notice not given by the driver.

facts.claim: The director may suspend the license or permit to drive, including any nonresident operating privileges, of anyone who fails to comply with the crash duties in sections 39-08-06 through 39-08-09, until those duties are fulfilled.
facts.quote: The director may suspend the license or permit to drive and any nonresident operating privileges of any person failing to comply with the duties as provided in sections 39-08-06 through 39-08-09 until those duties have been fulfilled

facts.claim: A driver whose crash damages only highway fixtures or other property must take reasonable steps to locate and notify the property's owner or the person in charge of it.
facts.quote: The driver of any vehicle involved in a crash resulting only in damage to highway fixtures or other property shall take reasonable steps to locate and notify the owner or person in charge of the property of the damage.

facts.claim: Crash reports that a city ordinance requires drivers to file with a city department are for that department's confidential use and are subject to section 39-08-14.
facts.quote: All such reports must be for the confidential use of the city department and subject to the provisions of section 39-08-14.

facts.claim: State law says crash reports made by people involved in crashes, or by garages, are for the confidential use of the department or of other state agencies that use the records for crash prevention purposes.
facts.quote: All crash reports made by persons involved in crashes or by garages shall be without prejudice to the individual so reporting and shall be for the confidential use of the department or other state agencies having use for the records for crash prevention purposes

facts.claim: In a civil or criminal trial arising out of a crash, the director must, on demand of any party or of any court, furnish a certificate showing whether a specified crash report was made to the director as the law requires.
facts.quote: any trial, civil or criminal, arising out of a crash, except that the director shall furnish upon demand of any party to such trial, or upon demand of any court, a certificate showing that a specified crash report has or has not been made to the director in compliance with law.

gaps.reason: Could not confirm whether the online portal adds a convenience, card or processing fee to the $7, or which payment methods it takes. The portal URL returned HTTP 404 and the site root returned 403, to both WebFetch and the fallback fetcher. Neither the NDDOT page nor the Highway Patrol FAQ mentions any extra fee.

No mail-in option or paper request form was found. NDDOT's Purchase Crash Report page describes only online purchase. NDDOT's forms list (https://www.dot.nd.gov/dot/view/forms.aspx) has no crash report request form; its only crash-titled form is SFN 62357, Application for Return of Crash Related Security Deposit. NDCC 39-08-13(6) says requests must be made on the form the director prescribes, but no official page names a paper form.
No official source was found that describes requesting a crash report in person from NDDOT.

Requirements inside the portal could not be confirmed because the vendor portal could not be opened. For example, it is unknown whether a buyer must certify being a party, insurer or legal representative to get a complete copy that includes exempt information.

No official page explains how NDDOT's online portal applies the statute's split between complete copies for parties, their legal representatives and insurers, and copies with exempt information removed for any other person.

No official state source says whether city police departments or county sheriff's offices release their own copies of crash reports, or how or at what fee. The NDDOT page only says to contact the investigating agency for the details needed to search. City and county sites are not state sources and were not checked. NDDOT says reports for crashes below the reportable threshold may not be found in its system, and no state source says where to get those.

No official source gives a typical number of days before a report is available. The only timing statements are NDDOT's note that a report may not be found within 10 days of the crash, and the law requiring officers to forward reports within ten days.

No official source was found that requires drivers to file their own written crash report form with a state agency. NDCC 39-08-09 requires immediate notice to local law enforcement. It adds insurance details to the driver's license division within five days only when the driver could not give them to the investigating officer. City ordinances that NDCC 39-08-16 allows to require driver reports were not checked.

WebSearch was unavailable because this turn's search budget was used up, so the research relied on navigating official sites directly (dot.nd.gov, statepatrol.nd.gov, ndlegis.gov, forms.nd.gov). The North Dakota Administrative Code was not checked for crash-report rules. A follow-up run with search available could check NDAC and the portal's terms and fees.

gaps.reason: The NDOT crash-reporting page (dot.nebraska.gov, 164.119.176.111) and the Nebraska Legislature's statute site (nebraskalegislature.gov) refused or timed out every connection from this environment. The fee for an NDOT copy therefore could not be read from the request page, the fee schedule or the statute. The City of York page only says to call 402-479-4645 for the correct tax before a mail request. The same page also says the York Police Department charges $10.00 for an Investigator's Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which conflicts with its own later statement that reports have been obtained through NDOT since August 27, 2021, so that figure was not used.

No reachable official page lists the details or documents NDOT needs for a crash report request (such as the crash date, county or driver names), and NDOT's own crash-reporting page could not be opened.
No reachable official source says how soon a crash report becomes available after a crash.
No reachable official source says who may get an investigating officer's report, or whether driver-filed reports are confidential. The NDOT page and the Nebraska statutes site could not be opened.

The current NDOT online purchase portal could not be confirmed. The City of York page links to an 'NDOT Storefront' at https://dotstore.nebraska.gov/storefront/AccidentReports.aspx, but that hostname returns 'Non-existent domain' from both the 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8 DNS resolvers, so it was left out. Lancaster County says NDOT's website sells reports for download, but the NDOT page itself could not be opened to get the portal URL or steps. The NDOT online driver-report portal (ecmndotportal.nebraska.gov) was also unreachable.
No name or number for a mail request form could be confirmed. The Nebraska State Patrol gives only NDOT's mailing address and phone number.
Only the City of York page gives an in-person location (Highway Safety Office, 1500 Highway 2-Room 14, Lincoln, NE). NDOT's own page could not be opened to confirm the current address, room or hours.

No reachable NDOT page says whether NDOT's records include crash reports from every law-enforcement agency or only some. Some local agencies use their own channels: the Sarpy County Sheriff's Office points requesters to CrashDocs.org. Readers should check with the agency that handled the crash.

The Omaha Police Department site (police.cityofomaha.org) returned 403 Access Denied. The Lincoln Police Department's Crash Reports page redirects to cjis.lincoln.ne.gov/~lpd/ACCIDENTS.htm, which refused connections. The procedures of Nebraska's two largest city police departments therefore could not be confirmed.

The Sarpy County Sheriff's page gives a $1,000 damage threshold for the driver's report, which conflicts with the $1,500 threshold in the 2025 Nebraska Driver's Manual; the manual's figure was used. The governing statute could not be read because nebraskalegislature.gov was unreachable.

The web-search budget shared by this workflow run ran out after two searches, so no further official pages could be searched for. The sources above were reached by following links on official pages. Archive and proxy services were not used to get around the blocked NDOT and Legislature sites.

facts.claim: When police respond to or investigate a crash, the officer submits a written report to the NH DMV on form DSMV 159, the State of New Hampshire Uniform Police Traffic Accident Report.

facts.quote: Do not leave cash or credit card information

facts.quote: Mail: NH DMV, 23 Hazen Drive, Concord NH 03305 (Please indicate “DSMV 505” on the envelope).

facts.claim: For a fatal crash report, the DMV says to complete a Release of Motor Vehicle Records (DSMV 505).

gaps.reason: No official online portal for crash report copies was found. The DMV's online services (driving record requests, accident insurance verification and others) do not include accident reports. The DMV Appointments and Services page lists only 'Drop Box service' under 'Requesting an Accident Report'. No official NH page names a vendor portal such as BuyCrash, Crashdocs or PoliceReports.US for state crash reports.

The sources conflict. The DSMV 505 lists in-person submission with photo ID, but the DMV accident report page says requests go through the 'Concord Drop Box ONLY', and the Appointments page offers only the Drop Box for accident reports. Whether walk-in or appointment requests for crash reports are accepted is unconfirmed.

DMV guidance conflicts. The accident report page says 'Concord Drop Box ONLY' but also describes 'mailing in your request' with a $5.00 check, and the DSMV 505 gives a mailing address (NH DMV, 23 Hazen Drive, Concord NH 03305). Mail should be confirmed with the DMV at (603) 227-4010 before the guide presents it as a sure option.

No official page states a card or convenience fee for paying by credit card. The statute or rule that sets the $1-per-page, $5-minimum fee was not read, because the NH General Court RSA and rules site (gc.nh.gov / gencourt.state.nh.us) returned 403 or connection errors.

No official source gives a typical turnaround for non-fatal crash report copies. The only time frames found are 'several weeks' for police to send reports to the DMV and 7 to 10 business days to process drop box items. Any statutory deadline for police to file crash reports with the DMV was not confirmed, because the RSA site was unreachable.

The statute and rules that define who may get another person's crash report (RSA 260:14 and the Saf-C 5600 Driver Privacy rules) were not read, because the RSA and rules site was unreachable. The DMV page only says to email NH.DMVHelp@dos.nh.gov or call (603) 227-4010 for third-party requests. The business-requester box on the DSMV 505 (banks, tow companies, insurers, law firms under RSA 260:14) was too garbled in the PDF text to quote reliably.

No state source says whether city or town police departments, or county sheriffs, also release copies of their own crash reports, or what they charge. State pages say only that responding police submit reports to the DMV on form DSMV 159, and that the DMV is the central site for data from all law enforcement agencies. Local agency websites were not used because they are not state sources.

The text of RSA 264:25 was not read because the RSA site was unreachable. The $1,000 threshold, 15-day deadline and penalties come from the DMV Accidents Reports page and the DSMV 400 form. The DMV page gives the Operator's Report mailing address (NH Dept. of Safety, DMV - FR / Accidents, 23 Hazen Drive, Concord NH 03305) as line-broken text, so it was not used as a quote.

This run's web search budget was used up at the first search, so sources were found by navigating official NH sites (dmv.nh.gov, nhsp.dos.nh.gov, dos.nh.gov) directly. An official page not linked from those sites could have been missed.

gaps.reason: I found no state-level official page that says whether crash reports written by municipal police or county agencies are in the State Police portal, or that tells requesters to ask the local agency. The NJSP pages describe only State Police reports and NJTA toll-road reports. NJDOT says it collects every NJTR-1 statewide for its database but does not offer copies on any page I read. The only local example found was Paterson PD's page on njoag.gov. I did not research county or municipal guidance more widely.

The portal's information and help pages list report prices but mention no convenience, service or card fee. I did not open checkout pages because the task is read-only. I found no statute or rule that sets the $13.00, $5.00 or $20.00 fees. Fees charged by municipal or county police departments were not confirmed.

I found no mail-in request form for State Police crash reports. The only written-request route found is for the Atlantic City Expressway. Serious/fatal records are mailed out to requesters, but the request itself is made online.
No official source found that describes requesting a crash report in person.

The portal's link for crashes older than six years (http://www.njsp.org/info/pdf/ucr/sp-275.pdf, which redirects to njsp.njoag.gov) returns 404 Not Found, so I could not confirm how to get older reports.

The NJTA OPRA form page (njta.com, which redirects to njta.gov) was blocked (HTTP 403). So the requirements, fee and timing for NJTR-1s of fatal Turnpike/Parkway crashes, and any Atlantic City Expressway fee or timing, were not confirmed.
The portal's later steps ('Crash Information', 'Requester', 'Review') can only be reached by submitting a form, so I could not see what requester details or ID are collected.
No official availability time frame was found for reports from municipal or county police departments.
No NJDOT or NJ MVC page found that says whether they give copies of individual police crash reports to the public.

I could not cross-check the SR-1 rules against N.J.S.A. 39:4-130 on an official statute site or the NJ MVC Driver Manual (the PDF is over 10 MB and would not download). The SR-1 Online (SimpliGov) page did not load. The SR-1 PDF is laid out in columns, so its raw text extraction mixes in words from the next column. The quotes from it follow the printed reading order.

WebSearch was not available for this run because the session search limit was reached. Official pages were found by following links from official state sites, so some relevant official pages may have been missed.

facts.quote: For Uniform Crash Report (UCR) requests from 2008-2013, you will need to provide the UCR number as this is the only searchable field in our system.

facts.claim: NMDOT asks requesters to give all the required information and warns that a request with too little information may not be processed.
facts.quote: please provide all required information listed below. Failure to supply sufficient information may result in your request not being processed or in your receiving unanticipated results.

facts.claim: A written public records (IPRA) request to NMDOT must include the requester's name, address and phone number, and must describe the records in enough detail to find them.
facts.quote: A written request must contain the name, address and telephone number of the person making the request. The request must describe the records sought in sufficient detail to enable the Records Custodian to identify and locate the requested records.

facts.claim: DPS does not charge for records provided electronically through its GovQA request portal.
facts.quote: A fee is not charged for records provided electronically through the GovQA request portal.

facts.claim: DPS charges $1.00 for the first page, $0.25 for each later page and $6.75 for discs for physical copies of records provided in person, by mail or by fax.
facts.quote: Physical copies of records provided in person, by mail, or by fax are subject to a copy fee of: $1.00 for the first page $0.25 for each subsequent page $6.75 for discs

facts.claim: DPS policy ADM: 38 sets the fee for accident and incident reports at one dollar ($1.00) for the first page and twenty-five cents ($.25) for each additional page.
facts.quote: The fee for accident and incident reports will be one dollar ($1.00) for the first page and twenty-five cents ($.25) for each additional page.

facts.claim: Under policy ADM: 38, you must pay before the report is released unless billing arrangements have been made.
facts.quote: Unless billing arrangements have been made, payment is required prior to the report being released.

facts.claim: NMDOT says it may charge if a request requires retrieving or manipulating information in its database, or copying a database for private or nonpublic use.
facts.quote: There may be a charge for the information requested if the request requires that information contained in the database be retrieved or manipulated or a copy of a database is made for private or nonpublic use.

facts.claim: NMDOT says it will tell requesters about any charges before it processes the request.
facts.quote: You will be notified of any charges prior to the processing of your request.

facts.claim: For copies of NMDOT public records requested under IPRA, NMDOT may charge a reasonable fee: $.25 per page for documents eleven by seventeen inches or smaller.
facts.quote: If a person requesting inspection would like a copy of public records, a reasonable fee may be charged. The fee for documents eleven inches by seventeen inches or smaller is $.25 per page.

facts.claim: NMDOT asks requesters to allow 15 business days for it to gather what it needs to fulfill a request.
facts.quote: Please allow 15 business days for our office to gather the information necessary to fulfill your request.

facts.claim: Section 66-7-207(C) NMSA 1978 requires the written crash report to be sent to the Department of Transportation within twenty-four hours after the investigation is completed.
facts.quote: shall, within twenty-four hours after completing the investigation, forward a written report of the accident to the department of transportation.

facts.claim: DPS policy says it will not turn down requests for original records of entry because they are 'not yet completed'. It will provide them, in whatever form they exist, within the 15-day limit set by Section 14-2-8(D).
facts.quote: DPS shall not deny requests for original records of entry on the grounds that the record(s) are "not yet completed", instead, within the 15-day time limit imposed by Section 14-2-8(D), DPS shall produce the records requested in whatever form they exist.

facts.claim: DPS releases these crash reports on a written or oral request (written is preferred) from any civilian, any law enforcement agency or officer, or any other agency.
facts.quote: Our department will release these reports upon a written or oral request (written is preferred) by any civilian, law enforcement agency or officer, and any other agency.

facts.claim: DPS's IPRA policy treats accident and traffic offense reports as 'original records of entry' as defined by the ARIA in Section 29-10-7(A)(2).
facts.quote: DPS shall treat 911 tapes, 911 transcripts, initial incident reports, initial offense reports, accident and traffic offense reports, radio tapes, dispatch tapes, radio logs, mug shots and CAD printouts as "original records of entry" as defined by the ARIA in Section 29-10-7(A)(2).

facts.claim: Under Section 66-7-213(A), accident reports made by people involved in crashes or by people in charge of garages are for the confidential use of the state highway and transportation department.
facts.quote: All accident reports made by persons involved in accidents or by persons in charge of garages shall be without prejudice to the individual so reporting and shall be for the confidential use of the state highway and transportation department

facts.claim: The annotations to Section 66-7-213 in the official statute compilation cite a 1959 Attorney General opinion that accident reports police officers make in their regular course of duty are public records.
facts.quote: Accident reports made by police officers as a part of their regular course of duty are considered public records. 1959 Op. Att'y Gen. No. 59-213.

facts.claim: The same annotations cite that 1959 opinion as saying an insurance adjuster getting accident reports is a lawful purpose, and that the reports cannot be limited to the parties involved or their attorneys.
facts.quote: Procurement of accident reports by an insurance adjuster constitutes a lawful purpose and one may not restrict the furnishing of these reports to only the parties involved or their attorneys. 1959 Op. Att'y Gen. No. 59-213.

facts.claim: Under IPRA, every person has the right to inspect NMDOT's public records, subject to certain exceptions and provisions.
facts.quote: every person has the right to inspect public records of the New Mexico Department of Transportation (NMDOT), subject to certain exceptions and provisions.

facts.claim: NMDOT's crash report request form asks for the VIN, the Uniform Crash Report number and the law enforcement agency that handled the crash.
facts.quote: Vin # Uniform Crash Report # Law Enforcement Agency that handled the crash

facts.claim: State law says crash notice goes to the city police department if the crash happens inside a municipality, and otherwise to the county sheriff's office or the nearest New Mexico State Police office.
facts.quote: give notice of the accident to the police department if the accident occurs within a municipality; otherwise to the office of the county sheriff or the nearest office of the New Mexico state police.

facts.claim: The New Mexico Department of Justice says the IPRA statute requires every New Mexico governmental entity, from the smallest municipality to the largest state agency, to post an IPRA notice on its website.
facts.quote: The IPRA statute requires every New Mexico governmental entity, from the smallest municipality to the largest state agency, to post a notice on their website similar to the one below.

facts.claim: A driver in a crash that causes bodily injury, death, or total property damage of an apparent $500 or more must send in a written report of the crash within five days.
facts.quote: The driver of a vehicle involved in an accident resulting in bodily injury to or death of any person or total property damage to an apparent extent of five hundred dollars ($500) or more shall, within five days after the accident, forward a written report of the accident

facts.claim: Under Section 66-7-207(A), that written report goes to the Department of Transportation.
facts.quote: within five days after the accident, forward a written report of the accident to the department of transportation.

facts.claim: State law requires immediate notice to police, by the quickest means of communication, of a crash that causes bodily injury, death, or apparent property damage of $500 or more.
facts.quote: involved in an accident resulting in bodily injury to or death of any person or property damage to an apparent extent of five hundred dollars ($500) or more shall immediately, by the quickest means of communication, give notice of the accident to the police department

facts.claim: A city, town, village or other municipality may pass an ordinance requiring drivers in a crash to also file a report, or a copy of the required state report, with a designated city department.
facts.quote: Any incorporated city, town, village or other municipality may by ordinance require that the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident shall also file with a designated city department a report of such accident or a copy of any report herein required to be filed with the division.

facts.claim: DPS says photos, dashcam footage, diagrams and other relevant information can also be requested if they are available.
facts.quote: If available, photos, dashcam, diagrams, and other pertinent information can also be requested.

facts.claim: Under 23 U.S.C. § 409, NMDOT and the State reserve the right to object if NMDOT's crash data, or opinions drawn from it, are used in an action for damages against NMDOT or the State.
facts.quote: If you should attempt to use this data in an action for damages against the NMDOT or the State, NMDOT and the State expressly reserve their right, under § 409, to object to the use of the data and including any opinions drawn from the data.

facts.claim: Under Section 66-7-213(D), in an arbitration or civil action over an insurer's liability under uninsured motorist coverage, the investigating agency must furnish a certified copy of the investigating officer's accident report to either party or to the court on request.
facts.quote: A certified copy of the investigating officer's accident report may be introduced into evidence in any arbitration or civil action involving the insurer's liability under a motor vehicle or automobile liability policy containing uninsured motorist coverage

facts.claim: For NMDOT public records (IPRA) requests, the Records Custodian will permit inspection immediately or as soon as practicable, and no later than 15 calendar days after receiving the written request, provided the request is not excessively burdensome or broad.
facts.quote: The Records Custodian will permit the inspection immediately or as soon as practicable, but no later than fifteen (15) calendar days after the Records Custodian receives the written request, provided the request is not excessively burdensome or broad

facts.claim: DPS says all invoices must be paid before it releases records.
facts.quote: ALL INVOICES MUST BE PAID PRIOR TO RELEASING RECORDS

facts.claim: DPS lists (505) 476-2400 as its direct phone number for Inspection of Public Records (IPRA) inquiries.
facts.quote: Inspection of Public Records (505)-476-2400 or File an IPRA

facts.claim: DPS policy ADM: 21 requires DPS to make original records of entry available for inspection and copying by the IPRA deadlines, with no redaction, omission or claim of exemption. The same policy says original records of entry include accident and traffic offense reports.
facts.quote: DPS shall make all such "original records of entry" available for inspection and copying on or before the deadlines imposed by IPRA without any redaction, omission or claim of exemption.

facts.claim: DPS policy ADM: 21 treats emailed and faxed requests as written requests.
facts.quote: DPS shall treat emails and facsimile requests as "written requests."

facts.claim: Under DPS policy ADM: 38, requests sent with the wrong fee are returned to the requester with a form letter explaining the problem.
facts.quote: Requests received with incorrect fees will be returned to the requestor with a form letter indicating what the problem is

facts.claim: For questions about public records requests, NMDOT's Records Custodian can be reached by phone at 505-469-0724 or by fax at 505-827-0662.
facts.quote: you may reach the Records Custodian at the email address above, or by phone or fax: Telephone number 505-469-0724 Fax number 505-827-0662

facts.claim: NMDOT charges $1.00 per page for copies of public records larger than eleven by seventeen inches.
facts.quote: The fee for larger documents is $1.00 per page.

facts.claim: If NMDOT does not allow inspection within three business days of receiving a written request, the requester gets a written response saying when the records will be available or when NMDOT will respond.
facts.quote: If inspection is not permitted within three (3) business days of receipt of a written request, the person making the request will receive a written response explaining when the records will be available for inspection or when the public body will respond to the request.

facts.claim: NMDOT's crash data request page says up to 15 business days are normally needed to fulfill data requests, and requesters will be told if more time is needed.
facts.quote: Up to 15 business days are normally required to fulfill data requests. You will be notified if additional time is needed.

facts.claim: NMDOT's crash data and crash report request form requires the requester's name, phone number, email, company or agency, and address.
facts.quote: Name (Required) First Last Phone (Required) Email (Required) Company/Agency (Required) Address (Required)

facts.claim: Under the state records retention schedule (1.21.2.927 NMAC), law enforcement records related to accident reports involving fatalities are kept until 25 years after the file is closed.
facts.quote: Description: Records related to accident reports and incidents involving fatalities. C. Retention: destroy 25 years from date file closed

facts.claim: Under 1.21.2.926 NMAC, other law enforcement accident and incident report records are kept until 10 years after the file is closed.
facts.quote: Description: Records related to accident reports and incidents. C. Retention: destroy 10 years from date file closed

facts.claim: The annotations to Section 66-7-213 also cite a 1953 Attorney General opinion. It says police officers' accident reports are not confidential and are open to inspection by interested persons, because the confidentiality rule covers only reports made by people involved in crashes or by garages.
facts.quote: Since the reports made confidential are limited to those made by persons involved in accidents or by garages, the reports made by police officers regarding an accident would not be considered confidential and would be subject to inspection by persons interested.

facts.claim: Section 66-7-213(B) says that, except as otherwise provided in that section, no accident report may be used as evidence in any civil or criminal trial arising out of an accident.
facts.quote: Except as otherwise provided in this section, no accident report shall be used as evidence in any trial, civil or criminal, arising out of an accident.

facts.claim: Under Section 66-7-208(B), if the driver is physically unable to make the required written report and is not the vehicle's owner, the owner must make the report within five days after learning of the crash.
facts.quote: the driver is physically incapable of making a written report of an accident as required in Section 66-7-207 NMSA 1978 and such driver is not the owner of the vehicle, then the owner of the vehicle involved in such accident shall within five days after learning of the accident make such report

facts.claim: Section 66-7-207(C) also requires the investigating officer to send the written report to the DPS Motor Transportation Division within 24 hours after completing the investigation, when the crash involves a commercial motor vehicle and has one of the results listed in that subsection.
facts.quote: A law enforcement officer shall also, within twenty-four hours after completing the investigation, forward the written report of the accident to the motor transportation division of the department of public safety if the accident involves a commercial motor vehicle and results in:

facts.claim: The Albuquerque Police Department sells its crash reports online through Carfax for Police, at $7.50 per report.
facts.quote: To improve the processing and delivery of crash reports, the Albuquerque Police Department contracts with Carfax for Police to manage and distribute its reports online. Online traffic accident reports cost $7.50 per report.

facts.claim: APD traffic accident reports can also be picked up in person at the Law Enforcement Center, 400 Roma NW, Albuquerque, from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday.
facts.quote: Traffic accident reports also can be obtained in person from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday at the Law Enforcement Center: 400 Roma NW Albuquerque, NM

gaps.reason: The DPS GovQA Records Request Portal returned HTTP 403 to every automated fetch, including the fallback fetcher. Its request categories, required fields, delivery method and any fees inside the portal could not be checked.

The DPS pages I read don't list what an accident report request needs, such as a report number, crash date, names or ID. The 'IPRA Written Request Form' the DPS page mentions isn't linked there, and no email address is given for emailed requests.
No official source I read gives a walk-in location or hours for requesting NMSP/MTPD crash reports from DPS in person. The DPS page lists only a P.O. box, a fax number and the online portal.

NMDOT doesn't give a specific fee for a copy of a Uniform Crash Report. It says only that there 'may be a charge' and that requesters will be told before processing. NMDOT's general IPRA copy fee ($.25 per page) isn't confirmed to apply to crash report copies. Neither agency mentions a convenience or card fee.

No official source says how soon after a crash a report is usually available to the public. What I found: the statutory 24-hour deadline for sending the report to NMDOT after the investigation, NMDOT's request to allow 15 business days, and the 15-day IPRA response limits.

No state source says outright whether NMDOT will release crash reports written by city police or county sheriffs, or tells requesters to ask the local agency instead. NMDOT's form only asks which agency handled the crash. Local agencies' own request steps and fees weren't researched because the web search budget was used up.

No official form name, form link or submission method was found for the driver's written report that Section 66-7-207(A) requires within five days. NMDOT's traffic records pages don't describe a driver report form, and the NM MVD website (mvd.newmexico.gov) returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching.

No official source was found that limits police crash report copies to involved parties or sets a confidentiality or waiting period. NMDOT's request form doesn't say who may ask for a copy of a Uniform Crash Report.

WebSearch was unavailable for this run because the shared search budget was already used up, so I reached official pages by navigating official sites and site maps directly. Official pages that aren't linked from the DPS, NMDOT, NMDOJ or NMOneSource pages may have been missed. The DPS policy PDFs (ADM: 38 and ADM: 21) are scanned images, so those quotes were transcribed from the page images.

facts.claim: Nevada's Department of Public Safety tells people who want a copy of an accident report under NRS 480.600 to contact the local Highway Patrol office for the area where the accident occurred.
facts.quote: To request a copy of an accident report pursuant to NRS 480.600, please contact your local Highway Patrol office, in which area the accident occurred.

facts.claim: Under its Nevada Highway Patrol Accident Reports heading, the DPS page lists 702-668-4100 for the Las Vegas Area office.
facts.quote: Las Vegas Area 702-668-4100

facts.claim: Under the same heading, the DPS page lists 775-687-9600 for the Reno Area office.
facts.quote: Reno Area 775-687-9600

facts.claim: Under the same heading, the DPS page lists 775-753-1111 for the Elko Area office.
facts.quote: Elko Area 775-753-1111

facts.claim: Nevada's Records, Communications and Compliance Division does not maintain traffic accident reports or traffic citations.
facts.quote: The Records, Communications and Compliance Division does not maintain traffic accident reports or traffic citations.

facts.claim: Nevada's records division tells people to get copies of accident reports from the law enforcement agency that investigated the accident.
facts.quote: Please contact the law enforcement agency that investigated the accident or issued the citation for copies of these documents.

facts.claim: When law enforcement investigates a crash, the investigating officer sends your insurance information and a description of damages or injuries to the Nevada DMV.
facts.quote: If you are in a crash that is investigated by law enforcement, your insurance information and a description of damages or injuries will be sent to the DMV by the investigating officer.

facts.claim: The Nevada Driver Handbook says that if law enforcement did not investigate a crash and it caused $750 or more in damages or anyone was injured, you must complete and send a Report of Crash Form (SR-1) within 10 days.
facts.quote: If you are in a crash that is not investigated by law enforcement and the crash causes $750 or more in damages or anyone is injured, you must complete and send a Report of Crash Form (SR-1) within 10 days

facts.claim: The handbook says to send the SR-1 to the Nevada Department of Motor Vehicles Central Services Division, Financial Responsibility Section, 555 Wright Way, Carson City, NV 89711-0400.
facts.quote: Nevada Department of Motor Vehicles Central Services Division — Financial Responsibility Section 555 Wright Way Carson City, NV 89711-0400

facts.claim: The Nevada DMV forms page says Form SR 1 must be filed within 10 days of any accident that was not investigated at the scene by law enforcement and that caused injury, death or more than $750 damage.
facts.quote: You must file this form within 10 days of any accident which was: (1) not investigated at the scene by law enforcement and (2) caused injury, death or more than $750 damage

facts.claim: The SR-1 form itself says it must be completed within 10 days after a crash in Nevada that law enforcement did not investigate at the scene.
facts.quote: Pursuant to NRS 484E.070, this SR-1 report needs to be completed within 10 days after a crash that occurred in the State of Nevada and was NOT investigated at the scene by law enforcement.

facts.claim: You must complete the SR-1 if you were either the driver or the registered owner of the vehicle.
facts.quote: You must complete the crash report form (SR-1) if you are either the driver or the registered owner of the vehicle.

facts.claim: The SR-1 is void unless it includes a copy of the insurance that covered the vehicle on the date of the crash.
facts.quote: THE FOLLOWING ATTACHMENTS MUST BE INCLUDED (this SR-1 report will be considered VOID if not attached): (1) a copy of your insurance that was in effect on the date of the crash for the vehicle involved;

facts.claim: You must attach an estimate of repairs or a statement of total loss to the SR-1 if any one person had $750 or more in vehicle or property damage.
facts.quote: An Estimate of Repairs or a Statement of Total Loss must be attached if there was $750 or more in vehicle or property damage (of any one person).

facts.claim: If the crash caused bodily injury or death, the SR-1 must include a doctor's statement of injury for each person injured in your vehicle.
facts.quote: (3) a doctor’s statement of injury for each person injured in your vehicle (if the crash resulted in bodily injury or death).

facts.claim: Once the SR-1 is complete, you sign it on the second page, attach the required documents and mail it to the DMV.
facts.quote: Once completed, please sign your name on the second page, attach all required documents, and mail the complete report to the DMV at the above address.

facts.claim: If the DMV asks for an SR-1 and you do not submit it, your driving privilege may be suspended for up to one year.
facts.quote: Failure to submit this report after it has been requested by the Department of Motor Vehicles may result in the suspension of your driving privilege for up to one year (per NRS 484E.080).

facts.claim: If you do not report a crash to the Nevada DMV, your driver license, your vehicle registration or both may be suspended.
facts.quote: If you do not report a crash to the Department of Motor Vehicles, your driver license and/or your vehicle registration may be suspended.

facts.claim: You can get the SR-1 form from any DMV office, the Nevada Highway Patrol, a local law enforcement agency or the DMV website.
facts.quote: You can get a report form from any DMV office, the Nevada Highway Patrol, a local law enforcement agency or the DMV website at dmv.nv.gov.

facts.claim: Completing an SR-1 authorizes the DMV to release your name, mailing address and insurance information to the other parties in the crash or to their insurer.
facts.quote: By completing this report, you are authorizing the Department of Motor Vehicles to release your name, mailing address, and insurance information to the other parties involved in the traffic crash and/or to their insurer (Nevada Revised Statute 484E.070).

facts.claim: The SR-1 says the DMV cannot accept or process the report unless all information has been completed for all drivers and vehicles involved in the crash.
facts.quote: This report cannot be accepted or processed unless ALL information has been completed for ALL DRIVERS AND VEHICLES that were involved in the crash.

facts.claim: The DMV will not keep an SR-1 that is incomplete or that does not meet the requirements of NRS 484E.070.
facts.quote: Any SR-1 report that is incomplete or does not meet the requirements of NRS 484E.070, as specified above, will not be retained by the Department.

facts.claim: The SR-1 says the estimate of repairs or statement of total loss must come from an established repair garage, an insurance adjuster employed by an insurer licensed to do business in Nevada, an adjuster licensed under NRS Chapter 684A, or an appraiser licensed under NRS Chapter 684B.
facts.quote: must be from an established repair garage, an insurance adjuster employed by an insurer licensed to do business in the State of Nevada, an adjuster licensed pursuant to Chapter 684A of Nevada Revised Statute, or an appraiser licensed pursuant to Chapter 684B of Nevada Revised Statute.

facts.claim: If more than two vehicles were involved, the SR-1 asks you to give the additional driver and vehicle information on a separate page.
facts.quote: If more than two vehicles were involved, please provide the additional driver and vehicle information on a separate page.

facts.claim: The SR-1 is void if it is not signed.
facts.quote: *** Void if not signed ***

facts.claim: The SR-1 says anyone who completes it knowing or having reason to believe the information is false is guilty of a gross misdemeanor, citing NRS 484E.080.
facts.quote: I agree and understand any person who completes this report knowing or having reason to believe the information is false is guilty of a gross misdemeanor. (Nevada Revised Statute 484E.080)

facts.claim: The SR-1 warns that if insurance was not in effect on the date of the crash, your driving privilege and registration may be suspended under NRS Chapter 485.
facts.quote: If insurance was not in effect on the date of the crash, your driving privilege and registration may be suspended under Chapter 485 of Nevada Revised Statutes.

facts.claim: The SR-1's header gives the DMV's address as 555 Wright Way, Carson City, NV 89711, with phone numbers (775) 684-4368 for Reno/Carson City and (702) 486-4368 for Las Vegas.
facts.quote: 555 Wright Way Carson City, NV 89711 Reno/Carson City (775) 684-4DMV (4368) Las Vegas (702) 486-4DMV (4368) dmv.nv.gov

facts.claim: On the Nevada DMV's DLD-68 Failure to Report a Vehicle Crash Affidavit, you swear that you did not willfully fail to report the crash to the DMV's Central Services, Financial Responsibility section.
facts.quote: I, the undersigned, being first duly sworn, depose and state: 1. I did not willfully fail to report the above-mentioned crash to the Department of Motor Vehicles, Central Services, Financial Responsibility.

facts.claim: The Nevada Driver Handbook says that for any crash, the DMV Financial Responsibility Section determines who was at fault, whether all vehicles or drivers were insured, and the total amount of liability.
facts.quote: For any crash, the DMV Financial Responsibility Section determines: — Who was at fault — If all vehicles or drivers were insured — The total amount of liability

gaps.reason: No online ordering option could be confirmed. The NHP crash report request page (https://nhp.nv.gov/Reports/Crash_Report_Request, found in search results) and the rest of nhp.nv.gov returned 'Request Rejected' to WebFetch, direct HTTP, a stealth fetcher and a real browser. Any vendor portal NHP may name (search results mention CARFAX Crashdocs at crashdocs.org) could not be checked against an official page. The DPS general online public records system (nevadadps.govqa.us) returned 403, and the DPS page does not say it handles accident reports. It sends accident report requests to the local Highway Patrol office instead.

No official page that could be read gives a mail-in process or form for NHP crash reports. The DPS page's general Public Records Request form covers DPS records in general, not accident reports specifically, so it is not reported as the crash report route.

The DPS page gives only phone numbers for the Las Vegas, Reno and Elko area Highway Patrol offices. No office addresses or opening hours for in-person crash report requests were confirmed on a readable official page.

What NHP requires for a crash report request could not be confirmed because the NHP request page was blocked. Unofficial search snippets say a crash number starting with 'NHP', an involved party's last name and the crash date; this needs checking.

No official fee for an NHP crash report could be confirmed. NRS 480.600 (leg.state.nv.us) returned Cloudflare 403 to every fetch, and the NHP request page was blocked. Unofficial search snippets say $10 per report and $5 for photos; this is unverified. The DPS 'actual cost' fee schedule covers general public records requests and does not mention accident reports.
No readable official source says how soon reports are available. Unofficial search snippets of the blocked NHP page say 7-14 days from the crash date; this is unverified.

NRS 480.600 sets who may get NHP crash reports, witness statements and photos, and what is excluded. The Nevada Legislature site (leg.state.nv.us and archive.leg.state.nv.us) returned 403 to every fetch method, so eligibility and any exceptions (for example fatal or hit-and-run crashes) could not be confirmed.

No official page that could be read says whether NHP's records include reports written by city police or county sheriffs. The DPS page covers only NHP accident reports under NRS 480.600. The state records division says only to contact the agency that investigated the crash. No statewide repository of report copies was found.

Procedures, fees and portals for local agencies (for example the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department or the Reno, Henderson and North Las Vegas police, and county sheriffs) were not researched. Their sites are not state government sources under the task rules.

NRS 484E.070 itself could not be read (leg.state.nv.us blocked), so the self-report facts come from DMV publications. Their damage threshold wording differs: the DMV forms page says 'more than $750 damage', while the SR-1 form and the Driver Handbook say '$750 or more'. The statute would settle which is right.

The shared WebSearch budget for this run ran out after two searches, so no further official Nevada pages could be searched for. Other *.nv.gov sites behind the same firewall also refused access, including ots.nv.gov and doi.nv.gov. A follow-up from a US connection, or a new run with more search budget, is needed to verify the NHP request page and NRS 480.600.
