facts.claim: The New York State Police says insurance companies routinely obtain copies of Police Accident Reports (form MV-104A) from the New York State Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) as part of the insurance claim process.
facts.quote: Insurance companies routinely obtain copies of Police Accident Reports (form MV-104A) from the New York State Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) as part of the insurance claim process.

facts.claim: The New York State Police page says that if a person is injured or killed, all the involved drivers and the police must file an accident report with the DMV.
facts.quote: If a person is injured or killed, immediately notify the police. All the involved drivers and the police must file an accident report with the DMV.

facts.claim: The New York State Police page says police departments other than the New York State Police submit Police Accident Reports to DMV, and those reports may or may not be submitted electronically.
facts.quote: Police Accident Reports submitted to DMV by police departments other than the New York State Police may or may not be submitted electronically, therefore, these guidelines may not be applicable.

facts.claim: Requests for copies of an MV-104A for collisions investigated by the New York State Police anywhere in New York State on roads or highways other than the Thruway must be made to DMV on form MV-198C.
facts.quote: Requests for copies of an MV-104A for collisions investigated by the New York State Police that occurred anywhere in New York State on roads or highways other than the Thruway must be made to DMV. The form required (MV-198C) to request a copy of the report is available online at: www.dmv.ny.gov.

facts.claim: NYPD holds collision reports at the precinct for 30 days before forwarding them to the New York State Commissioner of Motor Vehicles.
facts.quote: Collision Reports are held at the precinct for 30 days before being forwarded to the New York State Commissioner of Motor Vehicles.

facts.claim: DMV's online sales portal does not offer reports of crashes where no one was hurt and there was no property damage over $1,000 in value.
facts.quote: Reports of crashes where no one was hurt and where there was no property damage over $1,000 in value are not available for search or sale through this online transaction.

facts.claim: For crashes with no injuries and no property damage over $1,000, DMV says you can request the reports online using the Record Request Navigator or by mailing a completed form MV-198C.
facts.quote: You can request these reports online using the Record Request Navigator or you can mail a completed Request for Copy of Crash Report (PDF) (MV-198C) to the address listed on the form.

facts.claim: Reports of crashes involving e-bikes and e-scooters are also not available for search or sale through DMV's online portal.
facts.quote: Reports of crashes involving e-bikes and e-scooters are also not available for search or sale through this online transaction.

facts.claim: Form MV-198C is for use only for crashes that happen in New York State.
facts.quote: Use only for crashes that happen in New York State.

facts.claim: The New York State Thruway Authority's request form is for accidents that occurred on the New York State Thruway System only.
facts.quote: Purpose: This Request is completed for accidents that occurred on the New York State Thruway System only*.

facts.claim: DMV says you can search, purchase, and immediately download certified crash reports online.
facts.quote: You can search, purchase, and immediately download certified crash reports online.

facts.claim: DMV's page gives two paths into its Order Crash Reports Online Portal, depending on whether you already have an NY.gov ID.
facts.quote: There are two different paths to get to the Order Crash Reports Online Portal, depending on whether you already have an NY.gov ID or not.

facts.claim: After paying in DMV's portal, you can download your reports in PDF format inside the portal.
facts.quote: After you pay, you will be able to download your reports (in PDF format) inside the portal itself

facts.claim: DMV gives you 7 calendar days to access reports you purchased online, after which you must purchase them again.
facts.quote: You will have 7 calendar days to access reports you already purchased online. After 7 days, you will need to purchase the reports again.

facts.claim: DMV's Records Request Navigator lets you order a certified copy of a crash report online if you cannot use the online portal or would prefer a DMV agent to perform the search.
facts.quote: You can still order a certified copy of a crash report online if you are unable to use the method above or if you would prefer an agent of the DMV perform the search for you.

facts.claim: If DMV cannot find a crash based on the information you provide, it will notify you by certified letter.
facts.quote: If DMV cannot find a crash based on the information you provide, we will notify you by certified letter.

facts.claim: NYPD says you can request a collision report online using its Collision Report Retrieval Portal, which allows motorists to access collision reports taken after September 30, 2016.
facts.quote: You can also request a collision report online using the Collision Report Retrieval Portal. This online resource allows motorists to access collision reports taken after September 30, 2016.

facts.claim: The NYPD Collision Report Retrieval Portal has you submit information to receive an email with a verification PIN.
facts.quote: Submit the following information to receive an email with your verification PIN #.

facts.claim: DMV accepts crash report orders by mail on the Request for Copy of Crash Report (MV-198C) and says to fill out as much information as possible.
facts.quote: You may order a copy of a crash report by mail using the Request for Copy of Crash Report (PDF) (MV-198C). You must fill out as much information as possible.

facts.claim: Form MV-198C says to mail the completed form, payment and ID to NYSDMV, MV-198C Processing, 6 Empire State Plaza, Albany NY 12228.
facts.quote: Mail completed form, payment and ID to: NYSDMV, MV-198C Processing, 6 Empire State Plaza, Albany NY 12228

facts.claim: Form MV-198C lists payment by check or money order payable to the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles.
facts.quote: Check/Money Order - Payable to Commissioner of Motor Vehicles

facts.claim: NYPD says you can download and complete two copies of the Request for Copy of Collision Record and either mail them to the precinct of occurrence or drop them off in person at the precinct.
facts.quote: You can download and complete two copies of the Police Collision Report (Request for Copy of Collision Record), and either mail them to the precinct of occurrence or drop them off in person at the precinct.

facts.claim: NYPD's mail-in instructions say to enclose a stamped, self-addressed 9½ x 4 inch envelope.
facts.quote: Enclose a stamped, self-addressed 9½”x4” envelope.

facts.claim: The Thruway Authority's request form gives its address as New York State Thruway Authority, Department #116251, P.O. Box 5211, Binghamton, NY 13902.
facts.quote: New York State Thruway Authority Department #116251 P.O. Box 5211 Binghamton, NY 13902

facts.claim: NYPD says you may request a copy of the report at the precinct where the collision occurred during the first 30 days from when the report was filed.
facts.quote: If your motor vehicle has been involved in an collision, you may request a copy of the report at the precinct where the collision occurred during the first 30 days from when the report was filed.

facts.claim: NYPD's request form says to call 646-610-5000 or the local precinct for the precinct mailing address, and that you may also appear in person at the precinct to obtain a copy.
facts.quote: MAIL TO: Pct. of Occurrence. Call 646-610-5000 or local Pct. for Precinct Mailing Address. You may also appear in person at precinct to obtain copy.

facts.claim: NYPD's request form says forms prepared only in fatal motor vehicle collisions are requested by mail from the NYPD Highway District Collision Investigation Squad, 198-15 Grand Central Parkway, Hollis, Queens, N.Y. 11423.
facts.quote: (Above forms prepared in FATAL motor vehicle collisions only). MAIL TO: New York City Police Department Highway District Collision Investigation Squad 198-15 Grand Central Parkway Hollis, Queens, N.Y. 11423

facts.claim: The Thruway Authority accepts requests at its mailing address or by e-mail to accidentreport@thruway.ny.gov, and e-mailed requests must pay the fee by credit card.
facts.quote: Send completed Request and search fee to the above address or via e-mail to accidentreport@thruway.ny.gov. (Requests sent by e-mail require fee to be paid by credit card. This form must be signed below to process credit card.)

facts.claim: The New York State Police page says certain requests must be made to the New York State Thruway Authority, and that form TA-W4310 for requesting a copy of the report is available at www.thruway.ny.gov.
facts.quote: must be made to New York State Thruway Authority. The form required (TA-W4310) to request a copy of the report is available online at: www.thruway.ny.gov.

facts.claim: To search DMV's online portal you need at least one of these to start: DMV case number (an 8-digit number), local police code, date of crash, county of crash, Vehicle Identification Number (VIN), plate number of one of the involved vehicles, or driver license number.
facts.quote: To search for a report, you need at least one of the following to start: DMV case number (an 8-digit number) Local police code Date of crash County of crash Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) Plate number of one of the involved vehicles Driver license number

facts.claim: DMV says some of these online search fields require at least one other piece of information to continue the search.
facts.quote: Some of these fields will require at least one other piece of information to continue with your search.

facts.claim: For Records Request Navigator orders, DMV says you must provide the date of the crash and the county where it occurred, plus at least one of: the plate number of an involved vehicle, the driver license number of an involved person, or the name and date of birth of an involved person.
facts.quote: You must provide the date of the crash county where the crash occurred and at least one of the following the plate number of a vehicle involved in the crash driver license number of a person who was involved in the crash name and date of birth of a person who was involved in the crash

facts.claim: Form MV-198C requires a copy of your valid government-issued ID.
facts.quote: Attach a copy of your valid government-issued ID

facts.claim: NYPD's mail-in instructions say to enclose a photocopy of a current, valid form of picture identification, such as a driver's license or passport.
facts.quote: Enclose a photocopy of a current, valid form of picture identification (driver’s license, passport etc.).

facts.claim: NYPD's request form says sections 2 and 4 must be completed in all cases or the request will be returned.
facts.quote: NOTE: Sections 2 and 4 MUST be completed in all cases or your request will be returned.

facts.claim: The NYPD portal's request form asks for the collision date and the borough of occurrence.
facts.quote: Collision Date Borough of Occurrence

facts.claim: The NYPD portal's request form also asks for a driver license number, date of birth, license plate number and license plate state.
facts.quote: Driver License # Date of Birth License Plate # License Plate State

facts.claim: DMV's online portal charges both a $7.00 search fee and a $15.00 report fee for each report, charged at the same time.
facts.quote: You must pay both a $7.00 search fee and a $15.00 report fee for each report. You will be charged for both of these fees at the same time and receive a single confirmation email.

facts.claim: Ordering through DMV's Records Request Navigator costs a $10 search fee and a $15 report fee for each report.
facts.quote: You must pay a $10 search fee and a $15 report fee for each report you order.

facts.claim: Form MV-198C says to include $15 for each report requested plus the $10 non-refundable search fee.
facts.quote: NOTE: Be sure to include $15 for each report being requested PLUS the $10 non-refundable search fee.

facts.claim: Vehicle and Traffic Law § 202 sets the fee for a copy of an accident report at fifteen dollars, with copies certified at no additional fee.
facts.quote: The fee for a copy of an accident report shall be fifteen dollars. All copies of documents shall be certified at no additional fee.

facts.claim: Vehicle and Traffic Law § 202 sets the fee for a search made manually by the department at ten dollars, effective until April 1, 2028.
facts.quote: The fee for a search which is made manually by the department shall be ten dollars. * NB Effective until April 1, 2028

facts.claim: A version of Vehicle and Traffic Law § 202 effective April 1, 2028 sets the fee for a search made manually by the department at five dollars.
facts.quote: The fee for a search which is made manually by the department shall be five dollars. * NB Effective April 1, 2028

facts.claim: Public Officers Law § 66-a requires the division of state police to charge a search fee of fifteen dollars per accident report, with no additional fee for a photocopy.
facts.quote: the division of state police shall charge fees for the search and copy of accident reports and photographs. A search fee of fifteen dollars per accident report shall be charged, with no additional fee for a photocopy.

facts.claim: Public Officers Law § 66-a(2) sets an additional fee of fifteen dollars for a certified copy of any accident report.
facts.quote: An additional fee of fifteen dollars shall be charged for a certified copy of any accident report.

facts.claim: The Thruway Authority requires a non-refundable $15.00 search fee payable to New York State Thruway Authority by check, money order (U.S. Currency) or credit card.
facts.quote: A non-refundable $15.00 search fee payable to "New York State Thruway Authority" by check, money order (U.S. Currency) or credit card is required to process your Request.

facts.claim: The Thruway Authority charges a $25.00 returned check fee.
facts.quote: There is a $25.00 returned check fee.

facts.claim: DMV says an electronically filed police report from one of the 5 boroughs of New York City enters its system at least 14 days after the crash, a paper police report at least 30 days after, and a motorist report from anywhere in New York State at least 60 days after.
facts.quote: FILING METHOD REPORT ENTERS SYSTEM Electronically filed police report in one of the 5 boroughs of New York City at least 14 days after crash Paper police report at least 30 days after crash Motorist report from anywhere in New York State at least 60 days after crash

facts.claim: The New York State Police says all its Police Accident Reports are submitted electronically and are generally available within thirty days, though several variables affect when a report is available to the public.
facts.quote: Although all Police Accident Reports completed by the New York State Police are submitted electronically and are generally available within thirty days, there are several variables that affect the time in which the report is available to the public.

facts.claim: The New York State Police says some reports may be available within three weeks while others may take as long as six weeks to process.
facts.quote: Consequently, some reports may be available within three weeks while others may take as long as six weeks to process.

facts.claim: NYPD says it may take up to seven business days from the date of the incident for a report to be accessible on its online portal.
facts.quote: Please note that it may take up to seven business days from date of the incident for your report to be accessible on this portal.

facts.claim: Form MV-198C says to allow up to 5 business days for processing when ordering at dmv.ny.gov/rrn.
facts.quote: Visit dmv.ny.gov/rrn. Allow up to 5 business days for processing.

facts.claim: The Thruway Authority's form says reports may not be immediately available and to allow 4 weeks for processing.
facts.quote: Reports may not be immediately available. Please allow 4 weeks for processing.

facts.claim: DMV's online portal asks you to certify that you are legally authorized to obtain the report you are looking for.
facts.quote: Once you have enough information entered to perform a search, you will be asked to certify you are legally authorized to obtain the report you are looking for.

facts.claim: Form MV-198C must be signed on page 2, and the requester must select all applicable permissible uses under the Driver's Privacy Protection Act.
facts.quote: Complete this form and sign page 2. Be sure to select all applicable permissible uses per the Driver’s Privacy Protection Act.

facts.claim: Public Officers Law § 66-a opens accident reports and records kept by the state police or by any county, city, town, village or other district police department to inspection by any person having an interest in them, or that person's attorney or agent.
facts.quote: all reports and records of any accident, kept or maintained by the state police or by the police department or force of any county, city, town, village or other district of the state, shall be open to the inspection of any person having an interest therein, or of such person's attorney or agent

facts.claim: Under Public Officers Law § 66-a, the authorities holding accident reports may withhold any report whose disclosure would interfere with their investigation or prosecution of a crime connected with the accident.
facts.quote: may withhold from inspection any reports or records the disclosure of which would interfere with the investigation or prosecution by such authorities of a crime involved in or connected with the accident.

facts.claim: One of the requester statements on the Thruway Authority's form is that the requester is named in the accident report.
facts.quote: I am named in this accident report

facts.claim: DMV says one way to get a copy of your crash report is to call or visit the local police agency or precinct where the crash occurred and ask if the report is available and what the fee is.
facts.quote: Call or visit the local police agency or precinct where the crash occurred. Ask the agency if your report is available and what the fee is, or

facts.claim: DMV says that if the police and/or motorists' reports have already been filed and processed by the DMV, you can get PDF copies of the crash reports.
facts.quote: If the police and/or motorists' reports have already been filed and processed by the DMV, see how to get PDF copies of crash reports.

facts.claim: The New York State Police says motorists requesting an MV-104A submitted by another police department should follow the page's For Collisions on all Other Roads instructions or contact the investigating police agency directly.
facts.quote: Motorists requesting a copy of an MV-104A submitted by a police department other than the New York State Police should follow the instructions contained in paragraph above entitled, “For Collisions on all Other Roads” or contact the investigating police agency directly.

facts.claim: NYPD says that after 30 days from the date of the collision report, all requests must be made to the New York State Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) on form MV-198C.
facts.quote: After 30 days from the date of the collision report, all requests must be made to the New York State Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) on New York DMV form MV-198C.

facts.claim: Public Officers Law § 66-a authorizes Nassau County, upon adopting a local law, to require the Nassau County police department to charge a search fee of ten dollars per accident report.
facts.quote: the county of Nassau, upon adoption of a local law, is hereby authorized to require the police department of the county of Nassau to charge fees for the search and copy of accident reports and photographs. A search fee of ten dollars per accident report shall be charged

facts.claim: DMV says you must file a report of your motor vehicle crash if a person is injured or killed, if there is damage to the property of one individual (including yourself) that exceeds $1,000, or if an e-bike or e-scooter is involved and a person is injured or killed.
facts.quote: you must file a report of your motor vehicle crash if any of the following occurred: a person is injured or killed, there is damage to the property of one individual (including yourself) that exceeds $1,000, or an e-bike or e-scooter is involved and a person is injured or killed.

facts.claim: Vehicle and Traffic Law § 605 requires a written report to the commissioner within ten days after an accident in which any person is killed or injured or property damage to any one person exceeds one thousand dollars.
facts.quote: in which any person is killed or injured, or in which damage to the property of any one person, including himself, in excess of one thousand dollars is sustained, shall within ten days after such accident, report the matter in writing to the commissioner.

facts.claim: Form MV-104 says you must report within 10 days any crash occurring in New York State causing a fatality, personal injury or damage over $1,000 to the property of any one person.
facts.quote: You must report within 10 days any crash occurring in New York State causing a fatality, personal injury or damage over $1,000 to the property of any one person.

facts.claim: Form MV-104 says failing to report within 10 days is a misdemeanor and your license and/or registration may be suspended until a report is filed.
facts.quote: Failure to do so within 10 days is a misdemeanor. Your license and/or registration may be suspended until a report is filed.

facts.claim: DMV says that if you do not file a crash report, it may suspend your driving privilege until the report is on file.
facts.quote: If you do not file a crash report, DMV may suspend your driving privilege until the report is on file.

facts.claim: DMV offers an Online Motorist Crash Report Portal for filing, with separate paths depending on whether you already have an NY.gov ID.
facts.quote: There are two different paths to get to the Online Motorist Crash Report Portal, depending on whether you already have an NY.gov ID or not.

facts.claim: DMV says you can complete and mail the Report of Motor Vehicle Crash (MV-104) to the address listed on page two of the form.
facts.quote: Complete and mail the Report of Motor Vehicle Crash (PDF) (MV-104) form to the address listed on page two of the form.

facts.claim: Form MV-104 says to send the original to the Crash Records Center, 6 Empire State Plaza, PO Box 2925, Albany, NY 12220-0925.
facts.quote: Send original to: CRASH RECORDS CENTER, 6 EMPIRE STATE PLAZA, PO BOX 2925, ALBANY, NY 12220-0925

facts.claim: DMV's Online Motorist Report Submission Portal walks you through determining whether your crash requires an MV-104 motorist crash report.
facts.quote: The following steps will guide you in determining if your crash requires an MV-104 motorist crash report.

facts.claim: NYPD says you must still file a Report of Motor Vehicle Crash (MV-104) with the DMV even if police take a Police Crash Report (MV-104P) at the scene, if a report is required.
facts.quote: Must I still file a Report of Motor Vehicle Crash (MV-104) with the DMV even if a Police Crash Report (MV-104P) is taken at the scene by law enforcement? Yes, if a report is required (see above).

facts.claim: NYPD says vehicle collisions resulting only in property damage are not required to be reported to the police.
facts.quote: Vehicle collisions resulting only in property damage are not required to be reported to the police.

facts.claim: The State Police says requests for reports of Thruway collisions investigated by State Police Troop T go to the Thruway Authority. This covers I-87 south of Albany, I-90 west of Albany, the Berkshire Spur east of Albany, I-190, and the Westchester County portions of I-287 and I-95.
facts.quote: (Troop T) that occurred on the New York State Thruway (I-87 South of Albany, I-90 West of Albany & the Berkshire Spur East of Albany) and its subsidiary arterials (I-190 and Westchester County portions of both I-287 & I-95) must be made to New York State Thruway Authority.

facts.claim: On the Thruway Authority's form, you choose to receive the report by mail or by e-mail. E-mailed reports are PDFs.
facts.quote: Report should be sent to me by (choose one): Mail - Provide address Report should be sent to (if different than above). Address: E-mail - Reports sent via e-mail are in .PDF format.

facts.claim: The Thruway Authority's form gives (518) 471-4450 as the number to call with questions.
facts.quote: For questions, please call (518) 471-4450.

facts.claim: Form MV-198C asks whether you want the certified record delivered electronically through a secure portal or by USPS mail.
facts.quote: How do you want to receive your certified record? Electronically (from a secure portal) By USPS Mail

facts.claim: Form MV-198C says not to send cash.
facts.quote: Select payment method (Do Not Send Cash):

facts.claim: DMV says people without an NY.gov ID, such as out-of-state residents, can use the Records Request Navigator without logging in.
facts.quote: If you don't have an NY.gov ID, such as if you live in another state, you can use the Records Request Navigator without logging in.

facts.claim: In DMV's online portal, anyone looking for several reports must repeat the legal-authorization certification for each new search.
facts.quote: For those looking for multiple reports, you will need to complete this certification for every new search.

facts.claim: NYPD's Request for Copy of Collision Record needs a separate application for each record you want.
facts.quote: FOR EACH RECORD DESIRED, A SEPARATE APPLICATION IS REQUIRED

facts.claim: NYPD's mail-in instructions say the information must be typed or printed and that incomplete information may get the application returned.
facts.quote: Information MUST be typed or printed. Incomplete information may result in the return of your application

facts.claim: In collisions investigated by NYPD's Highway District Collision Investigation Squad (critical injury or fatal), the investigator contacts next of kin and gives them a free copy of the collision report at the start of the investigation.
facts.quote: The Highway District Collision Investigation Squad member investigating the collision will make an initial contact with next of kin and provide a copy of the collision report, free of charge, at the outset of the investigation.

facts.claim: Once an NYPD fatal or critical-injury collision investigation is complete, the public can request the full case file through NYPD's Freedom of Information Law Unit, and the fee is waived.
facts.quote: Once an investigation is complete, a member of the public may request a full collision investigation case file through the NYPD’s Freedom of Information Law Unit. The fee for this service has been waived

facts.claim: NYPD says investigative material from a fatal collision investigation, such as witness statements, scene photographs and findings, is available only once the investigation has concluded.
facts.quote: Investigative material, such as witness statements, photographs of a collision scene, and an investigator’s findings, are available once the investigation has reached its conclusion.

facts.claim: NYPD says its Highway Collision Investigation Squad usually completes an investigation within six months.
facts.quote: the Highway Collision Investigation Squad typically completes an investigation within six months.

facts.claim: Public Officers Law § 66-a(2) also sets the State Police fee for accident photographs at twenty-five dollars per photograph or contact sheet.
facts.quote: An additional fee of fifteen dollars shall be charged for a certified copy of any accident report. A fee of twenty-five dollars per photograph or contact sheet shall be charged.

facts.claim: The Nassau County accident-report fee authorization in Public Officers Law § 66-a(3) is marked to be repealed December 31, 2027.
facts.quote: The fees for investigative reports shall be the same as those for accident reports. * NB Repealed December 31, 2027

facts.claim: Form MV-104 says a crash report is not complete and filed unless it is signed, and an unsigned report may lead to suspension of your driver license.
facts.quote: A crash report is not considered complete and filed unless it is signed, and if not signed may result in the suspension of your driver’s license.

facts.claim: Form MV-104 says not to file it if the crash did not happen in New York State.
facts.quote: Did this crash occur in New York State? If “No”, STOP - do not file this report.

facts.claim: NYPD says you may leave the scene without notifying police or completing an MV-104 only when all three of these apply: damage is $1,000 or less, no person or animal is injured, and information is exchanged where required.
facts.quote: without notifying law enforcement or completing a Report of Motor Vehicle Crash (MV-104) – “Exchange info only”? (All three elements must be satisfied) a. Property damage $1,000 or less; AND b. No injury to any person or animal; AND c. Information exchanged, when required.

facts.claim: NYPD says the MV-104 form is available online at dmv.ny.gov/forms/mv104.pdf or at your local precinct or police service area.
facts.quote: This form can be found online at dmv.ny.gov/forms/mv104.pdf, or at your local precinct or police service area.

gaps.reason: DMV's crash report page does not say whether a card, convenience or processing fee applies to online payments on top of the search and report fees. The portal is behind an NY.gov ID login, so its payment terms could not be read.

None of the NYPD sources read (the collision reports page, the Collision Report Retrieval Portal and form PD 301-165) states a fee for a copy of an NYPD collision report, whether at the precinct, by mail or online.

Fees and procedures for county sheriffs and for city, town and village police departments other than NYPD were not confirmed one by one. DMV only tells requesters to ask the local agency whether the report is available and what the fee is. Web search was unavailable for this run because the session's search budget was used up, so pages were reached only by navigating from official sites. Agency-by-agency research would need a follow-up run.

NYPD's page says that after 30 days all requests must go to DMV on form MV-198C. Its Collision Report Retrieval Portal, however, covers reports taken after September 30, 2016. No official source read says whether the portal can still be used after the 30-day precinct period.

Public Officers Law § 66-a(3) only authorizes Nassau County to set its police report fees by local law, and that subdivision is marked repealed December 31, 2027. Whether Nassau County adopted such a law, and what it charges now, was not confirmed.
No official source was found that offers in-person crash report requests at DMV offices. DMV's crash report page lists only the online portal, the Records Request Navigator and mail.
DMV does not give a processing time for mail (MV-198C) requests. No official source gives a processing time for NYPD requests made at a precinct or by mail.

The DMV pages do not say in plain terms which requesters qualify (for example, involved drivers or owners). Online, eligibility is a certification that you are legally authorized; on MV-198C, it is a choice of Driver's Privacy Protection Act permissible uses. No official source sets a confidentiality or waiting period, apart from Public Officers Law § 66-a's permission to withhold reports that would interfere with a criminal investigation or prosecution.

No official page read states outright that DMV's system holds every crash report written by every New York law-enforcement agency. The sources say the State Police, NYPD and other police departments submit reports to DMV, that police must file a report with DMV when someone is injured or killed, and that NYPD does not require property-damage-only collisions to be reported to police.
No official New York government page read names a vendor portal (such as LexisNexis BuyCrash, CARFAX Crashdocs or PoliceReports.US) for crash reports, so none is included.
No official source read says how far back DMV crash reports can be ordered. The Thruway Authority's own crash-report web page was not read; only form TA-W4310 and the State Police page were used.

gaps.reason: Could not confirm whether Ohio drivers must file their own crash report with a state agency, or any form name, deadline or threshold. The Ohio BMV site (bmv.ohio.gov) rejected every request, and the official Ohio Revised Code site (codes.ohio.gov), where R.C. Chapter 4509 would be read, refused connections. No other official page read addressed it.

No official page read describes a mail-in form or procedure for ordering an OSHP crash report. The OHP 0410 card only says to contact the Central Records Unit if you cannot order online, and the mail and fax details on the ordering page are listed in its school vehicle (OHP 0413) section.
No official source read describes requesting a crash report in person from OSHP, ODPS or a Highway Patrol post.

No official source read says whether viewing or downloading the unofficial reports on the ODPS Crash Retrieval site costs anything. Fees charged by city police departments and county sheriffs were not confirmed.

The text of R.C. 5502.12 itself could not be read because codes.ohio.gov refused connections. Only OSHP's summary of it was read, so any further limits on who may get a report were not confirmed. No official source read mentions a confidentiality or waiting period.
No official source read gives a typical time frame for reports held by city police departments or county sheriffs.
No official statewide list of local agency request procedures, portals or vendors was found. OSHP and ODPS only say to contact the agency that investigated the crash.

R.C. 5502.11 (law enforcement's duty to file crash reports with ODPS, and any deadline) could not be read because codes.ohio.gov refused connections. The WebSearch budget for this run was used up before any search ran, so all sources were reached by fetching known official URLs and following links from them. Pages not linked from those were not found.

facts.quote: You may contact us by phone Monday-Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. (excluding state holidays) Local: (405) 522-7000 Toll Free: (833) 306-0128

gaps.reason: No official online ordering option for Oklahoma collision reports was found. Form 303RM-C says records requests must be submitted by mail or in person, Service Oklahoma's online-services page lists no collision report service, and no official Oklahoma page reviewed links to or names a vendor portal such as BuyCrash. WebSearch could not be used in this run because the search budget was already used up, so official pages were found by browsing oklahoma.gov and oklegislature.gov directly. A wider search for an official page naming a vendor portal was not possible.

No official source says whether Service Oklahoma adds a card or convenience fee when the $7.00 fee ($10.00 certified) is paid in person by credit or debit card. 47 O.S. § 2-109.1 lets the Commissioner of Public Safety add a 4% convenience fee to credit card payments made to the Department of Public Safety, but it was not confirmed that this applies to collision reports bought from Service Oklahoma, so it is not reported as a fact.

No official source gives a turnaround time for Service Oklahoma to fill a mailed or in-person request. The only time frames found are that reports 'may take up to 30 days to populate in the system' and that agencies must forward reports to DPS within 30 days, or 20 days after a death.

No official source says whether in-person requesters must show photo ID, or whether the case number is mandatory. The form marks Sections 2 and 3 'All information required' but says nothing similar about the Section 1 collision details.

Possible conflict. Form 303RM-C says 'By law, you are only allowed to obtain your own Collision Report. [47 OS § 6-117 D]'. In the Legislature's current compilation, § 6-117(D) covers Motor Vehicle Reports. Meanwhile § 40-102 lists other permitted requesters (parties' legal representatives, insurers, news media and others), and the same form lets third parties request with a DPPA reason or the driver's signed consent. How Service Oklahoma handles third-party requests was not confirmed.

Possible conflict over the deadline and recipient. 47 O.S. § 10-108 says the driver's written report goes to the Department of Public Safety if the collision is not settled within six months. The Service Oklahoma-branded DPS FR307 form (code 012008, file dated 11-23-22) says to submit within one year from the date of the collision and to mail it to Service Oklahoma. Which deadline Service Oklahoma applies now was not confirmed.

Getting a copy directly from a city police department or county sheriff (forms, fees, timelines) was not verified. State sources say only that DPS Open Records does not process other agencies' police reports and that you should contact the responding officer's department. City and county websites were not used because they are not state sources. It was also not confirmed whether crashes below the $500.00 reporting threshold, or private-property incidents, reach the state file that Service Oklahoma copies from.

The DPS FR307 driver form still says the official Oklahoma Traffic Collision Report 'can be obtained by calling Records Management at 405-425-2262'. This conflicts with DPS's current Open Records page, which sends collision report requests to Service Oklahoma, and may be out of date, so it is not reported as a fact.

The DPS Open Records page says collision reports can be requested 'by calling (405) 522-7000', which is Service Oklahoma's local number. Form 303RM-C says requests must be submitted by mail or in person with payment. Whether Service Oklahoma takes or completes collision report requests by phone was not confirmed.

The Oklahoma State Courts Network (OSCN) statute site could not be reached, so statutes were read from the Oklahoma Legislature's compiled Title 47 PDF (file dated 2025-12-30). Any amendments after that date are not reflected.

facts.claim: A mailed request to DMV must include a check or money order payable to Oregon DMV for the correct fee.
facts.quote: A check or money order, payable to Oregon DMV, for the correct fee (refer to Form 735-6691).

facts.claim: DMV says individuals requesting their own record use the Order Your Own Record Form 735-7266, and business entities without a DMV Record Inquiry Account use the Request for Information Form 735-7122.
facts.quote: If you are an individual requesting your own record use the Order Your Own Record Form 735-7266. If you are a business entity requesting records and you do not have a DMV Record Inquiry Account use the Request for Information Form 735-7122.

facts.claim: The Order Your Own Record form is used to order your own record by mail from DMV Headquarters.
facts.quote: This form can be used to order your own record by mail from DMV Headquarters.

facts.claim: The Order Your Own Record form includes a Police Traffic Crash Report option, code PA, at $8.50.
facts.quote: PA POLICE TRAFFIC CRASH REPORT $8.50

facts.claim: Order Your Own Record requests are mailed to DMV Records Services, 1905 Lana Ave NE, Salem OR 97314.
facts.quote: MAIL REQUEST TO: DMV RECORDS SERVICES, 1905 Lana Ave NE, Salem OR 97314

facts.claim: DMV's How to Request a DMV Record guide says DMV field offices can order records for customers, including a person's own record.
facts.quote: DMV field offices can order records for customers under the following conditions: 1. A person can order their own record;

facts.claim: A request for a police crash report must include crash information in addition to the driver information on the form.
facts.quote: Requests for police reports regarding automobile crashes REQUIRE the following information in addition to the driver information in Section B.

facts.claim: The required crash information is the crash date and the county, or the nearest city if the county is unknown.
facts.quote: Date of Crash: ___________ , County (or nearest city if county unknown):

facts.claim: DMV cannot find a police crash report by its police report number, and a request without the crash date and county is returned unprocessed.
facts.quote: DMV cannot locate the report by the police report number. If the above information is not provided, your request will not be processed and returned back to you.

facts.claim: To order your own record by mail, you must include enough information for DMV to verify your identity, such as date of birth, place of birth and address on record.
facts.quote: You must include enough information in your request to verify your identity, such as: date of birth, place of birth, address on record

facts.claim: A Form 735-7122 request must include the completed and signed form, any documents proving you qualify for personal information, and a check or money order payable to Oregon DMV.
facts.quote: 1. A completed and signed Form 735-7122; 2. Any required documentation proving you qualify for personal information; and 3. A check or money order, payable to Oregon DMV, for the correct fee.

facts.claim: DMV Records Services answers questions about the Order Your Own Record form at 503-945-5475 or DMVRequestforInfo@odot.oregon.gov.
facts.quote: Please call Records Services at 503-945-5475 or email DMVRequestforInfo@odot.oregon.gov with questions regarding this form.

facts.claim: DMV says requesters must qualify under ORS 802.175 to 802.191 to receive personal information from DMV records.
facts.quote: Requestors must qualify to receive personal information under ORS 802.175 - 802.191.

facts.claim: DMV's fee list says that if a requester does not qualify to receive personal information, the request and payment are returned.
facts.quote: If you do not qualify to receive personal information under Oregon law, your request and payment will be returned to you.

facts.claim: DMV's records privacy page says people who do not qualify for personal information can still order records, but those records are sanitized to remove all personal information other than their own.
facts.quote: You can still order records even if you don't qualify for personal information, but the records you receive will be sanitized to remove all personal information other than your own.

facts.claim: Under OAR 735-010-0220, to qualify for personal information under ORS 802.179(17), a person must submit a copy of a qualifying report, or information that lets DMV locate it if it was filed with DMV.
facts.quote: To qualify to receive personal information under ORS 802.179(17), a person must submit a copy of one of the following reports, or if the person does not have a copy, information that enables DMV to locate such report if it has been filed with DMV.

facts.claim: Under that rule, the report must show that the person was physically injured, or that property they own was damaged, as a result of the unsafe operation of a vehicle.
facts.quote: The report must contain information showing that the person was physically injured or that property they own was damaged as the result of the unsafe operation of a vehicle

facts.claim: A person who qualifies under that rule can get personal information about any owner, driver or occupant of a vehicle involved, as identified from the police crash report.
facts.quote: Personal information about any owner, driver or occupant of a vehicle involved in the unsafe operation and identified from the police crash report

facts.claim: Information from an Oregon Traffic Collision and Insurance Report, including the identity of owners, drivers and occupants, vehicle registration, insurance information and witness names, is available to any person involved in the collision.
facts.quote: Information contained in the report, including the identity of the owner, driver, occupants, vehicle registration number and insurance information and the names of witnesses are available to any person involved in the collision

facts.claim: DMV provides that collision report information as a certified letter for $12.50, charged whether or not the record is found.
facts.quote: Information is provided in certified letter format. The $12.50 fee is to cover the cost of the record search and will be charged whether or not the record is found.

facts.claim: A driver who cannot file within 72 hours must submit the report as soon as possible.
facts.quote: If you are not able to file within the 72 hours, submit it as soon as possible.

facts.claim: A DMV report is required when the collision caused injury or death, damage to your vehicle over $2,500, or damage to any vehicle over $2,500 with any vehicle towed from the scene.
facts.quote: You must submit a report of a motor vehicle collision to DMV when any of the following are true: Injury or death resulted from this collision. Damage to your vehicle is over $2,500. Damage to any vehicle is over $2,500 and any vehicle is towed from the scene.

facts.claim: A DMV report is also required when damage to anyone's property other than a vehicle involved is over $2,500.
facts.quote: Damage to anyone’s property other than a vehicle involved in this collision is over $2,500.

facts.claim: Drivers must still file a DMV report even if law enforcement files a report.
facts.quote: You still need to file a report with the DMV even if a report is filed by law enforcement.

facts.claim: If a required report is not filed, Oregon law requires DMV to issue a suspension notice.
facts.quote: If you do not file a report, Oregon law requires DMV to issue a suspension notice.

facts.claim: The online collision report on DMV2U is only for drivers involved in the collision who have an Oregon license, permit or ID number.
facts.quote: You must be a driver involved in the collision and have an Oregon License, Permit, or ID number to use the online collision report.

facts.claim: ODOT says the online collision reporting system for the public went online in April 2025.
facts.quote: The new citizen online collision reporting system went online in April 2025

facts.claim: The paper Oregon Traffic Collision and Insurance Report is Form 735-32.
facts.quote: and Insurance Report (Form 735-32) to DMV.

facts.claim: Paper reports can be mailed to the DMV Crash Reporting Unit, 1905 Lana Ave NE, Salem, Oregon 97314.
facts.quote: Mail to DMV Crash Reporting Unit 1905 Lana Ave NE, Salem, Oregon 97314

facts.claim: Paper reports can be faxed to the DMV Crash Reporting Unit at 503-945-5267.
facts.quote: Fax report form to DMV Crash Reporting Unit at 503-945-5267

facts.claim: Drivers should send DMV only one report per collision, because each report submitted shows as a new collision on the driver's record.
facts.quote: Do not send DMV more than one report for the same collision. Each report you submit shows as a new collision on your record.

facts.claim: Under ORS 802.220(5), DMV cannot give a driver a copy of the collision report they filed, so drivers should keep their own copy.
facts.quote: Under Oregon law ORS 802.220(5), DMV cannot give you a copy of your report.

facts.claim: DMV gives a free Certificate of Filing to people who have, or claim to have, filed an Oregon Traffic Collision and Insurance Report.
facts.quote: A Certificate of Filing is available at no charge to those persons who have, or claim to have, filed an Oregon Traffic Collision and Insurance Report with DMV.

facts.claim: Drivers can call the DMV Crash Reporting Unit at 503-945-5098 to ask whether their collision must be reported.
facts.quote: Contact the DMV Crash Reporting Unit at 503-945-5098 to find out why you are required to report and what you can submit to prove your collision is not reportable.

facts.claim: A driver involved in a collision that meets the DMV reporting requirements must notify police immediately.
facts.quote: You must immediately notify police if you are a driver involved in a collision that meets the reporting requirements described above.

facts.claim: Oregon law requires the driver of a motor vehicle involved in a collision in Oregon to submit a report (the Oregon Traffic Collision and Insurance Report) to DMV within 72 hours when any of DMV's listed reporting conditions is true: injury or death, or one of the $2,500 damage thresholds.
facts.quote: Oregon law requires the driver of a motor vehicle involved in a collision that happened in Oregon to submit a report to DMV within 72 hours when any of these are true:

facts.claim: DMV does not provide copies of an individual driver's Oregon Traffic Collision and Insurance Report.
facts.quote: Copies of an individual's Oregon Traffic Collision and Insurance Report are not available.

facts.claim: Information from a driver's Oregon Traffic Collision and Insurance Report is available to any person involved in the collision, that person's family, or that person's personal representative.
facts.quote: are available to any person involved in the collision, the person's family, or the person's personal representative.

facts.claim: DMV charges an extra $1.00 to certify a driver or vehicle document copy that is not already certified.
facts.quote: CERTIFICATION – $1.00 Additional charge to certify any driver or vehicle document when the copy is not already CERTIFIED.

facts.claim: On the Order Your Own Record form, the Police Traffic Crash Report option ($8.50) asks for the crash date and county.
facts.quote: POLICE TRAFFIC CRASH REPORT $8.50 CRASH DATE:__________ COUNTY:_________

facts.claim: Records ordered on Form 735-7266 are mailed to the address on DMV's record unless the requester says otherwise.
facts.quote: Records ordered using this form are mailed to you at your address shown on DMV’s record unless you indicate otherwise.

facts.claim: DMV records ordered on Form 735-7266 cannot be emailed.
facts.quote: EMAIL ADDRESS (Records cannot be emailed)

facts.claim: Form 735-7266 lets requesters give a fax number to have records returned by fax.
facts.quote: FAX NUMBER (IF YOU WANT YOUR RECORDS RETURNED TO YOU BY FAX)

facts.claim: Only certain entities qualify for personal information from DMV records, including attorneys, legitimate businesses, insurance companies, police agencies and other government agencies.
facts.quote: Only certain entities can qualify to receive personal information from motor vehicle records. Some of these entities are: attorneys, legitimate businesses, insurance companies, police agencies, and other government agencies.

facts.claim: A requester who qualifies for personal information but is not listed on Form 735-7122 may submit a written request explaining how they qualify and why they need the information.
facts.quote: If you qualify for personal information, but are not listed on Form 735-7122, you may submit a written request explaining how you qualify and why you need the information.

facts.claim: Sanitized records, with other people's personal information removed, can only be ordered by mail from DMV Headquarters.
facts.quote: Sanitized records can only be ordered by mail from DMV Headquarters.

facts.quote: Acceptable proof of identity when the request is made in person is an Oregon-issued driver license, permit, or identification card or one item from the proof of identity and date of birth list in OAR 735-62-0020.

facts.claim: Certain records ordered at a DMV field office are mailed from DMV Headquarters in Salem the following business day.
facts.quote: Certain records ordered at a DMV field office will be mailed to you from DMV Headquarters in Salem the following business day.

facts.claim: Under OAR 735-010-0220, the qualifying reports are a police crash report, a police incident report, or an Oregon Traffic Collision and Insurance Report filed with DMV under ORS 811.720.
facts.quote: (a) A police crash report; (b) A police incident report; or (c) An Oregon Traffic Collision and Insurance Report filed with DMV under ORS 811.720.

facts.quote: Personal information about any witness to the unsafe operation listed on the police crash report, the police incident report or the Oregon Traffic Collision and Insurance Report provided to DMV.

facts.claim: Under OAR 735-010-0010, DMV discloses personal information only to the person the record belongs to or a qualified requester. Otherwise the record is sanitized.
facts.quote: if the record is ordered by the individual whose record it is or if the person ordering the record qualifies to receive personal information. Otherwise the record will be sanitized with the personal information removed.

facts.claim: Drivers who are not eligible for the DMV2U online collision report must submit the paper form.
facts.quote: If you do not meet these eligibility requirements, you will need to submit the paper version of the form.

facts.claim: When a report is required, drivers licensed in another state and non-residents must also file it.
facts.quote: When required to report, you must file a report even if you are licensed in another state or you are not an Oregon resident.

facts.claim: A completed paper collision report can be handed in at a DMV office.
facts.quote: Take the form to a DMV office.

facts.claim: Paper collision report forms can be picked up at a DMV office or a local law enforcement department.
facts.quote: Pick one up at a DMV office or your local law enforcement department.

facts.claim: DMV Customer Assistance (503-945-5000, TTY 711) can send the collision report form by mail, fax or email.
facts.quote: Call DMV Customer Assistance at 503-945-5000 (Statewide Relay TTY 711) to request the report form by mail, fax or email.

facts.claim: DMV does not determine fault, but it must post the collision to the driving record of each driver required to report.
facts.quote: DMV does not determine fault in a collision, but we are required by law to post the collision to the driving record of drivers required to report.

facts.claim: Drivers who believe they did not need to report can submit evidence such as a repair bill or estimate, or a statement from an insurance company.
facts.quote: Examples of evidence you can submit include a repair bill or estimate from an auto repair business, or a statement from an insurance company.

facts.quote: If you do not file a report when required, Oregon law requires DMV to suspend your driving privileges.

facts.claim: Drivers should keep a copy of their report and proof of when they submitted it to DMV.

facts.claim: Oregon State Police charges a $12.50 flat rate for an investigative report (an OSP record separate from the DMV crash report copy) when processing takes 30 minutes or less, covering up to 10 pages.
facts.quote: Investigative reports $12.50 flat rate if staff time to find and process record request does not exceed 30 minutes. Includes up to 10 pages.

facts.quote: To request an Oregon State Police record: Complete the online records request form or Complete and submit the Public Records Request form.

facts.claim: OSP asks requesters to submit records requests without payment and then sends a letter explaining the fees.
facts.quote: You should submit your request without payment. We will review your information and provide you with a letter explaining the required fees.

facts.claim: OSP says a public records request may take up to 30 days or more.
facts.quote: It may take up to 30 days or more depending on staff availability, the nature of the request, and the volume of records being requested.

facts.claim: OSP's paper records request form is accepted by mail or in person only.
facts.quote: This form is accepted by mail or in person only.

gaps.reason: No official source offers online ordering of a Police Traffic Crash Report. DMV materials describe ordering one by mail (Forms 735-7266 and 735-7122). DMV2U is described only for filing a driver's collision report and ordering driving records. It needs cookies and sign-in, so it was not explored.

DMV's general guide (Form 735-7161) says field offices can order records for customers. No official source confirms that a Police Traffic Crash Report in particular can be ordered at a DMV field office.

No official source says how soon a police crash report is available from DMV after a crash. ORS 810.460, the statute on police submitting crash reports to DMV, could not be read: oregonlegislature.gov refused connections from both WebFetch and direct requests. OSP's 30-day processing estimate covers OSP public records generally, not crash reports, which OSP sends to DMV.
No official source mentions card payment or a convenience fee for crash report requests. The mail forms call for a check or money order payable to Oregon DMV.

No state source says whether city police departments or county sheriffs also release copies of their own crash reports directly, or what they charge. Local agency procedures were not checked, and local government sites fall outside this task's definition of official sources.

DMV sources differ on requesters who do not qualify for personal information. Form 735-6691 says the request and payment are returned. Form 735-7161 and the DMV privacy page say sanitized records can still be ordered. No source says how this applies to a Police Traffic Crash Report in particular. The statutes themselves (ORS 802.175-802.191, 802.179(17), 802.220) could not be read because oregonlegislature.gov was unreachable.
No official Oregon page was found that names or links to a vendor portal (such as LexisNexis BuyCrash) for state crash reports.

The shared web search budget was already used up when this task started, so no WebSearch queries ran. Research relied on fetching known official Oregon URLs directly and following links from them, so some relevant official pages may have been missed.

facts.claim: The Pennsylvania State Police (PSP) provides copies of crash reports for crashes PSP investigated, online or by mail.
facts.quote: Get a vehicle crash report of an incident investigated by the Pennsylvania State Police online or by mail.

facts.claim: PennDOT compiles statewide crash statistics from traffic crash reports that state, county, municipal and other law enforcement agencies submit to it.
facts.quote: The figures are compiled from the traffic crash reports that are submitted to the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation by state, county, municipal, and other law enforcement agencies, as specified in the Pennsylvania Vehicle Code (75 Pa. C.S., Chapter 37, Subchapter C).

facts.claim: The SP 7-0015 form covers certified copies of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania Police Crash Reporting Form, excluding appended documents and photographs, for crashes reported to the Pennsylvania State Police.
facts.quote: CERTIFIED COPIES OF THE COMMONWEALTH OF PENNSYLVANIA POLICE CRASH REPORTING FORM (EXCLUDING APPENDED DOCUMENTS AND PHOTOGRAPHS) FOR CRASHES REPORTED TO THE PENNSYLVANIA STATE POLICE

facts.claim: PennDOT defines a reportable crash as one resulting in a fatality within 30 days, an injury of any degree to any person involved, or damage to any vehicle serious enough to require towing.
facts.quote: Reportable Crash: A crash resulting in a fatality within 30 days of the crash; or injury in any degree, to any person involved; or crashes resulting in damage to any vehicle serious enough to require towing.

facts.claim: PSP crash reports can be requested through the Online Crash Report Requests site.
facts.quote: Use the Online Crash Report Requests site to get a crash report.

facts.quote: A COPY OF THE CRASH REPORT CAN BE OBTAINED ONLINE AT https://www.pa.gov/psp/crash-reports/

facts.claim: With a paper copy of the police crash report, you can search the online site by the Incident Number located on the top left of the page.
facts.quote: If you have an existing, paper copy of your Police Crash Report, you can search by the Incident Number located on the top-left of the page.

facts.claim: Without a paper copy, you can search the online site using a name and date.
facts.quote: If you do not have a paper copy of your Police Crash Report, you can search using a name and date to find possible results.

facts.claim: After finding the report online, you must fill out the Application To Obtain Copy of Police Report web form.
facts.quote: Once you have located a crash report, you must fill out the Application To Obtain Copy of Police Report web form.

facts.claim: If PSP approves an online request, the approval email includes a link to an online payment form, and the documents are sent in a separate email after payment.
facts.quote: Your approval email will include a link to an online payment form, which after submission will allow your requested documents to be sent in another, separate email.

facts.claim: To request a PSP crash report by mail, PSP says to download the form, complete and sign it, and print it.
facts.quote: Download the form, complete and sign it, and print.

facts.claim: The PSP mail-in form is numbered SP 7-0015 (6-2018).
The SP 7-0015 form is titled Application to Obtain Copy of Police Crash Report.
facts.quote: APPLICATION TO OBTAIN COPY OF POLICE CRASH REPORT

facts.claim: PSP says to mail the form with a money order or certified check for $22, payable to the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.
facts.quote: Mail the form with a money order or certified check for $22, payable to the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, to:

facts.claim: Mail requests go to PA State Police, Crash Reports Unit, 1800 Elmerton Avenue, Harrisburg, PA 17110.
facts.quote: PA State Police Crash Reports Unit 1800 Elmerton Avenue Harrisburg, PA 17110

facts.claim: The SP 7-0015 form lets you ask for the copy by email in Adobe Acrobat format instead of by mail, and notes this is not available for crashes prior to 1/2004.
facts.quote: REQUEST COPY VIA EMAIL (IN LIEU OF MAILING) COPY WILL BE PROVIDED IN AN ADOBE ACROBAT FORMAT *NOT AVAILABLE FOR CRASHES PRIOR TO 1/2004

facts.claim: The SP 7-0015 form says any person involved (not witnesses), their attorney, insurer and certain government officials may view or photograph the police crash report with personal equipment, only at the investigating station.
facts.quote: POLICE CRASH REPORT MAY BE VIEWED OR PHOTOGRAPHED (WITH PERSONAL EQUIPMENT) BY ANY PERSON INVOLVED (NOT WITNESSES), THEIR ATTORNEY, INSURER, AND CERTAIN GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS ONLY AT THE INVESTIGATING STATION.

facts.claim: PSP says Right-to-Know requests are not for requesting crash reports and directs people to the crash report request page for incidents PSP investigated.
facts.quote: Right-to-Know (RTK) requests are not for requesting crash reports. If you need a vehicle crash report of an incident investigated by PSP, please visit the Request a Copy of a Vehicle Crash Report page.

facts.claim: PSP's contact page lists 717-783-3380 as the phone number for crash reports.
facts.quote: Crash Reports – 717-783-3380

facts.claim: The online site lists the Crash Reports Unit at 1800 Elmerton Avenue, Harrisburg, PA 17110, phone 717-783-3380, email RA-pspcrashreports@pa.gov.
facts.quote: Crash Reports Unit 1800 Elmerton Avenue Harrisburg, PA 17110 717-783-3380 RA-pspcrashreports@pa.gov

gaps.reason: I found no official state page explaining how to get a crash report when a municipal police department or county sheriff investigated the crash. PSP's request page, online portal and SP 7-0015 form cover only crashes investigated by or reported to PSP. The statute on release of police crash reports (75 Pa.C.S. § 3751) could not be read because palegis.us and legis.state.pa.us refused connections, and openrecords.pa.gov also refused connections. This run's WebSearch budget was used up, so only pages reachable by browsing official sites directly were checked.
No official source was found for what municipal police departments charge for a crash report copy, and the statute that may set it (75 Pa.C.S. § 3751) could not be reached.
The online portal says a fee is due after approval but does not state the amount or whether a card or convenience fee is added. Only PSP's service page states the $22 fee.
PSP sources differ on how to pay by mail. The service page says money order or certified check, while the SP 7-0015 (6-2018) form says check or money order.

PennDOT's 2025 Crash Facts book says state, county, municipal and other law enforcement agencies submit crash reports to PennDOT. No official page was found saying whether the public can get copies of those police reports from PennDOT.
No official page describes requesting a copy in person from PSP. The SP 7-0015 form describes only viewing or photographing the report at the investigating station.
No official Pennsylvania page was found that names a vendor portal such as LexisNexis BuyCrash, CARFAX Crashdocs or PoliceReports.US. PSP's own portal is hosted on pa.gov.
No official time frame was found for crash reports held by municipal police departments.
75 Pa.C.S. § 3751(b) could not be read directly because the site was unreachable. The facts on who can request come from PSP's page and from the SP 7-0015 form, which cites that section.

The SP 7-0015 (6-2018) form header gives a PSP Investigative Records Section number, (717) 783-5514. That differs from the 717-783-3380 crash reports number on PSP's current contact page and portal. Which number is current for the form was not confirmed.

PennDOT sources name different bureaus for the same P.O. Box 2047, Harrisburg address. The DMV FAQ names the Bureau of Highway Safety and Traffic Engineering, while the AA-600 form names the Bureau of Operations (BOO - Crash Unit).
