gaps.reason: No official page I read gives the online price on BuyCrash.com or any convenience or card fee. BuyCrash.com (which redirects to buycrash.lexisnexisrisk.com) and policereports.lexisnexis.com blocked automated access with Cloudflare, so the online fee could not be confirmed.

I could not read the text of R.I. Gen. Laws § 42-28-37, which RISP and DPS cite for the crash report fee and for release to involved parties. The RI General Assembly statute server (webserver.rilegislature.gov / webserver.rilin.state.ri.us) refused connections throughout this research.
The Providence Police page does not give a fee for reports picked up at the Records Office or bought online.

No official page I read says whether the State Police Accident Bureau or BuyCrash.com holds crash reports written by city or town police departments. The RISP instructions describe crashes handled by a trooper. The guide should not say the state system includes municipal reports.

I verified only the Providence Police Department's official page. Other city and town departments may use different processes, fees or vendor portals. For example, the Warwick Police site (warwickpd.org, reached from warwickri.gov) names a different portal; I did not use it because it is not on a .gov domain. No official source I read addresses county sheriffs and crash reports in Rhode Island.

No official source I read requires drivers to file their own written crash report with a state agency; I found no form name, deadline or state filing address. The DMV Driver's Manual only describes reporting to the police. I could not check R.I. Gen. Laws chapter 31-26 because the statute server was unreachable.

I found no form name or number for mailing a crash-report request. RISP describes a written request with a stamped, self-addressed envelope, payment, the driver's name, the crash date and the report number.

RISP's crash report instructions list only online and mail options, plus fatal crash reports through the Accident Bureau. I found no State Police walk-in window, hours or walk-in fee for crash reports. The in-person facts I found apply to general public records requests.
No official source gives a processing time for mailed State Police crash report requests beyond processing them in the order received. The Providence page gives no availability time frame.

Official sources differ on release during an investigation. The RISP page says crashes under investigation cannot be released until the investigation is completed. The DPS regulation says reports shall be provided to involved individuals or their legal representation regardless of investigation status. I could not read the governing statute (§ 42-28-37).

I could not open the PDFs linked on risp.ri.gov (the Public Records Request Form, the DPS APRA Regulation PDF, GO.004A Traffic Administration and GO.002E Public Records Request Procedure) because downloads were behind a Cloudflare challenge. I read the regulation on rules.sos.ri.gov instead. RIDOT (dot.ri.gov) was unreachable.
The web search budget for this run was already used up, so I found official pages by navigating official sites directly. Some relevant official pages may have been missed.

facts.claim: Section 30-2-510 of the South Carolina Code refers to collision reports that are maintained and provided by the South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles.
facts.quote: the personal contact information is included in a collision report or uniform traffic ticket maintained and provided by the South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles as permitted by law;

facts.claim: South Carolina's ratified FY 2026-2027 budget act (proviso 82.9) requires the Department of Motor Vehicles to give the Department of Transportation access, without charge, to all collision data and collision reports.
facts.quote: The Department of Motor Vehicles shall provide access, in compliance with all state and federal privacy protection statutes, to the following data and reports without charge to the Department of Transportation: (1) all collision data and collision reports;

facts.claim: An April 2016 South Carolina Department of Insurance consumer alert told drivers to request a copy of the accident report from the DMV.
facts.quote: Request a copy of the accident report from the DMV.

facts.claim: The South Carolina Department of Public Safety must tabulate the accident reports required by Section 56-5-1270 and publish statistical information on the number and circumstances of traffic accidents.
facts.quote: The Department of Public Safety must tabulate and may analyze all accident reports as required in Section 56-5-1270 and shall publish annually or at more frequent intervals statistical information based thereon as to the number and circumstances of traffic accidents.

facts.claim: The officer reporting duty in Section 56-5-1270 applies to every law enforcement officer who investigates a crash causing injury, death, or apparent total property damage of one thousand dollars or more.
facts.quote: Every law enforcement officer who, in the regular course of duty, investigates a motor vehicle accident that results in injury to or death of any person or total property damage to an apparent extent of one thousand dollars or more

facts.claim: A 2019 South Carolina House Legislative Oversight Committee study of the Department of Motor Vehicles describes one DMV unit's purpose as storing crash reports occurring inside the boundaries of South Carolina.
facts.quote: Collects and maintains insurance information for all vehicles registered in South Carolina. Store crash reports occurring inside the boundaries of South Carolina.

facts.claim: The April 2016 Department of Insurance alert said a copy could be requested by mail using the Request for Copy of Officer's Report form (Form FR-50), downloaded from the South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles website.
facts.quote: To request a copy by mail, you can download a copy of the Request for Copy of Officer’s Report form (Form FR-50) from the South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles website.

facts.claim: The April 2016 Department of Insurance alert said in-person requests could be made only at the DMV offices at 10311 Wilson Blvd. in Blythewood or 1630 Shop Road in Columbia.
facts.quote: These reports may be requested in person, but only from the DMV Offices located at 10311 Wilson Blvd. in Blythewood or 1630 Shop Road in Columbia.

facts.claim: The April 2016 Department of Insurance alert said a mail request needed two completed copies of the form, sent with the fee to the address on the form.
facts.quote: You must submit two completed copies of the Form along with the $6.00 fee to the address provided on the form.

facts.claim: A written request to a law enforcement agency for a crash report must state the requester's name, address, and intended use of the report in enough detail to show the use is not commercial solicitation.
facts.quote: A written request under this section must state the requestor's name, address, and the intended use of the report in sufficient detail that the law enforcement agency may ascertain that the intended use is not for commercial solicitation purposes.

facts.claim: The April 2016 Department of Insurance alert gave the fee for a mailed Form FR-50 request as $6.00.
facts.quote: You must submit two completed copies of the Form along with the $6.00 fee to the address provided on the form.

facts.claim: The Department of Motor Vehicles may charge a fee of up to twenty dollars per document, on top of the normal fees, to expedite a request for copies of documents and records it maintains.
facts.quote: The Department of Motor Vehicles may collect a fee not to exceed twenty dollars per document to expedite a request for copies of documents and records it maintains. This fee is in addition to the normal fees associated with the request.

facts.claim: The ratified FY 2026-2027 budget act (proviso 82.2) lets the Department of Motor Vehicles collect processing fees and fees to recover the costs of producing, handling and mailing documents, publications, records and data sets.
facts.quote: The Department of Motor Vehicles may collect processing fees and fees to recover the costs of the production, purchase, handling and mailing of documents, publications, records and data sets.

facts.claim: Under Section 56-5-1270, the investigating officer must forward a written crash report to the Department of Motor Vehicles within twenty-four hours after completing the investigation.
facts.quote: within twenty-four hours after completing the investigation, must forward a written report of the accident to the Department of Motor Vehicles including the names of interviewed participants and witnesses.

facts.claim: The April 2016 Department of Insurance alert said a copy can be requested once law enforcement has completed its investigation and submitted the accident report to the DMV.
facts.quote: Once law enforcement has completed their investigation and submitted the accident report to DMV, you may request a copy of the report.

facts.claim: Section 56-1-550, which covers requests for copies of Department of Motor Vehicles documents and records, says expedited requests must be available within seventy-two hours of receipt and standard requests within thirty days.
facts.quote: Expedited requests must be available within seventy-two hours of receipt of the request and standard requests within thirty days.

facts.claim: Section 56-9-330(2), in a section about the Department of Motor Vehicles, says the department shall furnish any person a copy of a vehicle accident report on request and payment of a fee.
facts.quote: (2) The department shall, upon request, and the payment of a fee furnish any person a copy of a vehicle accident report.

facts.claim: South Carolina law bars anyone from asking a law enforcement agency for a crash report for commercial solicitation purposes.
facts.quote: No person shall request any law enforcement agency to permit examination or to furnish a copy of any such report for commercial solicitation purposes.

facts.claim: Anyone other than law enforcement personnel and persons named in the report must submit a separate written request to the law enforcement agency for each crash report.
facts.quote: All persons, except law enforcement personnel and persons named in the report, shall be required to submit a separate written request to the law enforcement agency for each report.

facts.claim: Section 56-5-1260 sends the immediate crash notice to the local police department if the crash occurs within a municipality, and otherwise to the county sheriff's office or the nearest South Carolina Highway Patrol office.
facts.quote: give notice of such accident to the local police department if such accident occurs within a municipality, otherwise to the office of the county sheriff or the nearest office of the South Carolina Highway Patrol.

facts.claim: Section 56-5-1270 sets a fifteen-day deadline for the operator or owner of a vehicle in a crash that no law enforcement officer investigated and that caused injury, death, or apparent total property damage of one thousand dollars or more.
facts.quote: The operator or owner of a motor vehicle involved in an accident resulting in injury to or death of any person or total property damage to an apparent extent of one thousand dollars or more which was not investigated by a law enforcement officer, within fifteen days after the accident

facts.claim: For such a crash not investigated by a law enforcement officer, a written report and verification of liability insurance coverage must be forwarded to the Department of Motor Vehicles within fifteen days after the accident.
facts.quote: which was not investigated by a law enforcement officer, within fifteen days after the accident, shall forward a written report and verification of liability insurance coverage of the accident to the Department of Motor Vehicles

facts.claim: Section 56-9-350 requires the completed and verified form to be returned to the Department of Motor Vehicles within fifteen days of the date the officer delivered it, and failure to return it is prima facie evidence that the vehicle was uninsured.
facts.quote: The completed and verified form must be returned by the operator or owner to the Department of Motor Vehicles within fifteen days from the date the form was delivered by the officer. Failure to return the form, verified in the proper manner, is prima facie evidence that the vehicle was uninsured.

facts.claim: Section 56-9-350 also requires the operator or owner to give the Department of Motor Vehicles a written report after a crash causing property damage of four hundred dollars or more, or bodily injury or death, that no law enforcement officer investigated.
facts.quote: The operator or owner of a motor vehicle involved in an accident resulting in property damage of four hundred dollars or more, or in bodily injury or death, which was not investigated by a law enforcement officer shall furnish to the Department of Motor Vehicles a written report

facts.claim: The April 2016 Department of Insurance alert said the investigating officer gives drivers a green Form FR-10, which their insurance company must complete regardless of fault and which must be returned to the DMV within 15 days of the accident.
facts.quote: If law enforcement is called to the scene, the investigating officer will give you a green form (Form FR-10), which must be completed by your insurance company – regardless of fault – and returned to the DMV within 15 days of the accident.

facts.claim: The April 2016 Department of Insurance alert said that if law enforcement did not investigate the accident, a driver may have to complete and submit a Traffic Collision Report (Form FR-309).
facts.quote: If the accident was not investigated by law enforcement, you may have to complete and submit a Traffic Collision Report (Form FR-309).

facts.claim: Any incorporated city or town may pass an ordinance requiring drivers in a crash to also file a report, or a copy of a report filed with the Department of Motor Vehicles, with a designated city department.
facts.quote: Any incorporated city or town may by ordinance require that the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident shall also file with a designated city department a report of such accident or a copy of any report herein required to be filed with the Department of Motor Vehicles.

facts.claim: Accident reports made by people involved in accidents are without prejudice to the person reporting and are for the confidential use of the Department of Motor Vehicles, the Department of Public Safety, or other State agencies that use the records for accident prevention purposes.
facts.quote: shall be for the confidential use of the Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of Public Safety, or other State agencies having use for the records for accident prevention purposes.

facts.claim: Section 56-9-350 says the investigating officer must give the operator or owner of a vehicle in a crash causing property damage of four hundred dollars or more, or bodily injury or death, a written request form for completing and verifying liability insurance coverage, either at the time of the accident or as soon after it as possible.
facts.quote: must be furnished a written request form at the time of the accident, or as soon after the accident as possible, by the investigating officer for completion and verification of liability insurance coverage

facts.claim: Under Section 56-1-540(2), the Department of Motor Vehicles must file all accident reports it receives under South Carolina law.
facts.quote: The department shall file all accident reports and abstracts of court records of convictions received by it under the laws of this State

facts.claim: SCDMV's 2024 Annual Accountability Report says its Driver Services program maintains driver records and collision reports and oversees the financial responsibility unit.
facts.quote: Responsible for oversight and compliance of issuing driver's licenses and identification cards of all types. Maintains driver records and collision reports. Oversees the financial responsibility unit and insurance-related matters.

facts.claim: Law enforcement agency employees may not let anyone examine or obtain a copy of an accident report or related investigative report when they know, or should reasonably know, that the request is for commercial solicitation.
facts.quote: no employee of any law enforcement agency shall allow any person to examine or obtain a copy of any accident report or related investigative report when the employee knows or should reasonably know that the request for access to the report is for commercial solicitation purposes.

facts.claim: A person who knowingly makes a false statement in a written request for a crash report under Section 56-5-1275 is subject to the provisions of Section 56-3-2520.
facts.quote: A person who knowingly makes any false statement in any written request under this section shall be subject to the provisions of Section 56-3-2520.

facts.claim: Section 30-2-50(A) of the Family Privacy Protection Act bars any person or private entity from knowingly obtaining or using personal information from a state agency, local government or other political subdivision for commercial solicitation directed at anyone in South Carolina.
facts.quote: A person or private entity shall not knowingly obtain or use personal information obtained from a state agency, a local government, or other political subdivision of the State for commercial solicitation directed to any person in this State.

facts.claim: A knowing violation of Section 30-2-50(A) is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of up to five hundred dollars, up to one year's imprisonment, or both.
facts.quote: A person knowingly violating the provisions of subsection (A) is guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction, must be fined an amount not to exceed five hundred dollars or imprisoned for a term not to exceed one year, or both.

facts.claim: Under Section 56-5-1340, the DMV may, on request, tell anyone who suffered injury to their person or property any information in an accident report about the existence of insurance.
facts.quote: may upon request disclose to any person who has suffered injury to his person or property any information contained on any report regarding the existence of insurance.

facts.claim: Under Section 56-5-1340, the DMV may disclose the identity of a person involved in an accident when that identity is not otherwise known or when the person denies being at the accident.
facts.quote: The Department of Motor Vehicles may disclose the identity of a person involved in an accident when such identity is not otherwise known or when such person denies his presence at such accident

facts.claim: When a person who made, or claims to have made, an accident report demands it, or a court does, the DMV must furnish a certificate showing whether a specified accident report was made to it.
facts.quote: the Department of Motor Vehicles shall furnish, upon demand of any person who has, or claims to have, made such a report or upon demand of any court, a certificate showing that a specified accident report has or has not been made to the Department of Motor Vehicles

facts.claim: Reports required by Sections 56-5-1260 to 56-5-1280 cannot be used as evidence of either party's negligence or due care at the trial of an action for damages.
facts.quote: None of the reports required by Sections 56-5-1260 to 56-5-1280 may be evidence of the negligence or due care of either party at the trial of any action at law to recover damages.

facts.claim: If the driver is physically unable to make the written report required by Section 56-5-1270 and does not own the vehicle, the vehicle's owner must make the report within five days after learning of the accident.
facts.quote: Whenever the driver is so physically incapable of making a written report as required in Section 56-5-1270 and such driver is not the owner of the vehicle, then the owner of the vehicle involved in such accident shall within five days after learning of the accident make such report

facts.claim: Crash reports filed with a city department under a municipal ordinance are for that department's confidential use and are subject to Section 56-5-1340.
facts.quote: All such reports shall be for the confidential use of the city department and subject to the provisions of Section 56-5-1340.

facts.claim: A law enforcement agency must not investigate a collision involving its own vehicle, motorcycle or employee if the collision results in injury or death or involves a privately owned vehicle or motorcycle.
facts.quote: A law enforcement department or agency must not investigate a traffic collision in which a motor vehicle, a motorcycle, or an employee of that department or agency is involved that: (1) results in an injury or a death, or (2) involves a privately-owned motor vehicle or motorcycle

facts.claim: For collisions involving a law enforcement agency's vehicle that are covered by Section 56-5-765(A), the State Highway Patrol must investigate and file a report with findings on whether the agency vehicle was operated properly.
facts.quote: the State Highway Patrol must investigate the collision and must file a report with findings on whether the agency motor vehicle or motorcycle was operated properly within the guidelines of appropriate statutes and regulations.

facts.claim: Proviso 82.2 of the ratified FY 2026-2027 budget also lets the DMV collect and keep fees to cover the cost of fulfilling a Freedom of Information Act request.
facts.quote: The department may collect and retain fees to defray the cost associated with fulfilling a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request.

facts.claim: The April 2016 Department of Insurance alert said the driver's insurance company can submit the Form FR-10 insurance information to the DMV electronically.
facts.quote: Your insurance company can submit this information electronically.

gaps.reason: I could not confirm whether SCDMV, SCDPS or the Highway Patrol sells or releases crash reports online, and I found no portal URL. scdmvonline.com refused connections from this network. dmv.sc.gov, scdps.sc.gov and sc.gov returned CloudFront 403 errors saying the distribution 'is configured to block access from your country'. No official page I could read names an online portal or vendor such as BuyCrash, Crashdocs or PoliceReports.US.

The only stated amount, $6.00 for a mailed Form FR-50 request, comes from an April 2016 SC Department of Insurance release. Section 56-9-330(2) requires a fee but does not set an amount, and proviso 82.2 allows cost-recovery and processing fees without amounts. I could not open the current SCDMV fee or any online convenience or card fee. Treat $6.00 as unverified for 2026.

The Form FR-50 name, the two-copy rule and the mail process come only from the 2016 Department of Insurance release. I could not open the current FR-50 form, its URL or its mailing address on the SCDMV site.
The two in-person DMV locations (10311 Wilson Blvd., Blythewood and 1630 Shop Road, Columbia) come from a 2016 release. I could not check them against current SCDMV pages.

No official source I read says how many days after a crash a report is usually available to the public. I found only the officer's 24-hour forwarding duty after the investigation is complete, and the general DMV turnaround in section 56-1-550 (30 days standard, 72 hours expedited) for copies of records.

No official page I read says whether SCDMV limits collision report copies to involved parties or redacts personal information, for example under driver-privacy laws. Section 56-9-330(2) says 'any person'. The written-request and anti-solicitation rules in section 56-5-1275 are written for law enforcement agencies.

I could not confirm from a state source whether city police departments and county sheriffs give out copies themselves, or what they charge. By statute their officers forward reports to the DMV (56-5-1270), and agencies accept written requests (56-5-1275). Each agency's own process needs checking.

SCDPS and SC Highway Patrol pages could not be opened because of the geo-block. I could not confirm whether the Highway Patrol also releases copies of its own reports directly, or what SCDPS currently tells requesters.

The statutes give different thresholds. Section 56-5-1270 uses injury or death, or apparent property damage of one thousand dollars or more. Section 56-9-350 uses four hundred dollars or more, or bodily injury or death. The form names FR-10 and FR-309 come only from the 2016 Department of Insurance release, and I could not check current SCDMV form numbers or instructions.

WebSearch could not be used. The shared search budget was already used up at this task's first query, so I found sources by fetching known official URLs directly, and some official pages may have been missed. Every SC agency site except the Legislature, Department of Insurance and SCDOT was unreachable from this network.

facts.claim: The South Dakota Office of Accident Records maintains a database of motor vehicle traffic crash information for public roadways.
facts.quote: The South Dakota Office of Accident Records maintains a database of motor vehicle traffic crash information for public roadways.

facts.claim: The South Dakota Office of Accident Records maintains safesd.gov so the public can purchase vehicle crash reports and download crash data.
facts.quote: The South Dakota Office of Accident Records maintains this site to allow the public to purchase vehicle crash reports and download crash data.

facts.claim: SDCL 32-34-10 requires the law enforcement officer or other person assigned by a law enforcement agency to investigate traffic accidents to forward an investigator's report to the Department of Public Safety within three days after the investigation is complete.
facts.quote: The law enforcement officer or other person assigned by a law enforcement agency to investigate traffic accidents shall forward to the Department of Public Safety, within three days after completion of the investigation of the accident, an investigator's report of the accident so reported.

facts.claim: The state crash-report site says vehicle crash reports are kept in its database for 15 years.
facts.quote: Vehicle crash reports are covered by South Dakota open records statute and are maintaned in our database for a period of 15 years.

facts.claim: The state crash-report site says a report may not be found if the crash occurred on private property, if Marsy's Law has been invoked, or if damage was under $1000 to any one person's property or under $2000 in total.
facts.quote: You may not be able to locate a crash report if the following conditions apply: Crash occurred on private property It has been less than 10 days since the incident occurred If Marsy’s Law has been invoked Under $1000 worth of damage to any one person's property Under $2000 worth of total damage

facts.claim: The mail-in request form says accidents in parking lots or on private property are not reportable to the Office of Accident Records.
facts.quote: Accidents which occur in parking lots or on private property are not reportable to the Office of Accident Records.

facts.claim: The Office of Accident Records' 2024 reporting manual tells officers to select private property for a crash deemed non-state reportable, and such a crash is not sent to the state repository.
facts.quote: Select private property if the crash is deemed non-state reportable, this will move the crash to the non-reportable tile in LEOS and will not be sent to the state repository.

facts.claim: Debit and credit card customers who buy through the state's online system receive their report immediately if the report is available for purchase.
facts.quote: Debit and credit card customers using the online system receive their report(s) immediately if the report is available for purchase.

facts.claim: To request a report by mail, download and fill out the mail-in form from the state crash-report site.
facts.quote: If you do not wish to purchase the online report today and would like to mail your request, download and fill out the mail-in form.

facts.claim: The state's mail-in form is titled Accident Report Request.
facts.quote: ACCIDENT REPORT REQUEST

facts.claim: The Accident Report Request form says to complete it and submit it to the address shown above on the form to get a copy of the accident report.
facts.quote: Complete and submit this form to the above address to obtain a copy of the accident report.

facts.claim: The form says to use one form for each accident report requested.
facts.quote: Please use one form for each requested accident report.

facts.claim: Mail-in requests can be paid only with cash, check or money order.
facts.quote: Mail-in requests can only be purchased using cash, check or money order.

facts.claim: The DPS Highway Patrol Crash Assistance Program page says accident reports can be obtained by mail or online through the Office of Accident Records.
facts.quote: Accident reports can be obtained through the mail or online through the Office of Accident Records.

facts.claim: To get a copy of a state crash report, a person must be able to provide at least two of: the date of the crash, the driver's last name and the county of the crash.
facts.quote: In order to obtain a copy of a State of South Dakota crash report, a person must be able to provide at least two of the following: Date of crash Driver's last name County of crash

facts.claim: The mail-in Accident Report Request form asks for the driver license number.
facts.quote: Driver License No.

facts.claim: The mail-in Accident Report Request form asks for the date of the accident.
facts.quote: Date of Accident

facts.claim: The mail-in Accident Report Request form asks for the location of the accident by street or highway.
facts.quote: Location of Accident (Street or Highway)

facts.claim: The mail-in Accident Report Request form asks for the city or county.
facts.quote: City or County

facts.claim: The mail-in Accident Report Request form asks for the investigating officer.
facts.quote: Investigating Officer

facts.claim: Buying a report online costs a $4 fee to locate and provide the report plus a $6 convenience fee.
facts.quote: There is a $4 fee to locate and provide the crash report and a $6 convenience fee to purchase the online crash report.

facts.claim: The mail-in fee is $4.00 per accident report requested; it covers the search and is kept whether or not an accident record is on file.
facts.quote: There is $4.00 fee per accident report requested that covers the search and is retained whether or not an accident record is on file in this office.

facts.claim: Checks for mail-in requests are payable to DPS - Accident Records.
facts.quote: Make checks payable to DPS - Accident Records.

facts.claim: SDCL 32-34-13 sets a four-dollar fee for each request to locate a report on file, and any report found is furnished at no additional cost.
facts.quote: The secretary of public safety shall collect four dollars for each request to locate a report on file. The secretary shall furnish to any person requesting a search, at no additional cost, any report located by the search.

facts.claim: A crash report becomes available for purchase after the investigating law enforcement agency submits it and it is accepted into the South Dakota Accident Records Database.
facts.quote: After a crash report is submitted by the investigating law enforcement agency and accepted into the South Dakota Accident Records Database, it becomes available for purchase.

facts.claim: The state crash-report site says a report may not be found if less than 10 days have passed since the crash.
facts.quote: You may not be able to locate a crash report if the following conditions apply: Crash occurred on private property It has been less than 10 days since the incident occurred If Marsy’s Law has been invoked Under $1000 worth of damage to any one person's property Under $2000 worth of total damage

facts.claim: The mail-in form recommends waiting until 20 days after the accident date to submit a request.
facts.quote: We recommend that you wait until 20 days after the accident date to submit a request.

facts.claim: SDCL 32-34-13 says reports made under SDCL 32-34-7 to 32-34-12, and the information in them, are not privileged and may not be held confidential.
facts.quote: Reports pursuant to §§ 32-34-7 to 32-34-12, inclusive, and the information contained in such reports is not privileged and may not be held confidential.

facts.claim: The state crash-report site says vehicle crash reports are covered by South Dakota's open records statute.
facts.quote: Vehicle crash reports are covered by South Dakota open records statute and are maintaned in our database for a period of 15 years.

facts.claim: The Office of Accident Records provides crash records and reports on request to individuals, insurance agents, law enforcement and others, in compliance with Marsy's Law.
facts.quote: Our Office provides crash records and reports upon request for individuals, insurance agents, law enforcement and others in compliance with Marsy’s Law.

facts.claim: If victims exercise their Marsy's Law rights after a crash report is submitted, the Office of Accident Records will promptly remove the report from all records.
facts.quote: However, if victims choose to exercise their rights under Marsy's Law after the submission of a crash report, the Office of Accident Records will promptly remove the report from all records.

facts.claim: The DPS Accident Records page says that, under Attorney General Official Opinion No. 16-02 dated December 5, 2016, state and local government entities may release crash reports to the public without violating Article VI, §29 of the South Dakota Constitution.
facts.quote: Pursuant to South Dakota Attorney General Official Opinion No. 16-02, dated December 5, 2016, state and local government entities may release crash reports to the public without violating Article VI, §29 of the South Dakota Constitution.

facts.claim: County or municipal law enforcement may collect four dollars for each copy of an accident report their office furnishes to any person.
facts.quote: County or municipal law enforcement personnel may collect four dollars for each copy of an accident report furnished to any person by their office.

facts.claim: If a requester does not have the details needed for a search, the state crash-report site says to contact the law enforcement agency that investigated the crash to get them.
facts.quote: If you don't have this information, please reach out to the Law Enforcement Agency that investigated the crash to obtain these details.

facts.claim: SDCL 32-34-7's duty to give immediate notice applies to the driver of any motor vehicle in a crash causing bodily injury or death, or apparent property damage of one thousand dollars or more to any one person's property or two thousand dollars per accident.
facts.quote: The driver of any motor vehicle involved in an accident resulting in bodily injuries or death to any person or property damage to an apparent extent of one thousand dollars or more to any one person's property or two thousand dollars per accident shall immediately

facts.claim: Under SDCL 32-34-7, that driver must give notice immediately, by the quickest means of communication, to the nearest available law enforcement officer who has jurisdiction, and a violation is a Class 2 misdemeanor.
facts.quote: shall immediately, by the quickest means of communication, give notice of the accident to the nearest available law enforcement officer who has jurisdiction. A violation of this section is a Class 2 misdemeanor.

facts.claim: The secretary of public safety may require drivers involved in accidents, or peace officers, to file supplemental reports on Department of Public Safety forms when the original report is insufficient in the secretary's opinion.
facts.quote: The secretary of public safety may require drivers involved in accidents or peace officers to file supplemental reports of the accidents upon forms furnished by the Department of Public Safety whenever the original report is insufficient in the opinion of the secretary.

facts.claim: The Accident Report Request form lists the phone number (605) 773-3868 and the fax number (605) 773-6893.
The safesd.gov site lists the address 118 West Capitol Avenue, Pierre, South Dakota 57501 and the email arinfo@state.sd.us.
facts.quote: 118 West Capitol Avenue, Pierre, South Dakota 57501 | arinfo@state.sd.us

facts.claim: The mail-in Accident Report Request form, which covers motor vehicle traffic accidents in South Dakota, says to submit it to the address in its letterhead: 118 West Capitol Avenue, Pierre, South Dakota 57501-2000.
facts.quote: 118 West Capitol Avenue Pierre, South Dakota 57501-2000 (605) 773-3868 | FAX: (605) 773-6893 ACCIDENT REPORT REQUEST (for motor vehicle traffic accidents occurring in South Dakota) INSTRUCTIONS: Complete and submit this form to the above address to obtain a copy of the accident report.

facts.claim: The mail-in form defines a state reportable accident: one that causes bodily injury or death to anyone or, if no one was injured, apparent property damage of $1,000 or more to any one person's property or $2,000 per accident.
facts.quote: A state reportable accident is an accident resulting in bodily injuries or death to any person or, if there was no personal injury, property damage to an apparent extent of $1,000 or more to any one person’s property or $2,000 per accident.

facts.claim: Under SDCL 32-34-10, the investigating officer must have a notice fixed to the damaged vehicle, in the way the secretary of public safety prescribes, saying the accident has been reported and is being investigated.
facts.quote: cause a notice to be affixed in a manner prescribed by the secretary of public safety to the vehicle damaged, indicating that the accident has been reported and the circumstances surrounding the accident are being investigated.

facts.claim: Under SDCL 32-34-23, the person in charge of a garage or repair shop may not start repairing a vehicle that shows evidence of a reportable accident unless it carries the SDCL 32-34-10 notice.
facts.quote: The person in charge of any garage or repair shop shall not commence repair on any motor vehicle which shows evidence of having been involved in a reportable accident or struck by any bullet unless the vehicle bears the notice provided for in § 32-34-10.

facts.claim: Under SDCL 32-34-9, if the driver is physically unable to give immediate notice of the accident, another occupant who was in the vehicle and is able to must give the notice.
facts.quote: If the driver of a vehicle is physically incapable of giving an immediate notice of an accident and there was another occupant in the vehicle at the time of the accident capable of doing so, such occupant shall make or cause to be given the notice not given by the driver.

facts.claim: Under SDCL 32-34-8, a person who is physically incapable of making an accident report does not have to make one while the incapacity lasts.
facts.quote: An accident report is not required from any person who is physically incapable of making such report during the period of such incapacity.

facts.claim: The 2024 state reporting manual says agencies without breath-testing equipment won't have chemical test results right away, and tells them to hold the crash report up to 5 working days for the results. This can delay when the report reaches the state.
facts.quote: For law enforcement agencies without breath testing equipment, results of chemical tests will not be available immediately. HOLD THE CRASH REPORT UP TO 5 WORKING DAYS TO ALLOW FOR THE RESULTS OF CHEMICAL TESTS TO BE RETURNED.

gaps.reason: The web search budget for this run was already used up, so no searches were run. Pages were found by following links from the official DPS site (sd.gov/dps), safesd.gov and the Legislature's statute pages. Other official pages, such as administrative rules or individual local agency pages, may exist and were not checked.

The safesd.gov 'Buy Now' button links to the vendor page https://sdbuy.primepublicsafety.com/sdbuy/ecommerce/ecommerce.jsp. On 2026-10-09 that page returned HTTP 404 to both WebFetch and a full browser fetch, and the site root returned HTTP 403. So the checkout page, its search fields and the fees it shows could not be read or confirmed, and the vendor's name is not stated on any official page that was read. Readers should start from safesd.gov.
No official page that was read says whether crash reports can be requested in person at the Office of Accident Records in Pierre. The DPS Crash Assistance Program page mentions only mail or online.
No official page that was read says whether a requester must show ID, sign anything beyond the mail-in form, or prove involvement in the crash. The mail-in form has no visible form number.

Official sources give different guidance. safesd.gov says a report may not be found if fewer than 10 days have passed, while the mail-in form recommends waiting 20 days. SDCL 32-34-10 gives officers three days after their investigation is complete. No official source states a typical overall wait.

Attorney General Official Opinion No. 16-02 and the Attorney General's Marsy's Law page were not read. Beyond the DPS summary (the report is removed from all records if victims invoke their rights), it is unconfirmed how Marsy's Law affects requests by others.

No official source that was read explains how individual city police departments or county sheriffs release copies (forms, hours, payment), or whether they release reports for crashes the state does not receive, such as private-property crashes. SDCL 32-34-13.1 only allows them to collect four dollars per copy.

No official source that was read requires drivers to file their own written crash report with a state agency, and no driver report form name or filing deadline was found. SDCL 32-34-7 requires immediate notice to law enforcement, and SDCL 32-34-11 only lets the secretary of public safety require supplemental reports when the original report is insufficient. Sections 32-34-14 to 32-34-22 are listed as repealed.
The $6 online convenience fee could not be confirmed on the vendor page, which returned HTTP 404. No official source that was read gives fees for certified copies or other formats.

facts.claim: The Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security describes a Crash Report as an official copy of a crash investigated by the Tennessee Highway Patrol or another law enforcement agency, and points people to its Request a Crash Report link to buy one.
facts.quote: A Crash Report is an official copy of an accident that is investigated by the Tennessee Highway Patrol or another law enforcement agency. To purchase a copy of your Crash Report, click on Request a Crash Report below.

facts.claim: The state's PurchaseTNCrash help page says that, per state statute, investigating law enforcement agencies have 7 days from the date of the crash to submit their report to the state.
facts.quote: Per state statute, Investigating law enforcement agencies have 7 days from the date of the crash to submit their report to the state.

facts.claim: The help page gives, as one reason a report cannot be found online, that the investigating law enforcement agency has not yet completed it and submitted it to the State of Tennessee.
facts.quote: The report has not yet been completed by the investigating law enforcement agency and submitted to the State of Tennessee.

facts.claim: Before you request a report, the Department says the most important question is whether the crash was investigated by the Tennessee Highway Patrol or by another agency, such as a county sheriff's office or city police department.
facts.quote: Most importantly, was the crash investigated by the Tennessee Highway Patrol (THP), or another agency (county sheriff's office or city police department)?

facts.claim: If a law enforcement agency other than the THP investigated the crash, the Department says you can also contact that agency to buy a copy of the report from its office.
facts.quote: If the crash was investigated by a law enforcement agency other than the THP: You can also contact the agency that investigated the crash to purchase a copy of the report from their office.

facts.claim: The PurchaseTNCrash help page says a crash report can also be bought in person at a THP District office or at the office of the agency that originally investigated the crash.
facts.quote: You can also purchase your crash report in-person at a Tennessee Highway Patrol (THP) District office (PurchaseTNCrash) or at the original investigating agency office.

facts.claim: If you are unsure which agency investigated, the help page says to contact the local police department of the city or town where the crash occurred, or, for a crash outside a town or city, the sheriff's department or State Highway Patrol.
facts.quote: If you are unsure which agency investigated the crash, contact the local police department of the city or town where the crash occurred. If the crash occurred outside of a town or city, you can contact the Sherriff's Department or State Highway Patrol.

facts.claim: The PurchaseTNCrash site says anyone who self-reported a crash through the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department's Report Minor Vehicle Crash Online portal must contact that department directly to get the record.
facts.quote: If you self-reported your crash to Metropolitan Nashville Police Department via their Report Minor Vehicle Crash Online portal, you will need to contact Metropolitan Nashville Police Department directly to obtain the record.

facts.claim: The site notes that crashes reported through Metro Nashville's Report Minor Vehicle Crash portal are crashes not investigated by a law enforcement officer.
facts.quote: These are crashes NOT investigated by a law enforcement officer.

facts.claim: The first step of the PurchaseTNCrash online process is to verify your involvement in the crash.
facts.quote: Verify your Involvement in the Crash.

facts.claim: The online process then has you enter the involved party and crash details to locate the report.
facts.quote: Enter the Involved Party and Crash Details to locate the report.

facts.claim: A prepaid card cannot be used to buy a crash report online.
facts.quote: You cannot use a prepaid card

facts.claim: A crash report bought online comes as an Adobe PDF, and the buyer must be able to print or save it.
facts.quote: Your Crash Report will be an Adobe PDF, and you must have the ability to print or save it.

facts.claim: After buying a report online, you have 48 hours to download it.
facts.quote: Once you have purchased your report, the transaction is complete. You have 48 hours to download the report.

facts.claim: Buying a crash report online costs $10.00, paid by credit card (Visa, MasterCard, American Express or Discover).
facts.quote: Cost: $10.00 - credit card (Visa, MasterCard, American Express or Discover)

facts.claim: The PurchaseTNCrash portal states that the cost is $10.00 per crash report.
facts.quote: The cost is $10.00 per Crash Report.

facts.claim: For a crash investigated by the Tennessee Highway Patrol, a copy of the crash report can be bought for a fee of $4.00.
facts.quote: If the crash was investigated by the Tennessee Highway Patrol: Any driver/owner/passenger or their agent or legal representative may purchase a copy of the Crash Report for a fee of $4.00.

facts.claim: A mail request must come with a cashier's check, money order, or personal or business check for $4.00.
facts.quote: A cashier's check, money order, or personal/business check in the amount of $4.00 must accompany your request.

facts.claim: The PurchaseTNCrash help page says you can order a crash report by mail for $4, with mail-order information at www.tn.gov.
facts.quote: Yes, you can order your crash report by mail for $4. Mail order information can be found at www.tn.gov.

facts.claim: Buying a report online requires the last name, date of accident, reporting agency and driver's license number.
facts.quote: Required: Last Name, Date of Accident, Reporting Agency, Driver's License Number

facts.claim: The online purchase also requires one of the following: VIN, license plate, or case or tracking number.
facts.quote: Required one of the following: VIN, License Plate, Case or Tracking Number

facts.claim: When buying a crash report, the Department says to provide the date of the crash, the county where it occurred, the name(s) of the driver(s) involved and the agency tracking number.
facts.quote:
When purchasing a Crash Report, you should provide the following information:
Date of crash
County in which crash occurred
Name(s) of driver(s) involved
Agency Tracking Number

facts.claim: Form SF-1595 has a crash information section where the requester prints as much information about the crash as they can.
facts.quote: CRASH INFORMATION (Please PRINT and provide as much information as you can.)

facts.claim: A THP crash report, available at the THP District Office, can be bought through the mail or by visiting that office in person.
facts.quote: The reports are available approximately 7 days after the date of the crash at the THP District Office. This can be purchased through the mail, or by visiting their office in person.

facts.quote: If sending by mail, be sure and include the address to which you would like the Crash Report mailed.

facts.claim: Form SF-1595 (Traffic Crash Report Request) must be completed, signed and mailed with a check or money order for $4.00 and a self-addressed, stamped envelope.
facts.quote: Please complete this form, sign it, and mail a check or money order for $4.00 along with a self-addressed, stamped envelope to:

facts.claim: THP crash reports are available at the THP District Office approximately 7 days after the date of the crash.
facts.quote: The reports are available approximately 7 days after the date of the crash at the THP District Office.

facts.claim: The help page says investigating agencies have 7 days from the date of the crash to submit their report to the state, though in certain circumstances investigations could take a bit longer to complete.
facts.quote: Per state statute, Investigating law enforcement agencies have 7 days from the date of the crash to submit their report to the state. In certain circumstances, investigations could take a bit longer to complete.

facts.claim: For a mail request, the state says to allow two-three weeks from the mailing date to receive the crash report.
facts.quote: Please allow two-three weeks from the mailing date to receive the requested crash report.

facts.claim: For a crash investigated by the Tennessee Highway Patrol, any driver, owner or passenger, or their agent or legal representative, may buy a copy of the crash report.
facts.quote: If the crash was investigated by the Tennessee Highway Patrol: Any driver/owner/passenger or their agent or legal representative may purchase a copy of the Crash Report for a fee of $4.00.

facts.quote: Notice: Motor Vehicle crash information is regulated as provided in T.C.A. 55-10-108(d). You must be a driver involved in the crash, the owner of property involved in the crash, the insurer of any party who is the subject of the report, or a legal representative of the driver or owner.

facts.claim: By signing Form SF-1595, the requester swears or affirms that crash report information made confidential by statute will not be used for any other purpose, including commercial solicitation of crash victims.
facts.quote: do swear or affirm that information contained in a crash report made confidential by statute will not be used for any other purpose including commercial solicitation of crash victims

facts.claim: Form SF-1595 warns that obtaining a crash report through the request under false pretense is a criminal offense.
facts.quote: Obtaining a Motor Vehicle Crash Report from this request under false pretense is a criminal offense.

facts.claim: The online portal's involvement options include a driver or passenger involved in the crash.

facts.claim: The online portal's involvement options also include someone other than the listed individuals or parties.

facts.claim: The help page quotes Tennessee Code Annotated 10-7-504(a)(31)(B), which applies to a written request from any person named in a crash report, or that person's agent, legal representative or attorney, who certifies that the person has permission.

Per Tennessee Code Annotated 10-7-504 31(B):
Notwithstanding subdivision (a)(31)(A) and upon written request, any person named in any motor vehicle crash report, or such person's agent, legal representative, or attorney, certifying that the person has permission

facts.quote: is authorized to receive an crash report containing personally identifying information of persons involved in the crash.

facts.claim: On the Department's Owner Operator Report page, the filing requirement applies to a car owner or driver involved in a crash that caused death or injury, more than $1,500 in property damage, or more than $400 in damage to state or local government property.
facts.quote: If you were involved in a crash as the car owner or driver that caused death or injury, or that caused more than one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500) in property damage or more than four hundred dollars ($400) in damage to state or local government property, you must file

facts.claim: Such a person must file an Owner Operator Report or have one filed on their behalf, regardless of who was at fault and in addition to any report filed by an investigating officer.

facts.claim: The Owner Operator Report must be submitted to the Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security within twenty (20) days of the crash.
facts.quote: You must submit an Owner Operator Report to the Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security within twenty (20) days of the crash.

facts.claim: Failing to file the Owner Operator Report may result in suspension of your driver license and registrations or nonresident operating privileges.
facts.quote: Failure to file the report may result in the suspension of your driver license and registrations or nonresident operating privileges.

facts.claim: The Owner Operator Report can be filed online through the Department's e-Services, using Submit an Owner Operator Report in the Driver Services section.

Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security
