gaps.reason: Web search was unavailable for this run because the shared search budget ran out on the first query. I reached official pages only by following links from tn.gov. The official Tennessee Code, hosted by LexisNexis, is script-only and would not open, so I did not read T.C.A. 55-10-108, 55-12-104 or 10-7-504 directly. The references to them come only from Department pages and forms that cite them.

No official page I read mentions a convenience or card-processing fee on top of the $10.00 online price. Seeing the checkout total would mean submitting the portal's involvement-verification form, which the read-only rule forbids, so I could not confirm whether an extra fee is added.
No state page gives the fees city police departments or county sheriff's offices charge for copies bought at their own offices. I did not research individual local agencies.

No official page says outright that every city and county agency's report can be bought on PurchaseTNCrash. The help page says investigating agencies submit reports to the state within 7 days, and the online search asks for the reporting agency. However, the site sends people who self-reported a minor crash to Metro Nashville Police back to that department.

The Department's crash report page puts mail and in-person purchase under the heading for THP-investigated crashes. Form SF-1595 asks for the investigating agency, and the help page describes mail orders generally. No official source says whether a mail request covers a crash investigated by a local agency. Payment wording also differs: the page accepts a cashier's check, money order, or personal/business check, while the form says check or money order with a self-addressed, stamped envelope.

The online portal offers an option for someone who was not involved in the crash. No page I read says what that requester receives (for example, a copy without personally identifying information) or whether any waiting period applies. I could not read the text of T.C.A. 10-7-504(a)(31)(A) on an official statute site.

No official source says when a city police or sheriff's report becomes available at that agency. The only official time frame is the help page's statement that agencies have 7 days to submit reports to the state.
Metro Nashville's Report Minor Vehicle Crash page on nashville.gov returned 403 (access denied), so I could not confirm how Metro Nashville provides copies of self-reported crashes.

facts.claim: TxDOT is the custodian of crash records for the state of Texas.
facts.quote: TxDOT is the custodian of crash records for the state of Texas.

facts.claim: In the Texas Transportation Code subchapter on written collision reports, "department" means the Texas Department of Transportation.
facts.quote: In this subchapter, "department" means the Texas Department of Transportation.

facts.claim: TxDOT collects crash reports from every law enforcement agency in Texas, for crashes on any public roadway and not just the state highway system.
facts.quote: TxDOT collects crash reports from every law enforcement agency in Texas and for crashes that occur on any public roadway in Texas, not just crashes occurring on the state highway system.

facts.claim: TxDOT collects crash reports from Texas law enforcement agencies for crashes on public roadways and the state highway system.
facts.quote: TxDOT collects crash reports from Texas law enforcement agencies for crashes occurring on public roadways and the state highway system.

facts.claim: A law enforcement officer who investigates a motor vehicle collision in the regular course of duty must write a report if the collision caused injury, death, or apparent damage of $1,000 or more to any one person's property.
facts.quote: A law enforcement officer who in the regular course of duty investigates a motor vehicle collision shall make a written report of the collision if the collision resulted in injury to or the death of a person or damage to the property of any one person to the apparent extent of $1,000 or more.

facts.claim: The state retention schedule for crash reports and data is 10 years plus the current year.
facts.quote: The state retention schedule for crash reports and data is 10 years plus the current year.

facts.claim: You can get a copy of a Texas Peace Officer’s Crash Report (CR-3) through TxDOT's Crash Report Online Purchase System.
facts.quote: You may obtain a copy of a Texas Peace Officer’s Crash Report (CR-3) by using our Crash Report Online Purchase System link below.

facts.claim: Reports bought through the online system are delivered by email after purchase.
facts.quote: Customers using the online system receive their report(s) via email following the purchase.

facts.claim: TxDOT's online application lets the public buy the Texas Peace Officer’s Crash Report (CR-3) 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year.
facts.quote: TxDOT offers an application that will allow the public to purchase Texas Peace Officer’s Crash Report (CR-3) online 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, and 365 days per year.

facts.claim: If you are unable to use the online system, you may buy a copy by completing request form CR-91 and mailing it with the required payment to the address shown on the form.
facts.quote: If you are unable to use the Crash Report Online Purchase System, you may purchase a copy of a Texas Peace Officer's Crash Report (CR-4) by completing the appropriate request form (CR-91) and mailing it with the required payment to the address shown on the form.

facts.claim: The CR-91 form can be downloaded from TxDOT's crash records forms page.
facts.quote: The CR-91 is available for download at https://www.txdot.gov/data-maps/crash-reports-records/forms-law-enforcement.html.

facts.claim: The CR-91 mailing address is Crash Data and Analysis, Texas Department of Transportation, P.O. Box 12879, Austin, Texas 78711.
facts.quote: Crash Data and Analysis, Texas Department of Transportation, P.O. Box 12879, Austin, Texas 78711

facts.claim: Subpoena and affidavit requests for crash records are filed through TxDOT's CRIS Request - TxDOT Subpoena and Affidavit Request System.
facts.quote: You may file a subpoena or affidavit request by using our CRIS Request - TxDOT Subpoena and Affidavit Request System link below.

facts.claim: Effective January 1, 2025, TxDOT no longer accepts subpoena and affidavit requests by mail.
facts.quote: Effective January 1, 2025, TxDOT will no longer accept subpoena and affidavit requests by mail.

facts.claim: TxDOT says the CR-91 is no longer required for subpoena and affidavit requests and that requests received by mail will be returned to the requesting company.
facts.quote: The CR-91 is no longer required for subpoena and affidavit requests; additionally, all requests received by mail will be returned to the requesting company for their records.

facts.claim: The CRIS Purchase Help Center lists search options of name, driver license/identification card number, vehicle identification number (VIN), TxDOT Crash ID and agency case ID.
facts.quote: There are four options for searching: Name, Driver License/Identification Card Number, Vehicle Identification Number (VIN), TxDOT Crash ID, and Agency Case ID.

facts.claim: A name search requires the first and last name of a person involved in the crash.
facts.quote: The First Name and Last Name fields are required for a Person Involved in Crash.

facts.claim: A name search can be for any person involved in the crash, including drivers, occupants, pedestrians, pedalcyclists and property damage owners.
facts.quote: Name – This can be for any person involved in a crash including drivers, occupants, pedestrians, pedalcyclist, property damage owners, etc.

facts.claim: You can also search by the driver license or identification card number of any driver (or primary) involved in the crash.
facts.quote: Driver License Number/Identification Card Number – This can be for any driver (or primary) involved in a crash.

facts.claim: County, city and crash date can be added to narrow a name search.
facts.quote: Additional Information can be added to narrow the search results. a. County – County in which the crash occurred b. City – City in which the crash occurred c. Crash Date – The date on which the crash occurred

facts.claim: To finish an online purchase you enter a valid email address and pay through Texas.gov.
facts.quote: To finalize the Purchase, enter a valid email address and select the ‘Pay Now at Texas.gov’ button. All payments are processed through Texas.gov.

facts.claim: Online purchases must be paid by credit/debit card (VISA, MasterCard, American Express or Discover) or electronic check (ACH).
facts.quote: Purchases must be made using a credit/debit card or electronic check (ACH). Accepted credit/debit cards include VISA, MasterCard, American Express, and Discover.

facts.claim: Choosing a non-redacted report online requires completing the Crash Report Purchase Certification form under Texas Transportation Code 550.065.
facts.quote: If the Non-Redacted report type is selected, you will have to complete the Crash Report Purchase Certification form per Texas Transportation Code 550.065.

facts.claim: The purchase certification form requires your first and last name, plus an organization name if applicable.
facts.quote: The First Name and Last Name Fields are mandatory. The Organization Name is optional and should be added if applicable.

facts.claim: The CR-91 mail form asks for the crash date and the crash location by county, city and street or highway.
facts.quote: CRASH DATE MONTH/DAY/YEAR CRASH LOCATION COUNTY CITY STREET OR HIGHWAY

facts.claim: The CR-91 includes fields for the driver's full name, date of birth and Texas DL number.
facts.quote: DRIVER'S FULL NAME DRIVER INFORMATION (if available) DATE OF BIRTH TEXAS DL NUMBER

facts.claim: Mail requests are paid by check or money order payable to the Texas Department of Transportation.
facts.quote: Make check or M.O. payable to: Texas Department of Transportation

facts.claim: The CR-91 includes a statement in which the requester certifies that they meet the requirements of Texas Transportation Code §550.065(c)(4).
facts.quote: certify that I meet the requirements of Texas Transportation Code §550.065(c)(4)

facts.claim: TxDOT charges $6 for a regular copy of a crash report.
facts.quote: $6 for a regular copy.

facts.claim: TxDOT charges $8 for a certified copy, which is requested when a person needs an official document, such as for a legal proceeding.
facts.quote: $8 for a certified copy - A certified copy is requested when a person needs an official document, such as for a legal proceeding.

facts.claim: There is a minimal surcharge for using the Crash Report Online Purchase System.
facts.quote: There is a minimal surcharge for using this system.

facts.claim: Additional processing fees may be applied for credit card transactions.
facts.quote: Additional processing fees may be applied for credit card transactions.

facts.claim: Credit/debit card purchases carry a minimal Texas.gov fee, while electronic check (ACH) payments have no fee but a 10-day holding period before reports are released.
facts.quote: The public will be charged a minimal Texas.gov fee for Certified and Uncertified crash reports for credit/debit card purchases. There is no fee for electronic check (ACH) payments, however, there is a 10-day holding period before reports will be released.

facts.claim: In the online system an uncertified electronic copy costs $6.00, a certified electronic copy costs $8.00, and a Letter of "No Records" is free.
facts.quote: The cost for an Uncertified electronic copy is $6.00. The cost of a Certified electronic copy is $8.00. The cost of a Letter of "No Records" is free.

facts.claim: State law sets the fee for a copy of a collision report at $6, and certification by the department (TxDOT) or the governmental entity costs an additional $2.
facts.quote: The fee for a copy of the collision report is $6. The copy may be certified by the department or the governmental entity for an additional fee of $2.

facts.claim: State law lets the department or the governmental entity charge $6 for a certification that no report or information is on file.
facts.quote: The department or the governmental entity may issue a certification that no report or information is on file for a fee of $6.

facts.claim: On the CR-91 mail form, a copy of the Peace Officer's Crash Report costs $6.00 each.
facts.quote: Copy of Peace Officer's Crash Report - $6.00 each

facts.claim: On the CR-91 mail form, a certified copy of the Peace Officer's Crash Report costs $8.00 each.
facts.quote: Certified Copy of Peace Officer's Crash Report - $8.00 each

facts.claim: The CR-91 says that if the officer's report is not on file when the request arrives, a certification saying so is provided instead and the fee is kept for the certification.
facts.quote: The Law also provides that if an officer's report is not on file when a request for a copy of such report is received, a certification to that effect will be provided in lieu of the copy and the fee will be retained for the certification.

facts.claim: Subpoena and affidavit requests through CRIS Request cost the required $8 fee plus a minimal surcharge.
facts.quote: The customer must pay the required $8 fee with a minimal surcharge for their associated request(s).

facts.claim: The officer's report must be filed electronically with the department (TxDOT) no later than the 10th day after the collision.
facts.quote: The report required by Subsection (a) must be filed electronically with the department not later than the 10th day after the date of the collision.

facts.claim: Once TxDOT receives a report, it may take up to 4 business days to process.
facts.quote: Once the report is received by TxDOT, it may take up to 4 business days to process.

facts.claim: It can take up to 14 days from the crash date for a report to appear in the online search results.
facts.quote: It can take up to 14 days from the Crash Date for your Crash Report to appear in Search Results.

facts.claim: The CR-91 says mail requests should not be sent until at least 10 days after the crash date.
facts.quote: Requests should not be submitted until at least 10 days after the crash date to allow time for receipt of the report.

facts.claim: A request by mail may take up to 30 days to process.
facts.quote: Please note a request by mail may take up to 30 days to process.

facts.claim: Non-redacted reports bought by credit card can be downloaded immediately, while electronic check purchases have a ten business day holding period.
facts.quote: Non-Redacted: Crash reports are available for immediate download if purchased by credit card. If purchasing with an electronic check, there is a ten business day holding period.

facts.claim: Redacted reports go through a TxDOT review, and purchases of fewer than 100 reports are available for download within ten business days.
facts.quote: Redacted: Crash reports must go through a TxDOT review process. Purchases of less than 100 reports will be made available for download within ten business days

facts.claim: TxDOT lists a processing time of 20 business days for state or federal subpoena requests.
facts.quote: State or Federal Subpoena - 20 business days

facts.claim: TxDOT lists a processing time of 10 business days for affidavit requests.
facts.quote: Affidavit - 10 business days

facts.claim: Under state law, crash report information is privileged and confidential except as provided by Subsections (c), (c-1) and (e) of §550.065.
facts.quote: Except as provided by Subsection (c), (c-1), or (e), the information is privileged and for the confidential use of:

facts.claim: TxDOT releases a crash report on written request and payment of the fee to any person directly concerned in the accident or having proper interest therein.
facts.quote: Texas Transportation Code §550.065 allows for the release of a crash report on written request and upon payment of the required fee to any person directly concerned in the accident or having proper interest therein, including:

facts.claim: People entitled to the report include any person involved in the collision, the authorized representative of any person involved, and any driver involved.
facts.quote: (A) any person involved in the collision; (B) the authorized representative of any person involved in the collision; (C) a driver involved in the collision;

facts.claim: An employer, parent or legal guardian of a driver involved, and the owner of a vehicle or property damaged in the collision, are also entitled.
facts.quote: (D) an employer, parent, or legal guardian of a driver involved in the collision; (E) the owner of a vehicle or property damaged in the collision;

facts.claim: Insurance companies that issued a policy covering a vehicle or a person involved in the collision are also entitled.
facts.quote: (G) an insurance company that issued an insurance policy covering a vehicle involved in the collision; (H) an insurance company that issued a policy covering any person involved in the collision;

facts.claim: Any person who may sue because of a death resulting from the collision is also entitled.
facts.quote: (L) any person who may sue because of death resulting from the collision; or

facts.claim: The department or governmental entity that receives the report must create a redacted collision report that any person may request.
facts.quote: On receiving information to which this section applies, the department or the governmental entity that receives the information shall create a redacted collision report that may be requested by any person.

facts.claim: Redacted crash reports are available to anyone.
facts.quote: Redacted Crash Reports are available to anyone.

facts.claim: Persons or entities who do not meet the eligibility criteria receive a redacted copy of the crash report.
facts.quote: Persons or entities who do not meet the criteria will receive a redacted copy of the crash report.

facts.claim: Requesters who do not fit the listed categories can explain how they meet the criteria in another way.
facts.quote: If a person or entity does not meet any of these criteria, TxDOT does provide an option for the customer to identify how they meet the criteria in a manner that is not listed in the above reasons (A) through (L).

facts.claim: If the justification submitted is insufficient or non-qualifying, a redacted copy is provided.
facts.quote: A redacted copy will be provided if an insufficient or non-qualifying justification is submitted.

facts.claim: The CR-91 warns that providing false information on it violates Texas Penal Code §37.10 and could result in criminal penalties.
facts.quote: Providing false information on this governmental record is a violation of Texas Penal Code §37.10 and could result in criminal penalties.

facts.claim: Texas Transportation Code §550.065 applies to crash report information held by the department (TxDOT) or another governmental entity.
facts.quote: This section applies only to the following information that is held by the department or another governmental entity:

facts.claim: On written request and payment of any required fee, the department or the governmental entity must release the information to the persons the law lists.
facts.quote: On written request and payment of any required fee, the department or the governmental entity shall release the information to:

facts.claim: If your crash was more than two weeks ago and your report is not available, contact the investigating agency, such as the police department, to ask whether the report has been submitted.
facts.quote: If your crash happened more than two weeks ago and your report is not available, please reach out to the Investigating Agency, i.e. Police Department, to inquire if the report has been submitted.

facts.claim: TxDOT is the custodian of record for the crash report only, and subpoena requests for dash cam videos, field notes, photographs or other on-scene information should go to the investigating agency.
facts.quote: TxDOT is the custodian of record for the crash report only. Any subpoena requests for dash cam videos, field notes, photographs, or other information taken on scene, should be submitted to the investigating agency.

facts.claim: Effective Sept. 1, 2017, under Senate Bill 312 of the 85th Texas Legislature, TxDOT no longer retains the Driver's Crash Report (Form CR-2).
facts.quote: Effective Sept. 1, 2017, per the 85th Texas Legislature Senate Bill 312, the Driver's Crash Report (Form CR-2) is no longer retained by TxDOT.

facts.claim: TxDOT no longer has any Driver’s Crash Reports in its custodial records and no longer hosts or provides copies of the CR-2 form.
facts.quote: As a result, TxDOT no longer has any Driver’s Crash Reports in its custodial records and no longer hosts or provides copies of the CR-2 form.

facts.claim: Drivers in a crash not investigated by a police officer who were given a CR-2 or similar local agency form should keep that information for their records.
facts.quote: Drivers involved in a crash not investigated by a police officer who were provided a CR-2 or similar local agency form should retain this information for their records.

facts.claim: Any CR-2 or similar local agency form submitted to TxDOT will be destroyed under its records retention policy.
facts.quote: Please note that any CR-2 or similar local agency form submitted to TxDOT will be destroyed as required by our records retention policy.

facts.claim: Texas Transportation Code §550.065 refers to Sections 550.061 and 601.004 as former sections, covering reports required under them before September 1, 2017.
facts.quote: (B) former Section 550.061 or 601.004 before September 1, 2017; or

facts.claim: A driver in a collision that causes injury or death, or leaves a vehicle unable to be normally and safely driven, must immediately give notice of the collision by the quickest means of communication.
facts.quote: The operator of a vehicle involved in a collision resulting in injury to or death of a person or damage to a vehicle to the extent that it cannot be normally and safely driven shall immediately by the quickest means of communication give notice of the collision to the:

facts.claim: If the collision happened in a municipality, that notice goes to the local police department.
facts.quote: (1) local police department if the collision occurred in a municipality;

facts.claim: A municipality may, by ordinance, require a driver involved in a collision to file a report with a designated municipal department if the collision causes injury or death or apparent total property damage of $25 or more.
facts.quote: A municipality by ordinance may require the operator of a vehicle involved in a collision to file with a designated municipal department: (1) a report of the collision, if the collision results in injury to or the death of a person or the apparent total property damage is $25 or more;

facts.claim: Because of their confidential nature, crash reports are not available for online viewing by the general public.
facts.quote: Due to their confidential nature, crash reports are not available for online viewing by the general public.

facts.claim: After purchase, additional copies can be made at no charge and the download feature is available for 10 days from the date of purchase.
facts.quote: Once a report is purchased, additional copies can be made at no charge and a download feature is available for 10 days from the date of purchase.

facts.claim: The CRIS help desk phone line is (844) CRIS-HLP, open 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM, 7 days a week, 365 days a year.
facts.quote: Phone: (844) CRIS-HLP, 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM, 7 days per week, 365 days per year.

facts.claim: State law also entitles an employee or authorized representative of a vehicle storage facility that stored a vehicle involved in the collision to the full report.
facts.quote: (M) an employee or authorized representative of a vehicle storage facility, as defined by Section 2303.002, Occupations Code, that stored a vehicle involved in the collision.

facts.claim: A person under contract to provide claims or underwriting information to a policyholder or insurer is also entitled to the full report.
facts.quote: (I) a person under contract to provide claims or underwriting information to a person described by Paragraph (F), (G), or (H);

facts.claim: FCC-licensed radio and television stations are also entitled to the full report.
facts.quote: (J) a radio or television station that holds a license issued by the Federal Communications Commission;

facts.claim: The report must also be released to the court where a case involving a person in the collision is pending, if the report is subpoenaed.
facts.quote: (3) the court in which a case involving a person involved in the collision is pending if the report is subpoenaed; or

facts.claim: TxDOT also releases reports to federal, Texas state and Texas local government agencies.
facts.quote: An agency of the United States, this state (Texas), or a local government of this state (Texas)

facts.claim: Redacted reports hide all personal information, including phone numbers, addresses and dates of birth.
facts.quote: Redacted: All personal information including but not limited to phone numbers, addresses, and dates of birth will be hidden from view. Redacted Crash Reports are available to anyone.

facts.claim: On the CR-91, a requester who does not check a qualification or give sufficient justification receives a redacted copy.
facts.quote: If you did not indicate that you meet the qualifications of Texas Transportation Code §550.065 (c)(4) by either checking a qualification listed above or providing sufficient justification for your qualification, then a redacted copy will be provided.

facts.claim: Only one non-redacted report can be bought per purchase; any additional reports in the cart must be redacted.
facts.quote: Only one Non-Redacted report can be purchased. Any additional purchased reports will be required to be Redacted.

facts.claim: Electronic check payments funded by a foreign source cannot be processed.
facts.quote: NOTE – Payments being funded by a FOREIGN source cannot be processed.

facts.claim: To download a report again, use the 'Download Previous Purchase' button and enter the Local Reference ID from the purchase receipt.
facts.quote: Select the green ‘Download Previous Purchase’ button. 4. Enter the Local Reference ID provided on the Purchase Receipt Confirmation.

facts.claim: Advanced name-search fields include license plate number and investigating agency, among others.
facts.quote: a. License Plate Number – The license plate number for any vehicle involved in the crash. b. Investigating Agency – The law enforcement agency that investigated the crash and submitted the crash report.

facts.claim: On the CR-91, an organization name is required when the requester qualifies under categories G through K (insurers, claims contractors, broadcasters, newspapers).
facts.quote: Organization Name (If checking G, H, I, J, or K above):

facts.claim: A certified copy includes a certification signed by the Custodian of Motor Vehicle Crash Records with the TxDOT seal. Certified copies are usually needed for legal proceedings or employment verification.
facts.quote: This document includes the signature of the Custodian of Motor Vehicle Crash Records as well as the official Texas Department of Transportation seal. Certified reports are usually required for legal proceedings, employment verification, etc.

facts.claim: For card purchases, the online total includes a Texas.gov processing fee and surcharge.
facts.quote: The price for each report is shown, as well as the Total Price that includes a processing fee and surcharge from Texas.gov for credit card purchases.

facts.claim: Non-redacted purchases that rely on a written justification are not available for immediate download.
facts.quote: Note 2 - Reports that require justification will not be made immediately available.

facts.claim: A combined affidavit and state or federal subpoena request takes 10 business days.
facts.quote: Affidavit and a State or Federal Subpoena - 10 business days

facts.claim: TxDOT will not supply bulk copies of crash reports. For bulk requests it provides matching crash ID numbers, and each report must then be bought individually.
facts.quote: The Texas Transportation Code requires that all crash records be purchased and therefore bulk requests for multiple crash reports cannot be provided. Crash ID numbers corresponding to the request parameters will be provided instead, allowing the requestor to purchase at their leisure.

facts.claim: In CRIS Request, subpoena and affidavit requesters search for the report and upload their legal documents in PDF format.

gaps.reason: No official page I read gives the exact amount of the Texas.gov surcharge or card processing fee. TxDOT calls it only a 'minimal surcharge' or 'minimal Texas.gov fee'. Finding the amount would mean starting a purchase, which was out of scope.

No official TxDOT page describes an in-person or walk-in way to get a crash report from TxDOT. The state pages describe only online purchase and the CR-91 mail form. Whether a local police department or sheriff offers walk-in copies varies by agency and was not researched agency by agency.

Official sources do not agree cleanly on mail. The live CRIS Purchase Help Center says you can still buy a copy by mailing the CR-91, and the CR-91 (Rev. 08/23) is still posted. TxDOT's main crash records page no longer mentions mail purchases of ordinary copies. It also says that since January 1, 2025 subpoena and affidavit requests are no longer accepted by mail, the CR-91 is no longer required for them, and 'all requests received by mail will be returned'. Confirm with the CRIS help desk before telling readers to mail an ordinary request.

The form number is inconsistent. TxDOT's crash records page, its CRASH page, its forms page and the CRIS Purchase User Guide call the officer's report the CR-3. The live CRIS Purchase Help Center, the purchase portal home page and the CRIS Request page call it the CR-4. I found no official explanation. Claims above keep each source's own form number.

The Texas Department of Public Safety page on crash records (https://www.dps.texas.gov/node/415) could not be opened: the connection was refused. So I include no DPS-specific facts, such as what DPS keeps for trooper-investigated crashes.

State sources show that TxDOT collects reports from every law enforcement agency. They also show that a governmental entity holding a report must release it under the same §550.065 rules and $6/$2 statutory fee. Each city police department's or sheriff's own request process, any extra fees, and any vendor portal it uses were not checked.

No current official source I read says plainly whether drivers must file their own written crash report with a state agency. It also gives no current form, deadline or threshold for one. TxDOT says it no longer keeps or provides the CR-2 and destroys any CR-2 submitted. The statute calls the old sections 550.061 and 601.004 'former'. The current law requires immediate notice to police for certain crashes (§550.026) and lets cities require reports by ordinance (§550.067). The CR-2's former deadline and threshold were not confirmed on a current official page.
No official source I read sets a time-based confidentiality period. Access depends on the requester's relationship to the crash under §550.065. Others get a redacted copy.

Official sources give only maximums, not a typical wait. These are: officers have 10 days to file, TxDOT may need up to 4 business days to process, a report can take up to 14 days to appear online, and mail can take up to 30 days.

gaps.reason: The shared WebSearch budget was already used up at the start of this task, so no searches ran. Every page was reached by opening known official URLs directly and following links from them, so some relevant official pages (such as other local agencies' crash report pages) may have been missed.
DMV's crash report page lists only mail, fax and in-person submission. No state-level online request portal was found, and the page names no vendor.

No official source read says how soon after a crash a report can be obtained from DMV or how long DMV takes to process and mail a request. The only timing found is the statutory 24-hour deadline for officers to forward reports to DMV, plus Fairfax County Police's three-to-four-week estimate for mailed non-reportable report requests.

No card, convenience or processing fee for crash reports appears on DMV's crash report page, CRD 93, DMS 004 or the DMV 201 fee chart. It is also unclear whether a certified copy of a crash report is offered: CRD 93 lists an additional $5.00 'Record Certification Fee', but the DMV 201 fee chart describes the $5.00 certification fee only for driving or vehicle records.

The fax numbers conflict. DMV's crash report page lists (804) 367-0390, while the DMS 004 payment authorization form (02/10/2026) lists the Customer Records Work Center fax as (804) 367-6710. Readers should confirm with DMV before faxing.
DMV's page does not say whether ID must be shown or sent for mail or fax requests. CRD 93 records proof of the requester's identification only in its staff-use customer service center section.

Only three local agency pages were read (Fairfax County Police, Loudoun County Sheriff's Office and Alexandria Police), and their practices differ. The Alexandria-linked Crashdocs page returned HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and smart_fetch, so its fees, search requirements and availability could not be confirmed.
No official source read requires drivers to file their own crash report with DMV (§ 46.2-372 says a person 'may' make a written report), and the FR 200 form gives no filing deadline.
Sources say DMV keeps crash reports for 'at least 36 months'. No official source read says whether reports older than 36 months can still be obtained from DMV.

facts.claim: On VG-116, the requester affirms under penalty of perjury under Vermont law that the information on the form is true and correct.
facts.quote: I hereby affirm, under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of Vermont, that the information on this form is true and correct.

facts.claim: The denial section of VG-116 tells requesters they can appeal a denial to the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles, in writing.
facts.quote: You have the right to appeal this denial to the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles (must be submitted in writing).

facts.claim: The VG-116 form says to call 802.828.2000 if you are unsure which identification and authorization documents are required.
facts.quote: If you are unsure of what documents are required, please call 802.828.2000.

facts.claim: The DMV's Public Records page says copy fees set by 23 V.S.A. § 114 may override the fees in the State's uniform schedule of public records charges.
facts.quote: Note that there are fees for copies of public records established by 23 V.S.A. § 114 that may override the fees established by this schedule.

facts.claim: VTrans says fatal crash reports go into its crash database as soon as there is enough information, but it may take 90 days or more to receive all the data for a fatal crash.
facts.quote: Fatal crash reports are submitted to the database as soon as sufficient information is available. Due to the complexity of a fatal crash investigation, it may take 90 days or more to receive all data related to a crash.

facts.claim: Vermont's FFY2024 Traffic Records Strategic Plan says VTrans does not enter data from operators' own crash reports into the crash repository. Those reports are used to support financial responsibility.
facts.quote: VTrans does not enter data from the operator reports into the crash repository or use the information for traffic safety analysis. The operator reports are used to support financial responsibility.

facts.claim: The VC-004 form says a crash involving more than two vehicles needs as many forms as it takes to include every vehicle involved.
facts.quote: A crash with more than two vehicles involved must fill out as many forms as needed to include all vehicles involved in the crash.

facts.claim: The VC-004 form warns that if the operator does not give full insurance information, DMV will assume they have no automobile liability insurance and will suspend their license or privilege to operate in Vermont.
facts.quote: IF YOU FAIL TO GIVE FULL INFORMATION BELOW, IT WILL BE ASSUMED THAT YOU DO NOT HAVE AUTOMOBILE LIABILITY INSURANCE AND A SUSPENSION OF YOUR LICENSE/PRIVILEGE TO OPERATE IN VERMONT WILL BE ISSUED.

facts.claim: Under 23 V.S.A. § 1129(b), a 'crash' that must be reported is only an event in which the motor vehicle physically contacts a person or object, including another motor vehicle.
facts.quote: As used in this section, the word “crash” only refers to incidents and events in which the motor vehicle involved comes into physical contact with an individual or object, including another motor vehicle.

It links straight to /sites/dmv/files/documents/VG-116-Record_Request.pdf, describes it as the form 'To request records and documents including driving records, certified copies, police and individual crash reports, etc.', and links to 23 V.S.A. § 114 on legislature.vermont.gov.

gaps.reason: No official page offers a way to order a Vermont crash report copy online. The DMV's online Public Records Request form excludes crash reports, the State Police online portal sends State Police crash reports to the DMV, and no official page names a vendor crash-report portal (such as BuyCrash) for Vermont.
No official page confirms in-person requests for crash reports. The DMV mentions scheduling an appointment at the Montpelier office only for individuals requesting a copy of their own driving record.

No official page says explicitly whether the DMV's certified 'police crash report' copies include crashes handled by municipal police departments or county sheriffs, or whether those reports must be requested from the local agency. The VTrans traffic records plan says all law enforcement crash reports go into the statewide Web Crash system, and the State Police portal says reports from other agencies must be requested from that agency, but neither addresses copies of local-agency crash reports directly.

No Vermont statute or official page was found that limits crash report copies to involved parties or sets a confidentiality period. The DMV form applies Driver Privacy Protection Act review and requires ID, but does not say which DPPA category a crash-report requester must fall under.

No card payment option or convenience fee is stated for DMV crash report requests; form VG-116 specifies check or money order. The State Police online portal FAQ mentions an 'enhanced access fee' with no amount, but that portal is for State Police records, not crash reports.

The DMV does not state its own processing time for crash report requests. The 30-day availability comes from the State Police page. The Investigator's Guide that the VTrans plan cites for the 30-day law enforcement forwarding period could not be opened (vtrans.vermont.gov/crash-manual returned 404).

No official page lists the crash-specific details (such as crash date, location, report or case number, or investigating agency) the DMV needs to find a crash report; form VG-116 has only general fields and a free-text 'specific information requested' box.

The VTrans traffic records plan cites 23 V.S.A. § 1603(b) for the crash repository designation, but the current § 1603 ('Investigation of crashes') has no subsection (b) and does not mention a repository, so that citation should not be relied on.

Web search was unavailable for this run because the shared search budget was used up on the first query. Official pages were found by navigating directly from vsp.vermont.gov, dmv.vermont.gov, legislature.vermont.gov, vtrans.vermont.gov and shso.vermont.gov, so official pages not linked from those sites may have been missed.

facts.claim: The Washington State Patrol's Collision Records Section says it is the repository for all collision reports in the state of Washington.
facts.quote: WSP Collision Record Section is the repository for all collision reports in the state of Washington.

facts.claim: State law makes the chief of the Washington State Patrol responsible for filing, tabulating and analyzing all accident reports.
facts.quote: It shall be the duty of the chief of the Washington state patrol to file, tabulate, and analyze all accident reports

facts.claim: WSP's Police Traffic Collision Report (PTCR) instruction manual says the PTCR was developed for use by all police officers investigating vehicle collisions.
facts.quote: The PTCR was developed for use by all police officers investigating vehicle collisions.

facts.claim: The same manual says officers' reports must be submitted to the Washington State Patrol Collision Records Section within 4 days after the accident.
facts.quote: Reports shall be submitted to the Washington State Patrol Collision Records Section within 4 days after any accident per Revised Code of Washington (RCW) 46.52.030.

facts.claim: If a collision does not meet the reporting requirements or happens on private property, the responding agency decides whether a PTCR is completed and filed.
facts.quote: If the collision does not meet the reporting requirements and/or occurs on private property, it is at the discretion of the responding agency whether or not a PTCR is completed and filed.

facts.claim: WSP Collision Records keeps only the official police report (PTCR) or civilian report (MVCR), not related case information.
facts.quote: We do not receive, store, or maintain any related case information. The section only maintains the official PTCR (Police Traffic Collision Report) or civilian MVCR (Motor Vehicle Collision Report).

facts.claim: WSP's retention schedule for collision records is 10 years.
facts.quote: Our retention schedule is 10 years.

facts.claim: WSP's online system, the Washington State Patrol Requests for Electronic Collision Records (WRECR), lets you search for a collision report from a computer with internet access and an email account.
facts.quote: The Washington State Patrol Requests for Electronic Collision Records (WRECR) system will allow you to search for a collision report from a computer station with internet access and an e-mail account.

facts.claim: WSP says you can use WRECR to order and download your collision report electronically, or request a report by mail.
facts.quote: Use the WRECR application above to order and download your collision report electronically, or you can request a report by mail using the process above.

facts.claim: On WRECR you provide the name of the involved party or parties and the date of the collision, then select Search.
facts.quote: Step 2) Provide the name of the involved party(s), the date of the collision, and select “Search”

facts.claim: To request a copy by mail, WSP says to complete the entire Request for Copy of Collision Report form.
facts.quote: Step 1) Complete the entire Request for Copy of Collision Report Form

facts.claim: The Request for Copy of Collision Report is WSP form 3000-345-008 (R 1/19).
The form says to mail requests to WSP, Collision Records Section, PO Box 42628, Olympia WA 98504-2628.
facts.quote: Mail to: WSP, Collision Records Section, PO Box 42628, Olympia WA 98504-2628.

facts.claim: WSP's Collision Records office is open by appointment only, and appointments are made by phone or email.
facts.quote: Collision Records office is available by appointment only. To schedule an appointment, call or email using the contact information below.

facts.claim: WSP's Collision Records office is at 106 11th Avenue SW, Suite 1300, Olympia, WA 98501.
facts.quote: 106 11th Avenue SW Suite 1300 Olympia, WA 98501

facts.claim: Collision Records staff are available Monday through Friday, 7:00 am to 3:30 pm, except on legally designated holidays.
facts.quote: Staff is available Monday through Friday, 7:00 am to 3:30 pm, except on legally designated holidays.

facts.claim: WSP does not accept cash for collision reports; it takes checks or money orders by mail and credit cards at the kiosk in its office.
facts.quote: Our office does not accept cash for the purchase of a collision report either by mail or at our office using the kiosk. Our Section only accepts check or money order through the mail, and credit card through our kiosk.

facts.claim: WSP Collision Records does not give out collision information over the phone.
facts.quote: No, we do not give out collision information over the phone.

facts.claim: For documents beyond the collision report itself, WSP says you must submit a public disclosure request to the agency that made the report.
facts.quote: You will have to submit a public disclosure request to the reporting agency for additional documents.

facts.claim: WSP's Collision Records page gives links for submitting public records requests to state agencies.
facts.quote: Submit a Public Records Request to the following State agencies using the links below.

facts.claim: WRECR's search accepts any of these: collision report number, case number, collision date, occupant's name, city, or county.
facts.quote: Use the search function to enter any of the following; collision report number, case number, collision date, occupants name, city, or county.

facts.claim: WRECR's help says 'involvement type' means your specific involvement in the collision, such as driver, passenger, witness, property owner, insurance company, law office, or parent or guardian of a minor.
facts.quote: This is your specific involvement in the collision. You could be a driver, passenger, witness, property owner, insurance company, law office, or parent or guardian of a minor.

facts.claim: On the mail-in request form, the date of collision and the county where it occurred are marked as required, and the collision report number is optional.
facts.quote: Collision Report Number (optional) * Date of Collision *County Where Collision Occurred

facts.claim: The mail-in form also marks the name of the roadway where the collision occurred as required.
facts.quote: *Name of Roadway Where Collision Occurred

facts.claim: The mail-in form's collision information section marks a last name and a first name as required.
facts.quote: *Last Name *First Name

facts.claim: The mail-in form asks the requester to check one box saying how they were involved in the collision.
facts.quote: How Were You Involved in This Collision? (Check One Box)

facts.claim: A requester who checks 'Other Authorized Representative' on the mail-in form must include an authorization letter.
facts.quote: Other Authorized Representative (Authorization Letter Required)

facts.claim: If you don't recall the collision date, WRECR's help suggests requesting your Driver's Abstract/Record from the Department of Licensing, which lists collisions you or your registered vehicle were reported to be involved in.
facts.quote: Go to the Department of Licensing website at dol@wa.gov and request a copy of your Driver's Abstract/Record. This will list all collisions either you or your registered vehicle have been reported to be involved in.

facts.claim: Searching WRECR is free, and buying a report costs $10.50 per report.
facts.quote: There is no fee to search for a report, however if you wish to purchase the report there is a fee of $10.50 per report.

facts.claim: WSP charges a $10.50 fee for a copy of a collision report, citing RCW 46.52.085.
facts.quote: If you wish to obtain a copy of your request, a fee of $10.50 will be charged per RCW 46.52.085

facts.claim: Each mail request must include a $10.50 check or money order payable to the Washington State Patrol, and cash should not be sent.
facts.quote: A $10.50 check or money order is to be made payable to the Washington State Patrol and is to be accompanied with each request. (Please do not send cash.)

facts.claim: RCW 46.52.085 allows releasable collision information to be provided in writing for a fee sufficient to meet, but not exceed, the costs incurred.
facts.quote: Any information authorized for release under RCW 46.52.080 and 46.52.083 may be furnished in written form for a fee sufficient to meet, but not exceed, the costs incurred.

facts.claim: WSP says it may take up to a total of 2-4 weeks before a report is available for request.
facts.quote: It may take up to a total of 2-4 weeks before the report is available for request.

facts.claim: WSP says officers have 2-4 weeks to complete their investigation and get the report approved by a supervisor, and reports are typically available much sooner.
facts.quote: Officers completing the collision reports have 2-4 weeks to complete their investigation and have their report approved by their supervisor. It is typically available much sooner, but that is the guideline.

facts.claim: The mail-in form says it may take up to 2-4 weeks for a report to be available for disclosure online or in office.
facts.quote: Please take into consideration it may take up to 2-4 weeks for a report to be available for disclosure online or in office.

facts.claim: Certified copies of collision reports are available and typically take 5-7 business days.
facts.quote: Can I get a certified copy of a collision report? Yes, but it typically takes 5-7 business days to complete that request.

facts.claim: WSP's request form says Washington law allows release of collision reports only to certain persons under RCW 46.52.080 and 083.
facts.quote: Washington State Law provides for the release of collision reports only to certain persons (RCW 46.52.080 and 083).

facts.claim: WSP says entitled parties receive a non-redacted copy of the collision record.
facts.quote: Please note, individuals who are entitled parties will receive a non-redacted copy of the record per the RCW listed below.

facts.claim: Individuals or agencies that do not meet the definition of entitled parties receive a redacted copy under RCW 42.56, the Public Records Act.
facts.quote: Additionally, those individuals or agencies that do not meet the definition of entitled parties will be provided a redacted copy of the collision report per RCW 42.56 Public Records Act.

facts.claim: RCW 46.52.080's list of interested persons includes the drivers involved, a driver's legal guardian, the parent of a minor driver, injured persons, owners of damaged vehicles or property, and authorized representatives, attorneys or insurers of such parties.
facts.quote: including the driver or drivers involved, or the legal guardian thereof, the parent of a minor driver, any person injured therein, the owner of vehicles or property damaged thereby, or any authorized representative of such an interested party, or the attorney or insurer thereof.

facts.claim: RCW 46.52.083 makes officers' factual data and all witnesses' signed statements, but not the reports signed by the drivers, available on request to the interested parties named in RCW 46.52.080.
facts.quote: All of the factual data submitted in report form by the officers, together with the signed statements of all witnesses, except the reports signed by the drivers involved in the accident, shall be made available upon request to the interested parties named in RCW 46.52.080.

facts.claim: State law requires any police officer of the state or of any county, city, town or other political subdivision who is at an accident scene, or has facts about an accident, to make a report of it.
facts.quote: Any police officer of the state of Washington or of any county, city, town, or other political subdivision, present at the scene of any accident or in possession of any facts concerning any accident whether by way of official investigation or otherwise shall make report thereof

facts.claim: RCW 46.52.030 requires the authority that receives a driver's accident report to forward the original immediately to the chief of the Washington State Patrol in Olympia.
facts.quote: The original of the report shall be immediately forwarded by the authority receiving the report to the chief of the Washington state patrol at Olympia, Washington.

facts.claim: If you are unsure whether a report was completed, WSP says to contact the officer or department that arrived at the scene to verify.
facts.quote: If unsure, please contact the officer or department that arrived at the scene for verification.

facts.claim: The Seattle Police Department says the Washington State Patrol is the custodian of all collision reports within the State of Washington.
facts.quote: Washington State Patrol is the custodian of all collision reports within the State of Washington.

facts.claim: For collisions outside Seattle city limits, the Seattle Police Department says you can contact the local agency where the collision occurred or search WSP's Collision Report Search application.
facts.quote: If you were in a collision outside of Seattle City limits, you can contact the local agency where the collision occurred, or you can search the WSP Collision Report Search application.

facts.claim: Any driver, pedestrian, pedalcyclist or property owner involved in a Washington collision with $1,000 or more of damage to any one unit and/or injury to any person must complete a Motor Vehicle Collision Report (MVCR).
facts.quote: Any driver, pedestrian, pedalcycle, or property owner involved in a collision within this state – with $1,000 or more of damage to any one unit and/or injury to any person must complete a Motor Vehicle Collision Report (MVCR)

facts.claim: You are not required to submit an MVCR if a police officer is present and indicates he or she will submit a collision report.
facts.quote: However, if a police officer is present and indicates he/she will submit a collision report, then you are not required to submit one.

facts.claim: State law requires the driver's written report within four days after the accident, made to the city or town chief of police inside an incorporated city or town, or to the county sheriff or state patrol outside one.
facts.quote: shall, within four days after such accident, make a written report of such accident to the chief of police of the city or town if such accident occurred within an incorporated city or town or the county sheriff or state patrol if such accident occurred outside incorporated cities and towns.

facts.claim: The driver's reporting duty applies to accidents with injury or death, or with property damage to any one person at or above the minimum amount set by rule of the chief of the Washington State Patrol.
facts.quote: the driver of any vehicle involved in an accident resulting in injury to or death of any person or damage to the property of any one person to an apparent extent equal to or greater than the minimum amount established by rule adopted by the chief of the Washington state patrol

facts.claim: Under WAC 446-85-010, beginning January 1, 2015, the accident-reporting threshold for property damage accidents is one thousand dollars.
facts.quote: Beginning January 1, 2015, the accident-reporting threshold for property damage accidents will be one thousand dollars.

facts.claim: The MVCR can be submitted online at www.wrecr.wsp.wa.gov/omvcr, and you automatically receive a copy of your report with a report number by email.
facts.quote: Option 1: Submit an online version at www.wrecr.wsp.wa.gov/omvcr and you will automatically receive a copy of your report with a report number via email.

facts.claim: WSP says filing online through OMVCR gives you your collision report and report number immediately, which is what most insurance companies need to process a claim.
facts.quote: This will allow you to complete and submit your report electronically and will provide your collision report and report number immediately. This is what most insurance companies will need to process your claim.

facts.claim: A completed and signed paper MVCR can be mailed to Washington State Patrol, Collision Records Section, PO Box 42628, Olympia, WA 98504-2628, or emailed to collisionrecords@wsp.wa.gov.
facts.quote: Mail the completed and signed report to Washington State Patrol, Collision Records Section, PO Box 42628, Olympia, WA 98504-2628 or email it to collisionrecords@wsp.wa.gov.

facts.claim: The paper Motor Vehicle Collision Report is WSP form 3000-345-161 (R 3/26).
Processing a paper MVCR may take up to 7 business days, after which the report number is available at www.wrecr.wsp.wa.gov.
facts.quote: Processing the report may take up to 7 business days. Once it has been processed, your report number will be available at www.wrecr.wsp.wa.gov.

facts.claim: A civilian Motor Vehicle Collision Report will not be investigated by law enforcement.
facts.quote: This report will not be investigated by law enforcement.

facts.claim: Under RCW 46.52.035, the director may suspend the driving license or permit of anyone who fails to report an accident as RCW 46.52.030 requires, until the report is filed.
facts.quote: The director may suspend the license or permit to drive and any nonresident operating privileges of any person failing to report an accident as provided in RCW 46.52.030 until such report has been filed.

facts.claim: Only the officer who completed a collision report has the authority to change it.
facts.quote: Only the officer that completed the report has the authority to make any changes to the report.

facts.claim: WSP Collision Records can be contacted at (360) 570-2355 or collisionrecords@wsp.wa.gov.
facts.quote: If you have any questions, please contact WSP Collision Records at (360) 570-2355 or via e-mail at collisionrecords@wsp.wa.gov.

facts.claim: On WRECR's search form, the search by date, name and location requires a collision date range; the other fields in that search are optional (the form also offers Collision Report # or Case # searches as alternatives).
facts.quote: Collision date range is required. All other fields are optional.

facts.claim: WRECR offers Billable Accounts, which sign in through SecureAccess Washington (SAW). To get one, contact the Collision Records Department.
facts.quote: Click the Log In button to be redirected to SecureAccess Washington (SAW) to log in to your Billable Account. After logging in, you will be taken back to the WRECR Portal. If you do not have a Billable Account and would like to request one, please contact the Collision Records Department.

facts.claim: The mail-in request form asks you to check one box for the report type: Police Traffic Collision Report (officer investigated) or Motor Vehicle Collision Report (not officer investigated).
facts.quote: Type of Report Requested (Check one box) Police Traffic Collision Report (Officer Investigated) Motor Vehicle Collision Report (Non Officer-Investigated)

facts.claim: RCW 46.52.030 does not prohibit drivers from filing an accident report when property damage is below the minimum amount or when a law enforcement officer has already submitted a report.
facts.quote: Nothing in this subsection prohibits accident reports from being filed by drivers where damage to property is less than the minimum amount or where a law enforcement officer has submitted a report.

facts.claim: If the other driver is submitting a civilian collision report, WSP highly recommends submitting your own report too.
facts.quote: If the other driver is submitting a civilian collision report, do I still have to complete one? WSP highly recommends submitting your own report.

facts.claim: If your car was hit in a parking lot and you don't know exactly when or where, you can still file an OMVCR. Use the date you found the damage, the county where you believe it happened, and 'unknown' for the other driver's information.
facts.quote: My car was hit in a parking lot, I don't know exactly when or where, what do I do? You can still complete an OMVCR report, you can put the date you located the damage, the county where you believe it occurred and unknown for the other driver's information.

facts.claim: WSP's OMVCR page says a civilian report will not be investigated by local law enforcement, WSP or the WSP Collision Records Section, and is for your records or for insurance purposes.
facts.quote: keep in mind that the report will not be investigated by local law enforcement, WSP, or the WSP Collision Records Section. This report will be for your records or for insurance purposes.

facts.claim: MVCRs filed online reach WSP electronically, and WSP says not to mail them to WSP Collision Records as well.
facts.quote: These reports will be received by WSP electronically. Do not mail them to WSP Collision Records.

facts.claim: WSP Collision Records only files the collision report itself, so do not send photos, estimates or statements with an MVCR.
facts.quote: WSP Collision Records only files the collision reports. Do not send photos, estimates, statements, etc.

facts.claim: On the paper MVCR, the date of collision is a mandatory field. If the date is unknown, use the date the damage was discovered.
facts.quote: Date collision occurred. If the date of the collision is unknown, use the date the damage was discovered (mandatory field).

facts.claim: The person completing the MVCR must sign and date it and give their address. The form says the signature is a legal requirement.
facts.quote: The person completing the form must sign and date the form and provide his or her address. The signature is a legal requirement (mandatory field).

facts.claim: In its FAQ about a 'no record found' result on WRECR, WSP says an officer who judges the damage to be under the $1,000 threshold would direct you to complete a citizen report.
facts.quote: If an officer arrived at the scene and completed a report, they typically would provide you an exchange of information or direct you to our website, if the damage threshold of $1,000 was not met based on their observation, they would direct you to complete a citizen report.

facts.claim: WSP's PTCR manual says that when a reportable collision happens on private property or no officer responds, the people involved should be advised to complete a Motor Vehicle Collision Report.
facts.quote: If the collision meets the reporting requirements and occurs on private property or an officer does not respond, the involved parties should be advised to complete a Motor Vehicle Collision Report (VCR).

facts.claim: WSP's PTCR manual says the Collision Records Section only retains PTCR forms. It tells officers not to attach citations, impound forms, DUI forms, photographs, public web maps or witness statements.
facts.quote: The Collision Records Section only retains PTCR forms. 1. Do not attach citations, impound forms, Driving Under the Influence (DUI) forms, photographs, public web maps, or witness statements to the PTCR form.

facts.claim: WSP cannot remove a collision from your driving record. The Department of Licensing is the custodian of your Abstract Driving Record, and mistakes on it go to DOL at 360-902-3900.
facts.quote: I have a collision on my record, can you remove it? No, The Department of Licensing (DOL) is the custodian of your Abstract Driving Record (ADR). If there is a mistake on your driving record, please contact DOL at 360-902-3900.

facts.claim: RCW 46.52.080 says a required accident report or copy may not be used as evidence in any civil or criminal trial arising out of the accident, subject to limited exceptions in that section.
facts.quote: No such accident report or copy thereof shall be used as evidence in any trial, civil or criminal, arising out of an accident

facts.claim: State law (RCW 46.52.088) prohibits knowingly giving false information in the oral or written reports required by chapter 46.52 RCW.
facts.quote: A person shall not give information in oral or written reports as required in chapter 46.52 RCW knowing that such information is false.

facts.claim: Under RCW 46.52.040, if the driver in a reportable accident is physically unable to make the required report, another occupant who was in the vehicle (not a passenger for hire) and is able to report must make or arrange it.
facts.quote: is physically incapable of making the required accident report and there is another occupant other than a passenger for hire therein, in the vehicle at the time of the accident capable of making a report, such occupant shall make or cause to be made such report.

facts.claim: WSP publishes overlay sheets that explain the side codes on a collision report.
facts.quote: Side coding is used on a collision report to categorize the massive amounts of collision details contained in the report. The Overlay Sheets will assist you in understanding what each box represents.

facts.claim: The Department of Licensing charges $15 for each copy of your driving record.
facts.quote: Each copy of your driving record costs $15.

facts.claim: DOL says a driving record shows collision involvement, not fault. Collisions involving non-commercial vehicles stay on it for 5 years from the collision date.
facts.quote: Collisions—Shows involvement, not fault, number of vehicles involved, whether they were legally parked or moving, whether the vehicles were occupied at the time of the collision, and whether the collision resulted in any injury or fatality Non-commercial vehicles: 5 years from collision date

That old link (www.dol.wa.gov/driverslicense/drivingrecfaq.html) now redirects to dol.wa.gov/driver-licenses-and-permits/driving-records/guide-driving-records, which links to this page as 'Order your record now'.

gaps.reason: WRECR states only '$10.50 per report'. I could not confirm whether a card or convenience fee is added at checkout, because checking would mean starting a purchase, and this research was read-only.
WSP says certified copies are available (typically 5-7 business days), but none of the official pages I read gives a separate fee for a certified copy or explains how to order one.

RCW 46.52.085 only allows a fee that covers costs and names no dollar amount. I found no statute or rule that sets the $10.50 figure. That amount comes from WSP's Collision Records page, the WRECR site and WSP's request form.

Apart from the Seattle Police Department's page, I did not confirm any city police department's or county sheriff's own process or fee for copies of collision reports or related records. Note that seattle.gov is a city government site, not a state site.
None of the official Washington pages I read names or links a third-party vendor portal such as LexisNexis BuyCrash. The only online channel named on official pages is WSP's own WRECR.

Official sources differ on officer-report timing. The PTCR manual says reports must be submitted within 4 days (citing RCW 46.52.030), but WSP's Collision Records page says officers have 2-4 weeks to finish and get approval. No official source says how long a mail request takes to fill or how quickly a kiosk purchase is completed.
I found no official explanation of how WRECR checks that an online requester is an entitled party before releasing a non-redacted copy.
I could not confirm whether copies can be requested by email. The WSP pages I read mention email only for questions, appointments and sending in civilian MVCRs.
Quotes cited to https://wrecr.wsp.wa.gov/wrecr/order that come from its FAQ appear only after the page's Help panel is opened. The site is script-rendered, so a plain HTTP fetch shows almost no text.

This run's web search budget was used up before research began. I found pages by opening known official URLs and following links from WSP's Collision Records page, so relevant official pages may exist that I did not see.

gaps.reason: I could not read Wis. Stat. s. 346.70. docs.legis.wisconsin.gov refused or timed out on every attempt (WebFetch ECONNREFUSED, hound fetch and a direct check all failed). The statute's wording on police forwarding deadlines, any driver report deadline, report copies, fees and confidentiality is therefore unconfirmed. The reporting thresholds come from WisDOT's summary of s. 346.70(1).

No official page I read gives a deadline for filing the Wisconsin Driver Report of Crash (DT4002). WisDOT's enforcement FAQ answers 'Immediately' to when a crash must be reported, but it doesn't name the form or who receives the report.

The $6 figure comes from WisDOT's DMV fee table. crashreports.wi.gov shows no price before you search, and I did not run a search or buy anything. No page I read confirms whether the up-to-2.35% card or PayPal convenience fee is added to online crash report purchases, or what a mailed paper copy costs.

WisDOT's DMV contact page links 'Purchase mailed crash report' to the DMV email inquiry form, which I did not submit. No page I read gives a mail-in form name or number, payment method, address or turnaround for a paper copy from WisDOT. Milwaukee Police lists a WisDOT Crash Records Unit mailing address but no instructions.

No WisDOT page I read says who may buy a crash report (for example, only involved parties) or sets a confidentiality period. The purchase site asks only for a document number, or a crash date plus a Wisconsin driver license number. The only statements on requester identity and DPPA redaction come from the Waukesha County Sheriff's page.
No page I read says how someone without the document number or a Wisconsin driver license number, such as an out-of-state driver, can search the purchase site.

The sources conflict. WisDOT's enforcement FAQ says crashes 'that have occurred in the last 90 days' can be bought online, but crashreports.wi.gov says reports are available for four years from the crash date. The portal's statement looks more current, but the conflict is unresolved.
No page I read describes an in-person option at WisDOT's Crash Records Unit. The purchase site says reports are not available for pickup at any DMV office.

I checked only the Milwaukee Police Department and Waukesha County Sheriff pages. Other city and county agencies' methods and fees were not reviewed. No WisDOT page I read says outright that crashreports.wi.gov carries every local agency's reports. It says reports are made available once received from the reporting law enforcement agency, and that its TraCS forms, including the DT4000, are for use by all Wisconsin law enforcement agencies.

Web search was unavailable during this run because the shared search budget was used up. I found pages by following links from official sites, so other relevant official pages, such as a DT4000 instruction manual, may exist.

gaps.reason: No online request portal was found on wvsp.gov, dmv.wv.gov or transportation.wv.gov, and no official page names a vendor portal (such as BuyCrash, Crashdocs or PoliceReports.US) for State Police crash reports. The WVSP pages offer only Form 141 (mail, email or fax) and phone numbers. WebSearch could not be used because this turn's search budget was used up, so this was checked by browsing the official sites and their sitemaps instead. A follow-up search could confirm it.

Neither the WVSP crash-report pages nor Form 141 mention in-person requests or walk-in hours at the Traffic Records Section, 701 Jefferson Road. The 2003 WVSP FOIA rule (81CSR7) allows in-person filing of general FOIA requests at the Superintendent's office, 725 Jefferson Road. No source applies that to crash reports.

No official source says how soon a crash report is available to requesters after a crash. The FFY2027–2029 Highway Safety Plan gives only the mean time for reports to reach the state crash database (7.926 days). The 2003 WVSP FOIA rule sets a five-working-day response for FOIA requests filed with the Superintendent's office. No source ties that to crash-report requests sent to the Traffic Records Section.

No official source says whether crash reports are limited to involved parties or held back for a period. The West Virginia Code could not be read: every request to code.wvlegislature.gov, including from a normal browser user agent, was redirected to an unrelated FBI page. So any statutory confidentiality rules (Chapter 17C, Article 4, and the FOIA exemptions in §29B-1-4) could not be checked.

Form 141 states no card or convenience fee for credit card payments. It also does not say whether the $20.00 fee (listed for 'Crime or Vehicle Crash Report Mail') covers emailed crash reports, although it shows Mail and Email options for crash reports. No statute or rule setting the dollar amounts was found; 81CSR7 says only that the department sets fixed-rate fees.

No official source says the WVSP Traffic Records Section can supply reports written by city or county agencies; the DMV sends those requests to the investigating agency. No official source says whether the WV Division of Highways, custodian of the statewide crash database, gives out copies of individual reports. Its Traffic Accident Data page mentions only data.

No statewide list of request steps, fees or portals for city police or county sheriff crash reports was found. The only official guidance found is the DMV's instruction to contact the investigating agency.

No official source was found that requires drivers to file their own written crash report form with a state agency. The DMV handbook describes only a duty to report qualifying crashes to the local police, the county sheriff or the nearest State Police office. The statute (§17C-4-6 and §17C-4-7) could not be opened because code.wvlegislature.gov was redirecting all requests.

gaps.reason: Neither WYDOT's Crash Reports page nor the WHP Public Records page gives a fee, payment method or card fee for a crash report copy. Two statutes allow reasonable fees but set no amount for crash reports: the Public Records Act (W.S. 16-4-204) and W.S. 31-1-201(b), which covers certified copies of WYDOT records. W.S. 16-4-204(c) requires any fee to be authorized by statute, rule or similar authority, but no WYDOT fee rule was found. The rules database at rules.wyo.gov only works through a search form, and the read-only rules meant that form was not submitted. The web search budget for this run was used up before research began, so no further searching was possible.

No official source says how soon a crash report is available to requesters. The only official time frame found is the ten-day deadline in W.S. 31-5-1106(c) for officers to forward reports to WYDOT. That deadline is not a release date for copies.

No official source says who may get a copy of the crash report itself, for example only involved parties. W.S. 31-5-1110(b) restricts only supplemental information filed for financial responsibility. WYDOT's page says reports are kept and distributed "per State Statute" but does not name the statute or any eligibility limits.

WYDOT lists only phone, email and mail. No official page reviewed names an online request portal or a vendor portal such as BuyCrash, Crashdocs or PoliceReports.US for Wyoming crash reports. The WHP NextRequest portal is for WHP citations and case reports, and its landing page does not mention crash reports.

Only the WHP Public Records page lists the in-person option at the Cheyenne WYDOT office. WYDOT's own Crash Reports page lists just three ways: phone, email and mail. No official source gives office hours for in-person requests.
No official source names a request form or form number. WYDOT asks for a list of details by phone, email or mail but does not link a form.
WYDOT's list does not mention photo ID, a signed form, notarization or proof of involvement. No official source confirms whether any of these are required.

No official source describes a written crash report that drivers must file with a state agency, or a form, deadline or dollar threshold for one. The current statute (W.S. 31-5-1105) requires only immediate notice to law enforcement. The statute text marks W.S. 31-5-1106(a)-(b) and 31-5-1107(a) as "Repealed By Laws 2013, Ch. 102", but their former wording was not reviewed.

No city police or county sheriff records pages could be opened: the Cheyenne and Casper city websites returned HTTP 403, and web search was unavailable. So it is not confirmed whether local agencies also release copies directly, or what they charge. WYDOT says it collects reports from all law enforcement agencies statewide.
